In this paper, we extend some of these results by proving the following: (1) every $(k+1)$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least $4k-1$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least 3 is Hamiltonian; (2) every $2k$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$; (3) every $(k+1)$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 3k+5$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 8$ is Hamiltonian; (4) every $2k$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with order at least $4k+9$ is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$.

papers.title: Mirror flow for semimartingale optimal transport
papers.abstract: Semimartingale optimal transport arises in a wide range of applications, including mathematical finance and flow-based generative models. A recurring computational challenge is that the dual energy functional is often poorly conditioned with respect to the dual potential, leading to slow convergence of gradient descent algorithms. To address this issue, we investigate a mirror flow approach that effectively preconditions the dual energy functional. We establish the geometric convergence of the mirror descent sequence. To obtain a practical numerical algorithm, we introduce a feasible discrete-time scheme based on first-order linearization. We prove that the scheme is well-defined and establish a uniform-in-time error bound for the accumulated linearization error, under a suitable smallness condition on the initial error. Finally, we apply the proposed mirror flow scheme to the specific-entropic martingale optimal transport (SEMOT) problem \cite{BuetGolfouseEtAl2026SEMOT} and observe a substantial improvement in computational efficiency.

papers.title: Convergence of Implicit Particle Methods for Wasserstein Gradient Flows
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the convergence of implicit particle methods for Wasserstein gradient flows as the number of particles tends to infinity, with the time step held fixed. The schemes combine the Jordan--Kinderlehrer--Otto (JKO) variational time discretization with particle approximations of the evolving probability measure. The main challenge lies in approximating the internal energy, which depends nonlinearly on the probability density and cannot, in general, be evaluated directly on empirical measures. We consider three approaches: a one-dimensional density reconstruction based on the spacings between ordered particles; a blob method using kernel-based density reconstruction; and a transport-map formulation in which the density is recovered from the pushforward relation through the change-of-variables formula. The latter two approaches apply in arbitrary spatial dimensions without requiring the spatial domain to be compact. For the blob method, we also establish simultaneous convergence as the particle number tends to infinity and the regularization parameter vanishes, under the scaling $N\varepsilon_N^d\to\infty$. Our analysis combines $Γ$-convergence and compactness arguments to establish convergence of the discrete variational problems and their minimizers. These results complement classical dynamical mean-field theory by providing a variational particle-to-continuum limit for implicit JKO schemes involving nonlinear internal energies.

papers.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Unlike conventional matrix-preconditioned methods that use fixed decay parameters, NABLA adjusts the second-moment averaging coefficient through a closed-loop feedback rule determined by the cumulative stochastic-gradient energy and its running average. The first-moment coefficient remains fixed, allowing the trajectory-dependent adaptation to act directly on the structured preconditioners. The resulting method is horizon-free, requires no prior knowledge of the noise level, and automatically adjusts the memory of its second-moment estimators to the observed optimization dynamics. Under standard lower boundedness, smoothness, unbiasedness, bounded-variance, and spectral-boundedness assumptions, we establish uniform stability and variation bounds for the time-varying block preconditioners and control their interaction with momentum estimation and parameter updates. These results yield the noise-adaptive stationarity guarantee $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2}+σ^{1/2}T^{-1/4})$, which automatically reduces to the nearly deterministic $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ rate when the stochastic-gradient noise vanishes. NABLA therefore provides a principled approach to combining closed-loop trajectory feedback with memory-efficient structured matrix preconditioning.

papers.title: Mixed local and fractional laplacian problems with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions
papers.abstract: The existence of non-constant solutions to a mixed local-nonlocal elliptic problem with $(α,β)$-Neumann conditions, critical exponent, and parameter $λ>0$ is established for any $λ$ large enough. Proofs exploit both mountain-pass-type arguments and appropriate boundary Sobolev inequalities patterned after those of [19].

papers.title: Quadratic Wasserstein transport for elliptical distributions
papers.abstract: The quadratic Wasserstein distance between Gaussian distributions is given by the classical Bures-Wasserstein formula, which depends only on the means, the covariance matrices $Σ_0$ and $Σ_1$, and their interaction $K=(Σ_0^{1/2}Σ_1Σ_0^{1/2})^{1/2}$. The same formula holds for elliptical distributions with a common radial law. In this paper, we extend this representation to general elliptical distributions by identifying an additional transport cost $Γ$ that depends on the radial laws and the spectrum of $K$. We describe $Γ$ via a weighted quadratic transport problem involving Dirichlet distributions and show that optimal couplings preserve directions within the eigenspaces of $K$. When $K$ has a single eigenvalue, we obtain an explicit cost formula and an optimal Monge map. For general spectra, we derive remarkably tight lower and upper bounds for $Γ$ using nested spectral projections and Knothe-Rosenblatt couplings. The lower bound is based on one-dimensional integrals and can be computed fast. For Gaussian, Student-$t$, uniform ball, and uniform sphere distributions, the upper bound also admits computationally efficient representations via dynamic programming. Numerical experiments demonstrate that we reduce the gap between the previously known bounds by more than 80% in many settings, and by over 99.9% in certain scenarios, even in dimension $10^6$. These improvements are particularly valuable in high-dimensional or heavy-tailed settings, where accurate numerical computation of quadratic Wasserstein distances is challenging.

papers.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
papers.abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

papers.title: A $2$-adic Kida-type formula for chromatic Selmer groups of elliptic curves and applications to quadratic twists
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ with good supersingular reduction at $2$. We study the chromatic ($\sharp/\flat$) Selmer groups of $E$ over the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of $\mathbb{Q}$, defined using Sprung's chromatic Coleman maps. We show that at least one of these Selmer groups is $Λ$-cotorsion and, assuming the vanishing of the corresponding $μ$-invariant, establish a $2$-adic Kida-type formula describing the change in the Iwasawa $λ$-invariants under base change from $\mathbb{Q}$ to a real quadratic field $F$ in which $2$ is unramified. When $E$ has square-free conductor, applying this formula to $E$ and its quadratic twist $E^D$ yields an explicit formula describing the variation of the chromatic $λ$-invariants under twists by positive square-free integers $D\equiv1\pmod4$. As an application, under suitable hypotheses on the root number and chromatic Iwasawa invariants of $E$, we construct explicit sets of primes $\ell$ such that the $2^{\infty}$-Selmer group of $E^{\ell}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ has $\mathbb{Z}_2$-corank one, and determine their positive natural densities.

papers.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
papers.abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of Kähler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

papers.title: Ordering Information in Multispecies Long-Range Swap Processes
papers.abstract: We measure how much the left-to-right species order $W_t$ of interacting particles on the integer lattice reveals about their initial configuration. For distinct species under long-range swaps, deleting stronger particles gives coordinates with independent Poisson increments. For a finitely supported initial law, the mutual information between any function $U$ of the initial configuration and $W_t$ is $C_U/t+O(t^{-3/2})$ as $t\to\infty$, where $C_U$, which may vanish, is determined by the means of Gaussian order statistics and the conditional means of the initial compressed coordinates given $U$. On consecutive sites with a uniform initial order, we compute the coefficient of the $t\log(1/t)$ term in the short-time information loss for arbitrary species counts. For three particles in this setting, repeating the weaker rather than the stronger species triples the long-time $t^{-1}$ coefficient, although both compositions have the same composition entropy and initial-order entropy. These long-time coefficients are the same whether equal particles block or push each other, but the nonuniform limiting output law is reversed. In the ordinary multispecies totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), two distinct particles at fixed sites with a uniform initial order instead give $t^{-1/2}$ decay.

papers.title: Large deviation principle of error of Euler--Maruyama method for stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: We study large deviations for the error of the Euler--Maruyama method applied to a one-dimensional stochastic differential equation with $C_b^3$ coefficients and a uniformly elliptic diffusion coefficient. We prove that the error at the terminal time, without rescaling, satisfies a large deviation principle (LDP) at speed $n$, where $n$ is the number of steps, with a good rate function that vanishes only at the origin. In particular, the probability that the error exceeds a fixed level decays exponentially in $n$. Two effects determine the rate function. A single Brownian increment of fixed nonzero size has finite cost at speed $n$, and the cumulative effect of smaller Brownian increments depends on the states at which their squares accumulate. To capture both effects, we introduce, for a cutoff $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, an empirical enhanced control that records the state-dependent quadratic variation of the small increments together with the time, state and size of each increment exceeding $\varepsilon$. We prove an LDP for the empirical enhanced control for every fixed $\varepsilon$, and deduce the LDP for the error by the contraction principle and an exponentially good approximation as $\varepsilon\to0$.

papers.title: An Asymptotically Sharp Form of the Overfull Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with maximum degree $Δ$. A subgraph $H$ of $G$ is \emph{$Δ$-overfull} if $|E(H)|>Δ\lfloor |V(H)|/2\rfloor$. The Overfull Conjecture, proposed by Chetwynd and Hilton in 1986, states that a graph $G$ with $Δ>|V(G)|/3$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. This conjecture would give a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index in this degree range and would imply several longstanding conjectures on critical graphs. In this paper, we prove that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, a sufficiently large graph $G$ with $Δ\ge(1/4+\varepsilon)|V(G)|$ is of class~2 if and only if it contains a $Δ$-overfull subgraph. Consequently, the chromatic index can be determined in polynomial time in this range. We also obtain the Just-overfull and Vertex-splitting Conjectures for large graphs, and Vizing's Independence Number, Average Degree, and $2$-Factor Conjectures in the same degree range. The coefficient $1/4$ is asymptotically best possible: for every odd integer $Δ\ge3$, we construct a connected class~2 graph on $4Δ+5$ vertices with maximum degree $Δ$ and no $Δ$-overfull subgraph.

papers.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
papers.abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

papers.title: Risk-Informed Path Planning: Collision and Grounding Avoidance Application for Autonomous Surface Vessels
papers.abstract: Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS) must demonstrate safety before and during operations, necessitating online risk assessment to guide decision-making at sea. This paper presents a risk-informed Rapidly Exploring Random Tree Star (RRT*) path planner that integrates a Bayesian Belief Network (BBN) as an online risk model. The BBN evaluates the probability and severity distribution of hazardous events, which are aggregated into a bounded scalar risk index. During the search, this risk index is evaluated at sample points along candidate edges. The planner optimizes a composite cost function comprising path distance, heading change penalties, and accumulated risk, subject to a hard constraint enforcing a risk acceptance limit. Each search tree vertex stores the BBN posterior at its state, enabling the tree to function as an explainable risk map for individual hazards. We define design requirements for the BBN to serve as the risk model in this context and introduce a runtime model that translates replanning deadlines into strict limits on single risk calculation times. The planner is demonstrated in a simulated harbor entry scenario involving collision and grounding hazards. Measured run times validate that the planner operates within the computational bounds predicted by the runtime model for a single replanning cycle.

papers.title: Elliptic Monotonicity Formulas for $p$-Green Functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we derive $p$-Laplace analogues of Colding's three monotonicity formulas in the original metric on complete noncompact $n$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature, for $n\geq3$ and $1<p<n$. We assume a normalized positive minimal $p$-Green function vanishing at infinity with Euclidean pole asymptotics. Two complementary linearizations and the $p$-Bochner formula yield exact derivative identities with a common nonnegative defect involving an anisotropic trace-free Hessian and Ricci curvature. These identities give exterior cone rigidity and integral defect estimates, and recover the sharp gradient estimate and Euclidean rigidity of Mari--Rigoli--Setti. A one-parameter extension of Colding--Minicozzi type connects the formulas with known monotonicity and convexity identities for $p$-capacitary potentials.

papers.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.

papers.title: Variance Reduction Note 5: The Convergence of Loopless SVRG
papers.abstract: A snapshot in loopless SVRG has no prescribed lifetime. At each step the algorithm may keep using an old full gradient or compute a new one. How does this choice enter the convergence proof, and how often is a new full gradient worth its cost? For a strongly convex finite sum we follow the age and objective gap of the snapshot. Its expected gap is a geometrically weighted average of earlier iterate gaps. This identity determines a weight for the snapshot in a one-step contraction argument and gives an objective bound for the last iterate. A two-component quadratic makes the estimator variance explicit, including on the step immediately after a refresh. We also evaluate the work bound as a function of the refresh probability and compare its minimizer with the condition-number-independent choice $p=1/n$.

papers.title: An elliptic Lehmer bound of exponent one at a supersingular prime
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with good supersingular reduction at a prime $\p$. We prove that the Néron--Tate height of every non-torsion $P\in E(\Kbar)$ satisfies $\hh_E(P)\ge c\,D^{-1}(\log3D)^{-1}\exp(-c'\sqrt{\log3D})$, where $D=[K(x(P)):K]$ and $c,c'>0$ depend only on $E$, $K$ and $\p$; so $\hh_E(P)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$. By a result of Elkies this applies to every elliptic curve over $\QQ$, and it improves the exponents of Masser and of Hindry and Silverman.

papers.title: Convex computation of cost bounds for data-driven nonlinear optimal control
papers.abstract: The paper addresses the optimal control problem of an input-affine polynomial system with an unknown (state-dependent) input matrix affecting the control effectiveness. Under assumptions on the existence of a data set and the Lipschitz continuity of the unknown part {of the dynamics}, an uncertainty set is constructed and used to adapt the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation towards a data-driven formulation. We solve it for the best-case scenario, thus giving a lower bound on the best cost achievable by means of a feedback control policy. After relaxing it into a moment-SoS hierarchy of semidefinite programs, a control law is extracted from the primal on moments and compared with other benchmark methods in a numerical application.

papers.title: The majority game chromatic number for dense random graphs
papers.abstract: We show that for every fixed $2/3<p<1$ the majority game chromatic number of the Erdős--Rényi random graph $G_{n,p}$ is $3$ with high probability.

papers.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
papers.abstract: The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.

papers.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
papers.abstract: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.

papers.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
papers.abstract: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

papers.title: A degree-sum condition for paths through prescribed vertices
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Denote by $κ(S)$ the minimum size of a vertex set separating two vertices of $S$, and by $σ_p(S)$ the minimum degree sum over all independent sets of $p$ vertices in $S$. We prove that if $κ(S)\ge k\ge2$ and $σ_p(S)\ge n+(p-1)^2$ for every integer $p\ge k$, then any two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by a path containing all vertices of $S$. This gives a path version of Ota's theorem on cycles containing a prescribed set of vertices. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Faudree, Faudree, Gould, Jacobson and Magnant: for $k\ge3$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $δ(G)>(n+k^2-2k)/k$ and $δ(G)\geα(G)+k-2$ is hamiltonian-connected.

papers.title: A sufficient criterion for ballistic behavior of forced geometric motions in random environment
papers.abstract: We introduce a sufficient criterion for ballistic motion of interface evolutions in random environments. More precisely, we consider interfaces moving by forced mean curvature flow in dimension $d=2$ with a spatially fluctuating (possibly negative) driving force. Such models arise e.g. from the motions of dislocation lines or magnetic domain walls in a material with impurities. We show that the evolution admits an `effective minimum speed on large scales' if for a sample of the random environment in some long and thin box there is a sufficiently large probability that an interface initialized in the bottom of the box evolves to reach its top. The concept of an `effective minimum speed on large scales' was introduced and is required for the quantitative stochastic homogenization result in the companion paper ``Quantitative homogenization of forced geometric motions through random fields of obstacles''. We show that our criterion and hence the requirements for the homogenization result in the companion paper are satisfied for compactly supported obstacle shapes distributed according to a Poisson point process with sufficiently low intensity.

papers.title: Quasifibrations in étale homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We study quasifibrations in étale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$Σ$ completed profinite étale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of étale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $Σ$-completed exact sequence of étale homotopy groups in low degree terms in general.

papers.title: Spectral and arithmetic classifications of mixed-power difference factor absorbing ideals
papers.abstract: For integers $n\ge2$ and $k\ge1$, a proper ideal $I$ is $(kn,n)$-mixed-power difference factor absorbing if $a^{kn}-b^n\in I$ implies that $a^k-b$ or the complementary geometric-sum factor lies in $I$. Extending the cubic spectral criterion, we classify radical ideals for all exponents via roots of unity in the fraction fields of their minimal-prime quotients, with no finiteness or comaximality assumptions; for radical ideals the condition is independent of $k$. We extend the finite comaximal-prime criterion for quartic pair absorption to all radical ideals and identify its three-component obstruction. Requiring one factor to lie in the radical is equivalent to the radical satisfying the condition for every multiplier, yielding radical descent and extending cubic primary descent. For radical ideals, the condition is equivalent under polynomial and power series extension. Applications include pullbacks of domains and, when the characteristic does not divide $n$, a characterization of geometric integrality of geometrically reduced algebras by stability under field extension; for $n\ge3$, a square-zero extension of such an algebra is stable precisely when the quotient is geometrically integral and the kernel is torsion-free. If the characteristic $p$ divides $n$, the condition depends only on the $p$-part of $n$ and is equivalent to a power-closure condition. We classify square-zero extensions of domains, including nonsplit extensions and idealization ideals with prime projection. For homogeneous idealizations over $P$-primary bases with $2\notin P$, a related quartic criterion

papers.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing). We establish tight first-order asymptotics for the size of the reachable set from a fixed vertex, and also determine the first-order asymptotics of the lengths of the longest and shortest increasing paths with one or two fixed endpoints.

papers.title: Dobrowolski-type lower bounds for canonical heights of polynomials of Frobenius type
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a number field and let $f\in\OK[x]$ be a monic polynomial of degree $d=p^r$ with $f\equiv x^d+c\pmod p$, such as $x^2+c$. We prove that every $α\in\Kbar$ of degree $D$ over $K$ with infinite orbit under $f$ satisfies $$\hh_f(α)\ \ge\ \frac{c_1}{D\log3D}\exp\bigl(-c_2\sqrt{\log3D}\bigr),$$ where $c_1,c_2>0$ depend only on $f$ and $K$. This implies $\hh_f(α)\ge D^{-1-o(1)}$, making progress towards the dynamical Lehmer conjecture. The polynomial $f$ need not be postcritically finite. For such polynomials, for instance $x^2+1$, no lower bound of polynomial decay in $D$ was previously known. For postcritically finite polynomials such as $x^2-1$, it improves the recent quadratic bound of Habegger and Schmidt. The method is motivated by Dobrowolski's proof on Lehmer's problem.

papers.title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
papers.abstract: We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices. Using this framework, we prove that a tree is anchor-free if and only if it is a path with one less vertex than a prime. We also introduce the related notion of unique-subgraph-freeness, which acts as an edge-based analogue of anchor-freeness. We show that the line graph of every unique-subgraph-free graph is anchor-free and obtain a complete classification of unique-subgraph-free trees as either prime paths, stars, or extended stars. Together, these results provide a classification of trees without unique subgraphs and suggest a general approach for extending the theory beyond trees.

papers.title: Pyoframe: A Python Library to Easily and Efficiently Construct Large Optimization Models
papers.abstract: Researchers and industry practitioners are constructing increasingly large optimization models to tackle problems in fields such as manufacturing, logistics, and energy systems planning. As the performance of solvers like Gurobi keeps improving, the performance of modeling frameworks like gurobipy which let users interact with solvers is increasingly becoming a bottleneck. We present Pyoframe, an open-source Python modeling framework to construct optimization models of various types (LPs, MIPs, QPs, and QCQPs). Pyoframe adopts a novel DataFrame-based software architecture that enables parallelized computations while also offering a legible syntax and a friendly user experience. We benchmark Pyoframe against other modeling frameworks (AMPL, CVXPY, Gurobipy, JuMP, Linopy, PuLP, Pyomo, and PyOptInterface) and find that Pyoframe is faster on every large or complex benchmark, while almost always using less memory and fewer lines of code. Switching to Pyoframe reduces the total time, memory, and code needed to solve these benchmark problems by up to 83%, 68%, and 64%, respectively, demonstrating the significant impact that modeling frameworks, not only solvers, can have in applied optimization. Overall, Pyoframe makes it easier and faster to develop and run large linear or quadratic optimization models.

papers.title: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals
papers.abstract: We study steady-state diffusion approximations for a many-server queue driven by overdispersed arrivals from a doubly stochastic Poisson process. Its arrival intensity follows a generalized Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) process, where $α\in [0, 1)$ governs how the arrival-count variance scales as $λ^{1+α}$ with the baseline arrival rate $λ$ under Taylor's law. For $α> 0$, arrival-intensity fluctuations grow faster with $λ$ than counting fluctuations from arrivals and departures, so normalizing by $λ^{(1+α)/2}$ pairs a nonvanishing intensity volatility with a vanishing queue-length volatility. This two-scale formulation differs critically from conventional diffusion approximations, which either apply a single $λ^{1/2}$ scaling with nonvanishing volatilities or drop the vanishing queue-length noise in the heavy-traffic limit. Retaining both scales, we compare two diffusions: one replaces the scaled intensity with its limiting Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process, and the other preserves the exact CIR intensity. Using Stein's method, we establish steady-state error bounds for smooth test functions of arbitrary polynomial growth that depend on $α$ in opposite directions. Both diffusions achieve the classical $O(λ^{-1/2})$ rate at $α= 0$. For $α\in (0, 1)$, however, the OU rate degrades to the sharp order $O(λ^{-(1-α)/2})$, whereas preserving the CIR intensity improves the rate to $O(λ^{-(2+α)/4})$. Our proofs establish new derivative bounds for the associated Poisson equations that remain valid when the diffusion has vanishing volatility and nonsmooth drift.

papers.title: Schnyder Woods and the Chromatic Polynomial
papers.abstract: Let $χ_G(q)$ be the chromatic polynomial of a graph $G$. Analogous to the classical results of Greene and Zaslavsky interpreting $(-1)^{n-1}χ_G'(0)$ and $(-1)^nχ_G'(1)$ as counting certain orientations of $G$, we show that if $G$ is a triangulation, $\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{n-1}χ_G'(2)$ counts the number of Schnyder woods on a plane embedding of $G$. We also generalise this result to graphs obtained by removing certain edges of $G$.

papers.title: Bicriteria Traffic Assignment
papers.abstract: The classical traffic assignment problem determines the equilibrium flows on a congested network with many infinitesimal users who choose paths to minimize their own travel times. Travelers care about cost (including tolls) as well as time, and different travelers put different weights on these two criteria. We study a bicriteria traffic assignment problem in which travelers differ in their tradeoff between a flow-independent cost, such as tolls, and a flow-dependent cost, such as travel time. Existing formulations require either finitely many user classes or positive preference densities, including formulations for positive preference densities that are either infinite-dimensional or nonconvex. We formulate a finite-dimensional convex optimization problem for arbitrary preference distributions with bounded support, including distributions with a mixture of atoms, densities, and gaps in their support, and we show how to convert an optimal solution to an equilibrium of the bicriteria traffic assignment problem. We propose an algorithm that alternates between solving a convex problem for a (typically small) number of paths, and solving a parametric shortest-path problem. Computational experiments on benchmark networks illustrate the performance of the algorithm relative to existing methods.

papers.title: A Learning-Based Numerical Method for Biharmonic boundary value problems via the Almansi Decomposition
papers.abstract: We extend the learning-based numerical method (LbNM) to two-dimensional biharmonic boundary value problems, combining high accuracy with efficient repeated solves for different boundary data on a fixed domain. The method reconstructs a discrete boundary-to-solution operator from explicit biharmonic samples generated by the Almansi decomposition, using their boundary values and normal derivatives through Tikhonov regularization. Once constructed at prescribed evaluation points, the operator provides solutions for new boundary inputs by a single matrix-vector multiplication. Moreover, additional sample solutions can be incorporated through rank-one updates without rebuilding the operator. We establish a quantitative convergence estimate under a biharmonic continuation assumption. Numerical experiments on nonconvex domains demonstrate accuracy close to the double-precision limit for a smooth benchmark and high accuracy for solutions induced by nearby exterior singularities.

papers.title: Unbounded GHZ dimension from fixed-order multiphoton sources
papers.abstract: We study the local dimension of Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) states obtained by selecting events with one photon per output path. Each coherent source emits photons with a fixed internal label into a distinct set of paths, and the sets for each label partition the outputs. For two-photon sources, the maximum local dimension is 2 for every even number of paths greater than 4. However, we show that three-photon sources can produce GHZ states of arbitrarily large local dimension. To prove this, we view the three paths fed by each source as an edge of a $3$-uniform hypergraph, so that accepted emission patterns correspond exactly to perfect matchings. We construct such hypergraphs with arbitrarily many edge-disjoint perfect matchings, one per label, and no others. The construction extends to $r$-uniform hypergraphs for every fixed $r\ge3$, yielding a GHZ dimension that grows at least polynomially as the number of paths ranges over the positive multiples of $r$.

papers.title: Erdős Distance Results for $k$-Degenerate Graphs with $m$ Edges
papers.abstract: The Erdős distinct distances problem asks how many distinct distances $N$ points must determine. In the plane, Guth and Katz determined the optimal power of $N$. A natural generalization fixes a finite graph $G$ with $m$ edges and records, over all injective embeddings of $G$ into a finite point set $P \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, the vectors of edge-lengths realized; we write $Δ_G^\circ(P)$ for this set of edge-distance vectors. Taking $G$ to be a single edge recovers the classical problem. In the plane, the exponent $|V(G)|-1$ is known up to an arbitrarily small loss for every connected graph. A graph is $k$-degenerate if its vertices can be ordered so that each has at most $k$ neighbors among those preceding it. We show that if $G$ is $k$-degenerate, then for every $d \ge \max(2k,3)$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, $|Δ_G^\circ(P)| \gtrsim_{G,d,\varepsilon} N^{m/(d-1)-\varepsilon}$ for $|P|=N\ge |V(G)|$. For a connected graph with $m/(|V(G)|-1)>2(d-1)/d$, the exponent $m/(d-1)$ exceeds the spanning-tree exponent predicted by the pinned-distance conjecture. Our result is motivated by the threshold $\frac{d+k}{2}$ obtained by Borges, Foster, Ou, Palsson, and Romero Acosta for edge lengths of $k$-degenerate graphs in fractal sets. The proof combines a bisector-energy estimate for pinned $k$-stars with an entropy argument of Katz--Tardos type, applied along a construction order of $G$ and combined with an induction on the dimension.

papers.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras
papers.abstract: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.

papers.title: One monoid to realize them all: a master monoid for homotopy types
papers.abstract: Homotopy theory has traditionally been approached either through topological spaces or through categories of presheaves on suitable combinatorial categories, a perspective subsumed by Grothendieck's theory of test categories. In this paper, we develop a more algebraic viewpoint: homotopy types can be represented by actions of a single monoid on sets. This monoid is obtained by identifying all the objects of the semisimplicial category while retaining its face operators. Every CW homotopy type is the classifying space of the translation category of one of its actions, and its truncation at dimension n is finitely presented and realizes exactly the homotopy types of dimension at most n. The construction rests on a general result: every set-valued functor on a small category freely generates an action of its universal monoid, and its category of elements is a full coreflective subcategory of the resulting translation category. Hence every weak test category gives rise to a monoid whose actions realize all homotopy types; when the category has more than one object, however, this monoid is not itself a weak test category, so that a single monoid may realize all homotopy types without modelling homotopy theory as a localization. The obstruction lies in identifying objects, not in having a single one: there are strict test categories with a single object, such as the monoid of all self-maps of an infinite set and a countable monoid of primitive recursive functions.

papers.title: Twisted Poincaré series at zero on surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $(Σ,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $Σ$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in Σ$, $ρ\in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincaré series $s \mapsto η_{g,ρ,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincaré series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.

papers.title: Burn and density control in uncertain tokamak models with prescribed error bounds
papers.abstract: The stored energy and the electron density of a burning tokamak plasma must be kept inside prescribed bands, with the auxiliary heating power and the fuelling rate as actuators. For the standard zero-dimensional burn model with a dynamic confinement closure we show that this two-actuator configuration has vector relative degree $(2,1)$, independently of the confinement parameters. We design a model-free funnel controller which uses an input filter instead of output derivatives and meets all actuator constraints - sign, amplitude and rate - by construction, the input deficit being returned to the loop as a correction of the reference. For a system class containing the model we prove, under the compatibility assumption that the corrections stay bounded by constants fixed in advance, that the tracking errors evolve in prescribed funnels about the corrected references. Sufficient conditions for the assumption are given, and the design is illustrated on an ITER benchmark.

papers.title: Teichmüller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
papers.abstract: We study Teichmüller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $θ= 2πβ$. For all $β>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $ω_β$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $β$, the form $ω_β$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit. For positive integers $β=n$, $ω_β$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $θ=2πn$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichmüller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

papers.title: Average density of rational points on quartic surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish an average asymptotic for the number of rational points of bounded height $B$ on quartic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ of height bounded by $A$, refining an argument of Le Boudec and using techniques of Browning-Le Boudec-Sawin. We extend the range of the asymptotic from $B=o(A)$ to $B=O(A^2)$. As an application, we show that almost all quartic surfaces of height $H$ have no rational point of height $o(H^{5/2})$.

papers.title: The sharp uniqueness threshold for the antiferromagnetic Potts model on regular trees
papers.abstract: We study Gibbs uniqueness for the $q$-state antiferromagnetic Potts model on the infinite rooted $d$-ary tree and the infinite $(d+1)$-regular tree, where $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. An edge has weight $p\in[0,1]$ if its endpoints have the same color and weight $1$ otherwise. We prove that there is a unique Gibbs state if and only if $p\geqslant p_c:=\max\{0,1-q/(d+1)\}$, except when $(q,p)=(d+1,0)$, thus completes the uniqueness thresholds for all $d\geqslant1$ and $q\geqslant2$. Our proof use a convex potential for the tree recursion and show that it strictly decreases away from the uniform distribution. Together with the result of Gu, Wu and Yang, our theorem gives the exact critical power law whenever $p_c>0$.

papers.title: The Lafforgue Transform
papers.abstract: In this report, we survey the \emph{Lafforgue transform}, a natural representation-theoretic map from the Kazhdan cocenter to the Bernstein center of a reductive group over a local field. Its motivation comes from our study of the Braverman-Kazhdan proposal, a conjectural framework for establishing the meromorphic continuation and functional equations of general automorphic $L$-functions through harmonic analysis on possibly singular varieties. For $G=\SL_2$ and $\GL_2$, we explain how the stable part of the Lafforgue transform and its distinguished section are realized as integral transforms on the Steinberg-Hitchin base, with formulas of motivic nature that are valid over every local field.

papers.title: On optimal packing of Minkowski spheres
papers.abstract: A method has been developed for the optimal packing of a continuum family of one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the real plane. By applying this method to the problem of packing one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the plane, an optimal lattice packing for a continuum family of such spheres has been obtained for the first time. Expressions for these optimal packing lattices have been derived, and their validity has been proven. Formulas for the packing density corresponding to these lattices have also been obtained.

papers.title: Accuracy and Efficiency of Lowest-order and Higher-Order Single-Source Integral Equations
papers.abstract: The single-source integral equation allows the modeling of the electromagnetic field by only tracking a single surface-supported current density. It features products of integral operators, which pose unique challenges for the modeler in both the discretization and solution of the equation. Due to the unique structure of the single-source equation, its conforming and stable discretization requires expanding one of the two physical traces in primal basis functions and the other in dual basis functions. Primal functions are expected to have better approximation properties than dual ones. In this work, we study the impact of this asymmetric representation on the accuracy of the solution and propose an approach from which both traces can be recovered using only primal functions with modest additional computational cost. Moreover, we propose an alternative discretization scheme based on approximating the inverse of the duality mapping induced by the surface normal cross-product operator through the quasi-Helmholtz decomposition. This discretization provides greater flexibility in the choice of function spaces, enabling both a higher-order extension of the single-source equation and a more efficient lowest-order discretization using only Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results show the impact of the representation in terms of primal and dual functions in both lowest- and higher-order discretization.

papers.title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
papers.abstract: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two. If the choice must be made equivariantly from independent vertex labels, every edge is forced. In this expository note we follow these two answers through other groups. Geometry alone forces a positive gap on each non-elementary hyperbolic Cayley graph, while on one four-regular nilpotent Cayley graph the choice of action realizes every additive cost in $[1,2]$. The minimum of the action spectrum recovers the geometric cost. Open problems are presented in the end.

papers.title: Recursive estimation of the Oja median and related simplex medians
papers.abstract: We study the recursive estimation of multivariate location functionals defined by minimizing the expected volume of a random simplex. This framework encompasses both the spatial median and the affine-equivariant Oja median. We introduce a sliding-window stochastic gradient algorithm and its averaged version, and establish their strong consistency and asymptotic normality. We further show that the sliding-window approach offers a favorable trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost compared with a naive disjoint-block stochastic gradient algorithm and offline methods, with the statistical comparison based on asymptotic covariances. Numerical experiments illustrate the computational advantages of the proposed procedures and their finite-sample accuracy.

papers.title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
papers.abstract: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.

papers.title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
papers.abstract: We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $γ^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.

papers.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

papers.title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
papers.abstract: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{Ω(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Bradač in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.

papers.title: New families of vertex-transitive quaternionic lattices in products of trees
papers.abstract: We describe infinite families of quaternionic arithmetic lattices in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_1)\times \cdots \times \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ acting transitively on the vertices of the Cartesian product $\mathcal{T}_1\times \cdots \times \mathcal{T}_n$, where $\mathcal{T}_1,\dots, \mathcal{T}_n$ are regular trees. We present an algorithm to determine a presentation for each of these lattices. We also introduce a method for constructing such lattices that act regularly on the set of vertices. We illustrate our results with numerous explicit examples, including several families of known cases, as well as many new instances in arbitrary characteristic.

papers.title: Identifying the critical mass in a quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production
papers.abstract: The mass threshold separating boundedness and unboundedness of global solutions to a critical quasilinear parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model with indirect signal production is identified in the radially symmetric setting in a ball. Specifically, solutions emanating from initial values with mass below a critical mass M\textsubscr{c} > 0, which is characterized in terms of a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality, are global and bounded. In contrast, for any M > M\textsubscr{c}, there are initial values with mass M such that the corresponding global solutions are unbounded. The proof relies on the variational structure of the system and a detailed study of the stationary states.

papers.title: Optimal polynomial meshes on quasicircles via conformal scale comparison
papers.abstract: We prove that every quasicircle $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}$ admits an optimal admissible polynomial mesh for univariate complex polynomials. More precisely, if $E$ denotes the closed Jordan domain bounded by $Γ$, then for every $Λ>1$ there are finite sets $A_n\subsetΓ$ with $\mathrm{card}(A_n)=O(n)$ and $\|p\|_E=\|p\|_Γ\leqΛ\|p\|_{A_n}$ for every $p\in\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The nodes may be chosen as images of equally spaced points of the unit circle under the inverse exterior conformal map, equivalently as equal-mass points for harmonic measure at infinity. The proof combines the classical conformal level-curve scale with a discrete norming principle. If $ρ_n(z)$ denotes the distance from a boundary point to the exterior level curve $|Φ|=1+1/n$, Bernstein--Walsh and Cauchy's formula show that any sufficiently fine $ρ_n$-net is norming. A scale-comparison property then turns $O(n)$ equally spaced angular samples into such a net. Quasicircles satisfy this property by quasisymmetry. The argument requires no smoothness or rectifiability and applies in particular to the classical von Koch snowflake.

papers.title: Convolution Algebras of Generalized Preprojective Algebras and Kac-Moody Positive Parts
papers.abstract: We realize the enveloping algebras of positive parts of symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras as convolution algebras of constructible functions on module varieties of Geiss-Leclerc-Schröer generalized preprojective algebras $Π(C,D)$. We characterize all pairs $(C,D)$ for which such a realization exists. These realizations generalize Lusztig's classical preprojective construction. The construction uses a folding embedding and torus actions on flag varieties.

papers.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, defines the sampling subspace of a guided evolution strategy rather than being used as a direct update. For any guiding subspace, the expected update is a descent direction of the smoothed objective, so an inaccurate guide adds variance while the expected step still descends. For six problem families, both guided estimators outperform the baseline. The decision-focused version reduces the mean gap by three-quarters, and on the two families with the most integer variables the reduced sets beat the exact solver's two-hour incumbent in most runs, using a fifth of the time.

papers.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

papers.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.

papers.title: How to facet a gemstone: from potential modularity to modularity lifting
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a totally real field and $p\ge7$ a prime unramified in $F$. We prove that a potentially modular $p$-adic representation of $G_F$ which is potentially crystalline with distinct Hodge--Tate weights above $p$, and whose reduction is modular, non-dihedral and satisfies the usual Taylor--Wiles hypothesis, is modular. This removes the hypotheses of [MF] on the Serre weights: the multiplicity-free hypothesis, and the exclusion of Steinberg weights. The same method applies to potentially semistable representations. The proof combines the identity of cycles of [MF] with the modularity of lifts whose local components are mixed along an extension in which $p$ splits. These lifts exist by a theorem of Emerton, Gee, Pan and Zhu, they are potentially automorphic by a theorem of Calegari, Emerton and Gee, and their modularity is proved by tensoring with lifts of an auxiliary residual representation of a different weight: the tensor products lie on a common component of a local deformation ring for $\GL_4$, a lifting theorem of Thorne applies, and the factors of an automorphic tensor product are modular by [Die26].

papers.title: Irreducibility, inertia and invertibility of the eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs
papers.abstract: The eccentricity matrix of a connected graph $G$, denoted by $\mathcal{E}(G)$, is obtained from the distance matrix of $G$ by keeping each entry that is the largest in its row or the largest in its column, and replacing all other entries by $0$. The eigenvalues of $\mathcal{E}(G)$ are called the $\mathcal{E}$-eigenvalues of $G$. In this article, we consider the eccentricity matrix of unicyclic graphs and study its various spectral properties. First, we give two sufficient conditions for the irreducibility of the eccentricity matrix of a connected graph, which generalize some previously known results. Then, we show that the eccentricity matrix of every unicyclic graph of girth $3$, $5$ or $7$ is irreducible and provide a unicyclic graph whose eccentricity matrix is reducible for every odd girth $g\ge 9$. On the other hand, we also provide a class of unicyclic graphs of odd girth, whose eccentricity matrices are always irreducible. Additionally, we find the inertia of eccentricity matrices of unicyclic graphs in which the trees attached to the cycle are nontrivial and have equal heights. Moreover, we characterize the graphs in this class whose E-eigenvalues are symmetric about the origin. Finally, we obtain necessary conditions for the invertibility of the eccentricity matrix of a unicyclic graph.

papers.title: Low-Frequency Stable Single-Source Integral Equation
papers.abstract: Among the integral equations for scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects, single-source integral equations (SSIEs) provide the advantage of having only a single electric or magnetic current unknown. A well-conditioned SSIE can be obtained by appropriately combining the interior and exterior Calderón formulas. The condition number of the resulting operator appearing in the well-conditioned SSIE remains bounded at low frequencies. However, SSIEs still suffer from low-frequency cancellation, causing loss of significant digits in the solution, the right-hand side, and the system matrix. In this work, we apply a rescaling strategy based on quasi-Helmholtz projectors to the well-conditioned SSIE. Primal and dual space projectors are required since both primal and dual spaces are used to discretize the SSIE operators. We show that the solution of the rescaled SSIE is immune to catastrophic cancellations at low frequencies. Numerical experiments corroborate the method by testing the accuracy of the radiated field for extremely low frequencies.

papers.title: On unique realisations of graphs under symmetry constraints
papers.abstract: Global rigidity asks whether a realisation of a graph is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean congruence, by its edge lengths. In this paper, we study global rigidity of bar-joint frameworks under finite point-group symmetry constraints. A framework is called forced-symmetric globally rigid in $d$-space if every realisation of the graph in $\mathbb R^d$ with the same edge lengths and the same prescribed symmetry is congruent to it. We establish symmetric extensions of two fundamental results on global rigidity. Our first result extends Hendrickson's necessary condition to the forced-symmetric setting. For symmetry-generic frameworks with an arbitrary finite point group acting freely on the vertices and with at least $d+2$ vertex orbits, we prove that forced-symmetric global rigidity implies forced-symmetric redundant rigidity. Our second result extends the classical characterisation of generic global rigidity for body-bar frameworks due to Connelly, Jordán and Whiteley. For the symmetric body-bar model considered here, we show that forced-symmetric global rigidity is a generic property and obtain a combinatorial characterisation in every dimension.

papers.title: A Proof of the Balister-Győri-Schelp Conjecture on Perfect Matchings with Prescribed Differences
papers.abstract: We prove the conjecture of Balister, Győri and Schelp on perfect matchings with prescribed differences. Let $n\ge 2$ and let $d_1,\dots,d_{2^{n-1}}$ be nonzero vectors in $\mathbb{F}_2^n$, with repetitions allowed. The space $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ can be partitioned into pairs $\{x_i,y_i\}$ with $x_i+y_i=d_i$ for every $i$ if and only if $\sum_i d_i=0$.

papers.title: Aerodynamic Collision Avoidance Manoeuvres in Very Low Earth Orbit: Exploiting Lift for Short Warning Times and Reduced Orbital Decay
papers.abstract: Very Low Earth Orbits (VLEO, below $450\,\mathrm{km}$ altitude) offer promising mission capabilities for future spacecraft, but increasing traffic and the presence of orbital debris create collision risks that pose a particular challenge for satellites without conventional propulsion. Aerodynamic drag, resulting from interaction with the residual atmosphere, has been shown effective for performing collision avoidance manoeuvres (CAMs). However, short warning times remain challenging, and current methods do not exploit aerodynamic lift forces that enable out-of-track manoeuvres, which could help enhance control authority and mitigate drag-induced orbital decay. This work addresses both gaps by developing and evaluating two complementary optimisation methods: a heuristic approach using reachable set analysis to determine minimum lead times, and a direct shooting method to limit the increase in orbital decay due to the manoeuvre. Analyses using data derived from real conjunctions show that achieving a sufficient reduction in collision risk in the considered scenarios is feasible with lead times lower than one orbital period. Results also show that lift-based manoeuvres outperform drag-only approaches, with modest lead time reductions and more pronounced benefits in limiting orbital decay. Performance sensitivity to variations in control authority due to the type of gas-surface-interaction, altitude, and the encounter geometry is characterised. The methods and results presented highlight the potential of aerodynamic CAM for short warning time scenarios, contributing to sustainable operations in the increasingly congested VLEO environment.

papers.title: Cup products with volume classes in bounded cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 2$, and suppose that either $M$ is negatively curved, or that it is a locally symmetric space of non-compact type. Via integration over straight simplices, every top-degree bounded differential form $ω\in Ω_b^n(M)$ defines a bounded cohomology class in $H^n_b(M)$. We prove that every such class belongs to the annihilator of the cup product in the whole graded algebra $H^{\geq 1}_b(M)$. In the case of closed orientable surfaces, this generalizes a result of Marasco, and, via transfer, provides a new proof of the fact that the cup product of the bounded Euler class of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ with itself vanishes. Our result also applies to degree-3 bounded classes constructed by Soma and Farre, thus showing that, for surface groups and for free groups, the annihilator of the cup product is infinite dimensional also in degree 3.

papers.title: The centre of mass of the primes and a reflection of Chebyshev's bias
papers.abstract: For $x\ge2$ we place a unit mass at $\log p$ for each prime $p\le x$, and let $D(x)$ be the distance from the centre of mass of this system to $\log x$; thus $D(p_n)=\log(p_n/G_n)$, where $G_n$ is the geometric mean of the first $n$ primes. Let $D_0(x)$ be the distance obtained when $π$ is replaced by $\mathrm{Li}(x)=\int_2^x dt/\log t$. We prove that $D(x)-D_0(x)\ll x^{Θ-1+\varepsilon}$, where $Θ$ is the supremum of the real parts of the zeros of $ζ(s)$, and that the exponent cannot be lowered; in particular, the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to $\log(p_n/G_n)=D_0(p_n)+O_\varepsilon(p_n^{-1/2+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. Under the Riemann hypothesis we prove a pointwise mirror theorem: for large $x$ the centre of mass lies to the left of its predicted position only when $π(x)<\mathrm{li}(x)-1.95\sqrt{x}/\log x$. Under the Riemann hypothesis and the linear independence hypothesis, the set of such $x$ has the same logarithmic density as the set on which $π(x)>\mathrm{li}(x)$, although for large $x$ the two sets are disjoint. We prove analogues for primes in arithmetic progressions, for the higher moments of the system, and, under a linear independence hypothesis, for $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$, where the biases of even and odd degrees are interchanged.

papers.title: The Min-Cut Formulation of Ollivier-Ricci Curvature
papers.abstract: Computing Ollivier-Ricci curvature normally requires a local distance matrix and a linear program per edge, prompting workarounds based on entropic regularization or combinatorial proxies. We show that exact curvature needs neither. For any one-step measures, the Kantorovich dual has an integral three-level optimum, reducing each edge to one minimum s-t cut on a distance-free network linear in the read adjacency lists. This solves instances requiring quadratically many distance queries in linear time, while a converse reduction shows that no exact algorithm can beat bipartite matching. Our solver is a median 6 times (up to 506 times) faster than distance construction plus $\mathtt{POT}$'s C++ simplex, 441 times faster than $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$, and 23 times faster than graph min-cost flow. Even given the distances, Sinkhorn iterations at $\mathtt{GraphRicciCurvature}$'s regularization are a median 12 times slower, and combinatorial proxies alter edge rankings, missing the bulk of the most negatively curved ones.

papers.title: Global Weak Solutions and Non-Formation of Vacuum States for Compressible Navier--Stokes--Korteweg Equations
papers.abstract: A long-standing open problem in the mathematical theory of M-D fluid dynamics in viscous compressible flow is whether vacuum can form in finite time from initial data with density bounded away from zero. The underlying assumption in the derivation of systems of Navier--Stokes type from physical principles is that the fluid is non-dilute and can be described as a continuum. A negative answer to this problem would support the self-consistency of the continuum assumption for the Navier--Stokes-type models. This issue is particularly important when the viscosity coefficients are constant, since, from a physical standpoint, it is unclear how to meaningfully define the fluid velocity in vacuum regions, which in turn makes it difficult to interpret the associated viscous stresses. In this paper, for the barotropic compressible fluid with capillary effects, when the coefficients of viscosity and capillarity are all constants, we establish the global existence of weak solutions of the Cauchy problem for the corresponding Navier--Stokes--Korteweg equations with initial data that are large, radially symmetric, and away from the vacuum in two and three spatial dimensions. The failure of the well-known BD entropy estimate poses a substantial challenge to establishing this existence theory. Moreover, we rule out finite-time vacuum formation for the 2-D radially symmetric weak solutions constructed here. This extends, for the first time, the well-known Hoff--Smoller non-vacuum-formation theory (Commun. Math. Phys. 2001) from 1-D compressible Navier--Stokes equations with constant viscosity coefficients to 2-D radially symmetric flows with capillarity.

papers.title: On Observability Decomposition of Boolean Control Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies the observability decomposition of Boolean networks (BNs) and Boolean control networks (BCNs) in the semi-tensor product framework. We characterize when a BN admits an observability decomposition in terms of the equivalence classes induced by indistinguishability. We prove that a decomposition exists if and only if all such equivalence classes have the same cardinality, and we explicitly construct the coordinate transformation together with the matrices of the observable and unobservable subsystems. The observable subsystem is shown to be the quotient graph obtained by contracting each class into a single vertex. For BNs whose equivalence classes have unequal cardinalities, we propose an extended observability decomposition by adding virtual states, and show that every finite BN admits an observability decomposition in an extended sense. These results are further generalized to BCNs, for which an algorithm and an illustrative example are provided.

papers.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
papers.abstract: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.

papers.title: Integral Means of Fibonacci Numbers: Divisibility, Density, and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent works of Fatehizadeh, Yaqubi, Flynn-Connolly, Luca and Marques on the arithmetic mean of Fibonacci numbers, we study divisibility properties of sums of Fibonacci numbers whose indices form arithmetic progressions. We show that infinitely many even and odd $n$ divide such sums, and also the corresponding sums of squares and cubes, and we find all $n$ for which the geometric and harmonic means of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ are integers. Further, we study the set $\mathcal{A}$ of integers $n\geq2$ for which the arithmetic mean of $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ is an integer. We show that $\mathcal{A}$ is both rich and sparse: it contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions and does not contain odd prime powers, yet $\#\{n\leq x: n\in\mathcal{A}\}\ll x/\sqrt{\log x}$. This density-zero bound holds more generally for every set $\{n: n\mid\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}F_{r+id}\}$. We also establish necessary conditions for three consecutive integral means (a question of Luca and Marques).

papers.title: Characterizing $2$-slices over finite groups
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, we characterize the $2$-slices of $G$-spectra in the regular slice filtration in terms of their homotopy Mackey functors and $k$-invariant. We explicitly compute this for cyclic $p$-groups and the alternating group $A_4$.

papers.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper. Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing

papers.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
