papers.title: Taylor invertibility and the completion problem for commuting tuples of upper triangular operator matrices
papers.abstract: We study commuting $n$-tuples of upper triangular operator matrices $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}} = \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix} \mathbf{A} & \mathbf{C} \\ \mathbf{0} & \mathbf{B} \end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ acting on a direct sum of Banach spaces. Using the long exact sequence in cohomology induced by the Koszul complexes, we show that $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is Taylor invertible if and only if the connecting homomorphisms $H^k(\mathbf{B}) \to H^{k+1}(\mathbf{A})$ are linear bijections in every degree, and that under natural closed-range hypotheses on the diagonal tuples these bijections are automatically topological isomorphisms. We determine which closed-range properties of the diagonal tuples are forced by the Taylor invertibility of $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ and show by an example that the remaining ones fail in general. We then study the multivariable invertible completion problem, that is, the existence of a coupling tuple $\mathbf{C}$ for which $\mathbf{M}_{\mathbf{C}}$ is Taylor invertible. We reduce it to the realization of a family of cohomological isomorphisms by a single coupling tuple, show that the cohomology of $\mathbf{B}$ and the shifted cohomology of $\mathbf{A}$ must be isomorphic as graded modules over the exterior algebra, and exhibit diagonal tuples whose cohomology spaces are topologically isomorphic in every degree but which admit no Taylor invertible completion, a phenomenon with no one-dimensional counterpart.

papers.title: Relaxation dynamics of Winfree oscillators on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study exponential relaxation to equilibrium for Winfree-type models on Riemannian manifolds. For the sphere model with entrainment point $p$ and canonical influence, we derive convergence to equilibrium, whenever no oscillator starts at the antipode $-p$. For the corresponding canonical model on $\mathrm U(d)$, we obtain the same convergence whenever no initial matrix has the eigenvalue $-1$. Both results hold above explicit coupling thresholds depending on the initial configuration and the frequency matrices. For a broader class of unitary influence functions, the same spectral condition yields exponential convergence for sufficiently large coupling strengths. Finite-time entrance into positively invariant stable regions and contraction estimates yield exponential convergence rates and equilibrium uniqueness within those regions. A finite symmetry construction on Lie groups realizes the unitary model and a special unitary analogue as invariant Kuramoto--Lohe subsystems, yielding local relaxation results. Finally, we formulate an abstract Winfree model on Riemannian manifolds and establish local exponential relaxation in a fixed coordinate neighborhood under quantitative attraction and regularity assumptions.

papers.title: Spectrality of additive measures with Bernoulli convolutions
papers.abstract: The spectral properties of additive measures of Lebesgue type are by now completely settled \cite{LLP21,ALZ23,KW25,Lu25}. In this paper we continue the study of spectrality for Cantor-type additive measures. For $0<r<1$, let $μ_r$ denote the Bernoulli convolution generated by the maps $x\mapsto rx$ and $x\mapsto r(x+2)$ with equal weights, and consider the Bernoulli-type additive measure \[ μ_{r,s}=\tfrac12(μ_r\timesδ_0+δ_0\timesμ_s). \] For every even integer $R=2k$ we construct an explicit spectrum of the one-dimensional measure $μ_{1/R}$, and from it an explicit spectrum of $μ^{1/R}:=μ_{1/R,1/R}$ lying on the antidiagonal is constructed. Combined with the recently established absence of Fourier frames for the Bernoulli convolutions $μ_{1/N}$ for odd integers $N\geq3$ \cite{DLT26,FSW26}, this yields a parity dichotomy: $μ^{1/R}$ is spectral if and only if $R$ is even. For unequal contraction ratios, we prove that $μ_{1/2,1/4}$ is not spectral. Several open problems and future directions are discussed.

papers.title: On Semilocal Convergence of a Semismooth* Newton Method
papers.abstract: We give conditions under which the semismooth$^*$ Newton method solves $0\in F(x)$ from a given initial point. At each step, we bound the distance from the corrected point $(x_{k+1},0)$ to the graph of $F$ by a function of the correction length. We also bound $\|A^{-1}B\|$ uniformly over the selected coderivative pairs $(A,B)$. Together, these bounds give a test on the initial graph residual and the radius of a prescribed ball. If the test holds, the iterates converge to a solution in that ball. If the decrease modulus tends to zero, every infinite run converges $q$-superlinearly. For mixed complementarity problems on a box, we assume that the smooth part has a Lipschitz continuous Jacobian and that every nonempty principal submatrix is nonsingular. We bound the error after one step for each regular pair. The bound is quadratic in the distance to a solution and depends explicitly on the norm of the correction matrix. For affine problems, we give a threshold on the norm of the vertical component of a graph point. Below this threshold, all regular pairs at that point give the same solution in one step, even when their rows come from different branches. Hence any run with vanishing graph residuals terminates in finitely many steps. For integer affine data, we give a test for an exact step using only the problem data and the current iterate.

papers.title: Poisson Statistics for Values of Binary Quadratic Forms in Short Intervals
papers.abstract: We study the number of integers represented by a binary quadratic form in short intervals. Extending the work of Freiberg, Kurlberg, and Rosenzweig on sums of two squares, we formulate an analogue of the Hardy--Littlewood prime $k$-tuple conjecture for the integers represented by a genus of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms of a fixed negative discriminant. We show that this hypothesis implies that the number of integers represented by a genus, and by each class in the genus, in a random interval $(n,n+y]$ with $n\le x$, where $y$ is $τ$ times the average spacing $\sqrt{\log x}/b(d)$, is asymptotically Poisson distributed with parameter $τ$. The proof uses the method of moments, with Bernays' asymptotic for the number of represented integers in place of the prime number theorem, and an adaptation of Ford's simplified argument for the average of the singular series. We also give numerical evidence for the hypothesis.

papers.title: Gaps between zeros of Epstein zeta-functions of binary quadratic forms on the critical line
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integral binary quadratic form $Q$ whose discriminant is, up to sign, not a perfect square, the Epstein zeta-function of $Q$ has a zero $\frac12+iγ$ with $|γ-T|\le T^{2/5+ε}$ for all large $T$. For indefinite $Q$, that is, for zeta-functions of ideal classes of real quadratic orders, this is the first exponent below the classical barrier $1/2$. For positive definite $Q$ it improves the exponents $5/11$ of Jutila and Srinivas and $3/7$ of the authors, and for discriminant $-4m^2$ with $m$ odd we obtain $1/3$. A main ingredient, of independent interest, is an explicit Voronoi summation formula with additive twists to every modulus for the representation numbers of an indefinite binary form. The resulting dual sums are treated by a two-dimensional Weyl differencing, controlled by an exact formula for the Hessian determinant of the differenced phase.

papers.title: The optimal exponent in the Babai-Goodman-Pyber theorem
papers.abstract: Babai, Goodman and Pyber proved that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le [X:H]^c$ for every finite group $X$ and every soluble subgroup $H\le X$, where $\operatorname{Rad}(X)$ denotes the largest soluble normal subgroup of $X$. We prove that the least possible value of $c$ is $b_0=1+\log_9(168\cdot 24^{1/3})\approx3.8141$. For nonsoluble $X$, we obtain the stronger inequality $[X:\operatorname{Rad}(X)]\le 24^{-1/3}[X:H]^{b_0}$, and the coefficient $24^{-1/3}$ is optimal for this exponent. We reduce the problem to bounds on soluble subgroups of automorphism groups of finite simple groups. Examples based on $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ establish sharpness.

papers.title: Weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation
papers.abstract: We prove weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation $\partial_t(|u|^{p-2}u)+\mathcal L_{s,p}u=0$, where $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$. The functions are assumed to be continuous in the equation domain and continuous in time with values in the weighted tail space. We treat both functions that are strictly positive in the equation domain, with signed exterior values, and globally nonnegative functions with interior zeros. Exterior values need not be bounded or spatially continuous. For $1<p<2$, the viscosity formulation tests the evolution variable $|u|^{p-2}u$, retaining the nonlocal interaction at zeros. The viscosity-to-weak implication follows from localized multiplicative regularization and energy estimates independent of a positive lower bound. The reverse implication uses comparison with smooth functions, justified by a relative-energy identity. A zero-slice property allows the weak identities on positive time intervals to be joined across the zero set.

papers.title: Group classification of a class of systems of nonlinear diffusion equations. I
papers.abstract: We study the Lie symmetries of a class of systems of (1 + 1)-dimensional nonlinear diffusion equations. The equivalence algebra and the kernel of the maximal Lie invariance algebras of this class are found. We prove that there exist exactly nine inequivalent subclasses of this class for which the corresponding diffusion systems admit Lie symmetry extensions. We also carry out the exhaustive group classification of the systems of nonlinear diffusion equations from the first subclass.

papers.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
papers.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $β_f^-(q)=β_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-ν_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $ν_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.

papers.title: Richárd Wiegandt's theory of Möbius products revisited
papers.abstract: In a 1959 paper Richárd Wiegandt defined a general notion of Möbius product of functions on arbitrary locally finite posets, and determined when this product is commutative and associative. He gave an example showing that not all locally finite posets allow such a Möbius product. Here we characterize those posets of height 3 that can be equipped with a commutative and associative Möbius product.

papers.title: Algebraic derivations and the first \(L^2\)-cohomology of free group factors
papers.abstract: Let \(M\) be the von Neumann algebra of a nonabelian free group of finite rank. We prove that its first \(L^2\)-Betti number in the sense of Connes and Shlyakhtenko is infinite. We show that every assignment of values in \(\Aff(M\bar\otimes M^{\op})\) to the standard semicircular generators extends to an algebraic derivation on all of \(M\). The extension follows from a rank identity for the Jacobians of finite systems of polynomial relations. We also prove that, for any \(\mathrm{II}_1\) factor with separable predual, the existence of an outer derivation with these coefficients forces the first \(L^2\)-Betti number to be infinite.

papers.title: Contractible 4-Manifolds with Nonnegative Ricci Curvature and Euclidean Volume Growth
papers.abstract: We prove that every contractible smooth 4-manifold admitting a complete Riemannian metric with nonnegative Ricci curvature and Euclidean volume growth is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^4$. More precisely, every compact subset lies in the interior of a connected compact regular domain with simply connected complement. The key construction produces compact domains whose boundaries admit positive scalar curvature and which are regular sublevels of global strictly three-convex Morse exhaustions. A topological criterion forces the exterior fundamental group to be trivial whenever it contains no nonabelian free subgroup and satisfies the resulting boundary, homological, and relative cell hypotheses; in the geometric application, this group is finite. Its proof uses a cellular formulation of the Gerstenhaber-Rothaus theorem and a smooth filling obstruction. The resulting complements give simple connectivity at infinity, and Freedman's recognition theorem completes the argument.

papers.title: Robust decision-dependent information discovery is harder than robust optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a four-stage variant of robust optimization with cost uncertainty described by the budget uncertainty polytope, known as decision-dependent information discovery (DDID). In this problem, the decision maker first queries a subset of the cost coefficients. Then, the adversary responds by revealing worst-case values for the queried elements, after which the decision maker chooses a feasible solution while facing the remaining uncertainty on the unqueried costs. Our contribution is twofold. On the negative side, we prove that, the DDID is NP-complete even when the underlying nominal problem is the 2-selection problem, for which only a polynomial number of feasible solutions exist. This contrasts with the min-max robust counterpart with budget uncertainty, known to be not harder than the nominal problem. On the positive side, we prove that the more general $p$-selection problem can be solved in polynomial time under the additional assumption that all deviations are equal.

papers.title: Partial Self-Similar Fractal Interpolation Functions and Surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of fractal interpolation functions with partial self-similarity. We first study fractal interpolation surfaces defined on rectangular domains, analyze the stability and sensitivity of the proposed construction to parameter perturbations. In addition, we investigate the partial $α$-fractal function in both the univariate and bivariate cases, as well as the invariant measure in the univariate setting whose support is the graph of the fractal interpolation function. Further, under suitable additional conditions, we derive bounds for the box-counting dimension of the graph of the univariate PFIF. The results presented in this paper are backed up by illustrative examples.

papers.title: The smallest singular value of a random sign matrix: the Spielman-Teng conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ matrix with independent uniform entries in $\{-1,1\}$. We prove that $\mathbb{P}(s_{\min}(A) \leq \varepsilon n^{-1/2}) \leq \varepsilon + e^{-cn}$ for all $\varepsilon \geq 0$ and an absolute $c > 0$, as conjectured by Spielman and Teng. For $e^{-cn} \leq \varepsilon \leq n^{-θ}$, with $θ> 0$ absolute and $n$ sufficiently large, the upper bound improves to $\varepsilon(1 - 1/(2n) + O(n^{-1.02}))$. The proof does not give numerical values for the dimension threshold or the exponential rate. We obtain the first-order improvement by comparing a Gaussian surface integral for the sign ensemble with its counterpart for independent spherical rows. An arithmetic small-ball estimate transfers this comparison to exponentially small scales. At polynomial scales, weighting by a coordinate of the least left singular vector yields a negative quadratic term in the crossing density.

papers.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
papers.abstract: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.

papers.title: Dissipative Geometric Flows and Certified Phase-Volume Contraction
papers.abstract: This paper develops an approach to uniform phase-volume contraction for prescribed dynamical systems. The main result is that every positive rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound can be certified in finite search time by a regularized Sobolev gradient flow. The resulting positive density ensures exponential contraction of the weighted phase volume with unit prefactor. For each fixed regularization parameter, the flow converges exponentially to a unique minimizer. As the regularization vanishes, these minimizers converge to the feasible potential of minimum Sobolev norm for a fixed feasibility margin. The certification procedure rests on a Holder estimate that converts a bound on the integral penalty into a pointwise bound on the weighted divergence over the entire invariant domain. This estimate yields a stopping criterion for the search. Finite termination is also established in growing finite-dimensional trial spaces for a staged scheme with exact gradient evaluations and controlled positive quadrature. The scheme requires neither a supplied feasibility margin nor a bound on the norm of a feasible potential. A disk example shows that the invariant-measure bound can be approached by smooth certificates even when no C^1 certificate attains it. Analytical properties of novel local D-Liouville, D-Yamabe, and D-Ricci evolutions driven by divergence penalties are established. For the unnormalized D-Yamabe flow, a scaling obstruction to exponential stability of stationary conformal factors is established. For the D-Ricci flow, the transformation law for the prescribed vector field under DeTurck pullback is derived. This law specifies how the vector field must transform when the gauge term is removed. Examples on the torus and sphere identify obstructions to smooth convergence of the geometric evolutions.

papers.title: Synchronized Memory-Dependent Intracellular Oscillations for a Cell-Bulk ODE-PDE Model in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We develop a hybrid asymptotic-numerical theory for a cell-bulk ODE-PDE model in $\mathbb{R}^3$ to analyze the long-range diffusive coupling of spatially localized, dynamically active cells. In the limit of small cell radius $\varepsilon\ll 1$, we derive a novel integro-differential ODE system for the intracellular dynamics, in which the 3-D bulk diffusion field is effectively replaced by a time-memory kernel whose strength depends on the inter-cell distances. To compute long-time solutions efficiently, we implement a fast time-marching scheme for this integro-differential system that is inspired by the \emph{sum-of-exponentials} method. This scheme is applied to Sel'kov intracellular kinetics, which is a conceptual two-component model for a conditional oscillator. Our analysis reveals that, in contrast to the more strongly coupled 2-D case, each cell in $\mathbb{R}^3$ experiences only a weak $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ coupling effect from the other cells in the population. Consequently, individual cells that exhibit oscillatory intracellular dynamics can only synchronize over very long time scales of order $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-1})$ when they are separated by $\mathcal{O}(1)$ distances. Moreover, cells whose kinetic parameters are $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ close to their marginal stability threshold will be influenced by the weak $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon)$ cell-cell coupling from the entire population. In order to resolve the effect of these subtle interactions on collective intracellular dynamics, we develop a novel matrix perturbation theory for the linear stability of steady-state solutions of the cell-bulk model. Finally, we validate our analytical predictions of the perturbed marginal stability thresholds of steady-state solutions using the time-marching numerical scheme, illustrating various types of synchronized intracellular dynamics that can emerge over long time scales.

papers.title: KKT Atlas: Learning Low-Dimensional Local Scenario Models for Contextual Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: In contextual stochastic optimization, integrated learning trains conditional models on operational loss, but repeatedly solving stochastic programs with many scenarios is costly. We propose KKT Atlas, which partitions contexts into local charts and identifies a low-dimensional subspace per chart from decision gradients of the scenario cost. It generates shared scenarios by jointly fitting subspace coordinates and context-dependent probabilities. We show that one more scenario than the subspace dimension suffices to approximate the conditional Karush-Kuhn-Tucker optimality condition under regularity conditions, yielding decision and risk bounds under local strong convexity, with generalization error scaling with the compact parameter dimension. On three synthetic problems, Atlas uses 4-18 scenarios per decision versus 500 for direct-solve full-support integrated learning. It attains comparable or lower risk with about $4$-$23\times$ construction and $13$-$61\times$ batch deployment speedups. Atlas also achieves lower risk than clustering-based reduction at matched support budgets. In real-world European grid reserve commitment, Atlas compresses 728 scenarios to 8-9, cutting construction and deployment times by factors of about 4 and 3 relative to full-support integrated learning. Its loss is lowest over 11 quarters and, over 17 later quarters with fixed settings, slightly higher than with full-support integrated learning and significantly lower than with the remaining benchmarks.

papers.title: Ranges of vector measures and copies of $c_0$
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a Banach space such that every weakly compact subset of $X$ is contained in the range of an $X$-valued countably additive vector measure defined on a $σ$-algebra. We prove that $X$ contains no isomorphic copy of $c_0$, thereby answering a question posed by R. Anantharaman and J. Diestel [Comment. Math. Prace Mat. 30 (1991), no. 2, 221--235]. In particular, every Banach lattice with this property is superreflexive.

papers.title: Learning Linear Time-Varying Koopman Models for Constrained Nonlinear Optimal Control
papers.abstract: This paper presents a learning-based Koopman framework for solving constrained nonlinear optimal control problems. Despite significant advances in Koopman-based modeling and control, challenges remain in achieving accurate representations of controlled nonlinear dynamics and constraints while maintaining computational efficiency for optimal control. Motivated by these challenges, a linear time-varying (LTV) Koopman representation is developed to provide a more expressive representation of controlled nonlinear dynamics while preserving a linear prediction structure suitable for efficient convex optimization. Modeling errors and their propagation over extended prediction horizons are analyzed, motivating a neural-network-based Koopman framework that jointly learns lifted dynamics and constraint representations with stability-oriented regularization to improve long-horizon prediction performance. Based on the learned Koopman model, the original constrained nonlinear optimal control problem is reformulated as a convex quadratic program with conservative constraint tightening to account for modeling uncertainty during constraint enforcement. Numerical results on a low-thrust orbit transfer problem and a Mars entry guidance problem demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in terms of prediction accuracy, computational efficiency, and constrained optimal control performance.

papers.title: $\ell$-abundant numbers and extremal divisor sums
papers.abstract: For an integer $\ell \ge 1$, we study the sum $σ_{(\ell)}(n)$ of the divisors of $n$ whose positive prime exponents are at least $\ell$. The associated abundant, perfect, superabundant, and colossally abundant numbers recover the classical notions when $\ell=1$. We prove strict nesting and infinitude of the abundant classes and derive obstructions to perfection. Our results extend classical work of Ramanujan, Alaoglu, and Erdős on superabundant prime-factor structure and colossally abundant exponent selection. For $\ell \ge 2$, we characterize all maximizers of \[ \frac{σ_{(\ell)}(n)}{n^{1+\varepsilon}} \] for every $\varepsilon>0$. An explicit logarithmic formula determines the optimal positive exponents, while comparison with exponent $0$ resolves prime entry and all ties. This characterization also yields infinitely many $\ell$-colossally abundant numbers.

papers.title: Support geometry of the stationary distribution for a parabolic nonlinear AR(1) process with binary innovations
papers.abstract: This paper studies the nonlinear AR(1) process \(X_{n+1}=f(X_n)+σξ_{n+1}\), \(n\ge0\), driven by binary innovations \(ξ_n\in\{0,1\}\), where \(f\) is strictly increasing and strictly concave, with \(f(0)=0\), \(f'(0)=1\), and \(f'(x)<1\) for \(x>0\). The process is shown to have a unique stationary distribution. The geometry of its support is described in terms of the noise amplitude \(σ\) and the function \(f\): the support is either an interval or a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero, and the two regimes are separated by the relation between \(σ\) and the unique number \(c_σ>0\) solving \(c_σ-f(c_σ)=σ\). Namely, the support is an interval when \(c_σ\ge2σ\) and a Cantor set when \(c_σ<2σ\). Under the additional condition \(\ell_\infty:=\lim_{x\to\infty}f'(x)<1/2\), there exists a unique critical value \(σ_c>0\), characterized by \(f(2σ_c)=σ_c\), such that the support is an interval for \(0<σ\leσ_c\) and a Cantor set for \(σ>σ_c\); if \(\ell_\infty\ge1/2\), the support is an interval for every \(σ>0\). In the Cantor regime the stationary distribution is non-atomic, and hence singular continuous.

papers.title: Optimal Weighted Volume Dissipativity and Sobolev Regularity at Limiting Rate
papers.abstract: Sharp pointwise divergence bounds for a nonlinear flow are studied under the requirement that the logarithm of the adapted positive density also be an exponentially decaying Lyapunov function. Invariant-measure duality supplies the unrestricted benchmark. Under two-sided quadratic Lyapunov bounds, scaling a prescribed Lyapunov function realizes every strictly suboptimal pointwise rate without reducing its decay rate, and the closure of the joint rate region is a rectangle. For a fixed reference volume form, the limiting pointwise rate has a smooth compatible certificate exactly when the differential of the reference divergence vanishes at the equilibrium. Otherwise, the infimal second-derivative supremum norm grows inversely with the gap to the limiting rate. Matching Sobolev cost bounds are proved in every finite dimension when the integrability exponent exceeds the dimension and the prescribed Lyapunov rate does not exceed half the baseline rate. The upper construction uses a regularized square root of the baseline Lyapunov function and keeps the potential and its gradient uniformly bounded. Matching contraction deficits under a Sobolev norm budget follow. A scalar borderline family has bounded second-derivative mass and a Lipschitz limit with atomic second derivative. The limiting exponent also holds in the reference measure with an explicit uniform volume prefactor, even when no smooth compatible instantaneous certificate exists. Scaling preserves the full baseline Lyapunov rate.

papers.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and α-stable processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $α$-stable Lévy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/α_2,\,1/(ν+2)\}}$, where $α_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $ν$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows. We first derive the intermediate step of the averaging principle to average out the effect of fast-variable oscillations on the system, although the averaged variable still depends on $\varepsilon$. We obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1-1/α_2}$. Furthermore, under the uniformly quasi-periodic conditions, we show that the slow component converges strongly to the solution of some autonomous averaged equation, whose coefficients independent of $\varepsilon$. We thus obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1/(ν+2)}$. The main contribution of this paper is to extend the additive Lévy noise to multiplicative Lévy noise and extend the fast equation of the system from the autonomous setting to the non-autonomous setting. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the quasi-periodic setting, extending the corresponding results for the periodic case.

papers.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
papers.abstract: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ngô support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ngô string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.

papers.title: An extended Matsumoto--Yor property for free GIG distributions
papers.abstract: We prove a two-parameter extension of the Matsumoto--Yor property for free generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. The transformation is the reciprocal form of a known matrix Yang--Baxter map. Our proof combines the independence-preserving property for matrix generalized inverse Gaussian distributions with asymptotic freeness. Since the relevant spectra stay in compact subsets of the positive half-line, continuous functional calculus and polynomial approximation suffice to handle all inverses. The same argument yields the free Matsumoto--Yor property itself for all positive rates of the free Poisson law, including those for which this law has an atom at zero. We also discuss the limit in which one of the two parameters tends to zero: the limiting laws are free Poisson only when the rate is at least one, so for smaller rates this limit does not recover the free Matsumoto--Yor property.

papers.title: The Anatomy of Piecewise-Linear Learned Indexes
papers.abstract: Piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) learned indexes (PGM-index, FITing-Tree, RadixSpline, PLEX, PLIN) compress sorted keys into $\pm\varepsilon$ segments, yet prior theory stops at coarse $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ single-segment bounds. At the bottom layer, optimal greedy PLA covers $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2/v_0 \approx 3.54\,\varepsilon^2/v_0$ keys per segment on independent gaps and $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2$ under any smooth density ($v_0=1$), while anchored and chord fitters retain $Θ(\varepsilon^2/v_0)$ coverage. Across recursive layers, a law-of-large-numbers heuristic--invoked to claim $O(\log\log n)$ height for the PGM-index--suggests summing $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ gaps averages out fluctuations. We prove this fails under Endpoint Promotion (EP): stopping-time fluctuations reset relative gap variance at every depth, locking fanout at $C_\varepsilon \approx 19.861\,\varepsilon^2$, expected height at $\log n/\log C_\varepsilon + O(1)$, and lookup at $Θ(\log n)$. To break this barrier, Rank-Equispaced Promotion (RE) samples pivots at equal rank strides. Each stride sums a fixed number of base gaps, so relative variance decays across layers and cumulative coverage squares at each step. Expected height drops to $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + O(1)$ on independent gaps and $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + \log_2^+(\log n/\log(\varepsilon/δ)) + O(1)$ on smooth densities with curvature $δ$. A compact bucket directory routes across unaligned RE pivots with $<1$ extra comparison per layer on average, giving RE-PGM $O(\log\varepsilon \cdot \log\log_\varepsilon n)$ expected lookup in $Θ(n/\varepsilon^2)$ space and $O(n)$ build time without radix skew sensitivity. Our constants match empirical fanout within $0.3\%$ down to $\varepsilon=2$, and all core theorems are formalized in Lean 4.

papers.title: A Unit-Gradient Neural Variational Method for Anisotropic Eikonal Equations
papers.abstract: We develop a variational neural method for computing viscosity solutions of the anisotropic eikonal equation. Building on the vanishing-viscosity principle, we minimize an energy functional whose Euler--Lagrange equation is the viscous anisotropic eikonal equation and introduce an auxiliary variable for the gradient, enforcing the constraint through a penalty. A key challenge in this formulation is to handle nonlinearity of the functional while controlling the interaction between the viscosity and penalty parameters. To address this challenge, we impose a unit-norm constraint on the auxiliary variable exactly, as prescribed by the eikonal equation. This removes the gradient from the exponentially weighted part of the functional and allows the viscosity and penalty limits to be studied separately. We establish two convergence results. First, for each fixed viscosity parameter $ε>0$, we prove convergence to the viscosity solution as the penalty parameter $λ\rightarrow\infty$. Second, for the distance function to the boundary of a convex or smooth domain, we prove convergence as $ε\rightarrow0$ for any fixed $λ>0$. The latter result motivates our stable numerical strategy, which keeps $λ$ fixed while decreasing $ε$ whenever the training loss stagnates. The formulation is implemented using a neural network that satisfies the unit-norm constraint by construction and a mesh-free approach that evaluates the singularly scaled functional at randomly sampled points without requiring mesh refinement as $ε\to0$. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method on diverse isotropic and anisotropic problems, including three-dimensional open-surface reconstruction from point clouds.

papers.title: The polygonal Steklov--Weinstock inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes the scale-invariant first positive Steklov eigenvalue $L(P)σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ of positive area with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity (and up to congruence at prescribed perimeter). Our proof combines two complementary realizations of the Rayleigh--Ritz variational principle. For convex competitors, we transplant a first Steklov eigenfunction of the regular reference polygon: for triangles, affine transplantation aligned with a longest side yields both the sharp inequality and a two-sided linear stability bound in terms of the maximal side-length deviation; for convex $N$-gons with $N \ge 4$, a piecewise harmonic fan transplantation across radial sectors matches traces along the internal seams. In the quadrilateral case, centering the fan at the vertex average pairs opposite sides and controls the displacement of the diagonal midpoints, whereas for $N=5$ the spectral deficit dominates both the area deficit and the squared vertex and Hausdorff distances to the regular pentagon. Nonconvex competitors are treated by stratifying them according to their number $p \le N-1$ of strictly convex corners: boundary moment inequalities handle $p=3$, while conformal disk tests localized on the gaps between positive turning prevertices rule out $p \ge 4$ via comparison with the regular $(p+1)$-gon. Finite parameter ranges are certified using exact rational arithmetic and outward-rounded integer interval enclosures. In addition, we establish the sharp fourth-order asymptotic expansion of the spectral deficit at a prescribed positive-corner count, together with a quantitative local and global stability theorem for polygons with a large number of sides.

papers.title: Aalen-Johansen as an augmented IPCW estimator
papers.abstract: We show that, in every sample, the widely used Aalen-Johansen estimator of a state occupation probability is an inverse probability of censoring weighted estimator augmented by a working Markov prediction from each subject's current state. This identity explains the robustness of the Aalen-Johansen against departures from the Markov assumption. It also reveals that its influence function differs from the semiparametric efficient one by two orthogonal components: the information in earlier history beyond the current state, and the error of the Markov prediction. Based on this decomposition, we propose a practical, model-free least-squares augmentation of the Aalen-Johansen that regresses the outcome on a history score, narrowing the gap under non-Markov processes without increasing the asymptotic variance. Its advantages are validated both theoretically and in simulations.

papers.title: Elastic rebound in viscous fluid: an efficient rigid--elastic splitting with an asymptotic gap model
papers.abstract: We formulate and test a model for an elastic body that falls under gravity onto the bottom of a container filled with a viscous incompressible fluid and rebounds without topological contact. The body is a rigid body plus a small, quasi-static elastic deformation, represented by a fixed compliance operator. In the near-contact patch, the thin fluid film is described by a Reynolds equation with cavitation. This allows the use of coarse meshes that need not resolve the gap, enabling efficient simulation. The film is coupled implicitly to the elastic surface displacement and to the rigid normal motion. The bulk fluid is coupled monolithically to the rigid body. For the axisymmetric case with vertical translation, the coupled step reduces exactly to a small dense nonlinear problem for the film pressure, with the bulk eliminated through a $2x2$ affine map. The model is implemented in NGSolve and compared with the experiments of Hagemeier et al. (2021) and the Eulerian FSI simulations of Wahl et al. (2021a). For a PTFE ball the approach agrees with the Eulerian FSI to 1\%. For a soft rubber ball (St $\approx 120$) the purely elastic model gives about three times the measured rebound. Material damping is the most important missing effect: a Kelvin--Voigt compliance with loss factor $\tanδ=0.6$ gives 4.0\,mm, against 4.4\,mm measured. A planar version of the model is compared with the recently published 2D benchmark of Corti et al. (2026). The radius of the film patch is the only numerical parameter of the splitting. It is fixed by one a-priori rule for all configurations, derived from a dry Hertz estimate of the approach, and the results depend only weakly on it.

papers.title: Finite rank and compactness of finite sums of Toeplitz products on the harmonic Bergman space
papers.abstract: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness for finite sums of products of Toeplitz operators on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk, assuming boundedness only of the full harmonic symbols. Reflecting the appropriate symbols reduces sums of Toeplitz products and small Hankel products to Toeplitz product sums. For sums of mixed Toeplitz and small Hankel products in either order, right multiplication by a fixed unitary reflection gives the corresponding reduction. These reductions preserve rank and compactness. Finite rank is characterized by symbol identities and a cubic divisibility condition on the coefficient polynomials obtained after choosing bases over one-variable rational function fields. We also obtain an exact rank formula. Compactness is characterized by boundary vanishing of the diagonal symbol sum and uniform decay of the centered symbol tensor on hyperbolic disks of fixed radius as their centers approach the boundary. For a sum of $N\ge1$ products, an equivalent compactness criterion uses weighted derivatives of the symbol components up to order $N$. When $N$ is even, the conditions of order $N$ cannot be omitted. Mixed commutators of finite rank vanish. We characterize small Hankel commutators of nonzero finite rank in terms of a bounded analytic function and its bounded reciprocal, both with rational primitives.

papers.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
papers.abstract: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

papers.title: An Exposition of Gerstenhaber's Proposition 1: Elimination of Coboundaries in Formal Deformations
papers.abstract: Gerstenhaber's foundational work on formal deformations of associative algebras relates the first non-trivial term of a deformation to the second Hochschild cohomology group. In the proof of Proposition~1 of his 1964 paper, a leading Hochschild $2$-cocycle which is a coboundary is successively removed by formal changes of variables. If this elimination terminates after finitely many steps, no limiting argument is required, but the possibility that coboundaries continue to be eliminated indefinitely is left largely implicit in the original treatment. This expository note makes that limiting argument fully explicit for deformations over $K[[t]]$ of a fixed associative $K$-algebra $A$. We use the $t$-adic topology on the relevant spaces of formal power series and formal endomorphisms, establish completeness and the continuity of composition, inversion and the action on formal multiplications, and show that an infinite sequence of successive changes of variables assembles into a single, well-defined formal equivalence. This yields a complete, self-contained proof of the classical result and its rigidity consequence.

papers.title: Driver Surge Maps for Supply Rebalancing with Downstream Matching
papers.abstract: Ride-hailing platforms use driver-facing surge maps to rebalance spatial supply by offering zone-level bonuses. These bonuses can reshape supply by inducing nearby drivers to relocate and encouraging latent drivers to become dispatchable, but both responses are voluntary. Within short decision windows, platforms risk offering bonuses that reshape driver supply without generating sufficient downstream matching value to justify the associated payments. We formulate the driver surge map design problem (DSMDP) to optimize zone-level bonuses while anticipating voluntary driver responses and downstream matching. To assess how bonus adjustments affect net operating profit, we conduct a marginal analysis that identifies when small bonuses improve on the no-bonus map and how spatial smoothness links bonus decisions across zones. Using these marginal values, we develop an iterative solution approach (ISA) to sample dual sensitivities of the matching linear program across nearby matching regimes and guide real-time bonus updates. Theoretical analysis provides certificates of approximate stationarity and establishes conditions for stationary limits. Computational experiments show that ISA improves net operating profit over the best-performing feasible benchmark by up to 19.37% on the generated instances and by up to 8.43% in the New York City study. Local shortage alone is not a sufficient basis for bonus allocation. Platforms should target responsive supply whose downstream matching value justifies the associated bonus payments. Latent-driver activation can support higher-value matches even when all demand is served, but the resulting gains must also cover additional payments to drivers who would already be matched without incentives. Results indicate diminishing returns to bonus spending and show that moderate spatial smoothness can preserve most of the gains from spatial targeting.

papers.title: Subnormality of $B$-operators of class $\mathscr{S}$
papers.abstract: We characterize subnormality of $B$-operators $T=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}V&E\\0&S\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$ on $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\mathcal{H}_2$, where $V$ is an isometry, $V^*E=0$, $S$ is subnormal, and $S|E|=|E|S$. We determine when $T$ admits compactly supported signed elementary measures and express them explicitly in terms of the elementary measures of $S$. Requiring the signed elementary measures of $T$ to be positive yields a complete measure-theoretic characterization of the subnormality of $T$. If $E$ is injective, $T$ is subnormal if and only if it is a contraction. In the general case, the subnormality of $T$ is equivalent to the contractivity of its restriction to $\mathcal{H}_1\oplus\overline{{\mathcal R}(|E|)}$. We also obtain equivalent criteria involving the Taylor spectra of $(S,|E|)$, its minimal normal and minimal quasinormal extensions, and the corresponding pairs of moduli. These results extend the characterization previously known for a quasinormal lower-right entry.

papers.title: Rigidity for semiconvex entire solutions of Hessian quotient equations
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth admissible semiconvex entire solution of $σ_k(D^2u)/σ_l(D^2u)=1$ in $\mathbb R^n$, where $0\le l<k\le n$ and $k-l=1$ or $2$, is a quadratic polynomial. The proof uses a shifted Legendre transform and interior Hessian estimates for Hessian quotient equations to reduce the problem to equations of lower order. We then conclude by induction on the order of the equation.

papers.title: Spontaneous Synchronization in Cellular Circadian Clocks
papers.abstract: We study a population of identical cellular circadian oscillators, each a four-species transcription--translation feedback loop of the type analysed by Wang and Peskin, coupled by the exchange of cytoplasmic mRNA with a shared, well-mixed bloodstream at rate $ε$. Simulations started from uniformly random phases show a collective damping of the mean rhythm followed by spontaneous synchronization. We show that the blood compartment tracks the population mean on the time scale $1/[N_c(ε+δ_m)]$, and that the population means obey the single-cell equations with a correction proportional to the variance $σ_{pn}^2$ of nuclear protein across cells; the correction is accurate only near synchrony. Deviations from the mean obey a linear system with periodic coefficients, whose leading Floquet exponent $-κ(ε)$ is the asymptotic synchronization rate. Using the fact that the four first-order stages of the feedback loop commute, we prove that $κ(ε)=ε/4+O(ε^2)$ on the limit cycle in the large-population limit. Numerically computed exponents agree with the decay rates measured in simulations to within $0.2\%$ for $5$ to $400$ cells. The approach to synchrony from an incoherent state is slower than $κ$, and at the weakest coupling tested the population remains in a two-cluster state. With intrinsic molecular noise, uncoupled cells lose their autocorrelation within about ten cycles, whereas coupled cells retain it and sustain a Kuramoto order parameter of $0.68$ to $0.93$.

papers.title: Mass gap for finite connections in supercritical percolation
papers.abstract: We consider finite open clusters based at the origin in Bernoulli bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for $d\geq3$ at a supercritical value $p>p_c(d)$, whose maximal height in the direction of a unit vector $\pmb{\ell}$ lies in a fixed-width window at distance $u$. Conditioned on this event, we prove that, except with probability exponentially small in $u$, such a cluster is populated at positive density by renewal points. Here, a renewal point $w$ is the only vertex of the cluster in the fixed-width band immediately below the height hyperplane through $w$. The main technical estimate is that, under this conditioning, the absence of a renewal point is exponentially unlikely. From it we derive an exponential mass gap for the irreducible pieces delimited by successive renewal points, and from the mass gap the stated renewal abundance. The mass gap, together with the renewal decomposition and endpoint estimates established here, yields a sharp point-to-point Ornstein--Zernike asymptotic for finite connectivity, with its Gaussian-type power-law correction. The multiplicative prefactor in this asymptotic is positive and real-analytic, and the associated equidecay and Wulff boundaries are real-analytic and strictly convex. The principal innovation of the article is the use of a slide resampling that preserves the conditioned law. The slide acts by cutting the long finite connection at a given $\pmb{\ell}$-height and relocating the upper piece by a random shift. The mass gap is obtained by a delicate analysis of an iterated version of the slide operation along a positive density of attempted heights.

papers.title: Wave interactions for the two-dimensional self-similar Euler equations of nonconvex gases
papers.abstract: Gases with nonconvex equations of state may differ significantly from polytropic ideal gases; for example, rarefaction and sonic shocks may occur. This paper studies a 2D Riemann initial-boundary value problem for the potential flow equations with a nonconvex equation of state. We construct global-in-time self-similar solutions by analyzing eight distinct types of wave interactions, including composite waves consisting of a sonic/double-sonic shock coupled with one or two fan waves. Three main difficulties arise in studying these wave interactions: the self-similar potential flow system is of mixed type, with its type at each point determined by the local pseudo-Mach number; the sonic or transonic nature of the shocks is not known a priori; and sonic singularities arise on sonic shocks. To overcome these difficulties, we proceed as follows. First, we introduce a density-dependent invariant region and apply the maximum principle to establish the hyperbolicity principle of the 2D self-similar Euler equations. Second, we establish a priori estimates for the shock types by differentiating the Rankine-Hugoniot conditions along the shocks, comparing the shock and acoustic speeds, and using the Oleinik-Liu entropy condition. Finally, we employ the hodograph transformation together with regularization to handle the various singularities on sonic shocks. These wave interactions serve as building blocks for more complicated 2D Riemann problems and as benchmarks for numerical algorithms for nonconvex conservation laws. We also propose several open problems.

papers.title: The Generalized Volterra Signature
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the generalized Volterra signature \(\gvsig(\bX)\) of a path \(\bX\), extending the classical Volterra signature introduced in [Hager, Harang, Pelizzari \& Tindel, arXiv:2603.04525, 2026], which extends Lyons' path signature to the Volterra setting. We establish a new algebraic structure to encode the generalized Volterra signature. We also establish a generalized Chen's identity. By restricting the differential trees to ladder trees, we introduce the geometric Volterra signature \(\geovsig(\bX)\) and establish the shuffle product of its signature components. To the best of our knowledge, the shuffle product for the Volterra signature is the first of its kind and allows us to formulate a universal approximation theorem for geometric Volterra signatures. For a special class of kernel functions, we prove the existence of an extended path \(\Bar{\bX}\) and relate its classical signature to the geometric Volterra signature of the original path \(\bX\).

papers.title: Blow-up size for the noncommutative rank of linear symbolic matrices with low-rank coefficients
papers.abstract: The noncommutative rank (nc-rank) of a linear symbolic matrix $A = A_0 x_0 + A_1 x_1 + \dots + A_m x_m$ is the supremum of $1/k$ times the rank of the $k$-th blow-up $\sum_i A_i \otimes X_i$ of $A$, where $X_i$ are $k \times k$ matrices consisting of distinct variables. In this paper, we show that the blow-up size needed to attain the nc-rank is bounded by the ranks of the coefficient matrices. More precisely, if $A_1, \dots, A_m$ have rank at most $r$, with no restriction on $A_0$, then the $k$-th blow-up attains the nc-rank for every $k \geq r$. This holds for rectangular matrices over an arbitrary field, and unifies and extends the known results that $k = 1$ suffices for rank-one coefficients (Lovász, 1989; Ivanyos, Karpinski, and Saxena, 2010) and that $k = 2$ suffices for skew-symmetric coefficients of rank two (Oki and Soma, 2025). We present two applications. First, if $r$ is a constant, then the nc-rank of an $n \times n$ linear symbolic matrix can be computed by a randomized algorithm with $O(m n^2 + n^ω)$ arithmetic operations over a sufficiently large field, where $ω$ is the matrix multiplication exponent. Second, the hierarchy of polytopes introduced by Hirai (2026), which converges to the nc-independent set polytope, stabilizes at the $r$-th level; this is based on a counterpart of our main result for the degree of the Dieudonné determinant.

papers.title: A new angle on matrix-vector complexity
papers.abstract: The theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity has been useful for guiding the design of fast linear algebra algorithms. However, there is a large theory-practice gap in the study of *one-sided* methods, which use matrix-vector products with $\mathbf{A}$ but not $\mathbf{A}^\top$. In practice, for fundamental problems like solving linear systems, one-sided methods like GMRES are often the fastest. By contrast, worst-case analysis often shows pessimistic results, for instance showing that one-sided methods cannot solve a linear system with ideal condition number 1 unless they read the whole matrix $\mathbf{A}$. Such worst-case complexity results do not reflect real-world experience. To address this issue, this paper proposes a different theory of worst-case matrix-vector complexity that includes information on the positioning of the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ *in the complex plane*. Specifically, we characterize the "well-behavedness" of a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ through its *spectral condition number* $κ$ and its *angular eigenvalue gap $θ$*, the angle of the largest sector not containing an eigenvalue. Under these parameters, we show that the one-sided complexity of the linear system problem is $Θ(θ^{-2}κ^{π/θ})$. These results interpolate between known results for positive definite matrices ($θ= 2π$), symmetric indefinite matrices ($θ= π$), and general matrices ($θ= 0$). This provides a rigorous explanation for the success of one-sided methods in practice, as it shows that one-sided methods beat the "optimal" two-sided algorithm (CGN) when the eigenvalues of $\mathbf{A}$ lie in less than half of the complex plane ($θ> π$). Our analysis relies on tools from numerical analysis, complex analysis, and information-theoretic complexity, and the results are presented in a modular way to facilitate future use.

papers.title: Finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for real-weighted quivers
papers.abstract: We study finiteness and completeness of $g$-fans for quivers with positive real weights. We characterize finite Coxeter type by the condition that every weight in the mutation class has the form $2\cos(π/m)$ for some integer $m\geq3$. Under total sign-coherence, we then show that a quiver with finitely many $g$-clusters is $2$-finite, that is, every weight in its mutation class is less than $2$. This also gives a new proof that $g$-finiteness implies finite Coxeter type. Assuming in addition that, for every initial quiver in the mutation class, each $c$-vector on a coordinate axis is a signed standard basis vector, we prove that the $g$-fan is complete if and only if there are finitely many $g$-clusters. The main geometric result states that the coordinate projection of every $g$-cone is contained in a $g$-cone of the corresponding full subquiver. Consequently, completeness and density pass to full subquivers.

papers.title: A Spectral Zoo of Genus-Zero Free Boundary Minimal Surfaces with Many Boundary Components
papers.abstract: We study critical points of the length-normalized first Steklov eigenvalue $\barσ_1$ on genus-zero surfaces with $b$ boundary components. By a theorem of Fraser and Schoen, their first eigenfunctions give free boundary minimal surfaces in the unit ball. After uniformization, the domain is the round sphere minus $b$ round caps, with a weight on the boundary circles. A layer potential formulation gives the eigenvalues, their derivatives and a certificate for each critical point, and an exact multipole system for the caps. We compute a spectral zoo of 268 numerically certified critical points with up to $b=2252$ boundary components, including the $27$ embedded examples listed by Schulz. With their symmetry groups and Morse indices, the critical points satisfy a signed count for $3\le b\le10$. Most belong to families built from rings of boundary components. As the rings fill in, these appear to converge to the free curve minimal surfaces of Karpukhin and Noutchegueme, unions of flat disks and catenoidal annuli that meet along circles on the sphere. We construct these limits, among them the critical drum and the cake stand, a flat disk with a catenoidal horn. The families approach their limits like $j^{-1}$ for rings of $j$ caps, and the equatorial family approaches $4π$ with deficit $4πb^{-1}e^{-b}$. For large $b$, the leading terms of the multipole system reduce to the logarithmic energy of the cap centers and a formal evaluation gives $\barσ_1^\star(b)=8π-16π\,b^{-1}\log b+O(b^{-1})$.

papers.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
papers.abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.

papers.title: Kernel Estimates and Calderón-Zygmund Theory in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish heat and Poisson kernel estimates for $\mathfrak L=\|x\|^{2-a}Δ_k$ in the $(k,a)$-generalized Laguerre setting, where $Δ_k$ is the Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group. The heat kernel is nonnegative, symmetric, and conservative, and satisfies a Gaussian bound in the orbit distance together with polynomial decay in the distance between the transformed coordinates. The Poisson kernel, obtained by subordination, satisfies corresponding size and time-derivative estimates, while $-t\partial_t p_t$ has integral zero in each variable. Motivated by these estimates, we introduce a class of $(k,a)$-Calderón-Zygmund singular integral operators and show that $L^2_{k,a}$-boundedness implies $L^p_{k,a}$-boundedness for $1<p<\infty$, together with weak type $(1,1)$ and $L^\infty$-to-$\BMO$ estimates. Finally, we establish a $T1$ theorem characterizing the $L^2$-boundedness of such operators by the conditions $T1\in BMO$, $T^*1\in BMO$, and the weak boundedness property.

papers.title: Symmetry-reduced High-index Saddle Dynamics for Saddle Point Search under Continuous Symmetries
papers.abstract: For energy invariant under continuous symmetries, critical points may form critical manifolds, leading to degeneracy of the Hessian. In such cases, the ascent directions in high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) may include symmetry directions, making it difficult to locate saddle points of a prescribed Morse index. To address this issue, we propose symmetry-reduced HiSD (SR-HiSD) by formulating the quotient HiSD on the quotient manifold and horizontally lifting the dynamics to the ambient Hilbert space. Under suitable regularity and Morse--Bott assumptions, we establish local exponential stability of the quotient HiSD equilibria associated with the prescribed index and instability of equilibria associated with critical points of different indices. We further prove local convergence of the SR-HiSD position trajectory to a single point on the target critical orbit. Numerical algorithms with direction updates restricted to the horizontal space are developed. Numerical experiments on Morse clusters, the Onsager model, and the Landau--Brazovskii model demonstrate reliable searches for saddle points of the prescribed index and the construction of solution landscapes, together with improved computational efficiency in large-scale problems.

papers.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $ε$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

papers.title: On SQG Patches with $H^2$ Regularity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study patch solutions of the generalized surface quasi-geostrophic (gSQG) equations, which is an interpolation between the 2D Euler ($β=0$) and the surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equations ($β=1$). We establish in the SQG case, the local well-posedness for patches with $H^2$ boundaries, which improves the previous result of $H^{2+s}$, $s>0$ by Gancedo--Nguyen--Patel \cite{Gancedo2022}. Also, in the gSQG case with $0<β<1$, the uniqueness of $H^2$ patch solutions is established. Our proofs are based on the contour dynamics formulation with constant speed, introduced in \cite{Gancedo2008}.

papers.title: Eisenstein Cohomology and Critical Values of Certain \(L\)-Functions: A Root-Theoretic Combinatorial Lemma
papers.abstract: This paper gives a root-theoretic extension of the Harder--Raghuram combinatorial lemma, relating criticality of adjacent $L-$values to degrees in nilradical cohomology, to maximal parabolics $P=MU$ of connected split reductive groups with irreducible, essentially tempered cohomological inducing data. At real places, the paper classifies the maximal parabolics for which the two Kostant degrees in the boundary comparison can agree at a regular shift. For each such parabolic, an admissible shift makes both adjacent arguments critical in every Langlands--Shahidi grade exactly when both Kostant degrees equal $\dim U/2$. The classification recovers the two-block parabolics of type $A$ with even product of block sizes (Harder--Raghuram, proved by Weselmann) and the isotropic-line parabolic of type $D_{2m+1}$ for $m\ge2$ (Bhagwat--Raghuram). The only exceptional cases are $P_1$ and $P_6$ of type $E_6$. In all other cases, roots of $U$ fixed by the longest Levi Weyl element confine simultaneous criticality to a singular wall, generalizing the odd-block obstruction for $\mathrm{GL}_N$. Their number is the difference of the fundamental ranks of $M$ and $G$. When the Kostant degrees differ, as in Harder's $\mathrm{GL}_2$ setting, the paper determines which boundary degrees can still coincide. At a complex place, an admissible shift is simultaneously critical exactly when the two conjugate Levi weights after the shift occur in Kostant degrees summing to $\dim U$. With a common relative center, total degree balance at a regular admissible shift characterizes simultaneous criticality at every archimedean place. For split $E_6$ over $\mathbb Q$, a half-spin family yields Eisenstein cohomology classes in degrees $20$ and $21$, including a degree-$20$ class with nonzero restrictions to both associate boundary face types.

papers.title: Gradient Descent Achieves $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ Convergence
papers.abstract: We propose a deterministic stepsize rule for gradient descent on a lower-bounded nonconvex function with Lipschitz-continuous gradient and Hessian. Classical analysis shows that a fixed stepsize guarantees a decrease of order $\varepsilon^2/L$ per update. In contrast, our rule uses a sequence of $\mathcal{O}(m)$ updates with a total stepsize of order $m^2/L$. We establish a weighted descent inequality for every prefix of the update sequence on a quadratic objective and control the error caused by Hessian variation on a general objective. This error determines the choice $m\asymp(L^2/(ρ\varepsilon))^{1/4}$ for small $\varepsilon$. We show that gradient descent with our stepsize rule finds an $\varepsilon$-stationary point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ gradient evaluations, matching the optimal gradient-complexity guarantee.

papers.title: Zeros of the Riemann Zeta Function on the Critical Line via Bombieri and Murty-Zaharescu
papers.abstract: We provide a new proof that the Montgomery--Taylor constant is a lower bound for the proportion of zeros of the Riemann zeta function, or of any fixed Dirichlet \(L\)-function, that are simple and on the critical line. The proof is based on the papers of Bombieri and Murty--Zaharescu.

papers.title: Linear programming certificates for dimension bounds of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes
papers.abstract: We use linear programming to derive upper bounds for the dimension of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes from local geometric and arithmetic estimates. Rational certificates give the bounds $57$ for finite-volume polytopes, $17$ for compact polytopes, and $15$ for compact arithmetic polytopes. In the finite-volume case, the certificate is a weight function on incidences between vertices and two-dimensional faces. In the compact cases, the inequalities concern squared norms of orthogonal projections of a fixed tangent vector at a vertex farthest from an interior point. We give a common formulation of these linear programs, prove monotonicity in the dimension threshold, and describe the exact verification of the certificates. The local estimates are taken from the companion geometric proofs.

papers.title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
papers.abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.

papers.title: Uniform stabilization of degenerate thermoelasticity with non-autonomous conductivities
papers.abstract: We study a one-dimensional thermoelastic system with space- and time-dependent conductivity vanishing at one endpoint, under Dirichlet or zero-flux thermal conditions. Uniform comparison with the initial conductivity and local temporal regularity yield global well-posedness for energy data. A quadratic lower bound ensures uniform exponential decay for every fixed coupling $κ>0$, with constants depending only on $κ$ and uniform spatial bounds, independently of the starting time and local temporal regularity norms. This includes the critical conductivity $a=x^2$ with noncompact thermal embedding. For autonomous powers $a=x^α$ with the corresponding boundary realizations, exponential stability holds uniformly in $α$ for $0<α\le2$. For $α>2$, concentrating approximate equilibria show that the semigroup norm equals $1$ at every time and preclude uniform decay even from the generator graph domain to the energy space. Proofs combine a common-domain construction, interior-average compensation and time averaging for Dirichlet conditions, and a strict Lyapunov functional for zero-flux conditions.

papers.title: Turnpike Estimates and Limiting Behavior for $N$-Player Differential Games under Displacement Monotonicity
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behavior of open-loop Nash equilibria of $N$-player stochastic differential games with nondegenerate idiosyncratic noise, under displacement monotonicity of the costs and joint strong convexity of the Lagrangians. We prove an exponential turnpike estimate: as the remaining horizon grows, the decoupling fields of the finite-horizon Pontryagin systems converge exponentially fast to the solution of a stationary Pontryagin system, which is unique in a natural stability class, and on bounded time intervals the equilibrium states and controls converge to those generated by this solution. The limiting control is a strong open-loop equilibrium of an associated ergodic $N$-player game, and the ergodic constant $λ^{i,N}$ of each player is the same at every such equilibrium. For the finite-horizon game, the law of the equilibrium state, at times away from the initial and terminal times, is exponentially close in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$ to the invariant measure of the limiting dynamics. Finally, the equilibrium cost of player $i$ on $[t,T]$ equals $(T-t)λ^{i,N}$ plus a uniquely determined corrector, up to an error exponentially small in $T-t$.

papers.title: A General Framework for Identifying the Joint Potential Outcome Distribution through Support Restrictions
papers.abstract: Many causal estimands depend on the joint distribution of potential outcomes, which is generally not identifiable because only one potential outcome can be observed for each unit. To obtain identification, researchers often impose assumptions such as monotonicity and exclusion restriction that constrain the support of this joint distribution. For treatments and outcomes that each take finitely many values, we define a similarity matrix whose entries count, for each pair of potential outcome strata, the number of treatments yielding the same outcome. We then prove that, under unconfoundedness, identification holds if and only if this matrix is invertible, yielding a criterion directly verifiable from the support. In addition, we derive an identification formula for the joint distribution under these support restrictions and show that an average causal estimand is identifiable if and only if its integrand admits an additive representation on the restricted support. Finally, we derive sharp testable implications of the support restriction. Our results unify and generalize a broad range of identification results in the literature.

papers.title: The Descriptive Complexity of Continuous Selections with Prescribed Hausdorff dimension of the Graph
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the existence of continuous selections of set-valued functions with prescribed Hausdorff dimension of their graphs. We consider Hausdorff-continuous functions defined on the unit interval whose values are nonempty compact subsets of the real line. We prove that, for every $β\in[1,2]$, the collection of all such functions admitting a continuous selection whose graph has Hausdorff dimension $β$ is $Σ^1_1$-complete and hence is not Borel. Further, we show that this result holds even when the set-valued functions have totally disconnected values. Thus, we obtain a complete classification of the descriptive complexity of the existence problem for all possible Hausdorff dimensions of continuous graphs over the unit interval.

papers.title: Needlepoints in Quasi-Normed Orlicz Spaces and a Question of Kalton and Peck
papers.abstract: We prove that the approachable points and the needlepoints coincide in every quasi-normed Orlicz function space on the probability interval. Their common set is either $\{0\}$ or $E_Φ$. The proof gives a characterization by finite probability laws and also applies to Orlicz function spaces with the modular topology, without assuming $Δ_2$. We then construct a separable real quasi-Banach space whose approachable points form a line and whose only needlepoint is zero. Every compact convex subset of this space is relatively locally convex. The construction gives a negative answer to the question of Kalton and Peck for general quasi-Banach spaces.

papers.title: Infinite lower triangular matrices that are similar to their inverses but are not products of two involutions
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, and let $\GL_{\cf}(F)$ be the group of invertible column-finite matrices over $F$ indexed by $\bbN\times\bbN$. Denote by $\LT(F)$ (resp.\ $\UT(F)$) the subgroup consisting of lower (resp.\ upper) triangular matrices whose diagonal entries are equal to $1$. Every matrix in $\UT(F)$ is a product of two involutions. We show that, if $F$ has at least four elements, then $\LT(F)$ contains a matrix which is conjugate to its inverse by an invertible lower triangular matrix, but is not a product of two involutions in $\GL_{\cf}(F)$. The matrices can be chosen to be $4$-periodic. This gives a negative answer to a conjecture of de Seguins Pazzis.

papers.title: Mixed moment of twisted modular $L$-functions and Dirichlet $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a Hecke holomorphic cusp form for $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$. Let $q=p^γ$ be a prime power, where $p$ is an arbitrary prime and $γ\geq 2$. We establish an asymptotic formula for the mixed moment of $L(s,f\otimesχ)$ and $L(s,χ)$ on the central point. We also establish an upper bound for the smoothed sum of Hecke eigenvalues twisted by hyper-Kloosterman sums modulo powers of $2$.

papers.title: Weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to Nakao's problem in three dimensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the Duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. The estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. As an application, we study Nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. Under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces. The result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. The proof combines the new Duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.

papers.title: Modular Schur functions and Macdonald characters
papers.abstract: Modular Schur functions arose from the problem of determining the characters of simple polynomial representations of the general linear group in positive characteristic. We prove three results about these functions. (i) In finitely many variables, we obtain two bases for a space of symmetric polynomials with bounded degree in each variable, one consisting of modular Schur polynomials and the other of products of truncated complete symmetric polynomials. (ii) We determine the signs of the nonzero Schur coefficients of modular Schur functions, show that their absolute values are at most the factorial of the block weight, and characterize equality. (iii) Over an infinite field of prime characteristic, a modular Schur polynomial is a simple polynomial character exactly when its indexing partition satisfies the Carter condition, provided the number of variables is at least the degree.
