papers.title: Posterior error bounds for prior-driven balancing in linear Gaussian inverse problems
papers.abstract: In large-scale Bayesian inverse problems, it is often necessary to apply approximate forward models to reduce the cost of forward model evaluations, while controlling approximation quality. In the context of Bayesian inverse problems with linear forward models, Gaussian priors, and Gaussian noise, we use perturbation theory for inverses to bound the error in the approximate posterior mean and posterior covariance resulting from a linear approximate forward model. We then focus on the smoothing problem of inferring the initial condition of linear time-invariant dynamical systems, using finitely many partial state observations. For such problems, and for a specific model order reduction method based on balanced truncation, we show that the impulse response of a certain prior-driven system is closely related to the prior-preconditioned Hessian of the inverse problem. This reveals a novel connection between systems theory and inverse problems. We exploit this connection to prove the first a priori error bounds for system-theoretic model order reduction methods applied to smoothing problems. The bounds control the approximation error of the posterior mean and covariance in terms of the truncated Hankel singular values of the underlying system.

papers.title: Fractional Besov-Sobolev Spaces on Chord-arc Curves
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a bounded rectifiable Jordan curve with interior and exterior domains $Ω_i$ and $Ω_e$. For $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$, we study harmonic functions $u$ on either domain $Ω$ with finite weighted energy $\int_Ω|\nabla u(z)|^p \operatorname{dist}(z,Γ)^{(1-s)p-1} dA(z)$. On the unit circle, the interior and exterior trace spaces both coincide with the fractional Besov-Sobolev space $B^s_{p,p}(Γ)$. We ask which rough curves preserve this trace identity and the corresponding seminorm estimates. For radial-Lipschitz curves, we prove that both trace spaces coincide with $B^s_{p,p}(Γ)$, with equivalent seminorms, in the following ranges: $1/p-1/2\le s<1$ for $1<p<2$; $0<s<1$ for $p=2$; and $0<s\le 1/p+1/2$ for $2<p<\infty$. For arbitrary chord-arc curves, the same conclusion holds when $1/p\le s<1/2+1/(2p)$. Taking $s=1-1/p$ yields an almost-Dirichlet principle on radial-Lipschitz domains: for $4/3\le p\le 4$, the unweighted $p$-energy of the harmonic extension is bounded by a constant times that of any extension with the same boundary values. Neither endpoint can be improved over this class. We also obtain a sharp endpoint counterpart of Brennan's integrability conclusion: every Riemann map $g$ from a bounded radial-Lipschitz domain $Ω_i$ onto the unit disk satisfies $g'\in L^4(Ω_i)$, and no exponent greater than $4$ works for all such domains.

papers.title: Uniformly bounded representations of discrete measured groupoids into finite Von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{G},ν)$ be a $t$-discrete ergodic groupoid. Consider a finite Von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ with separable predual. We prove that every uniformly bounded measurable representation $ρ:\mathcal{G} \rightarrow \mathrm{GL}(\mathcal{M})$ into the invertible elements of $\mathcal{M}$ is similar to a unitary representation.

papers.title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonlinear Estimation with Convex Models
papers.abstract: A linear functional of an object from a convex symmetric set can be optimally estimated, in a worst-case sense, by a linear functional of observations made on the object. This well-known fact is extended here to a nonlinear setting: other simple functionals of the object can be optimally estimated by functionals of the observations that share a similar simple structure. This is established for the maximum of several linear functionals and even for the $\ell$th largest among them. Proving the latter requires an unusual variation of the analytical Hahn--Banach theorem. The existence results are accompanied by practical recipes relying on convex optimization to construct the desired functionals, thereby justifying the term of estimation algorithms.

papers.title: Streamfunction-vorticity formulation for incompressible viscid and inviscid flows on general surfaces
papers.abstract: This paper presents a streamfunction-vorticity formulation for the Navier--Stokes and Euler equations on general surfaces. Notably, this includes non-simply connected surfaces, on which the harmonic components of the velocity field play a fundamental role in the dynamics. By relying only on scalar and finite-dimensional quantities, our formulation ensures that the resulting methods give exactly tangential and incompressible velocity fields, while also being pressure robust. Compared to traditional methods based on velocity-pressure formulations, where one can only guarantee these structural properties by increasing the computational costs, this is a key advantage. We rigorously validate our formulation by proving its equivalence to the well understood velocity-pressure formulation under additional regularity assumptions. Furthermore, we demonstrate the applicability of the approach with numerical examples.

papers.title: Dubrovin duality for open Hurwitz flat F-manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the Dubrovin dual of a Hurwitz Frobenius manifold extends naturally to an F-manifold with compatible flat connection on the universal curve, in the sense of the open WDVV equations. A similar result is proven for the Frobenius manifold itself in arXiv:2503.09258 . This equips the universal curve with two F-manifolds with compatible flat structure, and we study their duality. We show that they combine into a bi-flat F-manifold. Conditions on open WDVV solutions imposed in previous work are retrieved in this setting, thus providing them with a geometrical meaning. Finally, explicit examples are computed. For Saito Frobenius manifolds of types $A$ and $D$, the extended prepotentials coincide with open WDVV solutions computed independently, whereas even the existence of the solution in type $E$ had not been previously discussed. On the other hand, new non-homogeneous solutions are constructed by duality.

papers.title: An improved bound on the Overfull Conjecture for graphs with small minimum degree and large maximum degree
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a simple graph with order $n$, maximum degree $Δ(G)$, minimum degree $δ(G)$, and chromatic index $χ'(G)$. A graph $G$ is called $Δ$-critical if $χ'(G)=Δ(G)+1$ and $χ'(H) < χ'(G)$ for every proper subgraph $H$ of $G$, and $G$ is overfull if $\left|E(G)\right|>Δ(G)\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$. In 1986, Chetwynd and Hilton proposed the Overfull Conjecture, which is equivalent to the following $Δ$-critical form: Every $Δ$-critical graph $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$ is overfull. The Overfull Conjecture has many implications. For example, it implies a polynomial-time algorithm for determining the chromatic index of graphs $G$ with $Δ(G) > \frac{n}{3}$, and implies several longstanding conjectures in the area of graph edge coloring. Recently, Cao, Chen, Jing, and Shan (SIAM J. Discrete Math. 2022) verified the Overfull Conjecture for $Δ$-critical graphs $G$ when $Δ(G)-\frac{7δ(G)}{4}\ge \frac{3n-17}{4}$. In this paper, we establish the required bound $Δ(G)-\frac{5δ(G)}{3}\ge\frac{2n-7}{3}$.

papers.title: On moments of the Erdős--Hooley Delta-function
papers.abstract: For integer $n\geqslant 1$ and real $u$, let $Δ(n,u):=|\{d:d\mid n,\,{\rm e}^u<d\leqslant {\rm e}^{u+1}\}|$. The Erdős--Hooley Delta-function is then defined by $Δ(n):=\max_{u\in{\mathbb R}}Δ(n,u).$ We provide new upper bounds for weighted real moments of this function.

papers.title: From n-systems to Lie and Courant algebroids
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method for constructing pure algebroids, dull algebroids, and Lie algebroids. The construction relies on what we call $n$-systems on vector bundles, and we provide explicit formulas for all resulting structure maps. Analogously, metric $n$-systems defined on metric vector bundles allow us to construct metric algebroids, pre-Courant algebroids, and Courant algebroids.

papers.title: Fast Queries of Fibered Barcodes
papers.abstract: The fibered barcode $\mathcal{F}(M)$ of a bipersistence module $M$ is the map sending each non-negatively sloped affine line $\ell \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ to the barcode of the restriction of $M$ along $\ell$. The simplicity, computability, and stability of $\mathcal{F}(M)$ make it a natural choice of invariant for data analysis applications. In an earlier preprint [arXiv:1512.00180], we introduced a framework for real-time interactive visualization of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, which allows the user to select a single line $\ell$ via a GUI and then plots the associated barcode. This visualization is a key feature of our software RIVET for the visualization and analysis of bipersistent homology. Such interactive visualization requires a framework for efficient queries of $\mathcal{F}(M)$, i.e., for quickly obtaining the barcode along a given line $\ell$. To enable such queries, we introduced a novel data structure based on planar line arrangements, called an augmented arrangement. The aim of the present paper is to give an updated and improved exposition of the parts of our preprint [arXiv:1512.00180] concerning the mathematics of the augmented arrangement and its computation. Notably, by taking the input to be a minimal presentation rather than a chain complex, we are able to substantially simplify our main algorithm and its complexity analysis.

papers.title: Lexical tableaux and quasisymmetric functions
papers.abstract: We introduce dual lexical functions, which we construct as an iterated strict-minimum restricted product on Frobenius characteristics of the trivial representation of the cyclic group induced to the symmetric group, generalizing Grinberg's construction of the dual immaculate functions. To model these combinatorially, we introduce lexical tableaux, a generalization of immaculate tableaux in which each row is lexicographically minimal among its cyclic shifts. For a fixed shape, standard lexical tableaux can be counted by a hook length formula with a q-analogue, while summing over all shapes with a fixed size and number of rows gives the (q-)Stirling numbers of the first kind. The dual lexical functions are then the generating functions of lexical tableaux, and they form a basis of the quasisymmetric functions. The dual lexical functions have a positive expansion into the fundamental basis, with coefficients counting another new family of tableaux defined by conditions on the major index values of their rows. We also introduce column-strict lexical tableaux and their respective quasisymmetric functions. We show that standard column-strict lexical tableaux are in bijection with multidimensional Kreweras-type lattice paths.

papers.title: Solving the BGK Model and Boltzmann equation by Fourier Neural Operator with conservative constraints
papers.abstract: The numerical approximation of the Boltzmann collision operator presents significant challenges because of its high dimensionality, quadratic nonlinearity, and nonlocal integral structure. In this work, we develop a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO)-based framework for learning finite time evolution operators associated with the spatially homogeneous Boltzmann equation and its simplified BGK model in different velocity space dimensions. The framework learns mappings between distribution functions in either sequence-to-sequence or point-to-point form and, once trained, enables rapid evaluation without repeated classical time evolution. To improve physical consistency, we introduce a conservative FNO (C-FNO) by augmenting the training loss with soft penalties for deviations in mass, momentum, and energy from the conservation law. Several numerical experiments are presented to demonstrate that the learned operators accurately reproduce the principal collision dynamics, while C-FNO generally reduces macroscopic drift relative to the standard FNO, highlighting its potential as a promising framework for physics-constrained operator learning in kinetic theory and other nonlinear integro-differential equations.

papers.title: A posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: This work provides reliable a posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems. The classes of systems we study are quite general, with a focus on convection-dominated problems and systems with partial diffusion. Our a posteriori error bounds are valid for a family of discontinuous Galerkin spatial discretizations and various temporal discretizations that include explicit and implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, popular tools for practical simulations of this class of problem. We prove that our estimators provide reliable upper bounds for the error of the numerical method and present numerical evidence showing that, in the convection-dominated regime, the residual quantities converge at the same rates as the discretization errors. Since one of our main interests is the convection dominant case, we also track the dependence of the estimator on the viscosity coefficient.

papers.title: Quantum Adams operations in quasimap K-theory
papers.abstract: We define quantum deformations of Adams operations in $K$-theory, in the framework of quasimap quantum $K$-theory. They provide $K$-theoretic analogs of the quantum Steenrod operations from equivariant symplectic Gromov--Witten theory. We verify the compatibility of these operations with the Kahler and equivariant $q$-difference module structures, provide sample computations via $\mathbb{Z}/k$-equivariant localization, and identify them with $p$-curvature operators of the Kahler $q$-difference connections as studied in Koroteev-Smirnov. We also formulate and verify a $K$-theoretic quantum Hikita conjecture at roots of unity, and propose an indirect algebro-geometric definition of quantum Steenrod operations.

papers.title: Timelike conjugate points in Lorentzian length spaces
papers.abstract: We study notions of conjugate points along timelike geodesics in the synthetic setting of Lorentzian (pre-)length spaces, inspired by earlier work for metric spaces by Shankar--Sormani. After preliminary considerations on convergence of timelike and causal geodesics, we introduce and compare one-sided, symmetric, unreachable and ultimate conjugate points along timelike geodesics. We show that all such notions are compatible with the usual one in the smooth (strongly causal) spacetime setting. As applications, we prove a timelike Rauch comparison theorem, as well as a result closely related to the recently established Lorentzian Cartan--Hadamard theorem by Erös--Gieger. In the appendix, we give a detailed treatment of the Fréchet distance on the space of non-stopping curves up to reparametrization, a technical tool used throughout the paper.

papers.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
papers.abstract: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.

papers.title: A Higgs category for the cluster variety of triples of flags
papers.abstract: The cluster variety of triples of flags (associated with a split simple Lie group of Dynkin type Delta) plays a key role in higher Teichmuller theory as developed by Fock-Goncharov, Jiarui Fei, Ian Le, ... and Goncharov-Shen. We refer to it as the basic triangle associated with Delta. In this paper, for simply laced Delta, we construct and study a Higgs category (in the sense of Yilin Wu) which we expect to categorify the basic triangle. This category is a certain exact dg category (in the sense of Xiaofa Chen) which is Frobenius and stably 2-Calabi-Yau. We show that it has indeed the expected cyclic group symmetry and that its derived category has the expected braid group symmetry. A key ingredient in our construction is a conjecture by Merlin Christ, whose proof occupies most of this paper. The proof is based on a new description of the Higgs category in terms of Gorenstein projective dg modules. Our techniques are in the spirit of Orlov in his work on triangulated categories of graded B-branes.

papers.title: Optimal control of SDEs with merely measurable drift: an HJB approach
papers.abstract: We investigate an optimal control problem for a diffusion whose drift and running cost are merely measurable in the state variable. Such low regularity rules out the use of Pontryagin's maximum principle and also invalidates the standard proof of the Bellman principle of optimality. We address these difficulties by analyzing the associated Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation. Working in a weak formulation of admissible controls, we first establish the state-equation solvability and Krylov estimates needed to make the control problem well defined. Using PDE techniques together with a policy iteration scheme, we prove that the HJB equation admits a unique strong solution, and this solution coincides with the value function of the control problem. Based on this identification, we establish a verification theorem and recover the Bellman optimality principle without imposing any additional smoothness assumptions. We further investigate a mollification scheme depending on a parameter $\varepsilon > 0$. It turns out that the smoothed value functions $V_{\varepsilon}$ may fail to converge to the original value function $V$ as $\varepsilon \to 0$, and we provide an explicit counterexample. To resolve this, we identify a structural condition on the control set. When the control set is countable, convergence $V_{\varepsilon} \to V$ holds locally uniformly.

papers.title: Fractional domatic number and minimum degree
papers.abstract: The domatic number of a graph $G$ is the maximum number of pairwise disjoint dominating sets of $G$. We are interested in the LP-relaxation of this parameter, which is called the fractional domatic number of $G$. We study its extremal value in the class of graphs of minimum degree $d$. The fractional domatic number of a graph of minimum degree $d$ is always at most $d+1$, and at least $(1-o(1))\, d/\ln d$ as $d\to \infty$. This is asymptotically tight even within the class of split graphs. Our main result concerns the case $d=2$; we show that, excluding $8$ exceptional graphs, the fractional domatic number of every connected graph of minimum degree (at least) $2$ is at least $5/2$. We also show that this bound cannot be improved if only finitely many graphs are excluded, even for bipartite graphs of arbitrarily large girth. This proves in a stronger sense a conjecture by Gadouleau, Harms, Mertzios, and Zamaraev (2024). This also extends and generalises results from McCuaig and Shepherd (1989), from Fujita, Kameda, and Yamashita (2000), and from Abbas, Egerstedt, Liu, Thomas, and Whalen (2016). Finally, we show that graphs of sub-exponential expansion and sufficiently large girth $g$ have fractional domatic number $3 - o_g(1)$.

papers.title: Support measures in fractal geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce two novel families of geometric functionals-basic contents and support contents-for investigating the fractal properties of compact subsets in Euclidean space. These functionals are derived from the support measures arising in connection with the general Steiner formula due to Hug, Last, and Weil, and offer new tools for extracting geometric information beyond classical fractal dimensions. The basic contents are constructed from the support measures of the set itself, while the support contents arise from those of its parallel sets. Associated scaling exponents characterize the asymptotic behavior of these measures as the resolution parameter tends to zero. We establish a fundamental connection between the maximum of the basic scaling exponents and the outer Minkowski dimension. The proof relies on the novel notion of outer box dimension. Furthermore, we explore how support contents supply aggregated information on geometric features that is provided separately by the basic contents, and how they relate to fractal curvatures and complex dimensions. Our results provide a deeper understanding of which geometric aspects actually contribute to fractal invariants such as the (outer) Minkowski content. We provide some illustrative examples.

papers.title: Hamilton cycles in pseudorandom graphs: resilience and approximate decompositions
papers.abstract: Dirac's classical theorem asserts that, for $n\ge 3$, any $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree at least $\frac{n}{2}$ is Hamiltonian. Furthermore, if we additionally assume that such graphs are regular and sufficiently large, then, by the breakthrough work of Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown, they admit a decomposition into Hamilton cycles and at most one perfect matching, solving the well-known Nash-Williams conjecture. In the pseudorandom setting, it has long been conjectured that similar results hold in much sparser graphs. We prove two overarching theorems for graphs that exclude excessively dense subgraphs, which yield asymptotically optimal resilience and Hamilton-decomposition results in sparse pseudorandom graphs. First, our results imply that for every fixed $γ>0$, there exists a constant $C>0$ such that if $G$ is a spanning subgraph of an $(n,d,λ)$-graph satisfying $δ(G)\ge\bigl(\tfrac12+γ\bigr)d$ and $ d/λ\ge C,$ then $G$ must contain a Hamilton cycle. Second, we show that for every $\varepsilon>0$, there is $C>0$ so that any $(n,d,λ)$-graph $G$ with $d/λ\ge C$ contains at least $\bigl(1-\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, and, finally, we prove that the entire edge set of $G$ can be covered by no more than $\bigl(1+\varepsilon\bigr)\tfrac d2$ such cycles. All bounds are asymptotically optimal and significantly improve earlier results on Hamiltonian resilience, packing, and covering in sparse pseudorandom graphs.

papers.title: Iwasawa Theory of Elliptic Curves in Quadratic Twist Families
papers.abstract: In this article, we use two different approaches -- one algebraic and the other analytic -- to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants of rational elliptic curves in some quadratic twist families. The analytic approach involves a thorough investigation of half-integral weight modular forms. On the other hand, the algebraic proof requires studying the BDP-Selmer groups and the fine Selmer groups.

papers.title: A full-rank subgroup of Bloch Groups of CM Fields
papers.abstract: This article generalizes the result of Burns et al (2022), to find an algorithm to find some elements generating a full-rank subgroup of the torsion-free part of Bloch group of a certain CM number field, and compute the rank of it.

papers.title: Degenerate symplectic fixed points and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between Gromov--Witten invariants and the number of fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on closed rational symplectic manifolds, without assuming nondegeneracy, via deformed Hamiltonian spectral invariants. We obtain a Hamiltonian fixed point estimate involving Gromov--Witten invariants with one point insertion under an explicit minimum-area hypothesis. We propose three conjectures about Hamiltonian fixed point estimate and prove them for every generalized flag manifold $X=G/P$ equipped with a rational Kähler form. We extend Schwarz's quantum cuplength to deformed quantum cuplength for symplectic periods and use it to obtain estimates on monotone symplectic manifolds admitting nonzero mixed Gromov--Witten invariants. We use the quantum-factorization estimate to recover the Fano toric case of Givental's symplectic fixed-point theorem. Finally, a graded spectral-carrier argument gives uniform fixed-point bounds on negatively monotone manifolds.

papers.title: A Universe with a $Δ^1_3$-definable well-order of the reals, $\mathsf{CH}$ and $Σ^1_3$-separation
papers.abstract: We construct a cardinal-preserving forcing extension of $L$ in which CH holds, the reals have a parameter-free $Δ^1_3$ well-order, and the $Σ^1_3$-separation property holds both in its boldface and in its lightface form. In this extension there is no good $Δ^1_3$ well-order of the reals, and $\Pil^1_3$-reduction and $\Pil^1_3$-uniformization fail.

papers.title: Boundedness of complements for fibered Fano threefolds in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove a canonical bundle formula for Fano type fibrations and Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements for Fano type threefold pairs $(X,B)$ with fibration structures in large characteristics. In particular, we prove the conjecture when $-(K_X+B)\not\equiv 0$ is nef and not big in large characteristics.

papers.title: Gaussian integrals on symmetric spaces (the complex case and beyond)
papers.abstract: The present work deals with Gaussian integrals on Riemannian symmetric spaces of the non-compact type. These integrals arise in statistics as well as in physics. The present work offers a systematic approach to their asymptotic behavior in the high-rank limit. First, this limit is computed explicitly in the complex case (the isometry group is a complex Lie group). To go beyond the complex case, a variational formulation is introduced, which yields the required limit as (minus) the minimum of a certain energy functional defined on the space of probability distributions on the real line. This new formulation allows for the high-rank limit to be recovered in explicit form, from the original expression found in the complex case. This two-step approach is illustrated for two classes of symmetric spaces : symmetric cones and classical symmetric domains.

papers.title: Legendrian doubles, twist spuns, and clusters
papers.abstract: Let $λ$ be a Legendrian link in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^3$, such that $L_1$, $L_2$ are two exact fillings of $λ$ and $\varphi$ is a Legendrian loop of $λ$. We study fillability and isotopy characterizations of Legendrian surfaces in standard contact $\mathbb{R}^5$ built from the above data by doubling or twist spinning; denoting them $Λ(L_1,L_2)$ or $Σ_\varphi(λ)$ respectively. In the case of doubles $Λ(L_1,L_2)$, if the sheaf moduli $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a cluster structure, we introduce the notion of mutation distance and study its relationship with the isotopy class of the Legendrian surface. For twist spuns $Σ_\varphi(λ)$, when $\mathcal{M}_1(λ)$ admits a globally foldable cluster structure, we use the existence of a $\varphi$-symmetric filling of the Legendrian link to build a cluster structure on the sheaf moduli of the twist spun by folding. We then use that to motivate, and provide evidence for, conjectures on the number of embedded exact fillings of certain twist spuns. Further, we obstruct the exact fillability of certain twist spuns by analyzing fixed points of the cyclic shift action on Grassmanians.

papers.title: Affine standard Lyndon words
papers.abstract: In this note, we establish the convexity and monotonicity for affine standard Lyndon words in all types, generalizing the $A$-type results of arXiv:2305.16299. We also derive partial results on the structure of imaginary standard Lyndon words and present a conjecture for their general form. Additionally, we provide computer code in Appendix that, in particular, allows to efficiently compute affine standard Lyndon words in exceptional types for all orders.

papers.title: Further Comments on Yablo's Construction
papers.abstract: We continue our analysis of Yablo's coding of the liar paradox by infinite acyclic graphs. The present notes are based on and continue the author's previous results on the problem. In particular, our approach is often more systematic than before. We also show a representation result, and compare to work of other authors. NOTE: IF DIAGRAMS HAVE A PROBLEM IN THE PDF VERSION, PLEASE TRY THE HTML VERSION.

papers.title: On the $\mathcal{D}^+_J$ operator on higher-dimensional almost Kähler manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth exact $J$-invariant two-form on a closed almost Kähler manifold admits a unique scalar potential, and that the associated generalized Monge-Ampère equation has at most one solution. In real dimension four, \textcolor{black}{we establish} local existence and uniqueness for nearby volume forms with the same total volume under the condition $h_J^-=b^+-1$. We also construct a nonintegrable almost Kähler four-torus and volume forms on it that cannot be realized by cohomologous $J$-compatible forms. These volume forms have the same total volume as the original volume form and can be chosen arbitrarily close to it. Finally, we relate the resulting trace potential to existing \textcolor{black}{a priori} estimates.

papers.title: Homotopy types of complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs and applications to right-angled Artin groups
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove that, given two finite connected graphs $Γ_1$ and $Γ_2$, if the two right-angled Artin groups $A(Γ_1)$ and $A(Γ_2)$ are quasi-isometric, then the infinite pointed sums $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} Γ_1^{\bowtie}$ and $\bigvee_\mathbb{N} Γ_2^{\bowtie}$ are homotopy equivalent, where $Γ_i^{\bowtie}$ denotes the simplicial complex whose vertex-set is $Γ_i$ and whose simplices are given by joins. These invariants are extracted from a study, of independent interest, of the homotopy types of several complexes of hyperplanes in quasi-median graphs (such as one-skeleta of CAT(0) cube complexes). For instance, given a quasi-median graph $X$, the \emph{crossing complex} $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is the simplicial complex whose vertices are the hyperplanes (or $θ$-classes) of $X$ and whose simplices are collections of pairwise transverse hyperplanes. When $X$ has no cut-vertex, we show that $\mathrm{Cross}^\triangle(X)$ is homotopy equivalent to the pointed sum of the links of all the vertices in the prism-completion $X^\square$ of $X$.

papers.title: Non-solvable $2$-arc-transitive covers of the Petersen graph
papers.abstract: While solvable covers of 2-arc-transitive graphs have been studied extensively, non-solvable covers have remained largely unexplored. This paper takes a first step by constructing such covers for the Petersen graph and determining their structural properties.

papers.title: Extending van der Geer and Hirzebruch's generalization of Construction A
papers.abstract: This paper discusses a generalization of Construction A and its application to root lattices of type $A_n, D_n,$ and $E_n$. While the classical Construction A provides a correspondence between binary codes and lattices, and its extension to cyclotomic fields relates $p$-ary codes to lattices over the ring of integers of $\mathbb{Q}(ζ_p)$, we further extend this framework to a broader class of even root lattices. Specifically, for a given lattice $Λ$ of type $A_n, D_n,$ or $E_n$, we define a surjective mapping $ρ$ from the dual lattice $Λ^*$ to a finite ring $R$ isomorphic to the quotient $Λ^*/Λ$. We then characterize the conditions under which the resulting lattice $(ρ^{\oplus m})^{-1}(C)$, constructed from an $R$-code $C$ of length $m$, becomes an even unimodular lattice. Furthermore, we apply our generalized Construction A to the algebraic lattices of type $D_4$ and $E_6$ realized as fractional ideals of cyclotomic fields. Consequently, we show that the theta functions associated with these lattices can be expressed via the weight enumerators of the corresponding codes, proving that they are Hilbert modular forms over totally real fields.

papers.title: Controlling discrete semilinear wave equations toward flocks
papers.abstract: We construct pointwise bounded controls that steer a finite, periodic, fully actuated active harmonic lattice with Rayleigh-Helmholtz velocity forcing to flock states in finite time. In our setting, an initial Lyapunov-feedback phase brings the velocities and elastic forces into a prescribed small neighborhood of zero. Then, subsequent trajectory planning and cancellation of the known drift achieve exact arrival at a moving flock. For prescribed stationary or moving profiles satisfying a strict control-admissibility condition, a two-stage interpolation reaches the target. We provide explicit sufficient time intervals for the stages following the initial feedback phase. Finally, we formulate the associated minimum-time problem and its formal Hamilton-Jacobi equation, leaving the continuity of the value function open.

papers.title: Well-Posedness of the Hodge Wave Equation on a Compact Manifold
papers.abstract: In this work, we study the Hodge wave equation on a compact orientable manifold. We present the necessary differential geometry language to treat Sobolev spaces of differential forms and use these tools to identify a boundary triplet for the problem. We use this boundary triplet to determine a class of boundary conditions for which the problem is well-posed.

papers.title: On Cone Restriction Estimates in Higher Dimensions
papers.abstract: We revisit the Ou-Wang's approach to the cone restriction problem via polynomial partitioning. By recasting their inductive scheme as a recursive algorithm and incorporating the nested polynomial Wolff axioms, we obtain improved bounds for cone restriction estimates in higher dimensions.

papers.title: The Gilmer-Masbaum map is not injective on the Kauffman bracket skein module
papers.abstract: Gilmer and Masbaum use Witten-Reshetikhin-Turaev (WRT) invariants to define a map from the Kauffman bracket skein module to a set of complex-valued functions defined on roots of unity in order to provide a lower bound for its dimension. We compute the image of the evaluation map for a family of mapping tori of the 2-torus and find that the restriction of the map to certain homology classes is not injective. This provides an answer to a question posed by Gilmer and Masbaum in the latter paper. Moreover, we give a basis for the Kauffman bracket skein module in the case of the mapping torus of a power of the Dehn twist along the meridian of the 2-torus.

papers.title: Syzygies of general projections of canonical and paracanonical curves
papers.abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^r$ be an integral linearly normal variety and $R=k[x_0,\cdots,x_r]$ the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^r$. It is known that the syzygies of $X$ contain some geometric information. In recent years the syzygies of non-projectively normal varieties or in other words, the projection $X'$ of $X$ away from a linear subspace $W\subset\mathbb{P}^r$, were taken into considerations. Assuming that the coordinate ring of the ambient space that $X'$ lives in is $S$, there are two types of vanishing properties of the Betti diagrams of the projected varieties, the so-called $N_{d,p}^S$ and $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$. The former one have been widely discussed for general varieties, for example by S. Kwak, Y. Choi and E. Park, while the latter one was discussed by W. Lee and E. Park for curves of very large degree. In this paper I will discuss about the $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$ properties of the projection of a generic canonical and paracanonical curve away from a generic point and in particular whether they are cut out by quadrics. Some conjectures will be claimed based on the tests on Macaulay2.

papers.title: The standard generators of the tetrahedron algebra and their look-alikes
papers.abstract: The tetrahedron algebra $\boxtimes$ is an infinite-dimensional Lie algebra defined by generators $\{x_{ij} \mid i, j \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}, i \neq j\}$ and some relations, including the Dolan-Grady relations. These twelve generators are called standard. We introduce a type of element in $\boxtimes$ that ``looks like'' a standard generator. For mutually distinct $h, i, j, k \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$, consider the standard generator $x_{ij}$ of $\boxtimes$. An element $ξ\in \boxtimes$ is called $x_{ij}$-like whenever both (i) $ξ$ commutes with $x_{ij}$; (ii) $ξ$ and $x_{hk}$ satisfy a Dolan-Grady relation. Pick mutually distinct $i,j,k \in \{0,1,2,3\}$. In our main result, we find an attractive basis for $\boxtimes$ with the property that every basis element is either $x_{ij}$-like or $x_{jk}$-like or $x_{ki}$-like. We discuss this basis from multiple points of view.

papers.title: Quickly excluding an apex-forest
papers.abstract: We give a short proof that for every apex-forest $X$ on at least two vertices, graphs excluding $X$ as a minor have layered pathwidth at most $2|V(X)|-3$. This improves upon a result by Dujmović, Eppstein, Joret, Morin, and Wood (SIDMA, 2020). Our main tool is a structural result about graphs excluding a forest as a rooted minor, which is of independent interest. We develop similar tools for treedepth and treewidth. We discuss implications for Erdős-Pósa properties of rooted models of minors in graphs.

papers.title: Classification of solutions to the energy-critical complex Ginzburg-Landau equation and application to NLS
papers.abstract: For the energy-critical complex Ginzburg--Landau equation, we establish a dichotomy between global existence and finite-time blow-up below the ground-state energy. At the threshold energy, we classify solutions and describe their dynamics in terms of the \(\dot H^1\) norm of the initial data relative to that of the ground state. These results and their application to energy-critical focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equations extend our previous work [J. Math. Pures Appl., 2026] to all dimensions \(d\ge3\) and to the ground-state energy threshold. Furthermore, we strengthen the weak--strong uniqueness result for the focusing NLS by removing the additional smallness assumption imposed in our previous work.

papers.title: The transversal game
papers.abstract: Two players take turns claiming empty cells from an $n\times n$ grid. The first player (if any) to occupy a transversal (a set of $ n $ cells having no two cells in the same row or column) is the winner. What is the outcome of the game given optimal play? Our aim in this paper is to show that for $n\ge 4$ the first player has a winning strategy. This answers a question of Erickson. We also consider variants of the game in which the family of winning transversals is restricted, both in the original game and in its Maker--Breaker version.

papers.title: Elementary first-order model checking for sparse graphs
papers.abstract: It is known that for subgraph-closed graph classes the first-order model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable if and only if the class is nowhere dense [Grohe, Kreutzer, Siebertz, 2017]. However, the dependency on the formula size is non-elementary, and in fact, this is unavoidable even for the class of all trees [Frick and Grohe, 2004]. On the other hand, it is known that the dependency is elementary for classes of bounded degree [Frick and Grohe, 2004] as well as for classes of bounded pathwidth [Lampis, 2026]. In this paper we generalise these results and almost completely characterise subgraph-closed graph classes for which the model checking problem is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size. Those are the graph classes for which there exists a number $d$ such that for every $r$, some tree of depth $d$ and size bounded by an elementary function of $r$ is avoided as an $(\le r)$-subdivision in all graphs in the class. In particular, this implies that if the class in question excludes a fixed tree as a topological minor, then first-order model checking for graphs in the class is fixed-parameter tractable with an elementary dependency on the formula size.

papers.title: Para-fusion Category and Topological Defect Lines in $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermionic CFTs
papers.abstract: We study topological defect lines (TDLs) in two-dimensional $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermoinic CFTs. Different from the bosonic case, in the 2d parafermionic CFTs, there exist parafermionic defect operators that can live on the TDLs and satisfy interesting fractional statistics. We propose a categorical description for these TDLs, dubbed as ``para-fusion category", which contains various novel features, including $\mathbb Z_M$ $q$-type objects for $M\vert N$, and parafermoinic defect operators as a type of specialized 1-morphisms of the TDLs. The para-fusion category in parafermionic CFTs can be regarded as a natural generalization of the super-fusion category for the description of TDLs in 2d fermionic CFTs. We investigate these distinguishing features in para-fusion category from both a 2d pure CFT perspective, and also a 3d anyon condensation viewpoint. In the latter approach, we introduce a generalized parafermionic anyon condensation, and use it to establish a functor from the parent fusion category for TDLs in bosonic CFTs to the para-fusion category for TDLs in the parafermionized ones. At last, we provide many examples to illustrate the properties of the proposed para-fusion category, and also give a full classification for a universal para-fusion category obtained from parafermionic condensation of Tambara-Yamagami $\mathbb Z_N$ fusion category.

papers.title: On the action of the mapping class group on the fundamental group of a surface
papers.abstract: We describe the action of the mapping class group $M(g,n)$ on the fundamental group of $S_{g,n}$, the complement of $n$ distinct points in a compact orientable surface of positive genus $g$. This is achieved by computing the image of the generators of $M(g,n)$ as outer automorphisms of the fundamental group.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous long-range percolation in the weak decay regime
papers.abstract: We study a general class of percolation models in Euclidean space including long-range percolation, scale-free percolation, the weight-dependent random connection model and several other previously investigated models. Our focus is on the weak decay regime, in which inter-cluster long-range connection probabilities fall off polynomially with small exponent, and for which we establish several structural properties. Chief among them are the continuity of the bond percolation function and the transience of infinite clusters.

papers.title: The necessity of depth for artificial neural networks to approximate certain classes of smooth and bounded functions without the curse of dimensionality
papers.abstract: In this article we study high-dimensional approximation capacities of shallow and deep artificial neural networks (ANNs) with the rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation. In particular, it is a key contribution of this work to reveal that for all $a\in\mathbb{R}$, $b\in(a,\infty)$ with $\max\{\lvert a\rvert,\lvert b\rvert\}>1$ we have that the functions $[a,b]^d\ni x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^d x_i\in\mathbb{R}$ for $d\in\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\ldots\}$ as well as the functions $[a,b]^d\ni x=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\mapsto\sin(\prod_{i=1}^d x_i)\in\mathbb{R}$ for $d\in\mathbb{N}$ can neither be approximated without the curse of dimensionality by means of shallow ANNs nor insufficiently deep ANNs with ReLU activation but can be approximated without the curse of dimensionality by sufficiently deep ANNs with ReLU activation. More specifically, we prove that in the case of shallow ReLU ANNs or deep ReLU ANNs with a fixed number of hidden layers we have that the number of ANN parameters must grow at least exponentially in the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$ while in the case of deep ReLU ANNs with the number of hidden layers growing in the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$ we have that the number of scalar real parameters of the approximating ANNs grows at most polynomially in both the inverse of the prescribed approximation accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ and the dimension $d\in\mathbb{N}$, even if the absolute values of the ANN parameters are assumed to be uniformly bounded by $1$.

papers.title: Explicit two-sided estimates and exact boundary regularity for the kinetic Fokker-Planck equation
papers.abstract: Consider the transition density $\mathrm{p}^D_t(x,y)$ of the underdamped Langevin process absorbed outside of the cylindrical domain $D:=(0,1)\times\mathbb{R}$. We prove explicit and sharp \emph{two-sided estimates} satisfied by $\mathrm{p}^D_t$ on $D\times D$. We also establish the $C^\infty$ regularity of $\mathrm{p}^D$ on $\mathbb{R}_+^*\times(\overline{D}\setminusΓ^0)\times(\overline{D}\setminusΓ^0)$ where $Γ^0$ corresponds to the grazing boundary points. It is also shown to be $(1/6,1/2)$ Hölder continuous in the $(q,p)$ coordinates in a neighborhood of $Γ^0$. Finally, the long-time asymptotics of the absorbed transition density $\mathrm{p}^D_t(x,y)$ is obtained allowing to prove the uniform conditional ergodicity of the absorbed semigroup.

papers.title: Common fixed point results in partial cone metric spaces
papers.abstract: The main aim of this paper is to study of fixed point theory in partial cone metric spaces. Infact, some common fixed point theorems for two mappings in partial cone metric spaces are obtained.

papers.title: Directed acyclic graph-type distributed ledgers via young-age preferential attachment
papers.abstract: Distributed Ledger Technologies provide a mechanism to achieve ordering among transactions that are scattered on multiple participants with no prerequisite trust relations. This mechanism is essentially based on the idea of new transactions referencing older ones in a chain structure. Recently, DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are based on directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) were proposed to increase the system scalability through sacrificing the total order of transactions. In this paper, we develop a mathematical model to study the process that governs the addition of new transactions to the DAG-type Distributed Ledger. We propose a simple model for DAG-type Distributed Ledgers that are obtained from a recursive Young-age Preferential Attachment scheme, i.e. new connections are made preferably to transactions that have not been in the system for very long. We determine the asymptotic degree structure of the resulting graph and show that a forward component of linear size arises if the edge density is chosen sufficiently large in relation to the `young-age preference' that tunes how quickly old transactions become unattractive.

papers.title: Uniformly positive correlations in the dimer model and phase transition in lattice permutations on $\mathbb{Z}^d$, $d > 2$, via reflection positivity
papers.abstract: Our first main result is that correlations between monomers in the dimer model in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ do not decay to zero when $d > 2$. This is the first rigorous result about correlations in the dimer model in dimensions greater than two and shows that the model behaves drastically differently than in two dimensions, in which case it is integrable and correlations are known to decay to zero polynomially. Such a result is implied by our more general, second main result, which states the occurrence of a phase transition in the model of lattice permutations, which is related to the quantum Bose gas. More precisely, we consider a self-avoiding walk interacting with lattice permutations and we prove that, in the regime of fully-packed loops, such a walk is `long' and the distance between its end-points grows linearly with the diameter of the box. These results follow from the derivation of a version of the infrared bound from a new general probabilistic settings, with coloured loops and walks interacting at sites and walks entering into the system from some `virtual' vertices. In dimension $d=3$ we use a transfer matrix argument to obtain a sharper infrared bound.

papers.title: Koszul duality in exact categories
papers.abstract: In this paper we establish Koszul duality-type results in the setting of chain complexes in exact categories. In particular, we prove generalisations of Vallette's Koszul duality theorem and Koszul duality along the lines of Lurie and Pridham. We also prove a connective version. We conclude with some applications. These include our main example, the category of complete bornological spaces over a Banach field, as well as a sketch of deformation theory in formal geometry.

papers.title: Universality for persistence exponents of local times of self-similar processes with stationary increments
papers.abstract: We show that $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)=(c_X+o(1))T^{-(1-H)}$, where $\ell_X$ is the local time measure at $0$ of any recurrent $H$-self-similar real-valued process $X$ with stationary increments that admits a sufficiently regular local time and $c_X$ is some constant depending only on $X$. A special case is the Gaussian setting, i.e. when the underlying process is fractional Brownian motion, in which our result settles a conjecture by Molchan [Commun. Math. Phys. 205, 97-111 (1999)] who obtained the upper bound $1-H$ on the decay exponent of $\mathbb{P} ( \ell_X(0,T] \leq 1)$. Our approach establishes a new connection between persistence probabilities and Palm theory for self-similar random measures, thereby providing a general framework which extends far beyond the Gaussian case.

papers.title: The Green function for waves on the $2$-regular Bethe lattice
papers.abstract: We compute an explicit analytic expression for the Green function of the wave operator on the $2$-regular lattice called the ``Bethe lattice'', equipped with its standard metric. In particular, we exhibit a phenomenon of abnormal speed of propagation for waves: the effective speed of propagation of energy for large time is $c_*=2\sqrt2/3<1$, and there is a true propagation at any speed $c<c_*$. We also show that the propagator at integer times has two $\ell^2$ eigenvectors, with eigenvalues $\pm1$. They are standing waves whose amplitude is halved at each generation, and they keep one third of the energy of an initial Dirac mass trapped near the source for all times.

papers.title: Sharp double logarithmic Brezis-Gallouët-Wainger inequalities in dimension four
papers.abstract: The space $H^2(\mathbb{R}^4)$ is not contained in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^4)$. For functions in $H^2_0$ of the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are also Hölder continuous of order $α$, the supremum norm can nevertheless be controlled by the $L^2$ norm of the Laplacian, at the cost of a logarithm of the Hölder seminorm. We determine the optimal leading constant in this estimate. With a double logarithmic correction, the optimal constant is $1/(8π^2α)$. With a single logarithm, the estimate holds for every larger constant and fails for $1/(8π^2α)$ itself. No symmetry assumption is made. The proof reduces the question to a biharmonic obstacle problem with an obstacle of Hölder type. Its minimizer is radial and explicit, and the sharp constant is determined by the asymptotic behaviour of the free boundary radius. We also derive versions of these inequalities on balls and on the whole space. The results are second-order analogues in dimension four of the two-dimensional inequalities of Ibrahim, Majdoub and Masmoudi.

papers.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for the First Nonzero Steklov Eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian on Weighted Surfaces with Nonnegative Bakry-Emery-Ricci Tensor
papers.abstract: We consider compact connected weighted surfaces with smooth boundary whose Bakry-Emery-Ricci tensor is nonnegative. We assume that the geodesic curvature of the boundary is bounded below in terms of the normal and tangential derivatives of the weight function. Under these assumptions, we prove a lower bound for the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue of the Witten Laplacian, which is sharp in the sense that equality holds if and only if the surface is isometric to a Euclidean disk and the weight function is constant.

papers.title: Variational Thresholds and Multiplicity for a Nonlocal r-Laplacian Logistic-Type Problem
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $λ$: \[ \begin{cases} -Δ_r u - \displaystyle\int_Ω K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +λ|u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_ΩQ(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in Ω, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partialΩ. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $λ$. For $λ\ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(λ<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehatλ^*<λ^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(λ^*<λ<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with positive energy, yielding two distinct nontrivial weak solutions. The same holds at \(λ=λ^*\), where the global minimizer has zero energy. In a left neighborhood of \(λ^*\), two distinct nontrivial weak solutions persist, a local minimizer and a mountain-pass critical point, both with positive energy and the latter at a strictly higher level. For \(λ<\widehatλ^*\), only the trivial solution exists. Finally, as $λ\to 0^-$, the norm of the global minimizers blows up. Along subsequences, selected nonnegative mountain-pass solutions converge strongly in $W_0^{1,r}(Ω)$ as $λ\to 0$ to a nontrivial nonnegative weak solution of the problem at $λ= 0$. The associated mountain-pass levels converge to the same limit from both sides of zero, and the corresponding solution norms also converge to a common value.

papers.title: Counting solutions to Euclidean Fermat equations
papers.abstract: A solution $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^3-\{(0,0,0)\}$ to a Fermat equation \begin{equation} \label{eq:abstract-gfe} Ax^a + By^b + Cz^c = 0 \end{equation} is called \emph{primitive} if $\gcd(x,y,z) = 1$. In the \emph{Euclidean} regime (that is, when the Euler characteristic $χ= \tfrac{1}{a} + \tfrac{1}{b} + \tfrac{1}{c} - 1$ is zero), the equation above defines a smooth genus one curve in a weighted projective plane. We study these models and provide an asymptotic formula for the number of primitive integral solutions with bounded height.

papers.title: Classification of fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system
papers.abstract: We study fast reaction limits for a two-component reaction-diffusion system with four reaction exponents, in which only one component diffuses. For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
papers.abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.

papers.title: Online Statistical Inference for Derivative-Free Constrained Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for nonlinear equality-constrained stochastic optimization problems in settings where derivative information is unavailable or expensive to obtain. While recent advances in stochastic sequential quadratic programming (SSQP) have enabled efficient online optimization, existing methods either rely on gradient information or suffer from high computational costs. To address these limitations, we develop a sketched derivative-free SSQP (SDF-SSQP) method that simultaneously achieves computational efficiency and valid statistical inference. By leveraging randomized sketching, the proposed method reduces the per-iteration computational cost to $O((d+m)^2)$, where $d$ is the dimension of the decision variable and $m$ is the number of constraints, making it well suited for large-scale problems. To overcome the challenges that both sketching and zeroth-order approximations introduce for statistical inference, we adopt a random-scaling approach that eliminates the need for explicit estimation of the asymptotic covariance matrix. We establish the asymptotic normality of the averaged primal--dual iterates and construct a self-normalized statistic that is asymptotically pivotal. The resulting inference procedure is fully online, requires neither covariance estimation nor matrix inversion, and incurs an additional per-iteration cost of the same order as that of the optimization update. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in terms of both optimization performance and statistical inference accuracy.

papers.title: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of $\mathrm{GL}_N$
papers.abstract: The local intertwining relation for inner forms of general linear groups over a local field asserts that the normalized intertwining operator for every parabolically induced representation arising from a local A-parameter is the identity operator. Our main theorem verifies the claim over local fields of characteristic zero. This will serve as a vital ingredient for completing the local intertwining relation and endoscopic classification for non-quasi-split unitary groups.

papers.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

papers.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
papers.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

papers.title: Equivariant Levi restriction
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group over $\bbC$, $L\subset G$ a Levi subgroup, and $\cL\subset\cG$ their Langlands duals. Macerato \cite{macerato2023leviequivariantrestrictionsphericalperverse} computed the $\cL(\calO)$-equivariant cohomology of the $!$-restriction to $\GrL$ of the regular spherical perverse sheaf on $\GrG$, and identified it with the functions on the partial Kostant--Whittaker reduction $T^*(G/U,\psiL)$, where $\psiL$ is the possibly degenerate Whittaker character of $U$ determined by $L$. We add loop rotation. Our main result is: the $\LO$-equivariant cohomology of the same object is the ring $\Dh(G/U,\psiL)$ of asymptotic $\psiL$-twisted differential operators on $G/U$. For a single $\IC_V$ the answer is the space of intertwiners $\bM_\hbar(\psiL)\to V\otimes\bM_\hbar(\psiL)$ of the universal Verma--Whittaker module. This interpolates between results of Bezrukavnikov--Finkelberg ($L=G$) and Ginzburg--Riche ($L=T$).

papers.title: A Proof of the Ovals Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the lowest eigenvalue of the periodic Schrödinger operator $-\partial_s^2+κ^2$ on a closed curve of length $\ell$ is at least $4π^2/\ell^2$. Equality holds precisely for the family of ovals described by Benguria and Loss. The proof uses a new comparison argument for scalar ordinary differential equations.

papers.title: From invasion to replacement: excursions of the Moran model
papers.abstract: An excursion-theoretic description of the continuous-time Moran model with recurrent mutation is developed. Exploiting its birth--death structure, the killed Moran process is characterized through its Green function, resolvent, Laplace transforms of hitting times, and spectral decomposition. A duality between the Moran model and a pure-death process is also established, yielding a spectral representation of its transition probabilities. The characterization of the killed process leads to a boundary-switching excursion representation in which returning excursions correspond to unsuccessful invasions of an allelic type, whilst switching excursions describe population-wide allelic replacement. The resulting regenerative structure provides the exact joint distribution and Laplace transforms for several path statistics, including the number, height and duration of unsuccessful invasions preceding replacement. Using Doob h-transforms, convergence of the rescaled Moran excursion measures and associated point processes, restricted to excursions exceeding a fixed positive height, to their Wright--Fisher counterparts is established. These transformations also show how the law of a Wright--Fisher diffusion killed upon hitting the boundary can be related to that of a Wright--Fisher diffusion with appropriately transformed mutation parameters.

papers.title: The Residual Unitary Case for Almost Elusive Groups
papers.abstract: In this short note, we remove the residual unitary family in Hall's classification of almost elusive classical groups and the corresponding conditional family in the quasiprimitive classification. Using theorems of Zsigmondy and Schinzel together with some elementary number theory arguments, we prove that if n > 4 is odd, f > 1 is even, and r is the unique primitive prime divisor of (2^f)^{2n} - 1, then 4nf divides r - 1. For n > 4 prime and any positive integer f, we deduce that a unique primitive prime divisor r of (2^f)^{2n} - 1 satisfies r > 4nf, except when (n, f, r) = (5, 1, 11). We then obtain two conjugacy classes of derangements of the same prime order in a broader family of unitary subspace actions, and a quadratic lower bound for the number of such classes in the corresponding product actions.

papers.title: Inviscid limit of steady Navier--Stokes equations with Navier friction boundary conditions in a periodic channel
papers.abstract: The vanishing viscosity limit of the steady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations is studied in a periodic channel with Navier friction boundary conditions, where the slip length is assumed to be a nonnegative power of the viscosity. Depending on this power, the problem falls into subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes. In each regime, the Navier--Stokes solutions are constructed via the Prandtl expansion, and the validity of the expansion is rigorously justified. By the Prandtl--Batchelor theory, the leading Euler solution is a Couette flow, and the interaction between the interior and boundary-layer profiles is precisely characterized. Of particular interest is the critical regime, in which the leading order Prandtl profile solves a nonlinear steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition. The well-posedness of this problem is established using the von Mises transformation and the implicit function theorem, and an implicit Batchelor--Wood formula is derived that determines the coefficients of the leading order Couette flow from the boundary data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first well-posedness result for the steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition.

papers.title: Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
papers.abstract: For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.

papers.title: Second homotopy modules and infinite homotopy stable classes of four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many closed oriented smooth 4-manifolds which are all stably diffeomorphic but pairwise not homotopy equivalent. Our examples are distinguished by their second homotopy modules, and provide the first examples which demonstrate that stable diffeomorphism does not determine the second homotopy module. They have fundamental group $(\mathbb{Z}/4)^4*\mathbb{Z}$ and arise as doubles of presentation 2-complexes. In contrast, we give criteria for isomorphism of second homotopy modules of doubles of 2-complexes, covering finite abelian, quaternion, dihedral and symmetric fundamental groups. We also establish non-injectivity of the doubling construction by showing that there exist homotopically distinct presentation 2-complexes over $Q_{28}$ whose doubles are homotopy equivalent.

papers.title: Determinant and quasi-alternateness of checkerboard colorable links
papers.abstract: We give a connected state expansion of the determinant of checkerboard colorable links and extend the notion of quasi-alternateness from classical links to this setting. We provide an obstruction to quasi-alternateness and we characterize classicality of alternating virtual links. Then, we show that quasi-alternateness is preserved under rational extensions of quasi-alternating crossings. Finally, we define the family of almost alternating virtual links. We show that extending the dealternator of an almost alternating virtual diagram of a quasi-alternating checkerboard colorable link preserves the quasi-alternateness.

papers.title: Scaling Limits of Time-averaged Distributions for Symmetric Quantum Walks on Hypercubes
papers.abstract: We study continuous-time and discrete-time quantum walks on the hypercube $\{0,1\}^d$ associated with symmetric random walks, that is, random walks whose transition probabilities depend only on the Hamming distance, using the Hamming scheme and Krawtchouk polynomials. For continuous-time walks, we show that the time-averaged distribution of the Hamming distance is a discrete arcsine law whenever the eigenvalues are distinct. For discrete-time walks, exact formulas for the time-averaged distribution are known as combinatorial sums or as mixtures involving Krawtchouk polynomials, but their scaling limits as $d\to\infty$ (time average first) have not been specified. We obtain them explicitly for three random walks: the simple random walk (an arcsine law), the random walk with binomial weights (an equal mixture of arcsine laws with different supports), and the independent random walk (atoms of mass $1/2$ at $0$ and at $1/2$). Comparing with the continuous-time limits, the two models agree for the simple random walk but differ for the other two, so the correspondence between them is not universal.

papers.title: Sampling Error in Time-Discretized Stochastic Optimal Control
papers.abstract: We study sampling error for Euler discretizations of stochastic optimal control problems driven by Brownian motion. For ordinary Monte Carlo sampling, the error can diverge under time refinement when empirical-mean fluctuations accumulate as bias. Under global Lipschitz assumptions and a bounded noise coefficient, we derive finite-sample bounds for the value-function error without assuming smooth value functions or independence across sampling batches. The bounds isolate the empirical-mean contribution. For convergence under time refinement, ordinary Monte Carlo generally requires the number of samples per stage to grow at a faster rate than the number of intervals in the time mesh, whereas antithetic and recentered sampling eliminate the empirical-mean term and yield error bounds uniform over meshes with a fixed sample size per stage. We establish lower bounds showing that the ordinary and antithetic sampling terms are attained. We also prove sample-size convergence for all three methods on fixed meshes. For antithetic and recentered sampling, convergence is uniform over meshes in every noise dimension, with sharp sample-size rates in dimensions at least three.

papers.title: A Kernel Framework for Linear Operator Equations
papers.abstract: Solving linear operator equations with nonlocal terms or heterogeneous constraints often requires specific numerical schemes. We develop a unified approach based on embedding such equations into a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Differential, boundary, and integral operators are represented by their Riesz representers in the RKHS. The equations are solved in the regularized least-squares sense at finitely many collocation points. The solution is a finite linear combination of operator-induced representers and is obtained from a single linear system. Its sensitivities, such as financial Greeks, follow by direct differentiation. To reduce the computational cost for large collocation sets, we introduce a Nyström approximation based on subsampling the operator-induced representers. It yields the best approximation of this solution within the reduced trial space, in a regularized empirical norm. Numerical examples cover ordinary, partial, and partial integro-differential equations, including multi-asset and jump-diffusion option pricing.

papers.title: Two-Sided Weighted-History Transfer for Abstract Systems with Infinite Memory
papers.abstract: We prove a two-sided transfer principle for second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory. The squared norm of the coupled semigroup, from a centered weighted-history space into the energy space, is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $ρ_w(t)$. Here $ρ_w(t)$ is the squared norm of the right-translation semigroup between the corresponding weighted and unweighted memory spaces. The coupled system satisfies an energy identity, a mechanical multiplier estimate and a bounded observation. The memory density has decay of order at most polynomial, and the weight is admissible. Under these hypotheses the energy is bounded by the initial norm times $κ(t)+ρ_w(t)$, where $κ$ is the tail of the kernel. The two-sided equivalence holds when $ρ_w$ is integrable and the kernel has a finite first moment and satisfies a tail bound, or when $κ\le C_κρ_w$. For the density $pb(1+s)^{-p-1}$, with $p>1$ and $b>0$, and the weight $(1+s)^{2θ}$, with $θ>0$, the rate is $(1+t)^{-\min\{2θ,p+1\}}$. For kernels and weights with logarithmic factors, under explicit conditions on the exponents, the logarithm of the weight enters the rate below the saturation threshold, and the logarithm of the kernel enters above it. A theorem with a prescribed decay of the inherited history gives exact exponents for algebraically growing histories. The hypotheses are verified for gradient-memory waves without instantaneous damping, endpoint-damped strings, damped plates and oscillators.

papers.title: On the existence of PMC hypersurfaces in complete manifolds of finite volume
papers.abstract: Let $M^{n+1}$, $n+1\geq 3$, be a complete Riemannian manifold of finite volume, and suppose that $h\in C^{\infty}(M) \cap L^1(M)$ has the property that the width of $M$ \wrt\ the $\mathcal{A}^h$ functional, $W^h(M)$, is positive. Then there exists a hypersurface $Σ\subset M$ with prescribed mean curvature $h$, satisfying $0<\mathcal{H}^n(Σ)<\infty$. Furthermore, $Σ$ is a closed subset of $M$ and it is smooth and almost embedded outside a singular set of Hausdorff dimension $\leq n-7$. The condition $W^h(M)>0$ is satisfied if $\|h\|_{L^1(M)}< W(M)$ (where $W(M)$ is the width of $M$ with respect to the area functional) or $\|h\|_{L^\infty(M)}< [\mathscr{I}]_0$ (where $\mathscr{I}$ is the isoperimetric profile of $M$ and $[\mathscr{I}]_0:=\sup_{v>0} \frac{\mathscr{I}(v)}{v}$).

papers.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
papers.abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $τ$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,τ}-(F,S(τ)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

papers.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.

papers.title: Major progress on hamiltonian saturation in hypergraphs
papers.abstract: For $1\leq \ell< k$, an \emph{$\ell$-overlapping $k$-cycle} is a $k$-uniform hypergraph in which, for some cyclic vertex ordering, every edge consists of $k$ consecutive vertices and every two consecutive edges share exactly $\ell$ vertices. A $k$-uniform hypergraph $H$ is $\ell$-\emph{hamiltonian saturated} if $H$ does not contain an $\ell$-overlapping Hamilton $k$-cycle but every hypergraph obtained from $H$ by adding a new edge does contain such a cycle. For $n$ divisible by $k-\ell$, let sat$(n,k,\ell)$ be the smallest number of edges in an $\ell$-hamiltonian saturated $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. In the case of graphs Clark and Entringer showed in 1983 that, for sufficiently large $n$, sat$(n,2,1)=\lceil \frac{3n}2\rceil$. By ad hoc methods, the present authors proved previously that sat$(n,k,\ell)=Θ(n^{\ell})$ for some rather narrow and scattered ranges of $\ell$. In this paper we present a unified proof of this equality for all $k$ and $\ell>k/2$.

papers.title: Service location flexibility in dynamic vehicle routing
papers.abstract: Parcel lockers and delivery robots let a vehicle serve customers at nearby locations. We study this service location flexibility in the dynamic traveling repairman problem, where a single vehicle may serve each demand anywhere within a radius $r$ of its location. Arrivals form a Poisson process, demand locations are independent and uniform in the unit square, and on-site service times are i.i.d. with uniformly bounded second moments, where the radius $r$ may vary across systems as the on-site load $ρ$ tends to one.
