Under official voluntary-draw rules with unrestricted legal choices, however, the existence of a finite play is decidable (and primitive recursive) via reachability in fixed-dimension vector addition systems with states (VASS). Finally, the maximal duration of a finite greedy play has no total computable upper bound in the input length.

papers.title: Superpotentials for F-manifolds and bi-flat F-structures on the orbit spaces of reflection groups
papers.abstract: We extend Dubrovin's construction of a superpotential from Frobenius manifolds to biflat F-manifolds. The key step in this extension is choosing a flat coordinate of one of the connections studied in [11] and invert this coordinate with respect to the spectral parameter and the construction does not require an invariant metric. Suppose that the manifold has dimension n and that the superpotential admits a holomorphic continuation to n simple critical points with distinct critical values. These values give canonical coordinates, and the residue formulas recover both the product and the flat connection from the superpotential alone. Conversely, under suitable nondegeneracy conditions, a solution of the superpotential equations for a given product defines a biflat F-manifold. For $B_n$ and $G(m,1,n)$ we obtain the whole family of biflat structures from a polynomial superpotential by varying a twisted primary differential. For $G(m,m,n)$ we obtain the natural biflat structure from a Laurent superpotential. Keeping the Laurent polynomial fixed and varying the primary differential gives a new family of flat F-manifolds depending on one parameter. We use the superpotential and the poles of the dual product along the reflecting hyperplanes to prove the conjecture we formulated in [8] for irreducible Coxeter groups and in [10] for well generated complex reflection groups. The conjecture concerns biflat F-structures whose dual connection has the form studied by Dunkl and Kohno. When the reflecting hyperplanes form a single orbit, we identify the biflat structure associated with the flat structure of [24,25,27]. We obtain the remaining families from the polynomial construction for $G(m,1,n)$ and an explicit computation for $F_4$. In every case the first flat structure extends polynomially to the whole quotient, and the biflat structure is defined on the complement of the reflection discriminant.

papers.title: Counting Eulerian Orientations in Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a pseudograph, and let $\varepsilon(G)$ denote the number of Eulerian orientations of $G$. Lieb and Wu, and later Schrijver, showed that if $G$ has degree sequence $(d_1,d_2,\dots,d_n)$, where each $d_i$ is a positive even integer, then \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \prod_{i = 1}^n 2^{-d_i/2} \binom{d_i}{d_i/2}.\] Schrijver conjectured that for simple $d$-regular graphs, $\varepsilon(G)\leq\varepsilon(K_{d+1})^{n/(d+1)}$, with equality attained by disjoint unions of cliques of order $d+1$. In this paper, we prove a multigraph bound that implies the known case $d=4$, and we also improve Schrijver's lower bound for $d$-regular graphs, using an inductive relation between $\varepsilon(G)$ and the number $\ell_i(G)$ of cycles of each possible length $i \geq 1$ in $G$. We define \[ \ell(G) = \sum_{i = 1}^n \frac{\ell_i(G)}{(d - 1)^i}\] and we prove with $λ= (d - 1)\log(1 + 1/(d - 1))$ that for all $d \geq 2$, \[ \varepsilon(G) \geq \exp(λ\ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n),\] where $S_d(n)$ denotes $2^{-dn/2}\binom{d}{d/2}^n$. The bound sharply improves the lower bound of Lieb, Wu and Schrijver, and gives good estimates for $\varepsilon(G)$ for various graphs, such as integer lattices. The bound is almost tight for random regular graphs, and we conjecture for each even $d \geq 4$ that there exists a constant $c_d > 0$ such that $\varepsilon(G) \leq \exp(c_dλ\ell(G)) \cdot S_d(n)$ for every $n$-vertex $d$-regular pseudograph.

papers.title: Continuous-Time LQR from a Single Discrete-Time Off-Policy Batch
papers.abstract: We study discounted continuous-time linear--quadratic regulation (LQR) with unknown drift parameters and additive noise, using a single batch of discrete-time off-policy transitions. Discrete-time methods target a policy tied to the training interval, while shortening this interval can make learning from finite data more sensitive to noise. Learning an accurate continuous-time controller therefore requires balancing discretization and finite-sample errors while preserving stability throughout policy improvement. We develop a drift-only policy iteration algorithm, termed PhiBE-PI, using one quadratic state--action critic for policy evaluation and explicit greedy improvement. Reusing the batch makes later policies depend on the data. Exploiting the quadratic structure of LQR, we show that the data enter every policy evaluation only through one policy-independent empirical matrix, so a single high-probability bound controls all iterates. For sufficiently large discount~$β$, small observation intervals, and a sufficiently large batch, we prove that all iterates are stabilizing for the discounted problem and converge quadratically to a data-dependent fixed point. The gain bound separates iteration, finite-sample, and discretization errors. In this regime, the finite-sample and discretization terms scale as $1/(β\sqrt{nΔt})$ and $Δt/β$, respectively. The bounds thus reveal a tradeoff: at a fixed batch size, finer observations reduce discretization error but increase finite-sample error. Because PhiBE-PI approximates the continuous-time optimal gain rather than a discrete-time one, its policy can remain near-optimal when deployed at faster control rates. Experiments confirm this advantage over discrete-time Bellman-equation baselines when the observation interval is small relative to the system's time scale.

papers.title: Unary maps are restrictions of linear maps and $k$-ary maps are restrictions of homogeneous maps
papers.abstract: We study maps on a finite set $S$ under renaming elements of $S$ and extending $S$. We show that every unary map is linear and every $k$-ary map is homogeneous with respect to such renamings and embeddings.

papers.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
papers.abstract: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.

papers.title: Accurate rank-controlled step-truncation methods for matrix differential equations
papers.abstract: A class of explicit time stepping schemes is introduced for the integration of matrix differential equations in low-rank format. These schemes combine explicit Runge-Kutta time stepping with rank-adaptive recompressions. For suitably chosen truncation thresholds, they converge at arbitrary order, while having close to optimal ranks, without any prior assumptions on the best approximation ranks. The ranks of the scheme also necessarily depend on the time step, as shown by counterexamples. A numerical experiment illustrates the advantages and performance of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: Leray's Problem for the Stationary Navier-Stokes Equations with Low-Regularity Data in Planar and Three-Dimensional Axisymmetric Lipschitz Domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the steady Navier-Stokes Dirichlet problem in bounded planar and three-dimensional axisymmetric domains with finitely many disjoint Lipschitz boundary components. For prescribed velocities in $H^{1/2}(\partialΩ)$ and forces in the dual of the solenoidal energy space $V=H_0^1(\operatorname{div}0,Ω)$, we establish finite-energy solvability under the sole compatibility condition of zero total boundary flux. Individual component fluxes are subject to no smallness or sign restrictions. In three dimensions the domain and data are axisymmetric, and swirl is allowed. The result addresses the regularity of the domain and data within these two geometric classes. The proof combines Leray-Schauder continuation with pressure compactness on Lipschitz boundary collars and a total-head level-set argument. Continuation of the limiting Euler fields through complementary components supplies separating cycles, while viscous identities are evaluated inside the physical domain. A nonlinear correction of smooth force approximations controls the volume and surface errors in the passage to energy-dual data. An isometric extension from $V'$ to $H^{-1}$ preserves the prescribed symmetries and fixes the force representative used in the compactness argument. For each selected $H^{-1}$ representative, the resulting velocity admits an associated mean-zero $L^2$ pressure; the velocity equation depends only on the force class modulo gradients.

papers.title: Around the base ideal and the base locus of a Keller map
papers.abstract: Let $\varphi_F:\Bbbk^n\to\Bbbk^n$ be a Keller map defined by $n$ polynomials $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ in $n$ indeterminates $X=X_1,\ldots,X_n$ over a field $\Bbbk$ of characteristic zero. Miranda-Neto defined the base ideal of $\varphi_F$ as the ideal $I_F$ generated by $F_1,\ldots,F_n$ and the base locus of $\varphi_F$ as the affine algebraic set $V_F=V(I_F)$ determined by the ideal $I_F$. He proved that $I_F$ is a radical ideal, which is a finite intersection of $v_F$ maximal ideals, where ${\rm card}(V_F)\leq v_F$, understanding that $v_F=0$, when $I_F$ is improper. In this paper, we first prove that $v_F\leq \dim_{\Bbbk}(\Bbbk[X]/I_F)\leq [\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$. Using invertible affine transformations on the recent counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture announced by Alpöge, we show that $I_F$ might indeed be improper and that the following cases, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)=v_F=[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$, $0<{\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ and $0={\rm card}(V_F)<v_F<[\Bbbk(X):\Bbbk(F)]$ might occur. We finish by giving a purely topological equivalent reformulation of the Jacobian Conjecture in terms of the irreducibility of $V_F$.

papers.title: A high-dimensional perspective of assortative mating: definition, dynamics, and limiting results
papers.abstract: Assortative mating, or the systematic (dis)similarity of traits between mate pairs, has wide-ranging consequences. Chiefly, it modulates genetic variance in offspring due to the coupling of inherited trait-associated loci in parents. Over many generations, this buildup becomes appreciable at the trait level and may confound statistical genetics techniques, such as association analyses and heritability estimation. Theoretical characterisations of this effect are well-developed in the univariate case, where mates assort on a single trait pair. However, empirical studies increasingly show that assortment is not only multivariate, but high-dimensional, in that the correlation structure exhibited between mates cannot be represented by a single or few linear combinations of the constituent traits. In spite of this, the mathematical theory of assortment has not scaled with awareness of this fact. In this paper such a generalisation is developed. We begin by deriving sufficient conditions under which an estimator is invariant to assortment, followed by studying existence conditions and limiting behaviour of equilibria under assortment. Finally, univariate results involving trait heritability and consanguineal genetic correlation are generalised to the multivariate regime.

papers.title: Qualitative WALA, Alberti representations and Lipschitz differentiability
papers.abstract: We show that the existing theory of Lipschitz differentiability spaces implies that a metric measure space satisfying a qualitative analogue of the WALA condition of David--Semmes has many independent Alberti representations, and provides conditions for when such a space is rectifiable.

papers.title: Analytical modelling of compliance dynamics under fiscal feedback: tipping thresholds, intervention costs and hysteresis
papers.abstract: Compliance with taxes and other collective obligations is often enforced with resources that come from those who comply, so that non-compliance erodes its own deterrent. We develop an exactly solvable dynamical model of compliance under this fiscal feedback. Individuals choose between paying and evading by imitating those who do better, and the budget against evasion is a share of the revenue, split between enforcement and education. The model yields closed-form expressions for the equilibria, the tipping thresholds and their bifurcations, the budgets needed to maintain compliance and to restore it after a collapse, and the recovery time near the threshold. Fiscal feedback alone does not produce tipping points: hysteresis appears only when an instrument that changes individual incentives, such as fines or education, is funded by the tax base. Stronger sanctions reduce both the maintenance and the rescue budget, but beyond a critical level they make the system bistable, so that the choice of sanction is a trade-off between efficiency and resilience, which we quantify with a resilience indicator and a resilience-constrained design problem. The cheapest allocation of the budget between enforcement and education is also obtained in closed form. A sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that control prevention and recovery costs, and stochastic simulations of individual agents and a slow budget cycle confirm the analytical predictions. The framework provides quantitative guidelines for allocating scarce intervention resources in tax compliance and in other enforcement problems with similar feedbacks.

papers.title: Distinct Distances under Well-behaved Norms
papers.abstract: We improve our understanding of the Erdos' distinct distances problem under non-Euclidean norms, in two ways: (i) For norms that are definable in an o-minimal structure and whose non-line bisectors have a finite intersection, we obtain a lower bound of \(Ω(n^{5/6})\) for the minimum number of distinct distances. In particular, this improves the current best bound of \(Ω(n^{4/5})\) for all \(\ell_{p}\) norms with non-integer \(p > 1\). (ii) We derive the stronger bound \(Ω(n^{6/7-ε})\) under all semi-algebraic smooth norms. Our proof technique is based on deriving properties of bisectors under various norms.

papers.title: Model order reduction for space-time DPG approximations of the Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: This work extends the ultraweak space-time discontinuous Petrov-Galerkin (DPG) method for the linear time-dependent Schrödinger equation, introduced in [Demkowicz, Gopalakrishnan et al., SINUM 2017], from the free equation to bounded, time-independent, real-valued potentials. Continuous well-posedness is established in the graph norms with a potential-independent inf-sup constant. The potential is parametrized and the discretization is combined with model order reduction. To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first explicit coupling of the DPG methodology with reduced basis methods. Uniform well-posedness with respect to parameter-independent reference norms is proven and yields exponential decay of the Kolmogorov $N$-widths. Moreover, the distinctive structural features of this combination are discussed, in particular the parameter dependence of the optimal test spaces and norms, and the built-in residual-based error control of the DPG framework, which drives a greedy reduced basis construction. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension for both parameter-independent and parametrized potentials support the theoretical results and demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the resulting reduced-order models.

papers.title: Termination of the Kahler MMP with scaling
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove termination of klt flips with scaling for strongly \(\mathbb Q\)-factorial compact Kahler klt pairs $(X,B)$ with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary. In particular, compact Kahler klt pairs with effective \(\mathbb Q\)-boundary have minimal models when \(K_X+B\) is pseudo-effective, and admit Mori fibre space models otherwise.

papers.title: Gowers-uniform sets with few arithmetic progressions
papers.abstract: For each fixed $s\geq 2$, we construct sparse sets $A\subset \mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ such that the normalized indicator function $ν_A$ of $A$ satisfies $\|ν_A-1\|_{U^s}=o(1)$, while the number of three-term arithmetic progressions in $A$ is $o(|A|^3/N)$. This answers the counting form of a question of Gowers and Green, as formulated by Conlon, Fox and Zhao, on the pseudorandomness hypotheses needed in a relative Szemerédi theorem.

papers.title: Universal Implications Among $k$-Prime Graph Labelings
papers.abstract: For $k\ge1$, let $\mathcal P_k$ be the class of graphs admitting a bijective labeling by consecutive integers beginning at $k$, with coprime labels at adjacent vertices. We determine all universal inclusions between distinct such classes: $\mathcal P_i\subseteq\mathcal P_j$ holds for $i\ne j$ if and only if $(i,j)=(2,1)$ or $(3,1)$. In particular, the classes are pairwise distinct. The proof translates universal inclusion into a spanning-embedding question for coprimality graphs on consecutive integer intervals. Edge-count identities, arithmetic-progression estimates, and prime-residue switching exclude all other inclusions; a prime-gap argument reduces the remaining finite range to fifteen explicit rational inequalities. We further show that, for each nonexceptional ordered pair, the graph orders at which edge counts obstruct inclusion have a positive natural density. This density is described through a limiting distribution of correlated Euler products, for which we give an atomlessness argument. The classification resolves the distinct-index formulation of the universal-implication conjecture.

papers.title: Blocks of profinite group algebras and the extended Brauer correspondence
papers.abstract: We describe the centre of the completed group algebra of a profinite group and prove a generalisation of Brauer's Extended First Main Theorem to profinite groups.

papers.title: Scaled Relative Graph Separation for Unbounded Nonlinear Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate stability analysis of one-channel nonlinear feedback systems based on the recent notion of scaled relative graph (SRG). Our focus is on the SRG separation in the complex plane for feedback stability analysis that involves possibly unbounded open-loop nonlinear systems. Subject to a technical assumption, a homotopy-based SRG separation theorem is developed as the main result, where the incremental directed gap is utilized as a key instrument to quantify robust feedback stability along the homotopy path. Doing so enables us to incorporate commonly used integrators as unbounded systems in the SRG-based framework. Specializations of the main result to linear systems, along with illustrative examples, are also provided to demonstrate its effectiveness.

papers.title: Directed Hypergraphs: Tensor Representation, Embedding Modeling, and Community Detection
papers.abstract: Directed hypergraphs, in which each hyperedge connects a set of tail nodes to a set of head nodes, are the natural representation for many-to-many interactions in citation networks, metabolic pathways, and group communications. Despite their broad applicability, community detection for directed hypergraphs remains statistically underdeveloped: most existing methods either collapse hyperedges into pairwise edges, treat the two sides as interchangeable, or require the number of communities to be known. We propose a statistical framework for simultaneous embedding and community detection in nonuniform directed hypergraphs. The method allows each node to have distinct roles as a source and as a target, accommodates varying hyperedge sizes, and automatically determines the unknown numbers of communities on both sides, which need not be equal, through a fusion-penalized likelihood. We establish consistency of the estimated numbers of communities, exact recovery of both membership structures, and consistent probability tensor estimation. We further show that exact recovery is attainable without knowing the numbers of communities by a procedure that does not rely on any particular local solution, and we complement the upper bounds with a minimax lower bound for probability tensor estimation and a necessary condition for exact recovery. To ground the methodology, we construct the Cross-Statistics Citation Network, a new large-scale corpus linking Statistics with Biology, Computer Science, and Economics. Applying our method to this corpus reveals source and target roles of author communities in cross-field knowledge flow, and a pairwise representation of the same citations partly merges these roles.

papers.title: Inverse spectra and Wilson traces of $SU(2)$ connections on finite graphs
papers.abstract: We study a fixed $SU(2)$ connection on a known finite labelled simple graph through its full Laplacian spectra with independently variable positive edge weights. This family is equivalent to all vertex-simple cycle traces. For connected graphs, it determines every vertex gauge class exactly for trees and graphs with a single cyclic block that is a cycle, a theta graph, or a subdivision of a simple three-vertex-connected cubic graph. For arbitrary graphs, we describe the full fibers, including degenerate connections, and give criteria for generic uniqueness and Wilson observability under restricted edge controls.

papers.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
papers.abstract: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,α}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $α\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,α}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,α}$ is of class $C^{k+1,α}$.

papers.title: The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for CM elliptic curves of analytic rank one
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer formula for elliptic curves over the field of rational numbers with complex multiplication and analytic rank one.

papers.title: Group Buying through Bankruptcy Rules: Cost Sharing and Endogenous Pricing
papers.abstract: Group buying allows independent buyers to pool their demand and benefit from quantity discounts that would not be available to them individually. While collective purchasing reduces total procurement costs, it raises a fundamental allocation question: how should the resulting savings be distributed among heterogeneous buyers? We address this question by integrating cost-allocation and bankruptcy approaches into a unified group-buying framework. Starting from a continuous quantity discount function, we examine cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and develop an endogenous pricing representation in which each buyer's effective discount may depend on the demand profile of the entire group. We then establish a connection between group buying and bankruptcy theory by interpreting the aggregate savings from cooperation as the estate and each buyer's potential savings as its claim. This formulation allows us to derive cost-allocation mechanisms based on the proportional, constrained equal awards, constrained equal losses, and Talmud rules. For each rule, we obtain the corresponding buyer-specific price function and characterize the associated variable discount factor. We further examine the relationships between bankruptcy-based and cost-gap-based allocation mechanisms and use a numerical example with simulated data to compare their implications. The proposed framework links alternative fairness principles for allocating cooperative savings to economically interpretable pricing mechanisms, providing a unified basis for analyzing how group purchasing gains are distributed among heterogeneous buyers.

papers.title: Support functions of sections of $p$-minimal tubes
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact $p$-minimal hypersurface in ${\mathbb R}^{n+1}$ with boundary in two parallel hyperplanes. We study the convex hulls $Ω(τ)$ of its horizontal sections through their support function $H(τ,\cdot)$, without any assumption on the topology of $M$. We prove that $H$ is a viscosity subsolution of a degenerate elliptic inequality. For $n=2$ it is of Monge--Ampère type, and its equality case for minimal surfaces with circular sections is Riemann's system. A posteriori, $H$ is locally semiconvex and every hull is a smooth convex body; the inequality then also holds in the sense of measures, with the edges of the hulls appearing as atoms of Alexandrov's area functions. Averaging over directions gives a catenary-type inequality for the mean width of the hulls. It yields lifetime bounds for $p$-minimal tubes when $n>p$. For minimal surfaces in ${\mathbb R}^3$ it gives a sharp bound for the distance between the planes in terms of the perimeters of the hulls of the boundary curves, with equality only for a catenoid. For one convex curve in each plane this recovers, by a different method, the nonexistence and rigidity theorem of Bernstein and Breiner. The bound extends to non-convex curves and to boundaries with several components. Finally, we show that the Meeks annulus conjecture is equivalent to the absence of atoms in the area functions of the hulls of all intermediate sections.

papers.title: Fast growth of periodic orbits, translated points and short Floer bars for contactomorphisms
papers.abstract: We establish arbitrarily fast growth of distinct periodic orbits and geometrically distinct translated points for contactomorphisms of the unit cotangent bundle of a closed hyperbolic surface. The conclusions hold on residual subsets of a nonempty $C^1$-open set and follow from Chaidez's contact blender and localized contact perturbations. For a specified analytically admissible normalized Rabinowitz Floer family on a closed contact manifold with Liouville filling, we bound fixed-window barcode entropy by topological entropy. The proof compares long-bar counts with graph volume through contact tomography and filtered continuation. Under strong translated nondegeneracy, we show that super-exponential translated-pair growth in a compact interior window forces super-exponential growth of short bars born in the surrounding window.

papers.title: Hilbert measures of non-coregular representations of the circle and orthogonal groups
papers.abstract: We give explicit constructions of the Hilbert measure, which transports the integral of an invariant smooth function from a representation to the image of the Hilbert embedding, for certain representations of the circle, orthogonal, and special orthogonal groups that are non-coregular, meaning that the algebra of invariants is not a polynomial algebra. These include all $4$-dimension real circle representations, a family of $6$-dimensional circle representations, and $k$ copies of the defining representations of the orthogonal and special orthogonal groups when $k$ is large enough that the representation is not coregular. For the circle representations, we also construct the Hilbert measure on the singular symplectic quotient at level zero.

papers.title: Subshifts of finite type and parameter density for intermediate \(-β\)-transformations
papers.abstract: We study the subshifts \(Ω_{-β,α}\) associated with the intermediate \(-β\)-transformations \(x\mapsto-βx+α\pmod1\), where \((β,α)\inΔ_-:=\{(b,a):1<b<2,\ b-1<a<1\}\). We prove that $Ω_{-β,α}$ is of finite type if and only if both endpoints of \([0,1]\) reach the discontinuity \(c_{β,α}=α/β\). We also prove that the set of parameters \((β,α)\) for which \(Ω_{-β,α}\) is a subshift of finite type is dense in \(Δ_-\). The approximating parameters can be chosen so that both kneading invariants converge to those of the original map.

papers.title: A symplectic Hilbert hotel
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth global symplectomorphism of an infinite dimensional separable Hilbert space mapping a ball of large radius to a subset of a cylinder of small radius. This symplectomorphism and its inverse map bounded sets to bounded sets. This example shows that Gromov's non-squeezing theorem does not generalize to infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces without further assumptions.

papers.title: Dyadic Representation of Fractional Integrals on Spaces of Homogeneous Type and Related Boundedness Phenomena
papers.abstract: We establish a dyadic representation formula for fractional integral operators in the setting of spaces of homogeneous type. The formula expresses such operators in terms of simpler dyadic model operators, such as so-called paraproducts and shifts, and provides a unified framework that applies to different notions of fractional integrals arising in this general context. Motivated by the derivation of this representation, we also investigate the structure of fractional integral operators in spaces of homogeneous type. In this setting, two natural definitions, referred to as volumic and metric, are in general non-equivalent and exhibit markedly different boundedness properties. While the former enjoys well-known $L^p$--$L^q$ estimates, the latter may fail to satisfy any such bounds without additional assumptions; nevertheless, weaker forms of boundedness can still be recovered under suitable conditions. The representation formula is intended as a tool for the study of Schatten-type properties of commutators $[b,T]$ of fractional integrals and pointwise multipliers, which will be addressed in a forthcoming companion work by T. Hytönen and the author. Beyond this application, the representation itself may be of independent interest and useful in other contexts.

papers.title: Mixing time and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for the torus shuffle
papers.abstract: The torus shuffle acts on an $n\times n$ board of $n^2$ cards: each step chooses a row or a column uniformly at random and rotates it cyclically by one unit in a uniformly chosen direction. We prove that the half-lazy version of this chain has total variation mixing time of order $n^3\log n$ and logarithmic Sobolev constant of order $n^{-3}$ on each communicating class. The order of the mixing time is the one conjectured by Diaconis. The proof of the upper bound has two steps. First, the entropy of a function on the board is at most a constant times $n$ times its mean loss when a single row or column is completely rearranged. Second, this mean loss is at most a constant times $n^2$ times the Dirichlet form of the shuffle. The second step bisects each line recursively and charges the cost of a column rotation only to the intervals that contain the column, so that the costs over all scales add up without a logarithmic factor. A Fourier observable gives the matching lower bound on the mixing time.

papers.title: An example of a non-commutative division ring with abelian maximal subgroups
papers.abstract: We construct a cyclic division algebra $D$ of degree $6$ with center $F$ algebraic over $\Q$. The multiplicative group $K^\times$ of a maximal subfield $K$ is maximal in $D^\times$, disproving Conjecture~C of Akbari, Ebrahimian, Momenaee Kermani, and Salehi Golsefidy. The field norm $N_{K/F}$ maps $K^\times$ onto $F^\times$, and its kernel is maximal in the reduced norm-one group $D^{(1)}$. The quotient $D^{(1)}/Z(D^{(1)})$ is nonabelian simple, with the image of $\ker N_{K/F}$ as an abelian maximal subgroup. The proof uses matrix factorizations over local fields, a convolution theorem of Breuillard and Glazer, and Moret--Bailly's theorem on points over extensions with prescribed splitting.

papers.title: The generalized Franchetta conjecture for some hyper-Kähler varieties, III
papers.abstract: The generalized Franchetta conjecture states that for a locally complete family of polarized hyper-Kähler varieties, the generically defined cycles on any fiber of the universal family over the moduli stack inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. We prove the generalized Franchetta conjecture for the family of double EPW sextics discovered by O'Grady and for the family of double EPW cubes discovered by Iliev-Kapustka-Kapustka-Ranestad. We also prove a Franchetta-type result for the relative square of the universal family of double EPW sextics, which allows to relate double EPW sextics and Gushel-Mukai fourfolds on the level of motives. The proof involves the geometry of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds, whose Kuznetsov component allows to realize double EPW sextics and cubes as moduli spaces of Bridgeland-stable objects, relatively over the parameter space of Gushel-Mukai fourfolds. A key step is that the canonical Chow-Künneth decomposition of special Gushel-Mukai fourfolds is multiplicative; we use this to show that generically defined cycles on the third power of a special Gushel-Mukai fourfold inject into cohomology via the cycle class map. Along the way, we also show that the canonical Chow-Künneth decomposition of any Gushel-Mukai sixfold is multiplicative.

papers.title: Liouville systems II: Critical points at infinity in the resonant case
papers.abstract: For a Liouville system at a resonant parameter, we construct a bounded, locally Lipschitz pseudogradient, which classifies the non-compact ends of its flow at finite energy levels. If the reduced functional is Morse and the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical pair, each unbounded forward trajectory with energy bounded below converges in the bubbling parameters to a pair with negative coefficient. Conversely, each such pair, up to a permutation, is realized by an open set of escaping trajectories.

papers.title: A sharp conjugate radius bound for open four-manifolds with positive bi-Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We prove that every complete noncompact Riemannian four-manifold without boundary with bi-Ricci curvature at least $b>0$ has conjugate radius at most $π\sqrt{2/b}$. Equality holds on the round cylinder $\bS^3(\sqrt{2/b})\times\bR$. For $b=2$, the bound and the equality model agree with Gromov's prediction for open four-manifolds under a scalar curvature lower bound of $6$.

papers.title: Products of supersoluble groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=AB$ be a finite group, where $A$ and $B$ are supersoluble. We prove that every nonabelian composition factor of $G$ is isomorphic to $\PSL_2(p)$ for some prime $p\ge5$ and that the nonsoluble length of $G$ is at most one.

papers.title: On simultaneous left- and right-homometric sets on the positive affine line group
papers.abstract: On a non-abelian group $G$, the homometry problem comes in two flavors, depending on whether differences are computed on the left or on the right. A natural question is to determine whether simultaneously left- and right-homometric subsets of $G$ exist. This question has been answered positively in the case of dihedral groups by Genuys and Popoff. We here prove that no such subsets exist on the positive affine line group, if we impose that the subgroups generated by their left- and right-differences be non-abelian.

papers.title: Certified $p$-adic normal forms: an Eliasson-Vey theorem and zero sets of orbits
papers.abstract: I use the Smith form of the homological operator to construct partial Poincaré-Dulac normal forms near an equilibrium of a vector field on $\mathbb {Z}_p^d$ with coefficients divisible by $p$ (by $4$ if $p=2$). Retaining the directions whose removal would cost more than a fixed number of digits gives convergence on an explicit ball for any linear part. For polynomial fields, an exact integer check of the conjugacy defect certifies the computed flow to $K$ digits in rescaled coordinates. When the quadratic parts of an integrable Hamiltonian system at a rank-$0$ point span a Cartan subalgebra, the homological divisors in symplectic eigencoordinates are integers. This lets me use Newton iteration to obtain an exact $p$-adic Eliasson--Vey normal form at every prime and for every Williamson type. In exact linear normal coordinates, a polynomial restricted to an orbit gives a sum of exponentials, to which van der Poorten's bound of $2s-3$ zeros applies for a nonzero sum with $s\ge2$ distinct exponents. For integer orbits of polynomial maps, I combine exact modular orbits, Strassmann bounds and archimedean estimates in an adelic sieve. At every prime, increasing the modular depth eventually excludes a time class exactly when the interpolation along its center-manifold shadow has no zero in $\mathbb {Z}_p$.

papers.title: On the splitting of fractional Dirichlet eigenvalues in perforated domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic behavior of eigenvalues of the fractional Laplacian under singular domain perturbations produced by the removal of a hole with vanishing fractional capacity. First, we establish an expansion formula for eigenbranches bifurcating from a possibly multiple eigenvalue. We then investigate splitting phenomena: specifically, removing a family of holes concentrating at a zero-capacity compact set (lying outside a closed set of measure zero) causes a multiple eigenbranch to split into branches of smaller multiplicity. Finally, for holes concentrating at a point, we prove that the largest eigenbranch generically detaches from the rest and becomes simple.

papers.title: Small-time global exact controllability of nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with bilinear controls
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear Schrödinger equations on the circle with nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, a fixed smooth real potential $V$, and bilinear controls. Using only the three control potentials $\mathbf 1,\cos x,\sin x$, we prove global approximate controllability in $H^s$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$ for all integers $s,p\ge1$, every $κ\in\mathbb R$, and any prescribed positive time. The proof combines two ingredients: the approximate controllability between nowhere vanishing states from our companion paper, and a new mechanism that steers any nonzero initial state to a nowhere vanishing state in arbitrarily small time. When $V=0$ and the nonlinearity is defocusing or sufficiently weakly focusing, adding two explicit control potentials of finite regularity gives local exact controllability in $H^2$ near the constant state, via a moment problem and the inverse mapping theorem. Together, these results imply global exact controllability in $H^2$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$, at any prescribed positive time, with five control potentials. To~the best of our knowledge, this is the first global exact controllability result for a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with finitely many bilinear controls.

papers.title: Symplectizing stable generalized complex four-manifolds
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe a surgery that turns a stable generalized complex four-manifold into a symplectic four-manifold. As a consequence, we show that for $n\geq 2$, the almost complex manifold $(n^2+n+1)S^1\times S^3\#\overline{\mathbb{C}P^2}$ admits no stable generalized complex structures or constant type generalized complex structures. We also prove an irreducibility result for stable generalized complex four-manifolds and we show that the moduli space of generalized complex structures on an elliptic surface has infinitely many components.

papers.title: Approximate controllability in Sobolev spaces of periodic nonlinear Schrödinger equations with bilinear controls
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the torus $\T^d$ with a smooth real-valued potential and nonlinearity $κ|ψ|^{2p}ψ$, where the dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $p\ge1$, and the coefficient $κ\in\R$ are arbitrary. The controls act bilinearly through finitely many low Fourier modes. For every integer $s>d/2$, we prove approximate controllability in $H^s$ between any two nowhere vanishing states on the unit sphere in $L^2$ at any prescribed positive time. The proof combines small-time phase control, a transport approximation in $H^s$, and a construction of short uncontrolled trajectories connecting states with different winding vectors.

papers.title: Quadruples of integers whose elementary symmetric functions are perfect squares
papers.abstract: While Euler had considered the problem of finding three integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares, an extension of the problem to four integers has not been discussed in the mathematical literature till now. In this paper, we describe a method of generating infinitely many quadruples of positive integers whose elementary symmetric functions are all squares.

papers.title: A shock-fitting approach to high-order simulation of viscous hypersonic flows based on inviscid implicit shock tracking
papers.abstract: This work presents a framework for computing viscous, shock-dominated flows at high Mach and Reynolds numbers in which the bow shock is located by inviscid implicit shock tracking and then treated as a boundary of the viscous computation. The high-order implicit shock tracking (HOIST) method is applied to the Euler equations on a coarse, shock-agnostic mesh to produce a shock-aligned mesh and the shock geometry; the elements upstream of the shock are discarded, the post-shock domain is remeshed to resolve the boundary layer, and the compressible Navier-Stokes equations are solved on it with a high-order interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method, with the post-shock state prescribed along the shock boundary by the oblique shock relations. Because the shock structure is never resolved, the approach requires neither the extreme element compression nor the specialized formulations that fully coupled viscous shock tracking demands at these conditions; the tracking optimization is confined to the coarse inviscid mesh, and the viscous computation involves no mesh unknowns and no additional nonlinear stabilization. The framework is demonstrated on a Mach 10.6 axisymmetric blunt cone, a Mach 17.6 cylinder, and a Mach 5 sphere in three dimensions, with surface pressure and heat flux in good agreement with experimental measurements and reference computations.

papers.title: Hessian type equations with gradient source term and measure data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of nonnegative solutions to $F_k[-u]=|Du|^q\,dx+tμ$ for some $t>0$, where $μ$ is a finite nonnegative measure on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We consider the whole space $\mathbb{R}^N$ with $2\leq k<\frac{N}{2}$ and $q>\frac{Nk}{N-k}$, and a bounded domain $Ω$ with $2\leq k<N$ and $q>k$. We also establish pointwise gradient estimates in terms of the Wolff potential.

papers.title: High order tangencies, paratangencies, and universal dynamics
papers.abstract: Our research focuses on studying the dynamics in the Newhouse domain $\mathcal N(L)$ -- open regions in the space of $C^r$ diffeomorphisms of a $d$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M^d$ ($r=1,\ldots,\infty,ω$ and $d\ge 2$) where homoclinic tangencies to a saddle periodic orbit $L$ are persistent. We prove that diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-1 homoclinic tangencies of all orders are dense in such regions. If $L$ is a bi-focus, we reveal novel bifurcations in $\mathcal N(L)$ showing density of diffeomorphisms with infinitely many corank-2 homoclinic tangencies of all orders. These results entail genericity of one- or two-dimensional universal dynamics in $\mathcal N(L)$ (depending on the type of $L$). Moreover, we characterize the geometric complexity of the bifurcation sets corresponding to homoclinic tangencies. We prove that parametric families with paratangencies of arbitrarily high orders are dense in the space of parametric families intersecting $\mathcal N(L)$. If $r\le\infty$ and $L$ is sectionally dissipative, this implies density of families possessing infinitely many coexisting stable periodic orbits for some open set of parameter values.

papers.title: On the uniformity of definably amenable radicals and dfg-fsg decompositions in $p$-adically closed fields
papers.abstract: For definable families of groups over $p$-adically closed fields, we show that the definably amenable radicals and their dfg-fsg decompositions can be defined uniformly as the prime $p$ and the family parameters vary.

papers.title: Global topology and symmetry breaking in an indefinite superlinear Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: Motivated by the work of Fencl and López-Gómez [13] on global bifurcation diagrams, we study the connected components of positive solutions of $-u''=λu+a(x)u^p$ on $(-1,1)$ with $u(-1)=u(1)=0$, where $a$ changes sign and $p\ge2$ is an integer. For generic $\mathcal C^r$ weights, $r\ge2$, with $n$ positive intervals, simple zeros and negative endpoint values, we obtain at least $2^{n-1}$ noncompact components. Apart from the principal component, each is a curve with both ends at $λ=-\infty$. The proof distinguishes at least $2^n-1$ ends and yields bounds for branching and compactly supported cohomology. For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.

papers.title: Comparing the $K$-theory of two versions of $\ell^p$-Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that for any locally finite metric space $X$ and $1<p<\infty$, the canonical inclusion from the $\ell^p$-Roe algebra with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N)$ into that with coefficient space $\ell^p(\mathbb N;\ell^2(\mathbb N))$ identifies the former with a full multiplier corner of the latter. Consequently, the inclusion induces an isomorphism on $K$-theory, answering a question of Wang, Xie, Yu, and Zhu. Moreover, at the endpoint $p=1$, we show that the two corresponding Roe algebras are not Morita equivalent whenever $X$ is infinite.

papers.title: Rank-two twists of the Fermat cubic with $3$-primary Tate--Shafarevich group $(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$
papers.abstract: For each integer $m\ge0$ we construct infinitely many positive squarefree integers $k$ for which the Fermat cubic $E_k\colon x^3+y^3=k$ has Mordell--Weil rank two over $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\unicode{x0428}(E_k/\mathbb{Q})[3^\infty]\simeq(\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z})^{2m}$. Fixing $2m$ prime divisors of $k$ congruent to $-1$ modulo nine, with product $D$, we obtain $\gg_D X^{1/3}/(\log X)^6$ distinct parameters up to $X$. Two rational points on a $3$-isogenous curve come from the Stewart--Top sextic. Modulo their Kummer classes and a torsion class, the isogeny Selmer group has a basis given by the fixed primes. We realize every alternating matrix in this basis by prescribing the Frobenius classes of six primes in a fixed Galois extension. A nondegenerate matrix forces the rank to be exactly two and determines the entire primary group.

papers.title: Concentration in Hardy equations and singular heat flows
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability and loss of concentrated source data in critical Hardy equations and in singular heat flows. For the critical local Hardy form, a dyadic condition on the radial marginal characterizes admissibility and strong energy convergence under a uniform bound on angular densities. For general diffuse measures at inverse power one, strong convergence is characterized by mass convergence and condenser-capacity discrepancies. We also establish sharp moment inequalities and tightness criteria for the radial pole trace and boundary slope. At the sharp fractional $L^p$ Hardy coefficient, we identify the pole flux in a nonlinear power balance and show that finite remainder excludes nonconstant strong angular traces. For every fractional order, positive data can have finite remainder but infinite source pairing. Finally, for singular heat reactions with a positive nonincreasing factor tending to zero at infinity, we determine all attainable reaction limits of a time impulse and of data exhausted by parabolic Kato measures. A total variation estimate describes the combination of these mechanisms for countably many impulses.

papers.title: A Finiteness Result for Commuting Squares and Quantitative Ocneanu Rigidity
papers.abstract: We introduce the spanning relative commutant condition (SRC) for nondegenerate commuting squares of matrix algebras. The condition requires that the second relative commutant span the next algebra in the lower row of the basic construction as a right module over the preceding algebra. We prove that if a sequence of SRC squares with fixed tracial inclusion data converges, then all but finitely many terms are isomorphic to the limit square. We also show that the standard commuting square of every finite-index inclusion of $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors of depth two satisfies SRC. This gives a commuting-square proof of Ocneanu's finiteness theorem for standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph. We then obtain the explicit bound $B(D)=10^{7D^5}$ for the number of SRC squares up to isomorphism when the upper-right tracial algebra is prescribed and has dimension $D$. The same function bounds the number of standard invariants with a prescribed finite principal graph when $D$ is the number of closed walks of length $6\ell$ at the root, where $\ell$ is the least odd integer at least the diameter. We also characterize the Hadamard matrices whose spin model commuting squares satisfy SRC. These are precisely the matrices equivalent to character tables of finite abelian groups.

papers.title: Sixth-Order Q-Curvature of Conformally Euclidean Metrics: Improved Dimensional Thresholds, Quantitative Lower Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper studies the sign of the sixth-order \(Q\)-curvature of conformally Euclidean metrics on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) for integers \(n\ge2m\) and \(m\ge4\). Under suitable assumptions, we refine the sixfold integral estimates and prove that \(Q_g^{(6)}>0\) whenever \(2m\le n\le4m-6+[\widehat h_m]\), where \(\widehat h_m\) is the unique positive root of \(G_m\) and \(\widehat h_m\sim\frac{2\sqrt7-4}{3}m\) as \(m\to\infty\). Moreover, we strengthen this positivity result by establishing the quantitative lower bound \(Q_g^{(6)}(x)\geΘ_{m,n}\bigl(Q_g^{(2)}(x)\bigr)^3>0\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(Θ_{m,n}>0\) is an explicit constant depending only on \(m\) and \(n\). These quantitative inequalities also yield explicit lower bounds for intermediate Laplacians in higher-order elliptic equations. On the non-positivity side, we construct metrics satisfying \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)<0\) whenever \(n>\widetilde N_m\), where \(\widetilde N_m\sim\widetildeΛm\) as \(m\to\infty\) and \(\widetildeΛ\simeq9.74268\). These metrics extend smoothly to \(\mathbb S^n\) and are conformal to the round metric. In the same dimensional range, we further construct metrics with \(Q_g^{(6)}(0)>0\) and establish uniform positive lower and upper bounds for \(Q_g^{(2m)}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\). Our results extend the positivity range and lower the counterexample threshold obtained by Vétois and Zeitler (arXiv preprint, 2026). The sixth-order estimate also answers a question raised in our previous work on quantitative fourth-order \(Q\)-curvature bounds. These results provide new insights into Conjecture 1 of Li and Xu (J. Funct. Anal. 289 (2025), 111011) in the case \(k=3\), clarifying its validity and limitations across different dimensions.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Smooth Convex Optimization with a Comparison Oracle
papers.abstract: We study the minimization of a convex $d$-dimensional function with $L$-Lipschitz gradient when the only available information is a comparison oracle that reports which of two points has the smaller objective value. Given an initial point within distance $R$ of a minimizer, the constants $L$ and $R$, and $A = LR^2/\varepsilon$, we give a deterministic method that returns an $\varepsilon$-optimal point using $O(\sqrt{A}\,[d\log(2dA)+\log^2(2A)])$ comparisons for $A\ge1$, counting all comparisons spent in inner subroutines. The method is based on a normalized variant of Nemirovski's subspace method: each iteration performs a line search along an estimated gradient direction followed by a minimization over a two-dimensional affine subspace, and both subroutines rely on a comparison oracle and basic arithmetic operations only. With exact function values, combining finite-difference gradients with an accelerated method gives the well-known bound of $O(d\sqrt{A})$ evaluations; our bound shows that one bit per query suffices to match it up to logarithmic factors. Since two function values determine one comparison, the exact function-value lower bound of Dorn et al. implies that our bound is optimal up to logarithmic factors when $32\le A\le d^2$.

papers.title: Nonvanishing of mean indices and stability of symmetric closed characteristics on symmetric star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^4$
papers.abstract: H. Duan, H. Liu, Y. Long and W. Wang \cite{DLLW24} conjectured that if a compact star-shaped hypersurface in ${\bf R}^{2n}$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime closed characteristics, then each of them has nonzero mean index. They proved this conjecture for non-degenerate star-shaped hypersurfaces in ${\bf R}^6$. Motivated by their work, we study the symmetric counterpart of this problem. We prove that if a symmetric compact star-shaped hypersurface $Σ$ in ${\bf R}^4$ carries only finitely many geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics, and every odd iterate of them is non-degenerate in the symmetric sense, then each of them has nonzero symmetric mean index. Based on this result, we further prove that if $Σ$ carries exactly two geometrically distinct prime symmetric closed characteristics and all their iterates are non-degenerate, then both of them are irrationally elliptic.

papers.title: Some results on the isotropy groups of non-invertible simple derivations
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $2\le i<n$, and let $d_i$ be a $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots,x_i]$. We study the $k$-derivation of $k[x_1,\dots, x_n]$ of the form $d_n=d_i+\sum_{j=i}^{n-1}\bigl(a_jx_{j+1}+g_j(x_j)\bigr)\partial_{x_{j+1}}$ where $a_j\in k$ and $g_j\in k[x_j]\setminus k$. Under suitable conditions on $d_i$, we show that the isotropy group of $d_n$ consists of translations and is either trivial or isomorphic to $(k,+)$.

papers.title: Eight limit cycles in a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system
papers.abstract: Gyllenberg and Yan conjectured that a three-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system can have at least five limit cycles. We prove the conjecture by constructing a strictly competitive system in which eight distinct limit cycles coexist near a single positive equilibrium. For each $m=5,6,7,8$, we construct a weak focus of order $m$ and identify parameter directions on the Hopf hypersurface that allow us to vary the first $m-1$ focus quantities independently. We choose these quantities so that the drift of a scalar amplitude function alternates in sign on $m$ nested level curves, forcing a limit cycle between each consecutive pair. A perturbation transverse to the Hopf hypersurface creates one additional cycle inside the others. The one-turn displacement map shows that both local counts are sharp. For each $m$, we give a rigorous computer-assisted proof that an explicit rational interaction matrix yields at least $m$ distinct hyperbolic limit cycles. We thank GPT-6 Astra for helping us compare earlier constructions, identify the main obstacle to extending them, and develop the present approach.

papers.title: Convergence of Nonmonotone Schemes to Viscosity Solutions via Local Comparison
papers.abstract: We develop a convergence criterion for nonmonotone approximation schemes for Hamilton--Jacobi and fully nonlinear second-order equations. Under stability, consistency and suitable boundary assumptions, a local comparison hypothesis replaces monotonicity and yields convergence to viscosity solutions. For a semi-Lagrangian CWENO scheme for one-dimensional Hamilton--Jacobi equations, we establish convergence for bounded uniformly continuous initial data under $h=o(τ)$, relaxing the previously required mesh condition $h=O(τ^2)$. We also prove convergence of a nonmonotone one-dimensional $Q^2$ scheme for Isaacs equations whose operator cannot be written as a monotone operator plus a perturbation vanishing uniformly on bounded grid functions.

papers.title: A Goldbach-Type Problem for Random Multiplicative Functions
papers.abstract: We study the counts of the four sign patterns of a random multiplicative function on ordered decompositions $a+b=N$ into positive integers. The main term is $N/4$ in the nonvanishing model and $F(N)/4$ in the squarefree-supported model, where $F(N)$ counts the pairs with both summands squarefree and has asymptotic main term $\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{sf}}(N)N$. Let $ρ_q$ be the probability of a negative sign at the prime $q$. Set $m_q=\min(ρ_q,1-ρ_q)$, $A_N=\sum_{(\log N)^3<q\le N}m_q/q$, and $B(N)=\sum_{q\le N}m_q/q$. In the general model with independent prime vectors, almost surely for all sufficiently large integers $N$, the error for opposite-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(Ne^{-4A_N})$, and the error for same-sign pairs is $O_{\mathcal X}(N(e^{-4A_N}+e^{-2B(N)}))$. In four specified models, if the biases of the independent basic signs are square summable, then for every $\varepsilon>0$ the error is almost surely $O_{\varepsilon,\mathcal X}(N^{1/2+\varepsilon})$. In the completely multiplicative model under the same bias condition, we prove that $C_f(N)/\sqrt{N\log N}$ almost surely has limit superior $2$ and limit inferior $-2$. Together with a known bound for the one-point sum, this gives limit superior $1/2$ and limit inferior $-1/2$ for each normalized counting error about $N/4$

papers.title: The Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity
papers.abstract: In their 2007 paper on the log-convexity of combinatorial sequences, Liu and Wang conjectured that the Eulerian transformation preserves log-convexity. We completely solve their conjecture by showing that this transformation preserves strong $q$-log-convexity. More generally, we provide a sufficient condition for a linear transformation, defined by a triangular array satisfying a certain three-term recurrence relation, to preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. As applications, we show that both the $r$-colored Eulerian transformation and the $m$-Stirling Eulerian transformation preserve strong $q$-log-convexity. In particular, we confirm a conjecture due to Liu and Zhu, which states that the Eulerian transformation of type $B$ preserves log-convexity.

papers.title: A necessary and sufficient condition for steady Euler flows to be shear flows in an infinite strip
papers.abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient characterization of parallel shear flows among all $C^1$ steady incompressible Euler flows in an infinite strip, subject to the slip boundary condition. We show that a steady Euler flow is a parallel shear flow if and only if almost every regular streamline traverses the strip longitudinally. The proof relies on three key ingredients. First, the topological assumption on the streamlines yields global bounds on the stream function, the velocity, and the vorticity. Second, we establish a novel geometric formula for the total curvature which, together with the topological assumption on the streamlines, implies the finiteness of the total curvature via the area and coarea formulas. Third, once the total curvature is finite, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the flow in the far field, which in turn forces the total curvature to vanish.

papers.title: Kato-Milne cohomology over rational function fields in characteristic p>0
papers.abstract: Let F be a field of characteristic p > 0. In this note, we describe the Kato-Milne cohomology of the rational function field F(x) in one variable x over F. In particular, we extend the Milnor-Scharlau exact sequence [12, Theorem 5.2] to characteristic p. As an application of this exact sequence, we further obtain the norm theorem [16, Theorem A.3] in characteristic p.

papers.title: Higher Coherence of Flat Algebras
papers.abstract: We establish higher-coherence results for flat algebras over commutative base rings. If $K$ is noetherian and a $K$-flat algebra $A$ admits an $A^{\mathrm e}$-resolution of length $n$ with projective term in degree $n$ and flat terms in lower degrees, then every product of copies of $A$ has right flat dimension at most $n-1$ and $A$ is left strongly $n$-coherent. A projective $n$-th relative bar syzygy gives the corresponding two-sided conclusion. If $K$ is coherent and $A$ is $K$-flat and relatively quasi-free, then $A$ is left and right strongly $2$-coherent. In contrast, we construct a countable commutative ring $k$ that is strongly $n$-coherent for every $n\ge2$, while the one-variable polynomial algebra $k[z]$ is faithfully flat and relatively quasi-free over $k$ but fails strong $q$-coherence for every finite $q$. Explicit modules witness failure at each positive degree. These results establish coherence transfer over coherent bases and show that the analogous higher-degree transfer fails for every $n\ge2$, even after any fixed finite shift.

papers.title: The cardinal invariants of the $s$-dimensional Hausdorff null ideal are independent of $s$
papers.abstract: For $0 < s < 1$, let $\mathcal{N}^s$ denote the ideal of sets of $s$-dimensional Hausdorff measure zero. We prove that $\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ and $\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^s) = \operatorname{non}(\mathcal{N}^t)$ for all $0 < s, t < 1$. The proof uses Ren and Wang's solution of the Furstenberg set conjecture. This answers open questions of Shelah--Steprāns and Elekes--Steprāns.

papers.title: Pieri formula for the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of flag manifolds of type $A$
papers.abstract: We prove a Pieri formula for the quantum product of an arbitrary opposite Schubert class with the opposite Schubert class associated to the cyclic permutation of the form $c[k,p]=(k-p+1,\ldots,k+1)$ in the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory ring of the (full) flag manifold $Fl_n = SL_n(\C)/B$. In this formula, the quantum product is expressed as a sum over $k$-Pieri chains in the quantum Bruhat graph on $S_n$. We give the coefficient of each $k$-Pieri chain in terms of the first components of its labels and the descents among labels with the same second component. By setting all equivariant parameters equal to $1$, the coefficient of a nonempty $k$-Pieri chain becomes the signed number of its $p$-markings.

papers.title: The maximum number of edges in minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graphs
papers.abstract: A connected graph of order at least $2k+2$ is {\em $k$-extendable} if it has a matching of size $k$ and every such matching extends to a perfect matching. In particular, a 1-extendable graph is also called a {\em matching covered graph}. A $k$-extendable graph $G$ is {\em minimal} if $G-e$ is not $k$-extendable for every $e\in E(G)$. Lovász and Plummer [J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 23 (1977), 127--138] proved that every minimal matching covered bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge6$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(3|V(G)|-6)/2$, and this bound is sharp for every even order at least 6. Fabres, Kothari and Carvalho [J. Graph Theory 96 (2021), 490--509] proved that every minimal 2-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge12$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(5|V(G)|-20)/2$. Very recently, Mallik, Diwan and Kothari [J. Combin. 17 (2026), 559--606] characterized minimal matching covered bipartite graphs $G$ with $|E(G)|=(3|V(G)|-6)/2$ in terms of special trees. They also conjectured that, for every integer $k\ge1$, there exists an integer $N_k\le4k^2+2k$ such that every minimal $k$-extendable bipartite graph $G$ with $|V(G)|\ge N_k$ satisfies $|E(G)|\le(2k+1)(|V(G)|-2k)/2$. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for $k\ge3$ and prove that the upper bound is sharp for every even order at least $6k$ ($k\ge3$).

papers.title: A near-quadratic bound for critical sets of harmonic functions
papers.abstract: Let $u$ be a nonconstant harmonic function in $B_1 \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ with $n \ge 3$. Denote by $N$ the doubling index of $|\nabla u|$ in $B_1$. Let $\mathcal{C} := \{ x\in B_1: \nabla u(x) = 0 \}$ be the critical set. We show that $$\mathcal{H}^{n-2}(\mathcal{C} \cap B_{1/2}) \le C_n N^2 \log^2(N+2).$$ This estimate is sharp up to a squared logarithm loss.

papers.title: Combinatorics of equivariant blowups of spherical varieties
papers.abstract: We explicitly describe the colored fan of the blowup of a smooth spherical variety $X$ along a smooth irreducible $G$-stable subvariety $Y$. The answer is expressed in terms of the colored cone of $Y$ and the localization of the valuation cone at $Y$, and generalizes the star subdivision of fans of toric varieties. We also consider several examples illustrating the main result.

papers.title: An asymptotic form of Thomasse's directed path conjecture
papers.abstract: Thomassé conjectured that every oriented graph of minimum out-degree $d$ contains a directed path of length $2d$. We resolve this conjecture asymptotically by proving that every such graph contains a directed path of length at least $2d-O(d\log\log d/\log d)$.

papers.title: Berkovich's conjecture on noninner automorphisms of order $p$
papers.abstract: We prove a long-standing conjecture of Berkovich (Kourovka Notebook, Problem 4.13): every finite nonabelian $p$-group $P$ has a noninner automorphism of order $p$. If $p$ is odd, the automorphism $α$ can be chosen with $[P,α,α]=1$. More precisely, given a maximal normal elementary abelian subgroup $E$ of $P$, we can choose $α$ to fix both $F$ and $P/F$ pointwise, where $F$ is either $E$ or a hyperplane of $E$ normal in $P$. If $p=2$, the automorphism can be chosen with $[P,α,α,α]=1$, and with $[P,α,α]=1$ when $Z(P)$ is noncyclic. The dihedral group of order eight shows that the hypothesis on $Z(P)$ cannot be omitted.

papers.title: Asymptotics for Riesz means of integrable polygons
papers.abstract: We prove complete asymptotic expansions for Riesz means of order $γ> 0$ for the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on integrable polygons. The coefficients of the first three terms are the familiar ones involving the area, perimeter, and corner angles of the polygon. The coefficients of the lower-order terms are given by convergent trigonometric series. The proof is based on heat trace identities for integrable polygons, together with large-argument asymptotics for Bessel functions.

papers.title: On a question of A.N. Skiba concerning the modularity of the lattice of $σ$-permutable subgroups
papers.abstract: Let $σ=\{σ_i\mid i\in I\}$ be some partition of the set of all primes and let $G$ be a finite group. A subgroup $A$ of $G$ is said to be $σ$-permutable in $G$ if $G$ has a Hall $σ_i$-subgroup for every $i\in I$ and $A$ permutes with every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ for all $i\in I$. We describe the finite groups $G$ for which the lattice $\Lper(G)$ of all $σ$-permutable subgroups of $G$ is modular. This answers the first part of a question of A.N. Skiba. We also prove that if every Hall $σ_i$-subgroup of $G$ is nilpotent, then $\Lper(G)$ is modular if and only if every two members of $\Lper(G)$ are permutable.

papers.title: The norm axiom and factor hyperfields
papers.abstract: Touchard and the author asked whether every valued hyperfield, in Krasner's sense with the norm axiom, is of the form $\mathcal{H}_ρ(K)$: a valued field $K$ read up to relative error $ρ$. The question turns on the norm axiom. If a valued hyperfield is a quotient $K^\times/T\cup\{0\}$ of a field, the norm axiom forces $T=1+\mathfrak{m}_ρ$ for a valuation on $K$. This completes the proof of a published proposition, and it makes the question equivalent to asking whether every Krasner valued hyperfield is such a quotient. For value group $\mathbb{Z}$ we prove directly that it is. Without the norm axiom the answer is negative. Layering a hyperfield over a non-trivial ordered abelian group gives a factor hyperfield exactly when the hyperfield itself is one, so Massouros's hyperfields yield hyperfields with a non-trivial valuation, satisfying all the other axioms, that are not factor hyperfields. The general question remains open.

papers.title: Almost-Isometric Embeddings of Graphs into Riemannian Manifolds
papers.abstract: Graphs represent objects as vertices and relationships as edges; positive edge weights define shortest-path metrics. Metric embeddings leverage target-space geometry to analyze distances. Foundational results target linear spaces: Nash embedded Riemannian manifolds isometrically into Euclidean space, and Bourgain embedded $n$-point metrics into Hilbert space with $O(\log n)$ distortion. By contrast, the manifold hypothesis places high-dimensional data near low-dimensional smooth manifolds, making such manifolds themselves target spaces. What distortion is needed to embed a finite graph metric into such a manifold with its intrinsic distance? Although the star $K_{1,3}$ cannot embed isometrically into any complete Riemannian manifold, we prove almost-isometric embeddings always exist: for $\varepsilon>0$ and any finite connected positively weighted graph, we construct a smooth connected closed orientable surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ admitting a noncontractive $(1+\varepsilon)$-embedding of its vertices, with $\varepsilon$ arbitrarily small and independent of graph parameters. This construction transfers communication schemes between graphs and surfaces. For independent unicasts, fractional routing splits flows across paths while network coding lets relays combine messages. Space information flow permits relays anywhere, charging bandwidth times distance. Whereas coding advantage (optimal routing over coding cost) equals one in Euclidean space, we prove coding advantages on finite positively weighted undirected graphs transfer to smooth closed surfaces within factors approaching one. Counterexamples to the multiple-unicast conjecture and amplification yield smooth closed surfaces with unbounded coding advantage. Conversely, coding advantage is at most $C\log(g+2)$ on finite undirected graphs of orientable genus $g$ and smooth closed orientable surfaces of genus $g$, for absolute $C$.

papers.title: A generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for Gaussian rough paths
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a generalization of Lévy's stochastic area formula for the canonical rough path lift of a $2n$-dimensional centered Gaussian process with independent, identically distributed components. The formula extends the identity obtained by Aihara, Akahori, Fujii and Nitta [1] for Brownian motion. We compute the expectation of the exponential of a functional involving stochastic areas and quadratic forms in the terminal values. The result is expressed in terms of spectral data of a Hilbert--Schmidt operator associated with the stochastic area and an $n \times n$ determinant. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition for absolute integrability in terms of the covariance at the terminal time and the symmetric part of the quadratic form in the terminal values. As examples, we discuss the cases of fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $1/4<H<1$, Brownian motion and the Brownian bridge. In particular, we recover the formula in [1] under the exact condition for absolute integrability.

papers.title: An Annular Spiral Construction for Anomalous Dissipation in the Forced Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: Kolmogorov's 1941 theory of turbulence (K41) predicts that the rate of kinetic energy dissipation in a turbulent flow can remain positive as viscosity tends to zero. In 2023, Bruè and De Lellis used quasi-self-similar mixing to construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations exhibiting anomalous dissipation. In this paper, we show that anomalous dissipation can still occur for a flow with spiral geometry in an annulus. In the horizontal plane, we wind a radial segment into a two-turn spiral and then apply alternating shears. After each pair of shears, the image of the segment shares a subarc of positive length with the original spiral. We compare the vertical velocity with sine profiles whose angular period halves with each pair. After the horizontal flow stops, diffusion damps the final profile. By embedding this planar construction into the $(2+\frac{1}{2})$-dimensional framework, we obtain smooth solutions of the three-dimensional equations with the same smooth initial datum. For a sequence of viscosities tending to zero, their dissipation over a fixed subannulus and one vertical period has a uniform positive lower bound, and their forces converge in $C^α$ uniformly in time for every $0<α<1$. We use this spiral construction to produce solutions of the forced three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations that exhibit anomalous dissipation.

papers.title: On the 0-Rotatability of Regular Spider Trees of Leg Length 4
papers.abstract: A tree $T$ on $q$ edges is said to be $0$-rotatable if for every vertex $v \in V(T)$, there exists a graceful labeling $f : V(T) \to \{0, 1, \dots, q\}$ such that $f(v) = 0$. Rofa proved that all regular (symmetric) spider trees with leg length at most $3$ are $0$-rotatable and conjectured that the property holds for every leg length. In this note, we settle the first open case of this conjecture by proving that every regular spider tree $T(k, 4)$ with $k \ge 1$ legs of length $4$ is $0$-rotatable. Our proof combines Rofa's algebraic graceful labeling at the root with complementary labelings, an end-to-end leg-reversal construction placing $0$ at a leaf, and a two-leg reflection permutation placing $0$ at distance $2$ from the root.

papers.title: Scaling cores and dust-free layered sets
papers.abstract: We study Hausdorff-box dimension gaps in compact sets of finite positive Hausdorff measure. At each scale, the points of low local measure form a scaling core that carries all covering growth above the Hausdorff dimension. This gives gap criteria for both box and intermediate dimensions. We construct dust-free layered sets, in which every neighbourhood of every point has positive measure. Their dimensions are determined by the layer dimension and a product core formed from a horizontal limit set and a sequence of heights. Under a suitable approximation-rate condition, the volume remaining after subtraction of the product tube grows linearly with radius, with coefficient twice the total layer measure. Every compact null horizontal set admits such a construction. Cantor approximants, homogeneous cube constructions and Bedford-McMullen carpets illustrate the results.

papers.title: Controlled nonstationary G-diffusions: dynamic programming, weighted Harris contraction and entrance risk
papers.abstract: We study controlled nonstationary \(G\)-diffusions in a canonical-law formulation of covariance uncertainty. The principal structural result is an abstract weighted Harris--oscillation contraction theorem for translation-covariant nonlinear evolution families. A Lyapunov estimate for a dominating terminal-perturbation bound and a local space--time oscillation estimate for differences imply exponential contraction in a weighted quotient norm, without positive homogeneity, subadditivity or convexity. For elementary sample-and-hold feedback controls and a rectangular family of martingale laws, we construct a measurable controlled state map and prove deterministic- and stopped-time dynamic programming principles for the robust lower value. Under uniform ellipticity, differences of Bellman values belong to a common parabolic Pucci class; a local Harnack argument and an all-policy Lyapunov estimate verify the abstract hypotheses. For zero running cost, the contraction yields a unique tempered entrance nonlinear expectation and exponential attraction. With running cost, it yields a unique normalized nonstationary corrector and an additive cocycle, together with exponential convergence of relative values. Subtracting a scalar primitive of the cocycle gives an all-time viscosity solution of the backward Bellman--Isaacs equation. Autonomous and periodic coefficients yield additive eigenpairs, stationary and periodic ergodic equations, and convergence of long-time average costs. The results provide a long-time theory for optimally controlled dynamic risk evaluation under nonstationary covariance uncertainty.

papers.title: Agentic Discovery of Simple Symbolic Inventory Policies
papers.abstract: Designing simple inventory policies becomes increasingly difficult as operational features and system configurations expand. We develop an Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System based on explicitly defined simple operational formula (SOF) policy and template classes. Large language models (LLMs) revise symbolic structures, while a numerical engine fits parameters separately for each instance and evaluates the induced policies. Multicriteria parent selection, state-specific operational diagnostics, and reusable symbolic motifs guide structural evolution. A three-stage progression develops shared templates across instances and configurations with varying state dimensions. Experiments on 15,600 instances spanning 50 demand distributions cover lead times, perishability, their combination, and lead times with limited customer patience. The discovered templates improve aggregate empirical performance over evaluated SOF benchmarks and are competitive with policies requiring more elaborate online computations. For a lost-sales system with a three-period lead time, we develop an average-cost decomposition and prove that, under specified demand and cost conditions, a capped dual-shortfall specialization of a discovered policy strictly outperforms every policy in the considered capped base-stock benchmark class. This analysis links the performance advantage to the discovered replenishment mechanism. Together, these results highlight the potential of agentic discovery to generate simple inventory policies with strong empirical performance and identify operational mechanisms amenable to rigorous theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Bounds on periods of curves for split rational maps
papers.abstract: Let $A_1$ and $A_2$ be fixed complex rational maps of degree at least two, and let $(A_1,A_2)$ denote the endomorphism of $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ of the form $(x,y)\mapsto(A_1(x),A_2(y))$. We show that the periods of irreducible $(A_1,A_2)$-periodic curves with dominant coordinate projections are bounded, unless $A_1$ and $A_2$ belong to the exceptional power, Chebyshev, or Lattès families. We also extend this result to periodic subvarieties for endomorphisms of $(\mathbb P^1)^m$.

papers.title: Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension
