This construction captures the cancellation in the third-order corrector expansion without uniform Hessian bounds for the correctors.

papers.title: Quillen's finiteness conjecture for the cotangent complex in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Building on work of Turner, we propose a proof in positive characteristic of Quillen's conjecture on finiteness properties of the cotangent complex for homomorphisms between noetherian rings of possibly infinite flat dimension.

papers.title: Contraction-Based Model Predictive Control using Bilinear Koopman Realizations with Proportional Error Bounds
papers.abstract: Data-driven model predictive control based on Koopman operator theory is a promising approach for constrained control of nonlinear systems with unknown dynamics. This paper proposes a robust model predictive control framework for such systems using bilinear Koopman realizations with state- and input-dependent proportional approximation-error bounds that vanish at the target equilibrium. Since prediction in lifted coordinates with a finite-dimensional Koopman realization need not remain on the manifold of valid lifted states, multi-step prediction may leave the region where one-step error certificates apply. We avoid this difficulty by reprojecting each predicted lifted state onto the original state coordinates and lifting it again, yielding an error-aware discrete-time control-affine predictor in the original state space without assuming invariance of the Koopman dictionary. For this predictor, we develop a homothetic tube construction based on a discrete-time robust control contraction metric whose radius explicitly accounts for the proportional approximation error bounds. The tube tightening handles arbitrary continuously differentiable nonlinear constraints, and the resulting model predictive control problem includes terminal ingredients and a tube-radius penalty that exploits the vanishing uncertainty near the target. We prove robust satisfaction of the original nonlinear constraints, recursive feasibility, and exponential stability of the sampled true closed-loop system with high probability over the training data without requiring a globally optimal solution to the model predictive control problem. Numerical examples, including nonlinear obstacle-avoidance constraints, demonstrate robust stabilization and higher performance of the proposed approach compared to existing Koopman-based model predictive control methods in terms of smaller closed-loop cost and flexibility.

papers.title: Fixed point properties for random groups in the density model with $d > \frac{1}{4}$
papers.abstract: We prove that random groups in Gromov's density model have Kazhdan's property~\((T)\) asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.) at every density \(d>\frac14\). Together with Ashcroft's theorem for \(d<\frac14\), this establishes \(\frac14\) as the sharp threshold and settles the long-standing problem of determining the threshold for property $(T)$ in the density model. More generally, for every fixed number of generators \(n\ge2\) and density \(d\in(\frac14,1)\), there exists \(C_{n,d}>0\) such that, a.a.s., every affine isometric action on a real \(L^p\)-space has a fixed point simultaneously for all \[ 1\le p\le C_{n,d}\sqrt{\frac{l}{\log l}}, \] where \(l\) is the relator length. In particular, \(\frac14\) is also the threshold for each fixed \(L^p\) fixed point property, \(1\le p<\infty\). We also establish a simultaneous fixed point theorem for a large class of uniformly smooth real Banach spaces with a common power-type convexity bound and a suitable common bound on their uniform curvature moduli. We further prove that, for each fixed real Banach space in a class that, to the best of our knowledge, contains all currently known examples of super-reflexive Banach spaces, random groups at density $d>1/4$ a.a.s.\ have the fixed point property for affine isometric actions. The proof combines a fixed point criterion based on harmonic cocycles with spectral estimates for random bipartite multigraphs arising from decompositions of relators into four consecutive subwords. All asymptotic conclusions hold as \(\RelLen\to\infty\) through all positive integers.

papers.title: The smallest square tileable by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles
papers.abstract: Croft, Falconer and Guy (Unsolved Problems in Geometry, Problem C5) exhibit a tiling of the 27 x 27 square by eight pairwise incomparable integer rectangles and remark that it is not known whether 27 is the smallest side length of a square that can be tiled by pairwise incomparable integer rectangles, no restriction being placed on the number of tiles. Knuth has since stated, in a 2019 draft of a section of The Art of Computer Programming, that 27 is indeed the smallest. We give a complete, independently reproducible proof: for every integer n <= 26 and every k >= 2, the n x n square admits no tiling by k pairwise incomparable integer rectangles. The proof combines two structural reductions with an exhaustive search over the 167538 surviving candidate tile sets, carried out by two independently written programs. The same search shows that at least eight tiles are needed at n = 27 and that the tile set of Croft, Falconer and Guy is the only one that tiles this square; it does so in exactly two arrangements up to symmetry. We also give explicit eight-tile tilings of the n x n square for every n >= 27, and seven-tile tilings for every n >= 34. With the classical lower bounds (every tiling of a rectangle by two or more pairwise incomparable rectangles uses at least seven, and no square of integer side less than 34 can be tiled by seven pairwise incomparable integer rectangles), this determines the least number of tiles for every square: there is no tiling for n <= 26, eight tiles are needed for 27 <= n <= 33, and seven for n >= 34. The complete software, build instructions and output logs are included as ancillary files.

papers.title: A complete characterization of sequential testability and change detectability in i.i.d. models
papers.abstract: We give qualitative and quantitative necessary and sufficient conditions for sequential testing and change detection in an i.i.d. composite problem. A level-\(α\) test with power one against every alternative exists if and only if the alternatives are separated from the null by a countable family of finite-block events. Equivalent conditions use randomized tests, bounded scores, e-processes, reduced-filtration test supermartingales, and a countable cover with positive finite-block weak-$*$ convex-hull separation. The construction gives pointwise expected sample size \(O_Q(\log(1/α))\). Quantitatively, one e-process attains the intrinsic pointwise growth rate \(Γ(Q)\) at every alternative if and only if a countable family of bounded block bets recovers these rates. The same condition characterizes simultaneous attainment of the sharp expected-sample-size coefficient \(1/Γ(Q)\); arbitrary attainable lower rate profiles admit an analogous characterization. Total-variation separability of the alternatives suffices for recovery. Weak lower semicontinuity of the KL projection, in particular weak compactness of the null, also identifies \(Γ(Q)\) with \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P}\mathrm{KL}(Q\|P)\). The qualitative and quantitative conditions also characterize change detectability under fixed-time false-alarm bounds \(\Prob_{P^\infty}(T_γ\le n)\le n/γ\), together with ordinary ARL control. Whenever countable rate recovery holds, for any \(η>0\) one calibrated e-detector has robust Lorden delay asymptotic to \((\logγ)/Γ(Q)\) at finite positive rates, while satisfying the stronger optional-horizon inequality and placing every null ARL in \([γ,(1+η)γ+1]\). Examples exhibit a strict cost of simultaneous optimality and show that ordinary ARL alone supports neither characterization, even with finite, tightly calibrated null means.

papers.title: Derivation of a linearly elastic elliptic membrane shell theory in the framework of magnetoelasticity
papers.abstract: Starting from a three-dimensional model of linearized magnetoelasticity, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of a thin shell as its thickness approaches zero. Our analysis focuses on a family of linearly elastic elliptic membrane shells. Using $Γ$-convergence, we rigorously derive a two-dimensional linear magnetoelastic shell model and establish its relationship to the original three-dimensional model in terms of the convergence of minimizers.

papers.title: Sturm--Liouville-Type Parity and Oscillation of a Cubic Spline Eigenbasis
papers.abstract: We study the eigen-structure of the kernel matrix arising from cubic smoothing splines on equally spaced knots. Using matrix-theoretic methods, we show that its positive eigenvalues are simple, that the associated eigenvectors alternate between even and odd, and that the eigenvector for the $k$th largest positive eigenvalue has exactly $k+1$ sign changes. Building on established results on oscillatory and centrosymmetric matrices, we provide a more explicit proof of the known oscillation property of the eigenvectors and establish their alternating parity. We then verify, by a separate argument, that both properties extend to the associated continuous cubic spline eigenfunctions, showing that the resulting spline basis exhibits both an alternating parity structure and an oscillation pattern analogous to that of classical Sturm--Liouville eigenfunctions.

papers.title: Polynomial permutation stability, soficity, and universal polynomial groups
papers.abstract: We introduce polynomial permutation stability for maps between groups, extending ordinary permutation stability from homomorphisms to polynomial maps defined by iterated finite differences. We show that a group $G$ is polynomially permutation stable in degree $s$ if and only if its universal polynomial group $\operatorname{Pol}_s(G)$ is permutation stable. While every finite group is polynomially permutation stable in degree two, we prove that the cyclic group of order six is not stable in degree three. More precisely, we construct a finite-index direct-product subgroup of $\operatorname{Pol}_3(C_6)$ to which an instability theorem of Ioana applies. We also show that polynomial sofic approximations characterize the usual class of sofic groups. In degree two, we obtain a split exact sequence relating $\operatorname{Pol}_2(G)$ to a restricted wreath product, with applications to soficity and property $(T)$. A quotient-transfer principle yields infinite, finitely presented, nonperfect groups that are polynomially permutation stable in every degree. Finally, we obtain nonamenability and largeness results for higher-degree universal polynomial groups of finite groups.

papers.title: Exact Algebraic Computation of Learning Coefficients for Two-Dimensional Singular Models
papers.abstract: Classical information criteria such as the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) rely on regularity assumptions that break down for singular models, leading to incorrect model selection in settings such as deep learning. The Widely Applicable Bayesian Information Criterion (WBIC) relies on local learning coefficients $λ$, which in the analytic case coincides with local Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT) of the Kullback-Leibler divergence of the model, to capture correct marginal likelihood asymptotics. Exact computation of the learning coefficients has been limited to special cases, and only sampling-based estimation methods are generally applicable. We present the first deterministic algorithm that computes local RLCTs exactly for any two-dimensional model whose Kullback-Leibler distance is contact equivalent to a polynomial, derive a bound on its complexity, and demonstrate its effectiveness for a broad class of models, with applications including polynomial neural networks. Beyond providing ground truth to calibrate sampling-based estimators, exact computation reveals algebraic structure in learning coefficients that sampling cannot and out-speeds it in the shallow regime.

papers.title: Entrywise Positivity Preservers on Green Matrices
papers.abstract: We classify entrywise functions preserving positive semidefiniteness on Green matrices with positive parameters. For each fixed \(n\ge2\), PSD preservation is equivalent to \(f\) being nondecreasing and \((f(tr^{i+j}))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) being PSD for all \(t>0,r>1\). For \(f\in C^{2n-2}\), this is equivalent to \(f'\ge0\) and positive semidefiniteness of \(((t\,d/dt)^{i+j}f(t))_{i,j=0}^{n-1}\) at every positive \(t\). These fixed-order classes strictly decrease with \(n\); their intersection consists exactly of \(f(t)=\int_{[0,\infty)}t^α\,dμ(α)\), where \(μ\) is a finite positive measure and the integral is finite for every \(t>0\). At each fixed order, entrywise Loewner monotonicity is equivalent to \(f\in C^1\) and \(f'\) belonging to the corresponding PSD preserver class. In all orders, monotonicity itself implies smoothness. Nonnegative minors of orders one and two on every strict three-by-three Green input already force \(f\equiv0\) or \(f(t)=ct^α\), with \(c>0\) and \(α\ge0\). They give TN output in every order; the nonzero members also preserve PSD Green structure. We also classify PSD, TN, and Loewner-monotone extensions to the closure allowing zero entries. No regularity is assumed except in the differential criterion.

papers.title: Learning Forced Multibody Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.abstract: We introduce an architecture for learning the dynamics of forced mechanical systems evolving on Lie groups, based on discrete forced Euler-Lagrange equations. The proposed method, termed Lie Group Discrete Forced Euler-Lagrange Neural Network (LieDFLNN), learns mechanical dynamics directly from discrete configuration observations, without requiring velocity measurements. This formulation allows the simultaneous identification of unknown mechanical properties and forcing terms, while ensuring that the predicted configurations remain on the underlying Lie group. We develop explicit formulations for rigid body dynamics on $SO(3)$ and $SE(3)$, extend the framework to interacting multibody systems, and introduce a method for learning unknown control forces when the Lagrangian is known. Finally, we evaluate the method through numerical experiments involving rigid body dynamics, nonlinear external forces, controlled systems, and real-world human motion capture data. The numerical results confirm the advantages of incorporating Lie group geometry and discrete variational structure into data-driven modeling of forced mechanical systems.

papers.title: Shifted-Binomial Coordinates of Dilated Binomial Polynomials: Multinomial Decimation and Arithmetic Structure
papers.abstract: For integers $m\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, let $d=m+r-1$ and consider the unique expansion \[ \binom{mn}{d}=\sum_{k=1}^{d+1}T_{m,r,k}\binom{n+k-1}{d}. \] By a standard multisection of a rational generating function, the coordinates are a residue-class subsequence of multinomial coefficients: \[ T_{m,r,k}=[x^{mk-1}](1+x+\cdots+x^{m-1})^{m+r}. \] From this representation we obtain the exact support, a counting interpretation by words by drops (Theorem~\ref{thm:drops}), a reflection criterion (the nonzero row is palindromic precisely when $r\equiv2\pmod m$), and log-concavity, hence unimodality, of the nonzero row. An integer-valued polynomial argument gives the universal divisor $m/\gcd(m,r-1)$ of each row, and a prime-adic computation of the fixed divisor of $\binom{mX}{d}$ gives the exact greatest common divisor of each row, a sharpness criterion, and a family of rows in which the universal divisor is arbitrarily far from sharp. We also obtain the row sum $m^{m+r-1}$, a Catalan-number specialization, and explicit coefficient arrays for $m=2,3,4,5$. The methods are finite differences, multisection of rational generating functions, and fixed divisors of integer-valued polynomials.

papers.title: A few remarks on the Baez-Duarte Criterion
papers.abstract: We study exponentially damped Möbius approximants in $\mathscr H=L^2([1,\infty),dt/t^{-2})$. With \[ γ_n(t)=\left\lfloor\frac tn\right\rfloor -\frac{\lfloor t\rfloor}{n},\qquad f(u)(t)=\sum_{n\ge1}μ(n)e^{-nu}γ_n(t),\] we compute the relevant scalar products, characterize the Möbius coefficients as the unique coefficients giving pointwise convergence to the constant function, and prove $\langle1 \mid f(u)\rangle\to1$. Vasyunin's formula expresses $F(e^{-u})=\|f(u)\|_2^2$ as an arithmetic cotangent sum. In the final section we give a criterion that would help in the analysis of asymptotics of $F(x)$ as $x\uparrow 1$.

papers.title: Group action-stabilizer graph of group actions of a group on a set
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce the group action-stabilizer graph $GAS(G)$ of a group $G$ on a set $X$. Its vertex set is the collection of all non-trivial group actions of $G$ on $X$, and two vertices $φ$ and $ψ$ are adjacent if and only if the normal subgroups $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ and $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^ψ$ of $G$ intersect non-trivially, where $G_x^φ$ and $G_x^ψ$ are the stabilizers of $x$ with respect to the actions $φ$ and $ψ$, respectively. We show that $GAS(G)$ is obtained from the intersection graph of those normal subgroups of $G$ that occur as kernels of actions on $X$ by replacing each vertex by a clique of twin vertices, and we characterize a special subgraph $gas(G)$ of $GAS(G)$ in which the vertex set contains the actions $φ$ of $G$ on $X$ such that the kernels $\bigcap_{x\in X} G_x^φ$ are distinct. We determine the number of group actions within some specific groups and find certain conditions under which $GAS(G)$ is equal to $gas(G)$. We also show that, for a finite nilpotent group $G$ with at least two prime divisors, $gas(G)$ is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^3p_2$, and its complement is a derived graph exactly when $G$ is cyclic of order $p_1p_2$, $p_1p_2p_3$, $p_1^2p_2$ or $p_1^2p_2^2$.

papers.title: Penalized hyperviscous Navier-Stokes flows: well-posedness, incompressible limit and sharp decay
papers.abstract: We study a three-dimensional Navier--Stokes system obtained by Temam's penalty method in the presence of a biharmonic viscosity: the pressure and the divergence constraint are replaced by the term $-\varepsilon^{-1}\nabla\,div\,u$, and the convection term is written in skew-symmetric form. We prove global well-posedness in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$ and global regularity for data of arbitrary size in $H^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, with bounds uniform in $\varepsilon$ and in time. For data in $L^1\cap L^2$, the energy decays like $t^{-3/2}$, with a constant independent of $\varepsilon$; for data in $L^1\cap H^2$, the first two derivatives decay at the corresponding heat rates. We identify the leading asymptotic profile and show that $t^{3/2}\|u(t)\|_{L^2}^2\toγ_\varepsilon(8πν)^{-3/2}|m_\infty|^2$, where $m_\infty$ is an asymptotic momentum and the explicit factor $γ_\varepsilon\in(\frac23,1)$ measures the energy removed by the penalization. Consequently, the decay rates are optimal in $L^1\cap H^2$ under an explicit non-degeneracy condition. Finally, as $\varepsilon\to0$, the solutions converge globally in time to those of the incompressible hyperviscous Navier--Stokes equations at the rate $\sqrt\varepsilon$, up to an explicit initial layer, and $-\varepsilon^{-1}div\,u$ converges to the pressure.

papers.title: Harmonic weights in inverse central binomial series
papers.abstract: We study how the partial fraction coefficients of an inverse central binomial series change when the harmonic weight $H_{pn}$ is replaced by $H_{qn}$. For positive integers $p<q$, every coefficient increases. As the index $k$ grows, the increase tends to $2\log(q/p)$ uniformly over all angles $0<φ\leπ$, even when the angle approaches either endpoint. The increase is above the limit at every odd index and below it at every even index. We give the first correction, of order $k^{-2/q}$ for $q>2$ and of order $k^{-2}$ for $(p,q)=(1,2)$. For the normalized transforms, subtracting $c$ times the first from the second gives a Stieltjes function exactly when $c\le1$. We also determine which real dilations $0<p<q$ satisfy the same sign law. For $p\ge1$ it holds exactly when $q\ge2$. For $0<p<1$ it holds above a threshold $Q(p)$, and at the threshold it holds precisely on one interval $0<p<p_*$. Finally, we give angle identities at every odd weight from three onward and determine which Dirichlet $L$-terms cancel at angle $π/3$.

papers.title: The Stability of the Backward Problem for Photoacoustic Imaging in Attenuating Media via Carleman Estimates
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the backward problem in time for photoacoustic tomography (PAT) in attenuating media. It is well-established that photoacoustic imaging in attenuating media can be accurately modeled by spatial fractional-order damping. This inverse problem is ill-posed in the sense of Hadamard. In this work, we construct a novel class of Carleman estimates independent of spatial variables, and by virtue of these estimates, we establish conditional stability estimates for this problem for the first time. Building upon this, we propose a Tikhonov-type regularization functional and derive its associated adjoint system. Furthermore, leveraging the established conditional stability results, we derive the convergence rate of the proposed regularization approach. Finally, we validate the effectiveness of our theoretical findings through extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings
papers.abstract: In this paper, our aim is to establish several Landau-type theorems for $K$-quasiregular harmonic mappings $f=h+\overline{g}$ in the unit disk $\Bbb{D} = \{z\in\Bbb{C}: |z|<1\}$. Under various boundedness assumptions on the analytic part $h$, we obtain explicit univalence radii and corresponding schlicht disk radii that improve upon existing estimates in the literature. We also establish new Landau-type theorems under novel hypotheses. We provide examples to illustrate our results, and comprehensive numerical tables present quantitative values of the radii for various parameter choices, demonstrating the effectiveness of our results.

papers.title: A Gallager-Type Redundancy Bound for Binary Fano Coding
papers.abstract: Binary Fano codes build a complete prefix code by repeatedly splitting the sorted list of symbol probabilities into two halves whose total probabilities are as close to each other as possible. Krajči, Liu, Mikeš, and Moser proved in 2015 that the redundancy $R$ of this code satisfies $R\le1-p_n$, where $p_n$ is the smallest symbol probability. We prove that $R<U(p_1)$, where $U$ is a piecewise function of the largest symbol probability $p_1$ with $U<1$. In particular, $R<p_1+4-\tfrac53\log_2 5$ for every source, and $R<\tfrac52-\tfrac56\log_2 5$ when $p_1<\tfrac12$. The bound equals the supremum of the redundancy for $p_1\ge\tfrac12$ and on an interval just below $\tfrac13$, and we give a lower bound for the other values of $p_1$. Unlike the bounds for Huffman codes, the proofs do not use the sibling property. They work directly with the Fano split rule, mainly through the facts that every split is nearly balanced and that the redundancy is a sum of one term per internal node of the tree.

papers.title: The structure of FAC posets and the Aharoni--Korman conjecture
papers.abstract: A poset $P$ is said to satisfy the finite antichain condition, or FAC for short, if it has no infinite antichain. Such posets exhibit rich and complex structure, and it was conjectured by Aharoni and Korman in 1992 that any FAC poset $P$ possesses a chain $C$ and a partition into antichains such that $C$ meets every antichain of the partition. While a counterexample to this conjecture was recently discovered, in this paper we prove that the conjecture does hold true for a broad class of countable posets. In particular, we prove that the Aharoni--Korman conjecture holds for countable FAC posets containing no saturated chain $D$ such that either $D$ or its reverse $D^*$ is of the form $\bigoplus_{x\inω} D_x$, where each $D_x$ is infinite and co-well-founded. The proof of this result rests on novel structural theory for countable FAC posets, which may be of independent interest. One result states that every countable FAC poset is either scattered (contains no copy of the rationals) or may be broken up into a dense collection of scattered posets which reflect the structure of the poset as a whole. This provides a general reduction from arbitrary countable FAC posets to the far more tractable scattered ones. We also develop an extension $H(P)$ of a poset $P$ which includes ``limit points'' of $P$ and allows for intricate arguments involving these points. Amongst other points, one way in which $H(P)$ differs from existing poset completions and extensions is that it is sensitive to the order-type of a chain. Finally, we highlight a number of intriguing problems in this area which remain open.

papers.title: Convergence of Large-Stepsize SGD for the Cross-entropy Loss via Stochastic Lyapunov Stability
papers.abstract: Modern deep learning has been shown to operate using learning rates far larger than those justified by classical optimization theory. Most prior analyses of this phenomenon focus on deterministic gradient descent, leaving the stochastic setting largely unexplored. In this work, we provide sharp convergence guarantees for Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) applied to the multiclass cross-entropy loss, for both linear classifiers and two-layer neural networks. We show that the stochasticity of SGD may cause the dynamics to alternate between an edge-of-stability regime that is dominated by curvature-driven oscillations, and a stable regime in which the expected loss decreases at a controlled rate. Despite that, we prove that SGD stabilizes the dynamics, ensuring that the iterates return to stability in a fixed number of iterations and allowing convergence in the best-iterate sense even with large learning rates. Experiments validate our theoretical findings and illustrate the benefits of SGD in the large-stepsize regime.

papers.title: Spectral Properties of Dense Barabási-Albert Graphs
papers.abstract: Preferential attachment graphs model networks whose growth produces highly uneven degree distributions, describing many real-world systems. Their adjacency spectra are important because they allow graph-theoretic questions to be studied through the eigenvalues of matrices. We analyze the adjacency matrix of a dense Barabási-Albert (B-A) multigraph, where the number of edges added at each step is proportional to the final number of vertices. First, we compute the large-$n$ limit of the expected adjacency matrix and show that it is described by a rank-one limiting kernel, viewed as a continuous analogue of the adjacency matrix. After centering and scaling, the fluctuations form a random matrix with a computable variance profile. Using the quadratic vector equation approach, we derive the limiting bulk spectral distribution. We also determine the asymptotic location of the leading eigenvalue generated by the rank-one mean component.

papers.title: Bipartite cuts in Ramsey-Turán style
papers.abstract: We prove that every $K_5$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/18+o(1))$ edges, where the constant $1/18$ is best possible. The proof method is related to extensions of Turán Theorem in edge-weighted settings, and part of the proof uses flag algebra. Using a similar flag algebra formulation, AI proved that every $K_6$-free and $K_7$-free $n$-vertex graph with sublinear independence number can be made bipartite by removing at most $n^2(1/12+o(1))$ and $n^2(1/9+o(1))$ edges, respectively. These constants are best possible.

papers.title: Schubert cells for the super affine Grassmannian of $GL_{n|m}$
papers.abstract: We study Schubert cells in the affine Grassmannian of the general linear supergroup $GL_{n|m}$, focusing explicitly on the low-dimensional cases $n|m = 1|1$ and $2|1$. We define the affine super Grassmannian as an fpqc sheaf, describe its bounded-lattice filtration by finite-dimensional superschemes, and provide coordinate descriptions, equations, and morphisms for the cells that arise in low dimensions. For $GL_{2|1}$ the cells in the positive and negative chambers split as odd vector bundles over jet schemes of the projective line, and cyclic cells of $GL_{n|m}$ are jet schemes of projective superspaces. In the mixed-sign chamber the transition functions acquire nilpotent corrections in the even coordinate, and all cells except one are non-split. We also introduce decorations, which record the odd directions of the cells on the lattice graph.

papers.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
papers.abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dalečkii--Krein representation of the Fréchet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lovász $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lovász $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.

papers.title: Dynamic Programming without Contractivity
papers.abstract: Optimality results in dynamic programming are usually derived from contraction arguments, which require discounting or uniform bounds on termination times. We show that, in many useful settings, contractivity can be replaced by a simple global stability condition that requires no rate or uniformity. Under this condition and mild order-theoretic assumptions, we obtain existence of optimal policies, uniqueness of the value function as a solution to the Bellman equation, and convergence of value function iteration and of Howard and optimistic policy iteration. Applications include optimal stopping without discounting, where contraction methods can fail, and Bayesian sequential analysis.

papers.title: Gelfand--Kirillov dimensions of highest weight modules for basic classical Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We obtain explicit formulas for the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimensions of simple highest weight modules over basic classical Lie superalgebras. For the type II orthosymplectic superalgebras $D(m,n)$ and $B(m,n)$, we describe the associated varieties determined by highest weights relative to two Borel subalgebras. This gives algorithms valid for arbitrary complex highest weights, without integrality or typicality hypotheses. In type $B$, we further derive a formula for $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2n)$, distinguishing between integral and half-integral weights. For $G(3)$, $F(4)$ and $D(2,1;α)$, finite odd-reflection procedures give exact GK dimension formulas and finite-dimensionality criteria. We also describe the dependence on $α$ for $D(2,1;α)$. In type I, the GK dimension equals that of the simple even highest weight module for the distinguished Borel subalgebra. The computations rely on established ordinary Lie algebra formulas involving Lusztig's $\mathbf a$-function and Robinson--Schensted (RS) insertion.

papers.title: Non-Isomorphic Optimal Cayley Graphs
papers.abstract: We present eighty-nine optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs that are non-isomorphic to previously known optimal Cayley graphs with the same degree and diameter. For each graph, we provide comprehensive data on its parameters and structural invariants. Comparison with known constructions reported by Marston Conder on the Combinatorics Wiki and in related works reveals significant differences in girth, algebraic connectivity, domination number, automorphism group structure, cycle distributions, distance-related properties, and other graph invariants. These findings show that optimal degree-diameter Cayley graphs are frequently non-unique. The new examples enlarge the catalogue of known optimal graphs and provide benchmarks for investigations in degree-diameter problems, algebraic graph theory, and extremal graph theory. Since some of the graphs were identified through randomized search techniques, the collection is not exhaustive.

papers.title: Structured Adaptive Tensor Prediction for Streaming Data
papers.abstract: Matrix-valued time series arise in a wide range of applications, such as spatio-temporal data in medical imaging and geophysics. Existing forecasting methods are mainly designed for static settings, while adaptive filtering techniques have been largely limited to scalar- or vector-valued data. In this paper, we develop an adaptive tensor prediction framework for streaming matrix-valued data based on a Tensor-on-Matrix (ToM) regression model, in which the responses in a sliding window are lifted to a third-order tensor and the regression tensor is updated online by stochastic gradient descent (SGD). We derive the leading terms of the steady-state and tracking errors of SGD with overlapping windows, which show that the steady-state error is proportional to the step size and the noise variance, and that the step size governs a trade-off between noise and tracking. We further analyze the statistical accuracy of structured ToM regression within a single window. We establish a restricted isometry property, which holds when the window length is proportional to the input dimension, and derive recovery error bounds for sparse, low-rank and sparse plus low-rank regression tensors, which show that the recovery error scales with the intrinsic degrees of freedom rather than the ambient dimension. Simulations confirm the theoretical results, and the effectiveness of the structured adaptive updates is validated on the tracking of a drifting quantum gate, citywide crowd-flow prediction, and global total electron content (TEC) forecasting.

papers.title: Admissibility of Adaptive Monotone Step-Down Multiple Testing Procedures Under Arbitrary Covariance Dependence
papers.abstract: We study finite-sample admissibility for simultaneous testing of multivariate normal means under a vector loss whose components are the usual individual $0$--$1$ losses, with an arbitrary known positive-definite covariance matrix. For the two-sided problem, we establish admissibility for a broad class of procedures that rank active hypotheses using locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of suitably standardized conditional residuals. The result also covers residual-based sequential procedures with positive stage-specific cutoffs common to all active hypotheses at each stage, without requiring the cutoffs to be nonincreasing. The proof derives the interval structure of the acceptance sections from two properties: the previously rejected indices remain invariant while the hypothesis under study is active, and the stopping rule ensures that a perturbation leading to its rejection cannot defer that rejection beyond the stage at which the procedure at the unperturbed observation stops while accepting it. We also establish the corresponding one-sided result for locally adaptive, strictly increasing transformations of signed residuals, under both point-null and composite-null formulations and their respective vector losses. Together, these results extend vector-loss admissibility beyond the original Maximum Residual Down (MRD) procedure and identify a broader monotone ordering structure induced by covariance-adjusted residuals. We also show that the two-sided and one-sided classes are almost-everywhere limits of finite-support Bayes rules under their corresponding additive total losses; this representation, however, does not assert admissibility under those losses.

papers.title: Two Results on Outer-String Graphs
papers.abstract: An \emph{outer-string representation} of a graph $G$ is an intersection representation of $G$ where vertices are represented by curves (strings) inside the unit disk and each curve has exactly one endpoint on the boundary of the unit disk (the anchor of the curve). Additionally, if each two curves are allowed to cross at most once, we call this an \emph{outer-$1$-string representation} of $G$. If we impose a cyclic ordering on the vertices of $G$ and require the cyclic order of the anchors to respect this cyclic order, such a representation is called a \emph{constrained outer-string representation}. In this paper, we present two results about graphs admitting outer-string representations. Firstly, we show that for a bipartite graph $G$ (and, more generally, for any $\{C_3,C_5\}$-free graph $G$) with a given cyclic order of vertices, we can decide in polynomial time whether $G$ admits a constrained outer-string representation. Our algorithm follows from a characterization by a single forbidden configuration, similar to that of Biedl et al. [GD 2024] for chordal graphs. Secondly, we answer an open question from the same authors and show that determining whether a given graph admits an outer-1-string representation is NP-hard. More generally, we show that it is NP-hard to determine if a given graph $G$ admits an outer-$k$-string representation for any fixed $k\ge1$.

papers.title: An energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of ferronematic equilibrium states and its numerical realization
papers.abstract: We develop an energy-decreasing algorithm for the finite element approximation of two-dimensional ferronematic equilibrium states. The problem is formulated as the minimization of the harmonic energy of two two-dimensional vector fields, both with prescribed length, together with an additional nonlinear relation on the orientation of the two vectors. The finite element setting is based on piecewise continuous finite elements on a weakly acute triangulation. The numerical realization of the energy-decreasing algorithm employs a decomposition-coordination framework and a Uzawa-like iteration. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the computational performances of the algorithm.

papers.title: Homotopy exponents of polyhedral products
papers.abstract: We study Moore's conjecture and homotopy exponents for polyhedral products. For $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ where each $A_i$ is finite and has torsion-free homology, we prove that if $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$ is rationally hyperbolic, then it has no homotopy exponent at any odd prime. Under the additional hypothesis $ΣA_i$ is homotopy equivalent to a finite-type wedge of simply-connected spheres, we show Moore's conjecture holds for $(\underline{CA},\underline{A})^K$. We also give criteria such that, for a large family of polyhedral join products, the associated polyhedral products are rationally hyperbolic, mod-$p^r$ hyperbolic for all but finitely many primes, and have no homotopy exponent at all but finitely many primes.

papers.title: Structural Classes for Chollet's Permanent Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1982, Chollet conjectured that $\operatorname{per}(A\circ B)\le \operatorname{per}(A)\operatorname{per}(B)$ for Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices $A,B$, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard (entrywise) product. In this paper, we study natural structural classes for which the conjecture holds. We first show that a stronger inequality holds for a broad class of matrices with bipartite support. We then introduce a simple way of joining positive semidefinite matrices and give conditions under which Chollet's inequality is preserved under this operation. For graph Laplacians, this operation corresponds to vertex coalescence and gives larger structured graph families satisfying Chollet's inequality from simpler graph classes.

papers.title: Convolution invertibility for constructible sheaves and functions
papers.abstract: We characterize convolution-invertible, compactly supported piecewise-linear sheaves on a finite-dimensional real vector space. We show that they factor, up to a shift, as convolutions of constant sheaves on two bounded convex sets, one closed and the other relatively open. To this end, we first establish a more general characterization of convolution invertibility for compactly supported constructible functions. In the piecewise-linear case, this yields a convex factorization which lifts to sheaves. The key step is a geometric characterization of invertibility in the dual projective space via the Radon transform.

papers.title: Composition operators and Rational Inner Functions on the bidisc: A geometric approach
papers.abstract: We study composition operators acting on the weighted Bergman spaces on the bidisc, i.e. $C_Φ:A^2_β(\mathbb{D}^2)\to A^2_β(\mathbb{D}^2)$ where $Φ$ is induced by rational inner functions (RIFs) or a RIF and a smooth function (mixed case). Our approach is geometric. Our main result is a uniform criterion for all $β\in(-1,0]$ that can be summarized as follows: Boundedness of the composition operator is equivalent to transversal intersection of the level sets for non-smooth symbols, under the assumption that if any tangential intersection occurs on the singularity it must be of high order. This extends the characterization of Bayart-Kosiński to the non-smooth self maps of the bidisc. To reach our conclusions, we utilize results obtained by Anderson, Bergqvist, Bickel, Cima and Sola on Clark measures associated to RIFs and Puiseux factorizations.

papers.title: Sensor Placement for Tsunami Early Warning via Large-Scale Bayesian Optimal Experimental Design
papers.abstract: Real-time tsunami early warning relies on distributed sensor networks to infer seismic sources and seafloor motion. Optimizing these networks via Bayesian optimal experimental design (OED) is exceptionally challenging for systems governed by hyperbolic partial differential equations, which lack the spectral decay required by standard low-rank approximations. We present a scalable Bayesian OED framework for linear time-invariant systems. By reformulating the inverse problem in the data space, we transform OED into dense matrix subset selection. We propose a multi-GPU, Schur-complement-update-based, greedy algorithm that solves the OED problem using a pipelined approach that fully overlaps I/O with GPU computations. Our framework achieves near-perfect weak and strong scaling across hundreds of GPUs on Perlmutter and Frontier. Applied to the 2025 Gordon Bell Prize-winning digital twin for tsunami forecasting in the Cascadia Subduction Zone, we optimize a 175-sensor network, minimizing the uncertainty of a parameter field with over one billion degrees of freedom.

papers.title: On the size of $\{a: 1\leq a<n, n|a^2-1, a|n^2-1\}$ for number $n$: Connections to Fibonacci-like Sequences and Twin Primes
papers.abstract: For a positive integer n, let $\mathcal{A}(n)$ denote the set of integers $a$ satisfying $1 \leq a < n$ subject to the simultaneous modular conditions \(n \mid a^2 - 1\) and \(a \mid n^2 - 1\). In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and cardinality of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\). By establishing a precise algebraic correspondence between the elements of \(\mathcal{A}(n)\) and the integer evaluations of a family of Fibonacci-like sequences defined by a second-order recurrence, we prove that \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{} < \log_2 n +2\) for all composite $n > 1$. Trivially, $|\mathcal{A}(n)| = 2$ when $n$ is an odd prime power. Furthermore, we analyze the global distribution of these cardinalities, demonstrating that the asymptotic average of \(\vert{}\mathcal{A}(n)\vert{}\), for $n\leq x$, approaches $2 + o(1)$ as $x \to \infty$. Guided by the properties of the underlying algebraic mapping and supported by computational verification for all $n < 10^{15}$, we formulate the conjecture that $|\mathcal{A}(n)| \le 3$ uniformly for all $n$. In connection with this conjecture, we show that every integer $N$ that is the product of a pair of twin primes satisfies $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$, providing an explicit family of integers $N$ with $|\mathcal{A}(N)| = 3$.

papers.title: A Dyadic Frequency Law for a Perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the parity-perturbed Hofstadter $Q$-recursion defined by $$Q(1)=Q(2)=1,\qquad Q(n)=Q(n-Q(n-1))+Q(n-Q(n-2))+(-1)^n \quad(n\ge3).$$ for $n\ge3$. Cloître proved that the recursion is globally well-defined and encoded its odd- and even-indexed subsequences by binary arches and canonical plane forests. Let $F(s)=\#\{n\ge1:Q(n)=2s-1\}$, and let $ν_2(j)$ denote the exponent of $2$ in $j$. For every integer $k\ge0$, we prove the multiset identity $$ \{F(s):2^k\le s<2^{k+1}\}=\{3+ν_2(j):1\le j\le 2^k\}. $$ The proof expresses frequencies as sums of plateau lengths and folds reflected gap pairs to identify the excess frequencies $F(s)-3$ with the outdegrees of a canonical plane tree. For $k\ge2$, the maximum $k+3$ occurs at $s_k=\lceil 2^{k+2}/3\rceil$, and the second-largest frequency $k+2$ occurs at $s_k+1$. As a corollary, the sum with marks $z^{F(s)-3}$ and dyadic block weights $2^{-ku}$, multiplied by the Dirichlet eta function $η(u)$, has the Euler product of $ζ(u)$ with its factor at $2$ replaced by $(1-z2^{-u})^{-1}$. Finally, we prove that the dyadic defect $Q(2n)-2Q(n)$ attains order $n/\sqrt{\log n}$ in absolute value along a subsequence.

papers.title: An Alternative Proof of an Erd\H os-Rényi Law for the Longest Consecutive Monotone Block in a Random Permutation
papers.abstract: $\{X_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ of i.i.d.~($p$) coin-tosses, the longest run $L_n$ of heads in the first $n$ coin tosses approaches $\log_{1/p}n$ almost surely. In this paper we explore a formulation of this result in the case of random permutations and prove an Erd\H os-Rényi law for the longest consecutive monotone block in a random permutation. This problem has been studied before by several authors, and we offer a Poisson approximation viewpoint on this issue using the Stein-Chen method.

papers.title: Energy-variational solutions for geodynamical two-phase flows: From logarithmic to double-obstacle potentials by variational convergence
papers.abstract: In [Nonlinear Anal. Real World Appl. 93(2026), art. id. 104652] we studied a Cahn--Hilliard two-phase model describing the flow of two viscoelastoplastic fluids in the framework of dissipative solutions using a logarithmic potential for the phase-field variable. This choice of potential has the effect that the fluid mixture cannot fully separate into two pure phases. The notion of dissipative solutions is based on a relative energy-dissipation inequality featuring a suitable regularity weight. In this way, this is a very weak solution concept. In the present work, we study the well-posedness of the geodynamical two-phase flow in the notion of energy-variational solutions. They feature an additional scalar energy variable that majorizes the system energy along solutions and they are further characterized by a variational inequality that combines an energy-dissipation estimate with the weak formulation of the system adding an error term that accounts for the mismatch between the energy variable and the system energy multiplied by a suitable regularity weight. We give a comparison of these two concepts. We further study different phase-field potentials for the geodynamical two-phase flow model. In particular, we address the variational limit from a potential with a logarithmic contribution to a double-obstacle potential, then also allowing for the emergence of pure phases. This study underlines that, thanks to its structure, the energy-variational solution is better suited for variational convergence methods than the dissipative solution.

papers.title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for high dimensional Central Limit Theorem under moment conditions
papers.abstract: We characterize the dimension growth rate in the high dimensional central limit theorems (or CLTs) over hyper-rectangles. First, we find out the moment conditions that are both necessary and sufficient under the independence of the components. We consider four exhaustive classes, viz. when underlying random variables (I) have all polynomial moments, (II) have some polynomial moment of order higher than two, (III) have only second moment but no polynomial moment higher than two exists, and (IV) have infinite second moment, but belong to the domain of attraction of normal distribution. Next, we extend the sufficiency of the moment conditions in the Gaussian approximations of each of the aforementioned classes with same moment assumptions when the coordinates are dependent. For sub-Weibull marginals in Class (I), with $0<α\le1/6$, strong non-degeneracy yields the optimal range $\log p=o(n^{2α})$ which matches the rate obtained under coordinate-wise independence. However under marginal non-degeneracy, a Berry--Esseen bound gives the exponent $2α/(1+4α)$ up to logarithmic factors, and a counterexample proves that this exponent is optimal under marginal non-degeneracy. Under marginal non-degeneracy, Class (II) admits polynomial dimension growth up to logarithmic factors, while in Class (III) the marginal tails determine a growth rate, both of which again match with that when the coordinates are independent. In Class (IV), coordinate-wise normalization by truncated second moments yields a high dimensioonal CLT under additional tail and covariance conditions. Thus, we derive necessary and sufficient moment conditions for the validity of the CLT over hyper-rectangles in high dimensions in all possible regimes, showing that the CLT may hold under much weaker conditions compared to those present in the existing literature.

papers.title: Explicit analytic functions defining the images of simple wave-front singularities
papers.abstract: We construct explicit main-analytic functions for the images of the standard maps associated with simple wave-front singularities of types $A$, $D$, and $E$. The construction uses resultants of explicitly specified pairs of one-variable polynomials whose coefficients are expressed directly in the target coordinates of the standard maps. For types $A$ and $D$, it recovers one-variable discriminant representations. Using this, we give direct proofs of sharp bounds on the number of preimages of the standard map for types $A$ and $D$. For each of the exceptional types $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$, there exists an additional square factor in the resultant. Removing this factor gives the corresponding main-analytic function.

papers.title: Liouvillian integrability of vector fields in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider complex rational vector fields in dimension $n>2$ (equivalently, differential forms of degree $n-1$ in $n$ variables) which admit a Liouvillian first integral. Extending a classical result by Singer for $n=2$, our main result states that there exists a first integral which is obtained by two successive integrations from one-forms with coefficients in a finite algebraic extension of the rational function field. The proof uses Puiseux series in a novel way to simplify computations. We also apply this method to give elementary proofs of Singer's theorem for rational one-forms, and of the Prelle-Singer theorem on elementary integrability of rational vector fields.

papers.title: Random-Bridges as Stochastic Transports for Generative Models
papers.abstract: This paper motivates the use of random-bridges -- stochastic processes conditioned to take target distributions at fixed timepoints -- in the realm of generative modelling. Herein, random-bridges act as stochastic transports between two probability distributions when appropriately initialized, displaying either Markovian or non-Markovian, and continuous, discontinuous, or hybrid patterns depending on the choice of the driving process. We show how one can start from general probabilistic statements and branch out into specific representations for learning and simulation algorithms. Essentially, our framework formulates stochastic transports as noisy information processes governing the dynamic translation and propagation of information between arbitrary probability measures. Our theoretical and algorithmic presentation details training and simulation frameworks for both Gaussian and Lévy (specifically, Gamma, Poisson and Stable-$1/2$) random-bridge transports. The empirical validation focuses on the Gaussian case for demonstration and comparison purposes, where our construct delivers high-quality samples, achieving competitive Fréchet Inception Distance scores compared to widely used denoising diffusions and flow matching frameworks.

papers.title: Average-reward reinforcement learning in semi-Markov decision processes via relative value iteration
papers.abstract: This paper applies the authors' recent results on asynchronous stochastic approximation (SA) in the Borkar-Meyn framework to reinforcement learning in average-reward semi-Markov decision processes (SMDPs). We establish the convergence of an asynchronous SA analogue of Schweitzer's classical relative value iteration algorithm, RVI Q-learning, for finite-space, weakly communicating SMDPs. In particular, we show that the algorithm converges almost surely to a compact, connected subset of solutions to the average-reward optimality equation, with convergence to a unique, sample path-dependent solution under additional stepsize and asynchrony conditions. Moreover, to make full use of the SA framework, we introduce new monotonicity conditions for estimating the optimal reward rate in RVI Q-learning. These conditions substantially expand the previously considered algorithmic framework and are addressed through novel arguments in the stability and convergence analysis of RVI Q-learning.

papers.title: Minimally tough series-parallel graphs with toughness at least $1/2$
papers.abstract: Let $t$ be a positive real number. A graph is called \emph{$t$-tough} if the removal of any vertex set $S$ that disconnects the graph leaves at most $|S|/t$ components. The toughness of a graph is the largest $t$ for which the graph is $t$-tough. A graph is minimally $t$-tough if the toughness of the graph is $t$, and the deletion of any edge from the graph decreases the toughness. Series--parallel graphs are graphs with two distinguished vertices called terminals, formed recursively by two simple composition operations, series and parallel joins. They can be used to model series and parallel electric circuits. We characterize minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graphs for all $t\ge 1/2$. It is clear that there is no minimally $t$-tough series--parallel graph if $t>1$. We show that, for $1\ge t >1/2$, most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $t$ are minimally $t$-tough, but most of the series--parallel graphs with toughness $1/2$ are not minimally $1/2$-tough.

papers.title: Self-Normalized Inequalities for Time Series with Sample Variance Only and Their Application to Forecasting
papers.abstract: Evaluating a forecasting rule on a time series requires a risk bound that can be computed from the observed losses. Such generalization bounds rest on empirical Bernstein (EB) and self-normalized inequalities, which replace the unknown variance by a sample counterpart. These tools, however, have been developed almost exclusively for independent observations and martingale differences, and, for dependent data, the natural setting of forecasting, direct results are scarce. They require $β$-mixing and knowledge of the mixing coefficients, and their leading terms are not sharp. This paper fills this gap. We first establish, for martingale differences, an EB inequality in closed form that uses only the realized quadratic variation, holds with probability at least $1-α$ for every sample size, and is sharp under heteroscedasticity, whereas the sharpness of existing EB inequalities is established for a constant conditional variance. Building on this, we derive EB and self-normalized inequalities for the marginal mean of $\tildeφ$- and $τ$-mixing processes, a class that contains processes that are not even strongly mixing, such as autoregressions with Bernoulli innovations. The radii use nothing but a block sample variance: no variance proxy has to be designed or tuned, and, for $τ$-mixing processes, no dependence coefficient enters the radius. Under summability-type conditions on the dependence coefficients, their leading terms carry the constant of the oracle Bernstein inequality with the long-run variance, so, to our knowledge, these are the first sharp self-normalized inequalities under non-strong mixing conditions. As an application, we obtain a sharp upper bound on the risk of a time-series forecasting rule that is computed from its observed losses with a single block length and contains no dependence coefficient.

papers.title: A Riemannian Generalization of Wilks' Lambda for Testing Differences Among Brain Connectomes
papers.abstract: Analysis of variance (ANOVA) for grouped samples whose observations take values in a space with nontrivial geometric structure, either a differentiable manifold or a non-Euclidean metric space, is a problem that has received attention in recent years. This paper is concerned with brain connectomes. Functional data analysis is another important motivation. Most of the literature relies on approaches that assume very little about the geometric structure. The most prominent example is Fréchet ANOVA, a method that is valid in metric spaces under relatively weak hypotheses. We argue that the generality of these approaches has a price in statistical power. We propose an ANOVA test on the space of symmetric positive definite matrices with the affine-invariant Riemannian metric that exploits features specific to that space. The test is not easy to generalize to other settings, but we show that there is a notable difference in power relative to Fréchet ANOVA. We show it theoretically, by characterizing the asymptotic behavior of both tests for alternatives close to the null hypothesis. We also show it in practice, by describing the specific consequences of that difference for the analysis of brain imaging studies whose design involves collecting samples at multiple sites.

papers.title: A Semi-Lagrangian Adaptive Rank (SLAR) Method for High-Dimensional Vlasov Dynamics
papers.abstract: We extend our previous work on a semi-Lagrangian adaptive rank (SLAR) integrator, in the finite difference framework for nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson systems, to the general high-order tensor setting. The proposed scheme retains the high-order accuracy of semi-Lagrangian methods, ensuring stability for large time steps and avoiding dimensional splitting errors. The primary contribution of this paper is the novel extension of the algorithm from the matrix to the high-dimensional tensor setting, which enables the simulation of Vlasov models in up to six dimensions. The key technical components include (1) a third-order high-dimensional polynomial reconstruction that scales as $O(d^2)$, providing a point-wise approximation of the solution at the foot of characteristics in a semi-Lagrangian scheme; (2) a recursive hierarchical adaptive cross approximation of high-order tensors in a hierarchical Tucker format, characterized by a tensor tree; (3) a low-complexity Poisson solver in the hierarchical Tucker format that leverages the FFT for efficiency. The computed adaptive rank kinetic solutions exhibit low-rank structures within branches of the tensor tree resulting in substantial computational savings in both storage and time. The resulting algorithm achieves a computational complexity of $O(d^4 N r^{3+\lceil\log_2d\rceil})$, where $N$ is the number of grid points per dimension, $d$ is the problem dimension, and $r$ is the maximum rank in the tensor tree, overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Through extensive numerical tests, we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm and highlight its ability to capture complex solution structures while maintaining a computational complexity that scales linearly with $N$.

papers.title: On the Least Colossally Abundant Exception to Robin's Inequality
papers.abstract: Robin's Inequality posits $G(n)<e^γ$ for $n>5040$. Robin also showed that if the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) is false, then $G(n)>e^γ\left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^{b}}\right)$ for infinitely many values of $n$. By analyzing the prime or semiprime quotient $\displaystyle\frac{n}{m}$ for consecutive Colossally Abundant (CA) numbers $m$ followed by $n$ (where $m$ satisfies Robin's Inequality and $n$ violates it), we demonstrate that if the Riemann Hypothesis is false, then the least CA counterexample, $n$, must be constrained to the band $e^γ<G(n)<e^γ\left(1+\displaystyle\frac{c}{(\log n)^b}\right)$ where $0 < b < 1/2$ and $c\ge\displaystyle\frac{2\operatorname{gpf}(m)+1}{\operatorname{gpf}(m)^{2}}(\log n)^{b}$, i.e. for $c$ satisfying this lower bound, excluded from the infinite set beyond the higher threshold. The lower bound on $c$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.

papers.title: Dynamical feedback control with operator learning for the Vlasov-Poisson system
papers.abstract: To meet the demands of instantaneous control of instabilities over long time horizons in plasma fusion, we design a dynamic feedback control strategy for the Vlasov-Poisson system by constructing an operator that maps state perturbations to an external control field. In the first part of the paper, we propose learning such an operator using a neural network. Inspired by optimal control theory for linearized dynamics, we introduce a low-rank neural operator architecture and train it via adjoint state method. The resulting controller is effective at suppressing instabilities well beyond the training time horizon. To generalize control across varying initial data, we further introduce a novel cancellation-based control strategy that removes the destabilizing component of the electric field. This approach naturally defines an operator without requiring any training, ensures perturbation decay over infinite time, and demonstrates strong robustness under noisy feedback. Numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of the method in both one- and multidimensional settings.

papers.title: Teleoperator-Aware and CBF-Based Adaptive Nonlinear MPC for Shared Autonomy in Obstacle Avoidance of Legged Robots
papers.abstract: Safe and effective collaboration between humans and autonomous legged robots is a fundamental challenge in shared autonomy, particularly for teleoperated systems navigating cluttered environments. Shared autonomy for legged robots remains challenging due to uncertain human commands, collision-avoidance requirements, and the need to coordinate high-level planning with dynamically feasible locomotion. This paper presents a teleoperator-aware, control barrier function (CBF)-based, adaptive nonlinear model predictive control (ANMPC) framework for shared autonomy of quadrupedal robots in obstacle-avoidance tasks. The framework employs a prescribed arbitration weight between human and robot actions while modeling human inputs using a noisily rational Boltzmann model, whose parameters are adapted online through a projected gradient descent (PGD) law based on observed joystick commands. CBF constraints are incorporated into a computationally efficient NMPC formulation to promote obstacle avoidance while accounting for predicted human actions. The hierarchical architecture integrates high-level CBF-based ANMPC (10 Hz), mid-level dynamics-aware NMPC (60 Hz) enforcing single rigid body (SRB) dynamics, and low-level nonlinear whole-body control (500 Hz). Human-in-the-loop hardware experiments with ten participants on a Unitree Go2 quadruped demonstrate real-time feasibility and collision-free navigation across 50 trials. Shared autonomy reduced average human control effort by 51% and joystick activity from 88% to 42% of trial time, with comparable obstacle clearance and significantly higher perceived assistance than manual operation. Simulation-based ablation studies demonstrate improved obstacle clearance across operator rationality levels and up to a 66% reduction in median human-action prediction error through online adaptation.

papers.title: A Generalization of Ramanujan's Sum over Finite Rings
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalization of Ramanujan sums over finite rings and derive an explicit formula for these sums. These generalized Ramanujan sums coincide with the eigenvalues of the unitary Cayley graph $\mathrm{Cay}(R,R^{\times})$, as follows from Babai's result on Cayley graph spectra. This provides a useful approach to determining the spectrum of the unitary Cayley graph. Moreover, under a certain independence condition on the maximal left ideals, we show that our formula extends the classical formula for Ramanujan sums to finite rings.

papers.title: Conjugate continuous-discrete projection filter via sparse-Grid quadrature
papers.abstract: In this article, we study the continuous-discrete projection filter for exponential-family manifolds with conjugate likelihoods. We first derive the local projection error of the prediction step of the continuous-discrete projection filter. We then derive the exact Bayesian update algorithm for a class of discrete measurement processes with additive Gaussian noise. To control the stiffness of the natural parameters' ordinary differential equations, we introduce a regularization method via projection to the Fisher information metric's eigenspace. Lastly, we apply the proposed method to approximate the filtering density of a modified Van der Pol oscillator problem and a coupled stochastic FitzHugh--Nagumo system. The proposed projection filter shows superior performance compared to several state-of-the-art parametric continuous-discrete filtering methods.

papers.title: Strong convergence of uniformly random permutation representations of surface groups
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be the fundamental group of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. Consider the composition of a uniformly random element of $\mathrm{Hom}(Γ,S_n)$ with the $(n-1)$-dimensional irreducible representation of $S_n$. We prove the strong convergence in probability as $n\to\infty$ of this sequence of random representations to the regular representation of $Γ$. As a consequence, for any closed orientable hyperbolic surface $X$, with probability tending to one as $n\to\infty$, a uniformly random degree-$n$ covering space of $X$ has near optimal relative spectral gap --- ignoring the eigenvalues that arise from the base surface $X$. To do so, we show that the polynomial method of proving strong convergence can be extended beyond rational settings. To meet the requirements of this extension we prove two new kinds of results. First, we show there are effective polynomial approximations of expected values of traces of elements of $Γ$ under random homomorphisms to $S_{n}$. Secondly, we estimate the growth rates of probabilities that a finitely supported random walk on $Γ$ is a proper power after a given number of steps.

papers.title: Lyapunov Exponent Bounds for Random Products of Relaxed Projections
papers.abstract: Current performance bounds for randomized iterated projections, such as the Kaczmarz method, are often considered tight under per-iteration analyses, yet they are notoriously loose in practice. We derive asymptotic performance bounds that narrow this theory-practice gap, leveraging a new technique for bounding the spectral radii of operators arising in the Lyapunov exponent analysis of randomized iterations. The asymptotic analysis also uncovers the previously unexplained role of relaxation in improving performance, thereby resolving an open problem posed by Strohmer and Vershynin in 2007.

papers.title: Bridgeland Stability of Sheaves on del Pezzo Surface of Picard Rank Three
papers.abstract: We study the stability of line bundles and torsion sheaves under divisorial Bridgeland stability conditions. On the blow-up of $\mathbb{P}^2$ at two general points, we characterize stability and semistability of a line bundle, or of its shift in the tilted heart, in terms of the three $(-1)$-curves. We also prove that, on any smooth projective surface, the pushforward of a torsion-free sheaf of rank $1$ on an integral curve of nonpositive self-intersection is stable for every divisorial stability condition.

papers.title: Primitivity Testing in Free Group Algebras via Duality
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a field and $F$ a free group. By a classical result of Cohn and Lewin, the free group algebra $K\left[F\right]$ is a free ideal ring (FIR): a ring over which the submodules of free modules are themselves free, and of a well-defined rank. Given a finitely generated right ideal $I\leq K\left[F\right]$ and an element $f\in I$, we give an explicit algorithm determining whether $f$ is part of some basis of $I$. More generally, given free $K[F]$-modules $M\le N$, we provide algorithms determining whether $M$ is a free summand of $N$, and whether $N$ admits a free splitting relative to $M$. These can also be used to obtain analogous algorithms for free groups $H\le J$. As an aside, we also provide an algorithm to compute the intersection of two given submodules of a free $K\left[F\right]$-module. A key feature of this work is the introduction of a duality, induced by a matrix with entries in a free ideal ring, between the respective algebraic extensions of its column and row spaces.

papers.title: Localisation for the second-order Beckmann problem: bimartingale couplings and leaf decompositions
papers.abstract: We develop a second-order localisation theory for optimal transport based on leaf decompositions and bimartingale couplings, which impose martingale constraints in opposite directions on complementary orthogonal subspaces. It provides a second-order analogue of the classical decomposition of optimal transport into transport rays and monotone couplings: transport rays are replaced by the leaves of the $1$-Lipschitz derivative map $Du$ of an optimal dual potential $u\in C^{1,1}(\mathbb R^n)$, while monotone couplings are replaced by bimartingale couplings. We apply this framework to the three-marginal optimal transport problem introduced by Bolbotowski and Bouchitté, whose relaxation is the second-order Beckmann problem. We characterise the existence of bimartingale couplings through a convex-concave order condition. This yields a generalisation of Strassen's theorem from convex order to the convex-concave setting. Equivalently, the dual problem associated with the second-order Beckmann problem admits an optimiser whose derivative is an isometry. For absolutely continuous measures with common barycentre, assuming the existence of an optimal plan with absolutely continuous third marginal, we prove that every optimal plan decomposes into a family of problems on the leaves of $Du$. On each leaf, all optimal plans are completely described by bimartingale couplings between the corresponding conditional measures. Without this absolute continuity assumption on the third marginal, we show that the leaf decomposition persists in a more general form: optimal plans are mixtures of plans concentrated on triples $(x,y,z)$ satisfying $x\in \mathcal{S}_1$, $y\in \mathcal{S}_2$, and $z\in \mathcal{S}_1\cap \mathcal{S}_2$, where $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ are neighbouring leaves of $Du$.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of twisted maps to smooth pairs
papers.abstract: We study moduli spaces of twisted maps to a smooth pair in arbitrary genus, and give geometric explanations for the known comparisons between orbifold and logarithmic Gromov--Witten invariants. We classify the irreducible components of the space of twisted maps to the universal target in terms of tropical data, and show that each is built from torsors under semi-abelian varieties coming from Jacobians of the domain curves. Natural morphisms between these spaces for different rooting parameters measure how each component grows: for rooting parameters sufficiently large and divisible, the growth is monomial, with exponent between $0$ and $\max(0,2g-1)$, and the main component is the only one with exponent $0$. In genus $1$ the virtual class is the fundamental class, which recovers the polynomiality results of Tseng and You. We conclude with geometric examples, beginning with Maulik's original genus $1$ example.

papers.title: Criticality, splitting theorems under spectral Ricci bounds and the topology of stable minimal hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove general criticality criteria for operators $Δ+ V$ on manifolds with more than one end, where $V$ bounds the Ricci curvature, and a related spectral splitting theorem extending Cheeger-Gromoll's one. Our results give new insight on Li-Wang's theory of manifolds with a weighted Poincaré inequality. We apply them to study stable and $δ$-stable minimal hypersurfaces in manifolds with non-negative bi-Ricci or sectional curvature, in ambient dimension up to $5$ and $6$, respectively. In the special case where the ambient space is $\mathbb{R}^4$, we prove that a $1/3$-stable minimal hypersurface must either have one end or be a catenoid, and that proper, $δ$-stable minimal hypersurfaces with $δ> 1/3$ must be hyperplanes.

papers.title: Duality for Arithmetic $p$-adic Pro-étale Cohomology of Analytic Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove that the arithmetic $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper spaces over $K$ satisfies a duality, as conjectured by Colmez, Gilles and Nizioł. We derive it from the geometric duality on the Fargues-Fontaine curve by Galois descent techniques of Fontaine.

papers.title: The ring of stable characters over $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$
papers.abstract: For a fixed prime power $q$, let $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$ denote the family of groups $\text{GL}_N(q)$ for $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$. In this paper we study the $\mathbb{C}$-algebra of "stable" class functions of $\text{GL}_\bullet(q)$, and show it admits four different linear bases, each arising naturally in different settings. One such basis is that of stable irreducible characters, namely, the class functions spanned by the characters corresponding to finitely generated simple $\mathrm{VI}$-modules in the sense of [arXiv:1408.3694,arXiv:1602.00654]. A second one comes from characters of parabolic representations. The final two, one originally defined in [arXiv:1803.04155] and the other in [arXiv:2110.11099], are more combinatorial in nature. As corollaries, we clarify many properties of these four bases and prove a conjecture from [arXiv:2106.11587].

papers.title: Parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields)
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the parahoric reduction theory of formal connections (or Higgs fields) on a formal principal bundle with parahoric structures. This generalizes the reduction theory due to Hukuhara-Levelt-Turrittin and Babbitt-Varadarajan in the case without parahoric structures [7], and Boalch's result in the case of regular singularity [14]. As applications, we first prove that a formal connection is intrinsically regular if and only if it is a parahoric formal connection, in combination with the works of Bremer-Sage [45] and Chen-Kamgarpour [20], providing various criteria for the regularity of formal connections. We then introduce a notion of relative regularity for formal connections and give criterions. Finally, we demonstrate a parahoric version of Frenkel-Zhu's Borel reduction theorem of formal connections [33].

papers.title: A convergence result for a local planning problem for mean field games and rigorous proof of a Freidlin-Ventchel-type Large Deviations Principle for the $1+1$ KPZ equation
papers.abstract: We study an innovative connection between a very singular optimal transport variational problem with a congestion term connecting two Dirac measures, which is related to the planing problem in mean field games or gases with negative pressure, and a large deviation principle for the KPZ equation. The main result proves a limit of a singular approixmate problem with vanishing diffusive flux and a relaxed initial condition. The paper also provides a rigorous justification for the informal analysis of the ad hoc large deviation principle for the KPZ equation appearing in the physics literature.

papers.title: Cohomology of SL(3,Z) with coefficients in the standard representation
papers.abstract: This paper is a natural continuation of a joint paper with Bajpai, Harder and Moya Giusti \cite{BHHM}, even though it began as an answer to Goncharov's question. It that paper, we had complete description for all representations except for odd symmetric powers and their dual ones. For those representations we were left with two options: certain one dimensional module is a ghost space or not. Here we find the $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3)$ has ghost classes. It means that it is generated by a class from the cohomology of the Borel subgroup. With the techniques developed here, we show that the $d_2$ map of the spectral sequence for the boundary cohomology of $GL_4(\Z)$ is non-trivial if and only if there is a ghost class in $GL_3(\Z)$ (see Propositions 11 and 12.) We use a result of Elbaz-Vincent, Gangl and Soule to show that a spectral sequence related to $GL_4(\Z)$ does not degenerate at $E_2$-level. Then $d_2$ is non-trivial. Therefore, we obtain that $H^2(SL_3(\Z),V_3))$ is a ghost space, where $V_3$ is the standard representation.

papers.title: Local Statistics of Random Permutations from Free Products
papers.abstract: Let $α$ and $β$ be uniformly random permutations of orders $2$ and $3$, respectively, in $S_{N}$, and consider, say, the permutation $αβαβ^{-1}$. How many fixed points does this random permutation have on average? The current paper studies questions of this kind and relates them to surprising topological and algebraic invariants of elements in free products of groups. Formally, let $Γ=G_{1}*\ldots*G_{k}$ be a free product of groups where each of $G_1,\ldots,G_k$ is either finite, finitely generated free, or an orientable hyperbolic surface group. For a fixed element $γ\inΓ$, a $γ$-random permutation in the symmetric group $S_{N}$ is the image of $γ$ through a uniformly random homomorphism $Γ\to S_{N}$. In this paper we study local statistics of $γ$-random permutations and their asymptotics as $N$ grows.
