In this paper, we introduce the concept of strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators and then, discuss the properties about numerical radius orthogonality, strong numerical radius orthogonality of operators as well as relationship between them.

papers.title: Counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on weighted Catalan numbers
papers.abstract: We construct infinitely many counterexamples to a conjecture of Gao and Gu on when the 2-adic valuations of weighted Catalan numbers equal those of Catalan numbers.

papers.title: Tensor products of additive groups as reciprocity sheaves
papers.abstract: We compute the Nisnevich reciprocity sheaves associated with tensor products of the cube-invariant objects for the additive and multiplicative groups, with at least one additive factor. Over a perfect field of characteristic different from two, these sheaves decompose into direct sums of absolute K$ä$hler differential sheaves with binomial multiplicities. As an application, we compute the associated reciprocity sheaves of the Hochschild homology of the additive object.

papers.title: A Stochastic Tamed-Regularized Random Batch Method for Uncertain Particle Systems with Singularities
papers.abstract: The coefficients of particle systems often exhibit uncertainties due to incomplete knowledge. For particle systems with uncertainties and singularities in the drift and diffusion terms, existing methods may encounter numerical blow-up. In this paper, we propose a novel stochastic tamed-regularized Random Batch (str-RB) method for such uncertain particle systems with singularities. Specifically, since singularities in the diffusion term are more challenging than those in the drift term, building on a tamed scheme, we design an exponential regularization strategy that more effectively mitigates singularities in the diffusion term. This strategy ensures that the stochastic Galerkin (sG) projection coefficients remain finite even when the corresponding integrals for the original singular diffusion coefficient diverge. The sG method is applied to handle the random coefficients, and a random batch approach is then employed to reduce the computational complexity of large-scale simulations. Several theoretical properties of the proposed algorithm are established. Numerical tests demonstrate that the str-RB algorithm exhibits weak convergence, achieves lower errors than major existing methods across singular tests, and remains stable in a wider range of singular regimes. This work provides a robust and accurate approach for uncertain particle systems with singularities, laying a foundation for high-performance solvers in uncertain many-body dynamics.

papers.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
papers.abstract: Sample covariance matrices are fundamental objects in machine learning and statistics, with valuable information encoded into their eigenvalues. When treating modern problems, the scale of these matrices can become prohibitive for tractable computation. This creates a critical need for "spectral decompression": a method for inferring the eigenspectrum of a very large-scale model using only information from its smaller realizations. Existing methods fall into two main categories: those relying on spectral inversion; and those that rely on Free Decompression techniques. On the one hand, spectral inversion is a fundamentally ill-posed problem that is notoriously unstable, often failing to yield reliable results in finite-size settings. On the other hand, while Free Decompression was recently proposed to address this scaling, its reliance on the Nica-Speicher framework restricts its use to unitarily invariant ensembles, a symmetry condition that subsampled covariance matrices fail to satisfy. In this work, we introduce Deformed Decompression (DD), a novel framework for the stable, forward-extrapolation of spectral densities. By leveraging properties of the companion matrix, DD recasts the spectral decompression problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform of the companion matrix. This approach bypasses the instabilities of traditional inversion and provides a robust methodology for scaling covariance matrices and even their generalized variants (including Hessian matrices) that lack unitary invariance. We demonstrate the utility of our framework through experiments on a variety of random matrix examples, showing that DD successfully captures the complex spectral signatures of large-scale systems.

papers.title: An Infinite Family of Overpartition Congruences Modulo 1944
papers.abstract: Let $\overline p(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$. We prove that $\overline p(16^α(96n+76))\equiv0\pmod{1944}$ for all nonnegative integers $α$ and $n$, extending the congruence for $\overline p(96n+76)$ established by Smoot. The key step is a three-term congruence modulo $243$ relating $\overline p(m)$, $\overline p(16m)$, and $\overline p(256m)$ for $m\equiv4\pmod6$. We derive this relation and the two initial congruences using theta-function dissections. A separate theta-series argument establishes divisibility by $8$.

papers.title: On generation of the coefficient field of a primitive HMF by a single Fourier coefficient: An application of Nekovář's Theorem
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a non-CM primitive Hilbert modular form (HMF) over a totally real number field, of parallel even weight $k\geq 2$, with coefficient field $E_f$, and let $F_f \subseteq E_f$ denote the field fixed by the inner twists of $f$. In this article, we establish an analogue of Ribet's large image theorem for the residual Galois representations associated with $f$, by applying Nekovář's large image theorem (cf.~\cite[Theorem B.5.2]{Nek12}) to the automorphic representation $π(f)$ associated with $f$. As a result, we prove that if $f$ has no nontrivial inner twists, then $E_f$ is generated by a single prime Fourier coefficient, for a set of prime ideals of Dirichlet density one. We derive this result as a consequence of a more general theorem established for $F_f$.

papers.title: Semigroup Hessian Estimates for Underdamped Langevin Dynamics
papers.abstract:
For the semigroup $e^{t\mathcal L}$ of the underdamped Langevin dynamics, we bound the Hessian $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ when $
abla f$ is uniformly bounded. When the potential is strongly convex outside a ball and has bounded second and third derivatives, and the damping rate is above an explicit threshold, the bounds on $
abla^2(e^{t\mathcal L}f)$ decay exponentially in time with constants free of the dimension. The proof combines the Wasserstein contraction of the dynamics with a Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for the degenerate noise. As an application, we prove the uniform-in-time error of the stochastic gradient UBU integrator, with an explicit coefficient of the numerical bias in the step size, proportional to the covariance of the stochastic gradient noise.

papers.title: Uncovering Multimorbidity Patterns Through a Novel Randomized Clustering Algorithm
papers.abstract: Patients with several chronic conditions rarely share the same combination: in four years of the nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey (MEPS), we find 32,789 distinct combinations of two to seven conditions, and over 90% of those involving four or more occur in a single patient. Methods that search for common combinations discard most of this heterogeneity. We present the Randomized Length Sequential Clustering Algorithm (RLSCA), which links diseases by lift, a pairwise association measure counted only above a user-set support threshold. A mixed-integer program repeatedly selects and removes the group of conditions with the greatest internal lift, up to a random size; 100 iterations yield a database of clusters scored by size, rediscovery frequency, and body systems spanned. In MEPS 2019, stratified by age and sex, RLSCA recovers known groupings at a high threshold, such as diabetes with lipid disorders and hypertension, and at a lower threshold returns clusters of up to eight conditions spanning five body systems. Frequent itemset mining, at its lowest feasible support, finds no set above five conditions; hierarchical clustering cannot control cluster size. With a clinical large language model, the database could suggest which further conditions a patient is at risk of.

papers.title: Categorification of the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebras of polygons
papers.abstract: Let $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ be the reduced stated ${\rm SL}_n$-skein algebra of a polygon with $m$ boundary punctures ($m\geq 3$). Building on the quantum cluster algebra structure of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ established by Cao and the authors, and on the monoidal category $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ of finite-dimensional modules over the quantum affine algebra $U_q'(\widehat{\mathfrak{sl}}_n)$ introduced by Kashiwara, Kim, Oh and Park, where $Δ$ is the Garside element of ${\rm Br}_n$, we give a monoidal categorification of $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$. As a consequence, $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ has a basis with positive structure constants. A key role is played by the subalgebra $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ spanned by the stated $n$-webs whose $m-1$ edge weights are zero. We show that $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ is a quantum cluster algebra whose seed coincides with the Kashiwara--Kim--Oh--Park seed of $Δ^{m-2}$. Hence it is the quantum Grothendieck ring of a monoidal localization, at the frozen modules, of a subcategory of $\mathcal{C}(Δ^{m-2})$ with the same simple objects, and a quantization of the braid variety $X(Δ^{m-1})$. The whole algebra $\overline{\mathscr{S}}(\mathbb P_m)$ is a skew Laurent extension of $\mathcal A_{n,m}$ in $(m-1)(n-1)$ frozen variables.

papers.title: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
papers.abstract: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to explicit gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

papers.title: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
papers.abstract: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

papers.title: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
papers.abstract: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Rainbow Matchings in $K_{r+1}$-free Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}=\{G_1,\ldots,G_s\}$ be a system of graphs on the common vertex set with $n$ vertices. A graph $F$ with $s$ edges is rainbow if there is a bijection $φ:E(F)\to [s]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(F)$. For a family of graphs $\mathcal{F}$, the Turán number $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{F})$ is the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex graph which does not contain a member of $\mathcal{F}$ as a subgraph. Akiyama and Frankl proved that for $n\geq 2s$, the condition $e(G_i)>\operatorname{ex}(n,M_s)$ for each $i\in [s]$ guarantees a rainbow matching $M_s$. In this paper, we establish an analogous result for graph systems with bounded clique number. Namely, for positive integers $n,r,m$ with $n\geq 2m+2$ and $n$ sufficiently large in terms of $r$, we prove that if $G_i$ is $K_{r+1}$-free and $e(G_i)>\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_{r+1},M_{m+1}\})$ for each $i\in [m+1]$, then $\{G_1,\ldots,G_{m+1}\}$ admits a rainbow matching $M_{m+1}$. This result can be viewed as a rainbow analogue of a theorem of Alon and Frankl on the maximum number of edges in graphs with bounded clique number and matching number for sufficiently large $n$.

papers.title: The construction of a regular non-Berwald Landsberg surface
papers.abstract: We construct a regular non-Berwald Landsberg metric of zero flag curvature on an open subset of the plane via a periodically forced oscillator equation. We solve the associated return equation exactly to obtain closed, strongly convex coindicatrices. Starting from a finite truncation of a formal control, we use a uniform local inverse for a periodic comparison operator and a smoothing iteration to make the return map of the original oscillator equal to the identity on the chosen base neighborhood. A direct calculation of the spray exhibits a nonzero component of the Berwald tensor.

papers.title: Optimal long-time derivative estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the long-time behaviour of derivatives of the semigroup $P_t=e^{t\mathcal{A}}$ generated by the underdamped Langevin (kinetic Fokker-Planck) operator $\mathcal{A}$ on $L^2(μ)$, where the Gibbs measure $μ$ is not required to be finite. Under a weighted relative bound on the Hessian of the potential, we prove that for every integer $m\ge 0$ the squared $L^2(μ)$ norms of $\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ and of $\nabla_{x,v}\mathcal{A}^m P_t h_0$ are bounded by $C_m t^{-2m}\|h_0\|^2$ and $D_m t^{-(2m+1)}\|h_0\|^2$ respectively for large times, and the free dynamics shows that these exponents are optimal. The proof rests on a resolvent estimate near the imaginary axis, valid for every smooth potential, which follows from the adjoint relation between the generator and the velocity reversal and from the Gaussian Poincaré inequality in the velocity variable.

papers.title: Inference in High-Dimensional Linear Mediation Models
papers.abstract: Mediation analysis plays an important role in psychology, epidemiology, and genomics. Al- though high-dimensional mediation has been studied extensively, existing inferential methods typically rely on sparsity assumptions that may be difficult to justify when many individually weak mediators collectively produce a substantial effect. We study inference for both the over- all indirect effect and the effect transmitted through an individual mediator in a proportional high-dimensional regime, where the number of mediators and the sample size grow at compa- rable rates, without imposing sparsity on the mediator effects. Standard debiasing procedures for high-dimensional inference commonly rely on design-covariance information or additional structural assumptions on precision-matrix directions. In mediation models, however, the full outcome-design covariance depends on unknown mediator-model coefficients, creating an addi- tional challenge when such information or structure is unavailable. To address this challenge, we introduce an approximate debiasing procedure based on partial ridge regression and show that the resulting estimator is asymptotically bias-corrected and Gaussian. We also develop a cross-fitted estimator with a smaller asymptotic variance than its sample-split counterpart. In addition, we construct consistent estimators of the limiting variances of both the sample-split and cross-fitted estimators. Together, these results provide feasible inferential procedures for global and pathwise mediation effects.

papers.title: Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
papers.abstract: Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.

papers.title: Noncompactifiable Kähler threefolds with positive Ricci curvature
papers.abstract: We construct a complete Kähler threefold $(M,ω)$ with positive Ricci curvature and infinite-dimensional third rational homology. It admits no analytic compactification, answering Yau's compactification question negatively (see \cite{Yau1992}, Problem~71, p.~304). The metric is obtained by solving a complex Monge--Ampère equation on an affine threefold and lifting the solution to an infinite cyclic cover. Its Ricci form $ρ_ω$ satisfies $\int_Mρ_ω^3=\infty$, disproving the top Yang--Yau conjecture.

papers.title: Improved Constants in the Kautz-Singleton Construction for Probabilistic Group Testing
papers.abstract: We consider the probabilistic nonadaptive group testing problem, in which a uniformly random defective set of size $d$ is to be identified among $N$ items using a binary test matrix. For the explicit Kautz--Singleton construction, it is known that order-optimal scaling $T=Θ(d\log N)$ for high-probability recovery can be achieved in the regime $d=Ω(\log^2 N)$. However, the leading constant in this scaling remains uncharacterized even for standard low-complexity decoders. In this work, we revisit the probabilistic analysis of this construction and improve the leading constant for the COMP decoder, as well as establishing the same bound for the DD decoder. Our approach relies on a sharper analysis of the number of distinct roots associated with the defective items, yielding tighter bounds on the decoding error probability. In particular, we show that both COMP and DD achieve vanishing average error probability with $T\le (1/\ln 2+\varepsilon)d\log N$ tests for any $\varepsilon>0$, in the admissible regime $N=q^k$ for some prime power $q = Θ(d)$ and integer $k \ge 2$. For COMP, this leading constant matches that of the random near-constant column weight design, whereas for DD, a gap remains except in the sparse regime $d = N^{o(1)}$.

papers.title: Affine Boosted Gauss Curvature Flow
papers.abstract: We prove convexity in the affine orbit of entropies associated to Gauss curvature flow for sub-affine powers. This allows the construction of an affine boosted Gauss curvature flow, which keeps the evolving hypersurface at the affine minimizer of the Gaussian entropy. The modified flow has bounded isoperimetric ratio, and after rescaling it converges along a sequence of times to self-similar solutions of the Gauss curvature flow. The construction also proves existence of new self-similar solutions to Gauss curvature flow in the sub-affine regime.

papers.title: Certified pandigital approximations of $π$, $γ$, $δ$ and $e$
papers.abstract: In 2004 Erich Friedman asked for the best approximations of $π$, $e$, the Euler-Mascheroni constant $γ$ and Feigenbaum's constant $δ$ that use each of the digits $1, \dots, n$ exactly once, with addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponentiation, parentheses and the decimal point. We determine the optimal expressions for $π$, $γ$ and $δ$ for every $n \le 9$, with the digits in any order and in increasing order, and for $e$ when $n \le 6$. The optima are found by exhaustive search and certified by an independent algorithm that encloses every expression rigorously and decides each candidate with Arb and exact arithmetic; a second certified computation covers intermediate values of any size. Twenty-one entries improve the records published before this work; one of them, the optimal formula for $π$ with 1-9 (error $2.81 \cdot 10^{-14}$), was found independently by M. Verheyen, and we prove it optimal. For $e$, whose records come from identities between power towers, we prove that Bamberger's formula is optimal within the natural family of such identities. All code and certificates are public.

papers.title: Extinction conditions for a two-sex branching process with random mating and overlapping generations
papers.abstract: We propose a modification of the bisexual branching process with random mating and overlapping generations. Unlike the model of Molina and Mota (2024), our modification introduces probabilistic age-dependent survival that depends on the state of the population. Our modification preserves the general properties of the original process. We establish two sufficient conditions characterizing the subcritical and supercritical regimes of the process, i.e., extinction of the population with probability one and survival of the population with positive probability. The results are illustrated with numerical simulations of the process performed in Python.

papers.title: Max-Cut on Token Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

papers.title: Consistent interfacial flow numerics - Part II: The momentum convection term
papers.abstract: The two-phase Volume-of-Fluid solvers of OpenFOAM overpredict the horizontal water velocity near the crest of a water wave, and the error grows as the wave propagates. Part I of this series removed the spurious air velocities caused by the gravity term but left this error unchanged. Here we show that it is caused by the momentum convection term. Its mass flux is computed in the interface advection step from the velocity at the start of the time step, whereas the convected velocity is taken at the end of the step, because convection is discretised implicitly. In a progressive wave, where the horizontal and vertical velocities are 90 degrees out of phase, this time lag produces an upward flux of horizontal momentum, proportional to the time step, which accumulates in a spurious current near the surface. The same mismatch makes the response to a force depend on the density at the wrong time level. Explicit convection removes the lag and makes the response consistent with the gravity force, but requires the convected face velocity at the interface to be taken from the upwind cell. Only then is the new velocity of a cell a weighted average of old velocities, whatever the density ratio. We demonstrate both requirements with prescribed flows and with the full solver. For a progressive wave, explicit convection with upwind face velocities at the interface reduces the overprediction of the crest velocity from 26-31 % to within 1 % and removes the near-surface current. The resulting solver, fluxinator, is meant for maximum Courant numbers of 0.1 and below, where it keeps the wave height within 1.5 % over 15 periods on meshes with six or more cells per wave height. Because the spurious velocities that limit the time step are removed, it needs 34-42 % less wall-clock time than interFoam for the tested wave.

papers.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\mathscr{C}$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite. We prove a weak form of this conjecture and other results for Tannakian categories and in characteristic 0. Critical to the positive characteristic case is a functor constructed by Coulembier and Flake who were interested in higher Frobenius functors. We show that their construction, which relies on the theory of abelian envelopes, gives a natural source for semi-exact functors, and at least in the Tannakian setting gives all $\Bbbk$-linear, symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors.

papers.title: On pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian metrics
papers.abstract: In our previous work, we studied the squared $L^2$-norm functionals $\mathcal G$ of Gauduchon's torsion $1$-form and $\mathcal F$ of the Chern torsion over the space of all Hermitian metrics with unit volume on a compact complex manifold. We introduced torsion-critical metrics as critical points of $\mathcal F$. In this paper, We prove that a pluriclosed and astheno-Kähler metric is torsion-critical if and only if it is Kähler. In particular, every compact pluriclosed torsion-critical Hermitian threefold is Kähler. We also give explicit examples and derive geometric consequences under additional curvature assumptions.

papers.title: Character codegrees in $π$-separable groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the set $\operatorname{C}_π(G)$ of irreducible characters of a finite $π$-separable group $G$ whose codegrees (defined by Qian as $\operatorname{cod}(χ)=|G:\kerχ|/χ(1)$) are $π$-numbers, in relation to the Isaacs--Gajendragadkar classes of $π$-special characters $\operatorname{X}_π(G)$ and $\operatorname{B}_π$-characters $\operatorname{B}_π(G)$.

papers.title: The Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture fails over the reals
papers.abstract: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $F_A=[a_{i,j}\operatorname{per}(A(i,j))]$ for every positive semidefinite Hermitian $A$, where $A(i,j)$ deletes row $i$ and column $j$. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-$4$, $32\times32$ integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds $\operatorname{per}(A)$; verification uses integer arithmetic. Together, the two counterexamples resolve the Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture negatively over both fields. Counterexamples exist of every order $n\ge32$. As an application to quantum optics, the violation yields a $36$-mode orthogonal interferometer and a direction of relative arrival-time delays among $32$ photons with identical-variance Gaussian wave packets along which every sufficiently small nonzero delay increases the probability that all photons are detected within four designated output modes.

papers.title: Banchoff Curvature and Realisation Moduli of Piecewise-Affine Arrangement Immersions
papers.abstract: We compute the curvature concentrated on the flats of a piecewise-affine immersion of $\mathbb{R}^D$ into $\mathbb{R}^n$ creased along an affine hyperplane arrangement, and parametrise the immersions sharing its chamber metrics. Suppose every transverse crease cone is embedded (the positive-path-rank condition). Then the Gauss-Bonnet-Chern density of any convex coordinate-wise smoothing that is affine outside a compact transition zone reduces, on each transverse slice, to a Hafnian. This Hafnian integrates to Banchoff's critical-point curvature on each even-codimension flat. The curvature coincides with the Cheeger-Müller-Schrader density and equals an alternating sum of Gaussian orthant probabilities determined by Schur complements of the incident chamber metrics. In even dimension, under mild non-degeneracy, total vertex curvature equals the recession curvature at infinity and is unchanged when the walls are translated, even across multi-wall collisions. Under generic codimension-two intersections, realisations with prescribed chamber metrics form a compact rank-constrained spectrahedron of generic local dimension $\max(0,H-r(r+1)/2)$, where $r = \max(0,D+H-n)$. At minimal target dimension the given immersion is the unique realisation preserving orientation across each single wall, and a positive semidefinite stress matrix certifies universal rigidity.

papers.title: KL-Guided Support Selection and Subspace Cubic Newton Methods for Sparse Optimization
papers.abstract: We study sparse composite optimization with a smooth loss and a possibly nonconvex, nonsmooth regularizer. The objective is locally smooth on each fixed support. Our method combines full-space proximal-gradient steps with inexact cubic-regularized Newton steps on a subspace selected by thresholding. If the iterates are bounded and the objective satisfies the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property, the entire sequence converges to a first-order stationary point. A threshold based on the KL exponent ensures that the selected coordinate set coincides with the support of the limit after finitely many iterations, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption. We also provide a residual-based threshold when such an exponent exists and its value is unknown. Under an additional continuity assumption on the restricted Hessian, the line search eventually accepts full cubic steps. With bounded cubic regularization parameters and damping parameters chosen to meet the target tolerances, we bound the number of outer iterations needed to reach restricted approximate second-order stationarity after support identification and entry into the full-step regime. We conduct numerical experiments in two settings: when the KL exponent is known and when it is unknown. In the former case, we use a degenerate problem to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. In the latter case, we compare the proposed method and its adaptive variant with existing solvers on sparse recovery and logistic regression problems.

papers.title: Commutants of diagonal operators
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal, tiny or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.

papers.title: Equivariant Flow Matching on Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: Flow matching enables the training of networks that can flow samples from an initial to a target distribution. The network is regressed against simple vector fields that are conditioned on end points in the target distribution. In the Euclidean case, these conditional vector fields induce flows along straight lines. Various generalisations have been proposed to perform flow matching on spaces where straight lines are not well-defined, such as Riemannian manifolds and Lie groups. Riemannian flow matching applies to many domains, but typically requires expensive simulation, while flow matching on Lie groups is simulation-free but only works on Lie groups. In this work, we develop equivariant flow matching on homogeneous spaces, which generalises flow matching on Lie groups, while remaining simulation-free. We also derive all generators connecting pairs of position-orientations and perform a similar derivation for event-velocity space, the Lorentzian analogue of position-orientation space, so that we can perform flow matching on these spaces.

papers.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
papers.abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

papers.title: The monogenicity of $\boldsymbol{x^n+c\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}a^{n-j-1}x^j}$
papers.abstract: We say that a monic polynomial $f(x)\in {\mathbb Z}[x]$ is {\em monogenic} if $f(x)$ is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$ and $\{1,θ,θ^2,\ldots,θ^{{\rm deg}(f)-1}\}$ is a basis for the ring of integers of ${\mathbb Q}(θ)$, where $f(θ)=0$. Let $n,a,c\in {\mathbb Z}$ with $n\ge 3$, and suppose that \[{\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x):=x^n+cx^{n-1}+acx^{n-2}+a^2cx^{n-3}+\cdots +a^{n-2}cx+a^{n-1}c\] is irreducible over ${\mathbb Q}$. Recently, Jakhar, Kalwaniya and Yadav have given necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$, under the assumption that all prime divisors of the discriminant of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ not dividing $ac$ also do not divide $n+1$. In this note, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the monogenicity of ${\mathcal F}_{n,a,c}(x)$ without this restriction.

papers.title: Absence of binding for the helium anion
papers.abstract: We study the helium anion in the nonrelativistic Coulomb model with an infinitely massive nucleus and spin-$\frac12$ electrons. We prove the absence of binding, with $E^{\mathrm{F}}(3,2)=E^{\mathrm{F}}(2,2)$ and no three-electron ground state. A decomposition relative to the helium ground state and completion of the square reduce the problem to a one-dimensional variational inequality.

papers.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,ξ)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold with infinitely many Stein fillings. Since $(ST^*K,ξ_{\mathrm{can}})$ has a unique minimal symplectic filling up to homeomorphism, finiteness of fillings is not preserved under Legendrian surgery, even for planar contact $3$--manifolds. The same construction gives the planar contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings found earlier by the author. Finally, we use Luttinger twists along the Klein bottle to construct contact $3$--manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings, without the use of open books or Lefschetz fibrations.

papers.title: Weak and Strong Moments of Log-Concave Measures
papers.abstract: Let $X\in\mathbb{R}^d$ be a log-concave random vector, and let $N$ be a seminorm on $\mathbb{R}^d$. For $p\ge 1$, we show that $\|N(X)\|_p$ is at most $\mathbb{E} N(X)+C s_p$, where $s_p$ is the supremum of $\|u(X)\|_p$ over all linear functionals $u$ satisfying $|u(x)|\le N(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. A choice for $C$ is $2+2e$. This bound implies Latała's conjecture on weak and strong moments.

papers.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
papers.abstract: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. This includes the forward and reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and generalized Jensen-Shannon divergence (JSD), as well as Monte Carlo KL estimates and entropy. When the distributions are nearly equal, rounding and cancellation issues affect the forward and gradient computations. These issues can affect settings using divergences in optimization objectives, such as knowledge distillation, reinforcement learning, and proximal methods. We propose numerically stable reformulations and provide example implementations for each setting, validated by property-based tests.

papers.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.

papers.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
papers.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

papers.title: Completely Regular Growth of Transcendental Entire Solutions to Linear Difference Equations with Polynomial Coefficients
papers.abstract: Let \(f\) be a transcendental entire solution of order less than one of the linear difference equation \[ \sum_{j=0}^{m}P_j(z)Δ^j f(z)=0, \qquad P_m\not\equiv0, \] where \(P_0,\ldots,P_m\) are polynomials. Applying the inverse Newton transform \(\mathcal S\), which maps the falling factorial \(z^{\underline n}\) to \(z^n\), we obtain a function \(g=\mathcal S f\) satisfying a nontrivial linear differential equation with polynomial coefficients. We further prove that the Newton transform preserves completely regular growth in the Levin-Pfluger sense. Consequently, \(f\) is of completely regular growth, and its zeros are regularly distributed. An example involving the Gamma function shows that the conclusion may fail for solutions of order 1. Finally, we provide examples of linear difference equations with entire coefficients that admit solutions which are not of completely regular growth, even when all the coefficients are themselves of completely regular growth.

papers.title: Incidence Geometry with Polarity and Tiled Surfaces
papers.abstract: In 2023, Fomin and Pylyavskyy introduced the master theorem to find and prove linear incidence theorems using quadrilateral tilings of oriented surfaces. Each face of the surface corresponds to an incidence condition, which they call a coherence condition. We extend their master theorem by incorporating polarity into coherence and allowing nonorientable surfaces. Our new coherence condition can be interpreted as perpendicularity from the perspective of Cayley--Klein geometry. Moreover, a polarity incidence theorem on a nonorientable tiled surface gives rise to a self-polar linear incidence theorem on the orientation double cover. We also extend the master theorem to Hermitian polarities over division rings, with its validity depending on the topology of the surface. Finally, we determine which incidence presentations admit proofs using tilings. When such proofs exist, we express the minimum Euler genus of the corresponding tiling in terms of the fundamental group.

papers.title: Normal Limits of the Squeezing Function and Strict Pseudoconvexity
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a boundary point of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, and suppose the squeezing function tends to $1$ along the inward normal at $p$. We show that $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is $C^{2,α}$ near $p$ for some $0<α\le1$, without assuming finite type or convexity. The proof begins under local $C^2$ regularity near $p$. A comparison of Bergman kernels rules out nonconstant holomorphic curve germs through $p$ contained in the boundary. With these curve germs excluded, rescaled normal translations give rise to a holomorphic semigroup. Classifying this semigroup identifies the normalized kernel limit at selected scales and yields the logarithmic growth exponent $n+1$ for the diagonal Bergman kernel along the inward normal. Under the $C^{2,α}$ assumption, Levi degeneracy at $p$ would give a kernel upper bound with exponent strictly below $n+1$. This contradiction proves $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex.

papers.title: Solutions of the set-theoretic quantum Yang-Baxter equation arising from posets
papers.abstract: Victoria Lebed observed that the map $(x, \, y) \mapsto (\min\{x, \, y\}, \, \max\{x, \, y\})$ on a totally ordered set is an idempotent solution of the braid equation. We extend this example in several directions, by constructing four families of solutions of the braid equation associated to posets. First, for a given poset $P$, the map $R_P$ which sorts the comparable pairs and fixes the incomparable ones is an idempotent solution of the braid equation whose automorphism group is the automorphism group of the poset $P$. Combined with the classical theorem of Birkhoff, this shows that every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of an idempotent solution of the braid equation of the form $(P, \, R_P)$, for some poset $P$. Moreover, $R_P \cong R_Q$ if and only if $P \cong Q$, and the solutions of the form $R_P$ are exactly the idempotent solutions of the braid equation which permute the components of each pair. Secondly, we classify all the solutions $R$ of the braid equation on an arbitrary set $X$ such that $R(x, \, y) \in \{(x, \, y), \, (y, \, x)\}$ for all $x$, $y\in X$: they are exactly the solutions $R_{\mathcal{P}}$ associated to the decompositions $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ into posets. Finally, we associate to any finite poset $P$ two involutive solutions $D_P$ and $E_P$ of the braid equation, whose automorphism groups are $(\mathbb{Z}/2)^P \rtimes {\rm Aut} (P)$ and, if $P$ is connected and has at least two elements, the group of automorphisms and anti-automorphisms of $P$.

papers.title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization with Applications
papers.abstract: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

papers.title: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ is $12$
papers.abstract: The $\mathbb Q$-gonality of the modular curve $X_1(N)$ is known for all $N\le 40$ by work of Derickx and van Hoeij. We prove that the $\mathbb F_5$-gonality and the $\mathbb Q$-gonality of $X_1(42)$ are both $12$. The upper bound $12$ was already known, and we raise the previous lower bound from $10$ to $12$. Since the set of rational points of the Jacobian, $J_1(42)(\mathbb Q)$, is finite, it follows that $12$ is the least degree in which $X_1(42)$ has infinitely many points. The lower bound comes from an exhaustive search over Riemann--Roch spaces on $X_1(42)$ over $\mathbb F_5$, following Derickx and van Hoeij. We reduce this search by the orbits of a cyclic group of automorphisms of order $12$ on places of degree at most $5$. This leaves $743\,231$ Riemann--Roch spaces, about a quarter of the number needed by the earlier method. We prove the reductions and provide the code and data needed to reproduce the computations.

papers.title: Extensions from positive and full unit spheres of $C^\infty([0,1])$ with compatible Frechet metrics
papers.abstract: We study how the order of positivity determines the form of a linear isometric extension from the positive unit sphere of $C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb F)$, where $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$. At order zero, positivity means that $f(t)\in[0,\infty)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$. At order $m\ge1$, we require $f^{(m)}(t)\in[0,\infty)$ for every $t\in[0,1]$ and $f^{(j)}(x_0)\in[0,\infty)$ for $0\le j<m$, where $x_0$ is a fixed anchor. For the compatible Fréchet metrics $ρ_{m,p}$ studied here, we prove that every surjective isometry of the positive unit sphere extends uniquely to a surjective $\mathbb F$-linear isometry of the whole space. This holds for all $1\le p\le\infty$ at order zero and for $p=\infty$ under an explicit anchor condition at higher orders. At order zero, the extension either fixes every function or acts by reflection of the interval. Reflection is possible exactly when $p=\infty$ or $x_0=1/2$. At higher orders, the extension acts on the $m$th derivative by the identity or reflection and may permute the lower-order derivative values at the anchor. A counterexample shows that, for a different compatible metric, reflection can preserve distances on the positive unit sphere without admitting a real-linear isometric extension. We also classify the surjective isometries of the full unit sphere at order zero and prove that each extends uniquely to a surjective real-linear isometry of the whole space.

papers.title: Solid factors associated to the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ on $\mathbb{Z}^n$
papers.abstract: Let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. Set $Γ_n=SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$ (respectively $PSL_2(\mathbb{Z})$) for $n$ even (respectively for $n$ odd). Then $Γ_n$ acts on $\mathbb{Z}^n$ through the restriction of the linear action of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that the von Neumann algebra $L(\mathbb{Z}^n\rtimes Γ_n)$ is a solid factor. This generalizes the case $n=2$ proved by N. Ozawa.

papers.title: Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. Similar results are obtained in the completely bounded category as well as for the algebras $A(V)$ when $V$ is assumed homogeneous. In the case of homogeneous varieties $V$ and $W$, we obtain a sharper classification result, by which $H^\infty(V)$ is (completely) boundedly isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if there is a linear map which gives a bi-Lipschitz bijection between $\widetilde{W}$ and $\widetilde{V}$. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

papers.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
papers.abstract: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

papers.title: Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
papers.abstract: We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

papers.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
papers.abstract:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A separate package in the repository imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.1, which moves the whole library to Lean v4.35.

papers.title: The Maximum Second Zagreb Spectral Radius of Trees, Unicyclic Graphs and Bicyclic Graphs
papers.abstract: The second Zagreb matrix of a graph $G$ is $Z(G)=D(G)A(G)D(G)$, where $D(G)$ and $A(G)$ are the degree matrix and the adjacency matrix of $G$. For many degree-based weighted adjacency matrices, the trees, unicyclic graphs and bicyclic graphs with the largest spectral radius have a vertex adjacent to all others, and Mei et al. conjectured this for every such matrix on unicyclic graphs. Jiang et al. showed that $Z(G)$ is a counterexample. We prove that, for $q\in\{0,1,2\}$ and every $n\ge4$, the connected graph of order $n$ and cyclomatic number $q$ maximizing the spectral radius of $Z(G)$ is unique, and is obtained from two adjacent vertices with $q$ common neighbours by attaching $n-q-2$ pendent vertices to them as evenly as possible. The only exceptions are the star for $q=0$ and $n\le7$, and the triangle with one pendent vertex at each vertex for $q=1$ and $n=6$. This confirms a conjecture of Jiang et al.\ and all three parts of a conjecture of Shen and Shan for this matrix, with best possible thresholds on $n$. For $n\ge8$, the maximum value is $\lfloor (n+q)^2/4\rfloor+(n+q)/2+7q-2+O(1/n)$, whereas the star gives only $(n-1)^{3/2}$. A key tool is a determinant criterion that reduces spectral comparisons to sign conditions on explicit polynomials.

papers.title: Relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel of a reductive group over a global field
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm and a computer program computing the relative Tate-Shafarevich kernel $Sha^S(K,G)$ of a reductive group $G$ over a global field $K$ with respect to a finite set $S$ of places of $K$ containing no archimedean places. We assume that we know the algebraic fundamental group $Λ=π_1^{alg}(G)$ together with the action on it of the Galois group $Θ=Gal(L/K)$, where $L/K$ is a finite Galois extension with no real places such that $Gal(K^s/L)$ acts trivially on $Λ$. We also assume that we know the decomposition subgroups $Θ_v\subseteq Θ$ for all places $v$ in $S$, and all non-cyclic decomposition subgroups $Θ_v$ for $v$ outside $S$. Under certain conditions, we compute the set $Sha^S(K,G)$ also when $S$ contains archimedean places.

papers.title: Galois-modular obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings
papers.abstract: In this article we establish new obstructions to the categorification of near-group fusion rings by combining the values of irreducible characters of the Grothendieck ring with the Galois symmetry of the induced unit object $I(1)$ in the Drinfeld center. As a result, we show that a near-group ring of type $G+m$, where $G$ is an abelian group and both $|G|$ and $m$ are odd, can only categorify if $m=|G|$.

papers.title: Quadratic Hubbard trees, automata, and ray connections
papers.abstract: We describe an algorithm that, given a postcritically finite quadratic polynomial, outputs a finite state machine whose regular language is the set of angles whose dynamical rays land on the Hubbard tree, generalizing an example of Milnor. We do this by extracting orbit portraits from angled internal addresses, and constructing a suitable Markov partition of angle intervals. A main application is computing direct ray connections between Hubbard trees in matings of quadratic polynomials, and understanding when ray connections between the trees first appear when moving along veins of the Mandelbrot set. If one of the mating parameters is fixed, we prove that first ray connections are picked up at parabolic parameters or tips of veins. We also prove that the locus of parameter pairs in two given veins for which there are no ray connections between the trees is open. Additionally, we show that there are no ray connections between small Julia sets in matings of locally connected rabbit tunings.

papers.title: Chain Conditions for Abelian Normal Subgroups
papers.abstract: We investigate various chain conditions for abelian normal subgroups of groups, following Robinson (1968). We focus on the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups, an exceptional case excluded from his results except for some counterexamples. In particular we show that a hypercentral group satisfies the maximal condition for abelian normal subgroups if and only if it is is finitely generated nilpotent.

papers.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
papers.abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $τ$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $σ= σ(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|ζ(σ+ \mathrm{i}τ+ \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_θ = \smash{[ - (\log T)^θ,(\log T)^θ]}$, for every fixed $θ> 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $σ- 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + θ})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(σ+ \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.

papers.title: Gaussian-efficient nonasymptotic confidence sets for unbounded means
papers.abstract: Consider the classical statistical problem of sub-Gaussian mean estimation under martingale dependence: given $n$ observations with conditional mean $μ$ and a known conditional sub-Gaussian proxy $s>0$, we seek a nonasymptotically valid confidence interval for $μ$. The usual Chernoff interval has half-width $s\sqrt{2\log(2/α)/n}$; it neither adapts to the actual standard deviation $σ\le s$ nor attains the Gaussian quantile $z_{1-α/2}$. We construct an analytically closed-form nonasymptotically-valid interval under martingale dependence whose endpoints, at every iid law with $σ> 0$, agree almost surely to first order with $\bar X_n\pmσz_{1-α/2}/\sqrt n$. The two new building blocks are a sub-Gaussian exponential supermartingale with an \emph{empirical} quadratic variance and a cubic correction term, and a sub-Gaussian continuation supermartingale, the former delivering variance adaptivity ("Empirical-Bernstein'' for unbounded data), the latter also providing the Gaussian quantile ("Empirical-Berry-Esseen'' for unbounded data). The same constructions yield a closed-form time-uniform confidence sequence with asymptotically unimprovable half-width $σ\sqrt{2\log\log n/n}$. We also give closed-form multivariate ellipsoids with the true-covariance chi-square limit, and extend the scalar Gaussian and LIL constructions to handle heavy-tailed settings where one only knows a bound on any absolute central moment of order greater than two. Experiments show substantial width reductions when the true variance is smaller than the implied variance bound, at small loss in the boundary cases. The surprising (to us) takeaway message is: given any more than two moments, one can construct fully data dependent nonasymptotic confidence sets for the mean that are asymptotically efficient.

papers.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
papers.abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Zöberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

papers.title: Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of K3 surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex K3 surfaces of Picard number two. Together with the recent result for abelian surfaces and the known K3 cases, this settles the remaining case of Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic automorphisms of smooth projective complex surfaces with trivial canonical bundle. More generally, we prove Bloch's conjecture for (anti-)symplectic derived autoequivalences of projective K3 surfaces whose Picard number is at least three, or is two with anisotropic Néron--Severi lattice. The key new result is the congruence property of the subgroup generated by reflective involutions in $O(U\oplus N)$ for anisotropic even lattices $N$ of signature $(1,1)$. Combined with the local generation theorem and Chow-theoretic criterion of Li--Yu--Zhang, this gives the required reflective decompositions and their consequences for zero-cycles. For Picard number one and for isotropic Néron--Severi lattices of rank two, we further obtain modular-curve criteria for generation by reflective involutions and unipotent isometries, including a complete classification in the split case $N\cong U(d)$.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp bound $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$ for the threefold additive energy of every lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, with an absolute constant. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ estimate for eigenfunctions on $\mathbb{T}^2$, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical uniform $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and confirms Bourgain's conjecture in this range. For all $k\ge4$, we obtain the fixed power saving for the $k$-fold additive energy $J_k(P_n)\le C|P_n|^{2k-3-δ}$, with absolute constants $C,δ>0$. Applications include mean-square convergence of observables and the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.

papers.title: Error analysis and optimal sample allocation for randomized unbiased estimation: the single term estimator
papers.abstract: Randomized unbiased estimation can be highly efficient for approximating expectations of functionals of stochastic differential equations. However, in practice, the optimal computational efficiency is rarely attained due to errors arising from parameter estimation and truncation. The effects of these errors on computational efficiency have not been investigated. In this article, we study the error analysis and optimal sample allocation for the single term estimator. Specifically, under mild assumptions on the estimated parameters, we develop a unified error analysis that incorporates both sources of error, and establish the relevant convergence rates for the computational efficiency loss. Based on this analysis, we further investigate the optimal allocation of the computational budget for parameter estimation, and propose several efficient sample allocation strategies. Numerical experiments support the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods.

papers.title: A superprocess model for eDNA transport in random river environment
papers.abstract: Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.

papers.title: The generalized Dixmier conjecture and the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the two-dimensional Jacobian conjecture $\mathrm{JC}_2$ implies the generalized Dixmier conjecture $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ for the first Weyl algebra $A_1$, which states, in one of several equivalent formulations, that every endomorphism of the two-by-two matrix ring $\operatorname{Mat}_2(A_1)$ is invertible. To study the converse, we associate to each endomorphism of $\mathbb A^2_{\mathbb C}$ with Jacobian one a family of holonomic $A_2(k)$-modules over finite fields $k$. Kontsevich's conjecture predicts the existence of a $\mathcal D$-module in characteristic zero, unique up to isomorphism, whose reductions to positive characteristic are isomorphic to the prescribed modules. We prove uniqueness whenever such a lift exists. If these lifts exist for every such endomorphism, then $\mathrm{DC}'_1$ implies $\mathrm{JC}_2$. For every $n\ge2$, we construct a Lagrangian subvariety of $T^*\mathbb A^n$ that provides a counterexample to Kontsevich's conjecture. We also study an ultraproduct version of the lifting problem: whether these finite-field modules can be recovered as reductions of a single module in characteristic zero along a chosen ultrafilter. We prove that this is possible precisely when the Berest--Wilson invariants of these modules, regarded as left $A_1(k)$-modules, are bounded along that ultrafilter. Finally, we study two other conjectures of Kontsevich on arithmetic support, giving a counterexample to one and partial results on the other.

papers.title: Linear statistics in the Coulomb gas: cumulants beyond rotational invariance
papers.abstract: We consider a classical Coulomb gas of $N$ particles in dimension $d\geq2$, confined by a general external potential $U$ in the large-$N$ limit. In that limit the density of particles has a compact support called the droplet. We study smooth linear statistics ${\mathcal L}_N=\sum_{i=1}^N f({\bf x}_i)$ at large $N$. While the leading variance of ${\mathcal L}_N$ is by now well understood in many settings, much less is known about higher cumulants. When $f({\bf x})=f(|{\bf x}|)$ and the potential is rotationally invariant, these cumulants were computed recently at leading order. We derive explicit formulas for the leading third and fourth cumulants for general smooth droplets, without assuming that either the potential or the test function is radial. The answers are expressed as intrinsic boundary integrals over the equilibrium droplet. The third cumulant depends on the cube of the jump of the normal derivative of the harmonic extension of $f$, while the fourth cumulant also involves the exterior Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator, the mean curvature of the boundary, and normal derivatives of the background density. Our derivation uses the tilted potential $U_s=U+s f/β$, the associated deformation of the droplet, and shape derivatives of the Dirichlet energy. This deformation has a natural interpretation as the infinitesimal motion of the free boundary in the obstacle-problem formulation of the equilibrium measure. Our formulas extend previous studies by Wiegmann and Zabrodin in two dimensions for $β=2$. In their setting, we provide a rigorous proof of the limiting third and fourth cumulants, supporting the proposed formulas for general Coulomb gases. We specialize the general formulas to the disk, the half-plane and the sphere, and check them against exactly solvable non-radial deformations, including translated elliptic droplets in $d=2$ and spheroidal deformations in $d=3$.

papers.title: Singular Atiyah Configurations
papers.abstract: We construct arbitrarily large configurations of distinct points in Euclidean three-space with linearly dependent Atiyah polynomials, including planar configurations. The configurations consist of two coaxial cyclic orbits and axial points. We also obtain analogous configurations in hyperbolic three-space. In particular, our results disprove Atiyah's conjecture on configurations of points and its hyperbolic analogue.

papers.title: Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
papers.abstract: We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon, and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_{1}$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.

papers.title: Nashtopes and their A-discriminants
papers.abstract: An $n$-player game in normal form is said to be of format $\boldsymbol{d} = (d_1, \dots, d_n)$ if the $i$-th player has $d_i$ options for $1 \le i \le n$, and is said to be balanced if $d_n - 1 \le \sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(d_i - 1)$. The Nash equilibria of the game correspond to solutions of the system of indifference equations for the game, with payoff differences as coefficients and strategy probabilities as variables. As such, the mixed discriminant of this system gives some information about which games could have an unusual number of totally mixed Nash equilibria. This mixed discriminant can be regarded as an $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for some matrix $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of [Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky 1994], and the convex hull of the columns of $\mathcal{A}$ is a polytope, which we call the Nashtope. We study this $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant for each balanced game format with at least three players. This discriminant is a subset of the Nash discriminant variety introduced in [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026]. We compute the codimension and degree of this discriminant for all balanced game formats, including on-boundary formats, using the Euler obstruction formula in [Matsui--Takeuchi 2011]. Our $\mathcal{A}$-discriminant locus corresponds to a special multigraded Hurwitz locus studied in [Pratt--Sodomaco--Sturmfels 2026]. As a consequence of [Pokidkin 2026], we obtain the codimensions and degrees of the irreducible components of the Nash discriminant variety for each balanced game format with at least three players, fully resolving Problem 3.8 of [Abo--Portakal--Sodomaco 2026].

papers.title: The Art of Toda Brackets: A Journey through the Homotopy Groups of SO(n) in degrees 23-29
papers.abstract: One of the fundamental aims of the present book is to provide a reference for the computation of unstable homotopy groups using methods developed by the Toda school. The Toda bracket serves the art of constructing homotopy liftings and extensions of maps. The theory of Toda brackets is fundamental to the study of composition relations among homotopy classes. Appendix~A.3 brings together all known results on the $2$-primary components of unstable homotopy groups of spheres obtained primarily through Toda brackets, with explicit generators. Appendix~A.2 explains the conventions used to name the generators.
