Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition. Based on this state representation, we formulate a predictive controller that directly penalizes the state and control effort while enforcing the system constraints. Under persistent excitation and initialization conditions, we establish recursive feasibility and closed-loop stability of DeoPC in both noise-free and bounded-noise settings. In addition, we show that DeoPC can be calibrated to the physical state coordinates using a few offline state measurements, or treated as a model predictive control tuning problem when no state measurements are available. The effectiveness of DeoPC is demonstrated through simulations on an unstable batch reactor system.

papers.title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: Synthetic data has emerged as a powerful tool for data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twin development, with growing applications in biomedical research and drug development. However, limited attention has been devoted to synthetic time-to-event data, which are central to clinical trials and survival analysis. In particular, theoretical guarantees for the distributional fidelity of synthetic survival data remain largely unexplored. More importantly, even when a generator achieves distributional fidelity, it remains unclear whether the downstream statistical analysis is reliable. To address these gaps, we propose a general two-stage generative framework for survival data (TSGSurv) that jointly generates observed times and covariates conditional on event status, and establish its distributional convergence rate. Focusing on the widely used Cox proportional hazards model, we establish conditions under which generator fidelity guarantees consistency of model coefficient estimates. We further characterize the limitations of naive inference based on synthetic data, and develop a variance correction and a distribution calibration procedure to recover valid inference of original data. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed generative and inferential framework with extensive simulations and two real data applications.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Buffer Bounds for Compressed-Momentum Error Feedback
papers.abstract: Analyses of error feedback bound the memory buffer through a compressor contraction constant -- $r/p$ for the best rank-$r$ approximation of a $p$-dimensional spectrum -- which survives into the rate. We show it need not appear at all. When the compressed momentum is re-injected into the pre-compression accumulator, the previous compressed momentum $β_1 M_{t-1}$ is an admissible competitor in the projection, and the buffer obeys $\|E_t\|_F \le (1-β_1)\|G_t\|_F + γ\|E_{t-1}\|_F$, free of the dimensions $m,n$ and of the rank $r$. The argument uses only that the compressor is a metric projection onto a closed cone, so it covers top-$k$ selection as well as truncated SVD, holds for every selection from the projection set with no condition on singular-value crossings, and in its trajectory-tracking form assumes nothing about the gradients. In the two-stage template of the standard analyses it replaces a Stage-2 constant of order $p^2/r^2$ by one of order $1$, against $Θ(p/r)$ for the sharpest contraction-based bounds. Transferring the full rate costs a leakage term, which we bound by the step-weighted gradient mass $\sum_{u\le t}η_u\|G_u\|_F$ and show tight up to a factor $\sqrt{2}$; the price is an additive $O(\log^2 T)$ floor, not a slower rate. On BERT fine-tuning at rank ratio $32/768$ the feedback decay costs under $0.008$ validation $F_1$.

papers.title: Total acyclicity of Q-shaped diagrams and N-stable categories
papers.abstract: We study total acyclicity of $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective modules. We prove that an acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagram $P$ of projective $A$-modules is totally acyclic if and only if the associated module $K_q(P)$, or equivalently $C_q(P)$, is Gorenstein projective for every $q\in \Q$. We also establish Frobenius structures on the categories of acyclic and totally acyclic $\Q$-shaped diagrams of projective $A$-modules and introduce the associated defect category. Using adjunctions between $\Q$-shaped diagrams and chain complexes, we compare this category with the classical projective defect category and show that their vanishing is equivalent under a mild condition on the Serre functor of $\Q$. Finally, we apply our results to $N$-complexes and extend the $N$-stable equivalence of Brightbill and Miemietz beyond the Gorenstein setting, obtaining a triangle equivalence between the homotopy category of totally $N$-acyclic complexes of projective $A$-modules and the $N$-stable category of Gorenstein projective $A$-modules.

papers.title: Note on the random triadic process II
papers.abstract: For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process. Korándi et al. proved a sharp threshold probability ${p}= \frac 12n^{ - \frac 12}$ for the propagation of the random triadic process.Tian and Yang complemented those results by considering the final size of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when ${p}=o( n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ α(3-r)} n)$ for any fixed constant $α> \frac 12$.In this note, we further consider the sharp threshold probability $\tilde{p}_r$ for the propagation of the random $r$-generalized triadic process when $r\geqslant 4$. We prove that $\frac 12 n^{- \frac 12}<\tilde{p}_r\leqslant c\, n^{- \frac 12}\log^{ \frac 12} n$ for some positive constant $c$, and conjecture that $\tilde{p}_r= c_r\, n^{ - \frac 12}$, where $c_r= \frac 12(r-2)!^{ \frac{1}{2r-4}}\bigl( \frac{2r-5}{r-2}\bigr)^{ \frac{2r-5}{2r-4}}$.

papers.title: An explicit domain-preserving projected Milstein scheme with strong order one for stochastic systems
papers.abstract: A variety of domain-preserving numerical schemes have been developed for scalar stochastic differential equations and for several classes of multidimensional systems, including those defined on hyperrectangles and positive orthants. To accommodate more general domain constraints, we consider stochastic systems on bounded or unbounded open convex polyhedral domains, where coefficients may exhibit boundary singularities and polynomial growth. Under local regularity, growth and boundary assumptions, we establish well-posedness and integrability estimates for the exact solution. Then we construct an explicit projected Milstein scheme that preserves the domain by applying a Euclidean projection onto a step-size-dependent interior set after each Milstein update. For systems driven by multidimensional commutative noise, we prove strong order-one convergence for the maximum grid error in Lp, for suitable p > 1 and sufficiently small step sizes under additional weighted regularity and stability conditions. The proof combines these integrability estimates with local Milstein consistency, localization and weighted stability, without requiring a priori step-size-uniform moment or boundary inverse-moment bounds for the numerical approximation. Applications to constrained stochastic models and numerical experiments illustrate the observed first-order convergence behavior.

papers.title: Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk
papers.abstract: Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.

papers.title: A decoupled structure-preserving scheme for pressure-driven multispecies tumor growth
papers.abstract: We propose an Onsager-based scheme for an $m$-species pressure-driven reaction--cross-diffusion system with a common homeostatic pressure. The scheme uses a modified scalar energy structure to update the total density, followed by compatible updates of the individual species. The global nonlinear problem remains scalar, and the species densities sum exactly to the updated total density. We establish unique solvability and show that the scheme preserves species nonnegativity, the pressure bound and total-mass monotonicity and satisfies a discrete energy dissipation law without a time-step restriction. We further develop a predictor--corrector extension to improve temporal accuracy while retaining these structural properties. Numerical experiments verify the accuracy and structure-preserving properties of the proposed schemes and demonstrate their computational efficiency.

papers.title: A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line
papers.abstract: We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.

papers.title: Covering Location Optimization at GPU Speed
papers.abstract: Large-scale covering location optimization often involves NP-hard combinatorial problems that pose substantial computational challenges in urban facility planning. This paper proposes a GPU-accelerated parallel search framework for the maximal covering location problem, combining device-resident multi-trajectory exploration with lightweight CPU-side coordination. Exploiting the structure of one-swap moves, exact incremental gains are evaluated through sparse coverage representations and tiled CUDA kernels. A hierarchical reduction identifies the best exchange without materializing the full swap-gain matrix, while GPU-resident destroy-and-repair and elite-guided restarts balance intensification and diversification. Computational experiments on nine real-world urban configurations demonstrate consistent improvements over GRASP, achieving a mean relative gap of 0.029\% against published best-known solutions (BKS) and reaching BKS in 50 of 90 independent runs. On the largest urban benchmark, Kings, with 7,730 candidate locations and a budget of 50 facilities, the proposed method reaches BKS in all ten runs using a consumer-grade NVIDIA GTX 1660 Ti GPU, requiring only 45.2 seconds on average to obtain its final incumbent, compared with 99.5 seconds reported for AILS-PR in a high-performance computing cluster environment. The source code and benchmark reproduction scripts are publicly available at https://github.com/Yuntian-Zhang/GPU4CO

papers.title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models
papers.abstract: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. A first-order term, present because regularized solutions are not stationary for the task loss, is not reduced in the same way. Experiments on an exact non-quadratic model confirm the budget and the ceiling, show the first-order term dominating for strong penalties, and find the curvature-guided penalty slightly better than an isotropic one. In a three-seed transformer study the functional is rank-correlated with merging degradation, but no more strongly than the Euclidean displacement norm.

papers.title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
papers.abstract: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation. Every polynomial relation of degree at most $d$ is detected modulo $t^{d+1}$. For $d\ge1$ this bound is sharp for each elliptic curve. A rational quasi-period row gives a Galois-stable Tate line. Together with an algebraic holomorphic period ratio it forces potential splitting, which identifies the exact ordinary CM obstruction. We compute the full Tate matrix. For ordinary non-CM curves with $p\ge5$, the standard quasi-period row is rational precisely at a zero of Katz's $E_{2,p}$. Away from the zeros the two full ratios are algebraically independent. At the zeros, a nonzero quasi-period and the normalized holomorphic ratio have algebraically independent images in $\mathbb C_p$. The complex question that motivates these results, the analogue for Drinfeld modules, and a conditional arithmetic consequence for Katz values complete the comparison.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools
papers.abstract: This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.

papers.title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
papers.abstract: Equilibrium-based conic formulations of elastoplasticity and limit analysis provide statically admissible stress fields but generate large Newton systems whose sparse factorization limits three-dimensional computations. This work develops and analyzes a macro-element condensation tailored to the Newton systems arising from primal--dual interior-point methods. Exploiting four-tetrahedron macro-elements, the method eliminates stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers, yielding reduced systems that can be solved using positive-definite factorizations, with estimated reductions of approximately \(4\times\) in dimension and structural nonzeros relative to stress-only elimination. The validity of this elimination is established through global and macro-local nonsingularity conditions. Local nonsingularity is independent of the yield criterion in elastoplasticity, whereas in limit analysis it holds directly for Rankine and is ensured for von Mises through trace-bound augmentation. Numerical results show that, relative to stress-only elimination, the proposed condensation achieves CPU speedups of up to approximately \(2\times\) and reduces peak linear-solver memory by up to \(66.5\%\). We further develop a CUDA Fortran implementation that exploits uniform macro-local blocks through batched routines and uses cuDSS for the reduced sparse solve. This implementation achieves speedups of up to \(13.5\times\) over its CPU counterpart and up to \(87.5\times\) over MOSEK, while successfully solving the largest tested 3D problems that exceed the device-memory capacity of the GPU solver CuClarabel. For elastoplasticity, we also propose a preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver that reduces device-memory requirements relative to the direct GPU solver, at the expense of increased solution time.

papers.title: Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
papers.abstract: The strong chromatic index $χ_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $θ(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $θ(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $χ_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$. For simple graphs, this improves the direct greedy bound from 32 to 28. In particular, it verifies the Erdős-Nešetřil conjecture for simple graphs of maximum degree five whose vertices of degree five form an independent set, using one fewer color than the conjectured bound of 29. When $θ(G)=9$, our bound is four colors above the bound of 24 predicted by the Ore-degree conjecture of Chen, Huang, Yu, and Zhou.

papers.title: Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains
papers.abstract: Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.

papers.title: The Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology: A Methodological Shift from the Perspective of Natural Science and Engineering Practice
papers.abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, fundamentally driven by the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm, rely on setting external objectives and iterative trial-and-error. When confronted with complex nonlinear problems containing noise and conflicting constraints, this paradigm inherently induces statistical smoothing and compromise, yielding black-box models that lack interpretability and out-of-distribution generalization. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the Four-Element Theory of Structure-Driven Methodology, reconstructing the solving process into four irreversible stages: Deconstruction, Structure, Construction, and Solving. The method suspends a priori presuppositions to strip unit coupling, extracts rigid invariants inherent to the problem, constructs equivalent mappings anchored to these invariants, and executes the mapping directly to generate the solution. Evaluation metrics and experience are relegated to a posteriori verification. Demonstrated through cross-disciplinary practices including number theory, Hamiltonian systems, deep learning, and seismic inversion, this methodology transcends the statistical fitting bottleneck. Structure-Driven and Objective-Driven methodologies are complementary: when structure is sufficient, solutions are directly constructed; when lacking, it degenerates into the OD path.

papers.title: A proof of Casselman's comparison conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove Casselman's comparison conjecture for parabolic subgroups of real linear reductive groups. Let $Q=LU$ be a standard parabolic subgroup of a real linear reductive group $G$, with Levi subgroup $L$ and unipotent radical $U$. For every Casselman--Wallach representation $π$ of $G$ and every $i\geq0$, the natural inclusion $π_K\hookrightarrowπ$ induces a topological $L$-equivariant isomorphism \[ H_i(\mathfrak u,π_K)^\infty\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ } H_i(\mathfrak u,π). \] Put $\mathscr U=\mathcal U(\mathfrak u)$ and $F_k=\mathscr U/I_{\mathfrak u}^k$, where $I_{\mathfrak u}$ is the augmentation ideal. For every $k\geq1$ and $i\geq0$, we establish natural topological $L$-isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathscr U}(F_k,π),\ \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π_K)^\infty \simeq \operatorname{Ext}^i_{\mathscr U}(F_k,π). \end{aligned} \] We also obtain closedness of $\mathfrak u^kM$ for the (co)chain spaces $M=C_j(\mathfrak u,π),C^j(\mathfrak u,π)$, and for $M=J_a,J_{a-1}/J_a$, where $(J_a)$ is the smooth Bruhat filtration of a principal series representation.

papers.title: Dynamical edge universality and the Airy$_β$ line ensemble
papers.abstract: We prove dynamical edge universality for three families of interacting particle systems for every $β>0$: $β$-Dyson Brownian motion with an analytic potential, weighted $β$-corners processes, and a class of discrete-time Markov chains. Our results apply to general non-equilibrium initial data and show that the Airy$_β$ line ensemble emerges at positive times whenever the limiting density has a regular square-root edge. More precisely, after centering at the moving deterministic edge and rescaling space and time on the $n^{-2/3}$ and $n^{-1/3}$ scales, respectively, the trajectories of the top $k$ particles converge jointly in distribution to the top $k$ curves of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble, for every fixed $k$, in the topology of uniform convergence on compact time intervals. The proof combines dynamical loop equations with characteristic-flow estimates to establish local laws near the moving edge and upper bounds on the extremal particle. We then identify the stochastic evolution of every subsequential limit of the rescaled Stieltjes transform and establish convergence through the pole-evolution characterization of the Airy$_β$ line ensemble.

papers.title: A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size
papers.abstract: Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.

papers.title: On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems
papers.abstract: In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent

papers.title: A Nonadaptive Sparse Fourier Transform in Every Dimension
papers.abstract: Let $G=(\mathbb{Z}/2^a\mathbb{Z})^d$, of order $N=2^{ad}$. Given point-query access to any complex signal $X$ with Fourier transform $\hat{X}$ over $G$, we provide a randomized algorithm that constructs a $k$-sparse estimate $\widetilde{X}$ via non-adaptive queries such that, with large probability, $\|\widetilde{X}-\hat{X}\|_2^2 \leq C \cdot \|H_k(\hat{X})-\hat{X}\|_2^2$, for an absolute constant $C>0$, where $H_k(\cdot)$ denotes the best $k$-sparse approximation. The constant $C$ can be improved to any desired $1+\varepsilon$ by either supplying a constant-factor estimate on the $k$-sparse tail norm or allowing an arbitrarily small additive error term $δ\|\hat{X}\|_2^2$ on the right-hand side. With a supplied tail estimate, we can also satisfy an $\ell_\infty/\ell_2$ heavy hitters guarantee. For fixed $δ$, the number of samples is $O((k/\varepsilon^2)(\log N)\log(k/\varepsilon))$, and the recovery algorithm requires a polynomial in $(k/\varepsilon)\log N$ exact operations. The algorithm naturally extends to $G=(\mathbb{Z}/b^a\mathbb{Z})^d$ for any fixed integer $b>1$.

papers.title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths. Inspired by properties of the Calkin--Wilf tree, we study several parameters of our tree and use them to obtain new results on semi-Fibonacci partitions. We also derive generating functions for partition statistics and determine the average and extremal partition sizes at each level.

papers.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer. We obtain the asymptotic order of growth for both the number of group elements and the number of conjugacy classes in $G$, with length at most $L$, and fixed genus (orientable or non-orientable) $n$. For free groups, our methods give precise asymptotics for each of the counts.

papers.title: Gaussian Quasi-Likelihood Estimation for Nonsynchronously Observed Lévy processes
papers.abstract: We study parametric inference for a two-dimensional simple Lévy process observed at high frequency over an expanding time horizon, where the two components are sampled in a possibly non-synchronous manner. Combining Gaussian quasi-likelihood estimation for Lévy SDEs with the non-synchronous quasi-likelihood methodology, we construct a Gaussian-type quasi-likelihood based on the covariance structure of non-synchronous increments, and we prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the resulting estimators. The convergence rates coincide with those in the synchronous setting, while the asymptotic variance depends essentially on the sampling design and becomes more complicated under non-synchronicity. To handle the different moment structure of pure-jump Lévy processes, we introduce an additional convergence assumption and provide tractable sufficient conditions linked to the observation scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed estimators.

papers.title: Kakutani equivalence of higher rank unipotent abelian actions I
papers.abstract: We study Kakutani equivalence of higher-rank abelian unipotent actions. We construct a Kakutani invariant for general $\mathbb{R}^n$-actions and establish a quantitative vanishing criterion. By this criterion, we prove that ergodic abelian horocyclic actions on finite-volume quotients of connected semisimple Lie groups are loosely Kronecker. We also include a proof of the Abramov entropy formula for time changes of Rn-actions, following the strategy developed by Nadler.

papers.title: Arithmetic Upper and Lower Bounds for the Denumerant Function III
papers.abstract: We extend the denumerant to a weighted denumerant, the sum of a function $μ$ over the solutions in non-negative integers of $a_1x_1+\cdots+a_kx_k=n$. For the monomial weights $x_1^{α_1}\cdots x_k^{α_k}$, with exponents $α_i\in\mathbb{R}_{\geq0}$, we prove upper and lower bounds of the kind of those of the first paper of this series (arXiv:2204.13689), with an explicit constant and explicit shifts. As an example of application, summing these bounds over all the numbers $a_1,\dots,a_k$ we find, by elementary means, the asymptotic main term of the sums $\sum_{y_1+\cdots+y_k=n}σ_{α_1}(y_1)\cdotsσ_{α_k}(y_k)$ of products of divisor functions, for every $k$ and for real exponents $α_i\neq0$ of either sign.

papers.title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
papers.abstract: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic. For left-invariant discrete Lagrangians, they reduce to Lie-Poisson maps that preserve coadjoint orbits and, when $G$ is connected, every Casimir function. A variational error analysis establishes second-order accuracy of the midpoint-Cayley method. We also construct an exactly symplectic, projectable extension on $T^*(\mathbb R\times G)$ whose formal modified Hamiltonian is affine in the momentum conjugate to time and admits symmetry reduction. Under uniform analyticity, coefficient bounds, and domain-containment assumptions, optimal truncation yields exponentially accurate interpolation and near-conservation of the modified extended Hamiltonian over exponentially long intervals. For a connected attitude network on $SO(3)^N$ with damping and uniformly positive, non-increasing coupling weights, we prove local asymptotic stability of the static consensus set for the continuous dynamics and exact preservation of total spatial momentum by the discrete scheme. Numerical experiments on the network and on a time-dependent rigid body on $SO(3)$ illustrate second-order convergence and the extended energy balance.

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
papers.abstract: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.

papers.title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
papers.abstract: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric combined-field-only integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calderón-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calderón regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

papers.title: Regularity and stabilization of integral closures of powers of homogeneous ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish explicit polynomial bounds for the regularity defect and the stabilization index of integral closures of powers of arbitrary homogeneous ideals over fields of any characteristic. Specifically, let $I \subseteq K[x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}]$ be a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal generated in degrees at most $d$. We prove that $\reg \overline{I^{s}} \le ρ(I)s + d^{(n-1)2^{n}}$ for every $s \ge 1$, where $ρ(I) \le d$ denotes the eventual slope of $\reg \overline{I^{s}}$. Furthermore, the stabilization bound is polynomial in $d$ for a fixed number of variables $n$. In characteristic zero, an upper bound for the first Hilbert coefficient yields a significantly sharper exponent. Our approach relies on exact equigenerated reductions, free lattice constructions within normalized Rees algebras, monic Frobenius presentations, and Tor-module regularity controls, complemented by generic source hyperplanes that reduce the stabilization behavior to the eventual nonvanishing of graded components.

papers.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
papers.abstract: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two rows of a random $n\times n$ Latin square are statistically indistinguishable from a random derangement (answering a conjecture of Cameron and Cavenagh-Greenhill-Wanless).

papers.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
papers.abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

papers.title: A Complete Classification of the One-Dimensional Nonlocal Eigenvalue Problem
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the spectral stability of the following one-dimensional nonlocal eigenvalue problem (NLEP) $$ \partial_x^2φ-φ+pw^{p-1}φ-γ(p-1)\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^{r-1}φdx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^r dx}w^p=λφ, $$ where $w$ is the unique positive even solution of $w''-w+w^p=0$ decaying at infinity, $p,r>1$, and $γ\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\Reγ\ge0$. This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. Their common endpoint is $γ=1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ=γ_H>1$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$. In each case, the two arcs approach a common vertical asymptote. As an application, for real $γ\ge0$, the condition for strict spectral stability is $γ>1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ>γ_H$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$, where $γ_H>1$ is the value at which a conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. The key ingredient in determining how the number of eigenvalues in the open right half-plane changes at imaginary-axis crossings is a cumulative estimate for the mixed-sign spectral weights that arise for certain $p$ and $r$ with $1<p<3$ and $1<r<2$.

papers.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
papers.abstract: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem. Erdős (1992) conjectured that every connected graph $G$ with girth $g$ and average degree $d$ has a cycle spectrum of size at least $Ω(d^{\lfloor (g-1)/2 \rfloor})$. Sudakov and Verstraëte (2008) proved the full conjecture of Erdős in a stronger form. It is natural to consider the size of the circuit spectra of binary matroids. Murty (1971) characterized all connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size one. Lemos et al. (2011) characterized the connected binary matroids with circuit spectra of size two, where the largest size is odd. For general binary matroids, it is still an open question to find a lower bound for the size of the circuit spectra. In this paper, we give best-possible such lower bounds for connected binary matroids that do not contain both the Fano matroid and its dual as minors. Let $M$ be a simple connected binary matroid that does not have both the Fano matroid and its dual as a minor, and $d\geq 3$ be the minimum cocircuit size of $M$. We prove that (1) for each element $e$ of $M$, the circuit $e$-spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-2$. This bound is best possible. (2) The circuit spectrum of $M$ must have size at least $d-1$, unless $M\cong F_7,F_7^*,R_{10}$. In exceptional cases, the spectrum of $M$ has size equal to $d-2$.

papers.title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

papers.title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S. We prove the Ramsey Theorem for Edge Ideals: For any betti number indices i,j, and any number of colors m, there is a graph F such that for every m-coloring of the edges of F, there is a color l such that beta_{i,j}(S/I_{F_l}) >0, where F_l is the subgraph of F whose edges are in color l. Moreover, the number of vertices of F is at most jm^2.

papers.title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

papers.title: Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
papers.abstract: DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.

papers.title: A Two-Spectrum Deterministic Equivalent for Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
papers.abstract: Rank-one perturbations of the mean characteristic polynomial of a random skew-kernel matrix assign a positive spatial weight to each root. For independent centered isotropic rows, the resulting response tracks the sample almost surely against each deterministic spatial test, uniformly over positive scales and arbitrary inputs, exactly when row energies concentrate on common projections of proportional rank. Directional absolute first moments determine this condition. The determinant Jensen gap controls the spatial response in every real orthonormal basis. For identity spatial covariance, logarithmic derivatives of the mean determinant give the temporal weights of the row energies it detects. Flat kernels of one prescribed rank suffice to test the row condition. A scalar equation in the two input spectra approximates the matrix response of the roots within $4/d$ in normalized trace norm. A varying ordinary response and the same-scale overlap of independent samples recover both input laws up to reciprocal rescaling, with Lipschitz stability of the relative spatial parameter and an optimal logarithmic modulus for the compactified laws on intervals of positive variation. Brownian area gives explicit spatial half-Cauchy mixtures.

papers.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
papers.abstract: A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

papers.title: Hyperkähler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $α$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $σ$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $π:\mathscr M\toΛ_0$ where $Λ_0$ encodes the admissible pairs $(α,σ)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in $Λ_0$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(α,σ)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.

papers.title: Decision-Weighted Limit Theorems: Less Conservative Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Limit theorems provide a natural way to construct tractable models for optimization under uncertainty. Existing approaches typically apply them to unweighted sums of uncertain parameters and use the resulting bounds to construct uncertainty sets. We show that sharper formulations are obtained by applying limit theorems directly to the uncertain linear expressions in the optimization problem, with the decision variables as weights. For independent random variables with finite variance, the weighted central limit theorem yields a second-order cone constraint with a decision-dependent protection term, and for heavy-tailed random variables governed by stable limit laws, the weighted approach yields power-cone constraints. Using norm duality, we show that, under a condition on the individual bounds, the feasible region of the unweighted formulation is contained in that of the weighted one. In 16,000 knapsack instances with a prescribed violation probability of 5%, the weighted formulation improves the optimal objective value by 20.9% on average, with overall average violation probabilities between 3.45% and 4.95%, whereas those of the unweighted formulation are near zero.

papers.title: A Scalable Decentralized Event-Triggered Topology-Switching Protocol for Verifiable Safe Control in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a decentralized event-triggered topology-switching protocol that allows agents to disconnect from the communication network while preserving state safety and excluding Zeno behavior. We establish a robust barrier function condition that guarantees safety as long as the estimation error remains within a prescribed threshold. Each agent uses locally computable certificates to determine when to connect and disconnect from the network. The certificate construction improves scalability by reducing the complexity of topology-dependent computations from $O(2^N)$ to $O(N)$, where $N$ is the number of agents. We formally prove that the protocol ensures the estimation error does not exceed the prescribed threshold and is non-Zeno. An alternating method computes an error-weighting matrix and a quadratic barrier function that guarantee safety under the proposed protocol. Finally, we evaluate the protocol on four interconnected microgrids. Compared with maintaining network connectivity at all times, the protocol reduces the time agents remain connected while keeping phase and frequency within their safe operating region.

papers.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be the blow-up of a smooth quadric threefold along a twisted quartic, and let $G\subset\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ be a finite subgroup such that $\mathrm{Pic}^G(X)$ has rank one. We prove that $X$ is $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. The action of $G$ on $X$ is linearisable if and only if it is projectively linearisable, and this holds precisely when $G$ contains no subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
papers.abstract: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. A nonempty subset of the positive integers $X$ is second-order Schreier if $X$ is a union of $d$ first-order Schreier sets for some $d \leq \min X$. We study a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets and the Fibonacci sequence. Specifically, we show that the second-order Schreier set with minimum $2$ and maximum $n+4$ is one more than the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers $(F_1, F_2, \ldots)$ with $(F_2, F_3, \ldots)$ (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Diophantine subset of $\mathbb{Q}$. More precisely, there exist an integer $m\ge 1$ and a polynomial of total degree at most four in $m+1$ variables whose rational zero set projects onto $\mathbb{Z}$ under the first coordinate. We construct a Diophantine model of $\mathbb{Z}$ on an elliptic curve and use it to define real intervals with rational endpoints, each containing an integer. A denominator bound identifies a rational number in a sufficiently short interval with that integer. The key ingredients are a criterion for square denominators, obtained using the Tian--Yuan--Zhang genus-point criterion for congruent number elliptic curves, and a height bound from quaternionic abelian surfaces. The Green--Tao theorem supplies prime progressions needed to define squaring, and hence multiplication, in the model. Our proof is inspired by OpenAI's approach to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$, but does not rely on the $2$-converse or $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and invoked by OpenAI.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Riemannian Real-Time Optimization for Robotics: Active Set SQP Parametric Pathfollowing
papers.abstract: Robot optimal control often combines Euclidean states with configurations on Lie groups and other smooth manifolds. This paper develops a parametric Riemannian Newton pathfollowing method based on homotopy quadratic programs and parallel strict-working-set tasks. It specifies the event handling, working-set exchanges, matrix factor updates, synchronization, and residual checks used by the algorithm. Tracking guarantees are given under mildly degenerate regularity conditions and the Riemannian strong second-order sufficient condition. Drone navigation and arm manipulation are formulated as geometric optimal-control problems, including finite-force grasp acquisition, transport and supported release. Numerical examples illustrate drone navigation and arm pick-and-place through KKT-residual histories and MuJoCo simulations, together with preliminary initialization results for the full-horizon optimal-control problems.

papers.title: Does Merge Form a Hopf Algebra? Coproducts, Traces, and the Prospects of Algebraic Minimalism
papers.abstract: Marcolli, Chomsky, and Berwick (2025; henceforth MCB) formulate the Merge operation of Minimalism on a Hopf algebra of Connes-Kreimer type, and claim that language and physics obey the same algebraic structure. This paper examines the premise of that claim: whether Merge on workspaces can be described as a Hopf algebra. We first survey five coproducts for coassociativity and a connected grading: the Connes-Kreimer coproduct $Δ_ρ$, MCB's two coproducts $Δ_d$ and $Δ_c$, the contraction coproduct of Marcolli and Skigin (2025), and the coproduct of Xiao (2026). $Δ_d$ is not coassociative. For $Δ_c$, MCB gives no rule for the labels of trace leaves in trees that already contain trace leaves; under the literal extension it is not coassociative, but once a rule and a grading are supplied it yields a graded connected Hopf algebra. The coproduct of Xiao is coassociative, and so is that of Marcolli and Skigin once its definition is extended to trees with trace leaves. These properties do not tell the coassociative coproducts apart; what distinguishes them is the representation that movement leaves behind. We then review how generative grammar has treated moved elements, and confirm that semantic interpretation requires two things of the representation that results from movement. Retention requires that the structure the lower position had before movement be recoverable; Identifiability requires that, in interpreting the lower position, it be determinable which upper element, if any, corresponds to it. None of the five coproducts meets both conditions: Retention is met only by $Δ_c$, and there only in the form of a label, and Identifiability by none. In light of the results on coassociativity, we also reassess the Birkhoff factorization that MCB employs at the syntax-semantics interface. Finally, we indicate at least three directions for algebraic Minimalism.

papers.title: On the dynamics of weighted shifts on Fréchet sequence spaces over trees
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give characterizations of Li--Yorke chaos, mean Li--Yorke chaos and distributional chaos for weighted backward shifts acting on general Fréchet sequence spaces over directed trees. As corollaries, we obtain explicit characterizations in the setting of Köthe spaces $λ_p(A,V)$, where $p\in\{0\}\cup[1,\infty)$ and $V$ is a directed tree. In particular, we obtain criteria for the case of the classical Banach spaces $\ell^p(V)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$, and $c_0(V)$.

papers.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

papers.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

papers.title: Constrained Mean Variance Portfolio Selection under Reflected Factor Dynamics: Stochastic Riccati Equations, Neumann Problems,and a Deep Solver
papers.abstract: We study extended stochastic Riccati equations (ESREs) arising in constrained continuous time mean variance portfolio selection with random market coefficients. Reflected Markovian diffusions are introduced to model factor dynamics in a bounded state space, naturally leading to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. A logarithmic transformation converts the extended stochastic Riccati equations into quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) driven by the reflected factors. We establish their probabilistic representation through semilinear parabolic Neumann problems and prove existence and uniqueness of bounded continuous viscosity solutions. Existence is obtained through stability and comparison arguments for quadratic BSDEs, whereas uniqueness is established by combining a Kobylanski-type transformation with a viscosity comparison principle adapted to the Neumann boundary setting. We further develop a Deep BSDE method combining reflected-path simulation, geometry-aware boundary treatment, and efficient evaluation of the constrained Hamiltonian. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, providing a mesh-free framework for high-dimensional constrained portfolio problems with Neumann boundary.

papers.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
papers.abstract: We extend the method of van Woerden to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_F)$-equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_F)$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\mathcal{O}_F)$ obtained by Soulé and Bayer-Fluckiger, Emery, and Houriet. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb{Q}$, unchanged since Soulé's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.

papers.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
papers.abstract: We determine the monochromatic three-arm exponent for critical planar percolation through the exact spectral threshold of an explicit positive integral operator family with elementary kernels, obtaining $ξ_3=0.76928375\cdots$. Unlike the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) event, the three-arm event can be obstructed by two distinct white clusters, so a Markovian exploration must retain the past connections. We introduce a two-point boundary observable that records these connections. Using the coupling between conformal loop ensemble (CLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG), this observable satisfies a renewal equation in terms of quantum boundary lengths, and yields the explicit operator whose spectral information determines $ξ_3$. Our approach also gives an explicit spectral characterization of monochromatic $n$-arm exponents for all $n\ge4$.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Deterministic Principal-Ideal Responses of Random Operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a random compact operator for which each fixed compact shift $X+B$ generates an almost surely deterministic principal ideal. We show that all these ideals are determined by one ideal and one coset. The ideal is generated almost surely by the difference of independent copies of $X$, and the coset consists of all minimizing shifts. For alternating quadratic evaluations under two-sided curvature bounds, the spatial and kernel spectra determine the least ideal and the covariance determines the coset. With the spatial weights and a trace-class skew kernel fixed, the attainable raw ideals fill an explicit order interval. Every ideal in the interval occurs with standard Gaussian row marginals and joint covariance arbitrarily close to the identity. For finite-dimensional operator spaces with infinite-rank coefficient ideal we characterize almost-everywhere saturation in every translate by a spectral summability criterion. For independent Gaussian rows we also compute the least ideal attainable after observing a noise subspace. For Wiener area, finitely many fixed Hilbert-valued temporal integrals leave this ideal unchanged.

papers.title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

papers.title: Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension: Absorption and Intersection Probabilities
papers.abstract: For every $d\ge1$, we determine prescribed-point absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of standard Brownian motion and Brownian bridges in $\mathbb R^d$, obtaining explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability for a point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r)=\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}}\int_0^\infty\left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right)\mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4}(K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d}v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For fixed $d$, the non-absorption probabilities of a prescribed nonzero point by Brownian-motion and Brownian-bridge hulls over $[0,T]$ are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively, as $T\to\infty$. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of the first time $τ_d$ a Brownian-motion hull absorbs a prescribed point at unit distance. In high dimensions, both $τ_d$ and the time $τ_d^{\mathrm{ball}}$ to absorb the entire unit ball satisfy the same central limit theorem: \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d}\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1),\qquad\frac{\logτ_d^{\mathrm{ball}}-2d}{2\sqrt d}\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty.\] Thus both times have leading exponential scale $\mathrm{e}^{2d}$. For Brownian bridges, prescribed-point and unit-ball absorption also exhibit the same Gaussian transition, but on the shorter scale $\mathrm{e}^d$. For two independent Brownian motions started one unit apart, we show that the non-intersection probability of their convex hulls is of order $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$ for fixed $d$ and large $T$. In high dimensions, the first intersection time has leading exponential scale $\mathrm{e}^d$, and its logarithm satisfies a central limit theorem.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $τ$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A=Λ_{\mathbf R}$ be the surface rigid algebra associated with a partial tagged triangulation $\mathbf R$ of a punctured marked surface with nonempty boundary, and let $C_A$ be the Cartan matrix of $A$. We classify the connected components of the support $τ$-tilting graph of $A$. For connected $A$, such a graph is disconnected if and only if $A$ is non-local and weakly symmetric with $\operatorname{rank}C_A=1$. The graph then has exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero basic $τ$-rigid pair over connected $A$ is connected. When $\mathbf R$ is nonempty and all arc endpoints are punctures, we construct an explicit homotopy equivalence from the realization of the support $τ$-tilting complex to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Under the same hypothesis, $A$ is $τ$-tilting finite if and only if $C_A$ is positive definite. In the finite case, we give a root-system realization of the $g$-vectors of indecomposable $τ$-rigid pairs, with types $A$, $D$ and $C$ determined by the tagged surface configuration.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schrödinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: A DG algebra structure for the edge ideal of any split graph
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit DG algebra structure on the minimal free resolution of the quotient of a polynomial ring by the edge ideal of any split graph (that is, a graph whose vertex set is a disjoint union of a clique and an independent set). The algebra structure is based on a simple combinatorial notion, which we call the fixing edge of a pair of edges, that directly captures the structure of the underlying graph. Our construction involves an explicit description of the minimal free resolution of the edge ideal of such a graph, including formulas for both the Betti numbers and the differentials.

papers.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
papers.abstract: For every integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We also prove that every convex combination of the $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes has degree $2r-2$ and only simple negative roots. Its coefficients are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$. These results settle the real-rootedness conjecture of Lundström and Saud Maia Leite for crown order polytopes.

papers.title: Computer-Assisted Results for $n$-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in $[n]$
papers.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with $n$ sides restricted to taking face values in the set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. We give a computer-assisted proof that $n=6$ is the smallest $n\ge3$ which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length $n$ with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For $n=6$, we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length $6$. We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that $n=6$ is the largest $n\ge3$ which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length $n$ with uniform and minimal winning advantage.

papers.title: Fast rates for the classification of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths
papers.abstract: In binary classification problems, plug-in classifiers can sometimes achieve faster excess risk rates than the underlying estimation rate. In this work, we study a supervised classification problem based on repeated independent observations of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, with both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous drifts. We show that, under a suitable separation condition on the class-dependent drifts, a plug-in classifier attains an excess risk of quadratic order in the corresponding parametric or nonparametric estimation error. The theoretical approach utilizes the Wiener chaos representation and spectral theory to characterize the log-likelihood ratio as a quadratic form of Gaussian random variables, enabling a precise analysis of margin behaviour and deviation results. This extends the fast-rate results from classification problems with linear discriminant models and Gaussian white noise models to dynamical diffusion systems with Gaussian structure.

papers.title: Beyond Robustness of Magic: Quantifying Quantum State Convertibility
papers.abstract: In fault-tolerant quantum computing, magic states provide essential resources for implementing non-Clifford operations. The robustness of magic (RoM) quantifies the magic contained in a quantum state and is closely related to the cost of classical simulation. However, knowing how much magic two states contain is not sufficient to determine whether one can be converted into the other using free operations. In this work, we develop a geometric framework in which RoM is represented as half the distance to the set of free states, and extend this framework to state conversion.
