We introduce a directed conversion deficiency that measures how far a target state lies from the states freely reachable from a given input. This quantity vanishes exactly when free conversion is possible and, beyond being a mathematically well-defined measure, has an operational interpretation in terms of stabilizer quasiprobability. Furthermore, our framework provides lower bounds on the additional magic states required for conversion that can be strictly stronger than conventional RoM-based bounds. We demonstrate this distinction analytically by constructing a continuous family of mixed single-qubit states with identical RoM for which free conversion is possible in one direction but impossible in the reverse. Our results reveal that the usefulness of magic for quantum state conversion depends not only on its amount but also on the specific transformation being performed.

papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which the positive residue characteristics of $S$ are invertible. We identify Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients with the category of modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The equivalence takes the free module on a smooth $S$-scheme to its motive with transfers and commutes with pullback and extension of coefficients. It applies to singular and nonreduced schemes and to mixed-characteristic bases. The main geometric input is the base change stability of Voevodsky's motivic Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum $HR_S$. We prove this using permutation quotients of tori, families of relative cycles and arithmetic power homotopies. The identification over fields and the reconstruction theorem of Cisinski--Déglise then give the module equivalence.

papers.title: A 1.932 Guarantee for (r,Q) Policies in Continuous-Review Lost-Sales Inventory Systems
papers.abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an $(r,Q)$ policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most $(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6})/2<1.932$ times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor $\sqrt{2}$ relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic $1.79$ upper guarantee to a uniform $\sqrt{2}$ guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about $1.59$ for our heuristic $(r, Q)$ policy and $1.47$ after joint optimization of $r$ and $Q$. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from $2.33\%$ to $3.91\%$, depending on the setup cost.

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean in a grounded logic, where a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? This paper takes Kripke's answer for truth, the least fixed point, as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term; Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, making each an inductive definition. IGA is omega-sound and proof-grounded: sound and complete for a semantics whose certificates are its own proofs. IGA proves Goodstein's theorem, the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, and, along Gentzen's route, the consistency of Peano Arithmetic. IGA certifies the Veblen notation below every $\varphi(n,0)$: its accessibility ordinal there is $\varphi(ω,0)$, that of the paracomplete truth theory PKF. Every theorem is machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL; order types and PKF's ordinal are cited. IGA proves the Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for it, which it does not, and that bivalence is sound exactly when the order is well-founded. So $Γ_0$ lies exactly one instance of excluded middle away, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in an internal form of Kleene's $\mathcal{O}$ are interderivable over IGA. Bivalence at the Bachmann-Howard order keeps proof-groundedness. One such claim buys well-foundedness of the countable part of Buchholz's notation at every finite level, of type $ψ_0(Ω_ω)$, and $k$ stratified bivalence rules give a proof-grounded system proving the countable part up to level $k$ well-founded; $k$ iterated closings-off of truth do too, sound only for a closed-off model. Unrestricted conditional proof is inconsistent (Curry's paradox); the purchase is implication at a hypothesis not provably decided.

papers.title: Sharp enumeration and growth of admissible sets of integers
papers.abstract: A set of positive integers is admissible if equal sums of finite subsets always have equal numbers of summands. Let $a(N)$ count the nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and let $b(N)$ count those with maximum $N$. We prove $\log a(N)\sim\log b(N)\simπ\sqrt{2N/3}$, establishing the sharp logarithmic asymptotic proposed by Nicolas. More generally, let $Q_h(N)$ count the subsets for which each integer has subset-sum representations of at most $h$ distinct cardinalities. Uniformly for all positive integers $h,N$, we prove $\log Q_h(N)\asymp\min\{N,\sqrt{hN}\}$ with absolute implied constants. Every infinite set satisfying the same condition for some fixed $h$ has counting function $o(\sqrt x)$. At $h=1$, the uniform count proves the conjecture $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$ of Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy, and the infinite-set theorem strengthens their conjectured vanishing lower limit to a full limit. The proofs record each subset sum together with its cardinality and use the counting theorem of Campos and the structure theorem of Carpenter, Defant and Kravitz. The sharp count also uses Nicolas's partition enumeration and an elementary construction of a long restricted-sum progression. Finally, we give an exact partition formula and asymptotics for the odd sets with separated alternate cardinality layers suggested by Nicolas, and deduce lower bounds for the number of non-stratified admissible sets.

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $X_f=\{f=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model. We define the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\C^n/\Z_n$ as a modification of the torsion-type invariant introduced by Fan and Fang, and prove that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension. The proof depends on a holomorphic anomaly formula for families of LG models and a uniform estimate for the torsion near a one-node degeneration of $X_f$.

papers.title: Locally eventually onto cellular automata
papers.abstract: We give a new checkable criterion to ensure that a one-dimensional cellular automaton on a finite alphabet is open and locally eventually onto. In this setting, openness is equivalent to being n-to-1 for some n and therefore implies surjectivity. Bipermutive cellular automata are known to be open and locally eventually onto, while open cellular automata that are neither bipermutive nor bijective appear to have received less attention. Building on Sutner's work with de Bruijn graphs, we describe a method for deciding openness and at the same time determining n. We then introduce the notion of block-regularity of local rules as a generalization of bipermutivity and prove that it implies openness. We further identify two conditions that, together with block-regularity, ensure that every nonempty cylinder set is mapped onto the whole configuration space after a finite number of iterations, and hence that the cellular automaton is open and locally eventually onto. The appendix provides the algorithms that check these finite criteria and then presents examples of open, locally eventually onto, non-bipermutive cellular automata for small diameters.

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

papers.title: The Laplace transform of the stationary measure of the open KPZ equation in the shock region
papers.abstract: The stationary increment measure of the open Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded interval can be represented as the independent sum of a Brownian motion and another process defined via an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative with respect to the measure induced by a Brownian motion. In the fan region, its finite-dimensional Laplace transform was previously expressed in terms of the continuous dual Hahn process. The main contribution here consists of computing the finite-dimensional Laplace transform for a range of parameters in the shock region by an analytic continuation argument. As an application, we provide a direct proof of the convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the increment height function of open WASEP under the stationary measure in the shock region, by computing the convergence of finite-dimensional Laplace transform without relating to the open KPZ equation.

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for all sufficiently large $d$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

papers.title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge-Ampère Equation under a Quadratic Lower Bound
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$ and let $u$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solution of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$. Assume that in a sufficiently large ball centered at the origin in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ \[ u(z)\ge δ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i|^2,\qquad x_i=\operatorname{Re}z_{i},\qquad δ>0, \] and $u(0)\leq H$. If $f$ is Dini-continuous, bounded above and bounded away from zero, and satisfies $Δ_{\mathbb {R}}(f^{1/n})\ge-K$ in distributions, we derive an interior bound for the real $C^{2}$ norm on the unit ball $B_{1}(0)$. When $f\equiv1$, every entire solution satisfying $u(z)\geδ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\operatorname{Re}z_i|^2$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^{n}$ and some $δ>0$ is a real quadratic polynomial.

papers.title: A Polynomial Criterion for Adaptive Stabilization of Discrete-Time Stochastic Nonlinear Systems with an Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: We consider scalar discrete-time systems whose nonlinear function is a linear combination of known power functions with unknown coefficients. The input gain is nonzero and unknown, and the noise is iid zero-mean Gaussian with unknown positive variance. We show that global stabilizability is equivalent to the joint positivity of a family of polynomials determined solely by the power exponents. When this condition holds, a feedback law depending only on the exponents makes the average squared output converge almost surely to the noise variance, the smallest possible value. When the condition fails, every Borel feedback law yields divergence of the output magnitude with positive probability for some fixed parameters and a deterministic initial state.

papers.title: Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
papers.abstract: Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.

papers.title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: Theory, Fast Algorithms, and Chirp-Adaptive Filtering for Rigid-Body Pose Signals
papers.abstract: We develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) for rigid-body pose signals, with left-, right-, and two-sided formulations that account for noncommutative kernel ordering. We establish inverse relations, kernel unitarity, energy preservation, perturbation stability, and spatial and frequency convolution relations. A chirp--Fourier--chirp factorization enables fast forward and inverse algorithms using complex FFTs, with two-dimensional complexity $\mathcal O(N_1N_2(\log N_1+\log N_2))$. For pose denoising, we introduce a two-stage chirp-adaptive method that estimates rotation before refining translation while enforcing unit-dual-quaternion constraints. Numerical experiments demonstrate agreement with direct transforms, substantial computational gains, and lower pose errors than the tested baselines on measured sequences and constructed two-dimensional fields. A downstream $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ synchronization study further demonstrates the potential of the proposed preprocessing approach, with performance depending on graph configurations. These results support efficient and geometry-aware processing of rigid-body pose signals.

papers.title: Millicharged particles and the degree-3 Prouhet-Tarry-Escott problem
papers.abstract: We use geometry to solve a problem in arithmetic relevant for physics. Namely, for any $m$ we find all integer solutions to the equations $\sum_{i=1}^m x_i^k = \sum_{i=1}^m y_i^k$, where $k \in \{1,2,3\}$; this seems to be new for $m \geq 5$. In physics, these are the anomaly cancellation conditions for models with $m$ fermions which can be naturally light and carry small electric charges (a.k.a. millicharged or minicharged particles). The small charges arise by kinetic mixing of the Standard Model $U(1)$ gauge symmetry with an unbroken non-chiral (a.k.a. vector-like) $U(1)$ and the masses are suppressed by a spontaneously-broken chiral $U(1)$.

papers.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
papers.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.

papers.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

papers.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.

papers.title: An infinite completely normal basis theorem
papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem.

papers.title: On the Hardy--Littlewood--Chowla conjecture
papers.abstract: An old conjecture dating back at least to Hildebrand's work in 1989, asserts that the Möbius function exhibits cancellation on shifted primes; that is, $$\sum_{p\le x}μ(p+2)=o(π(x)),\quad \text{or equivalently}\quad \sum_{n\le x}Λ(n)μ(n+2)=o(x).$$ This is also a well-known model case for the parity problem in sieve theory. In this paper, we prove this conjecture. As an application, we show that each of the two sets $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=1\}$ and $\{p:\, μ(p+2)=-1\}$ has asymptotic density $1/2$ among the primes $p$ with $μ^2(p+2)=1$: \begin{equation*} \lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\#\{p\le x:\ μ(p+2)=κ\}} {\#\{p\le x:\ μ^2(p+2)=1\}} =\frac12, \quad κ\in\{-1,\,1\}. \end{equation*}

papers.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
papers.abstract: We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the quadratic Hessian and Monge-Ampère equations with Dini continuous right-hand sides. Our approach uses a three-point maximum principle and requires no differentiation of the equations. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the proof is localised on sublevel sets of a strictly convex solution.

papers.title: Mixing Regularization for Average-Reward $Q$-Learning and $Q$-Planning
papers.abstract: The average-reward setting for reinforcement learning is challenging because, without discounting, the span-contraction of the Bellman operator depends on the mixing properties of the underlying Markov dynamics. Whereas existing work typically assumes contraction, for instance through environment mixing, we study regularization toward a given reward-agnostic, $m$-step mixing policy to control the mixing properties of the learned policy. Our central mixing lemma quantifies how the reference policy's mixing properties transfer to the resulting learned policies. In particular, a single regularizer-dependent quantity simultaneously controls the contraction of the regularized Bellman operator and the exploration of the resulting policies. A second regularizer-dependent quantity controls the bias introduced by regularization, revealing a trade-off between convergence speed and approximation accuracy. Building on this result, we establish finite-time guarantees for regularized $Q$-iteration, synchronous and single-trajectory $Q$-learning, and $Q$-planning. Under one-step mixing, our bounds for approximating the regularized fixed point match the classical model-query bound for relative value iteration and, up to logarithmic factors, an existing sample-complexity bound for synchronous $Q$-learning. We also establish finite-time guarantees under multi-step mixing. For $Q$-planning, we characterize how the planning horizon trades off boundary bias against sample complexity. Finally, we present numerical studies validating the analysis: (i) knowledge of a strong mixing policy improves convergence and exploration, with larger benefits under more severe bottlenecks; and (ii) the observed rankings of $α$-divergence regularizers by bias and convergence speed are consistent with our theoretical analysis.

papers.title: A note on Guo's perturbation result for symmetric nonnegative matrices
papers.abstract: In 1997 Guo Wuwen proved that if $(λ_1,λ_2,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and $λ_2$ real, then $(λ_1+t,λ_2\pm t,λ_3,\dots,λ_n)$ is the spectrum of a nonnegative matrix for every $t\ge 0$. Whether the same holds for symmetric nonnegative matrices has remained an open question. We give an affirmative answer, in a slightly stronger form: if $A$ is a symmetric nonnegative matrix with Perron eigenvalue $λ_1$ and further eigenvalues $λ_2,\dots,λ_n$, and $d_1\ge|d_2|+\dots+|d_n|$, then there is a symmetric matrix $B\ge A$ with eigenvalues $λ_1+d_1,\dots,λ_n+d_n$, and $B$ has the same diagonal as $A$ when $d_1+\dots+d_n=0$. This leads us to call a symmetrically realizable list \emph{Guo-extreme} if none of Guo's moves can be reversed for this list. Every symmetrically realizable list is a Guo-extreme list plus a vector from the cone of Guo's moves. Our second main result is a certificate, modeled on a theorem of Laffey on extreme symmetric matrices: if every nonnegative symmetric matrix that commutes with $A$ and is equal to zero on the entries where $A$ is positive is a multiple of the identity, then $A$ is orthogonally similar to a positive matrix if $A$ has a positive diagonal entry, and to a matrix with zero diagonal and positive off-diagonal entries if $A$ has zero diagonal. Consequently, the spectrum of $A$ can be moved by a small amount in every direction, respectively in every trace-preserving direction, and remain symmetrically realizable. In particular, the spectrum of such a matrix is not Guo-extreme.

papers.title: Digraph Laplacian spectra: The 2005 polygon conjecture fails for all orders above four
papers.abstract: Let $Λ_n$ be the set of all eigenvalues of standardized Laplacian matrices of order $n$, equivalently, of stochastic $n\times n$ matrices with off-diagonal entries at most $\frac1n$. In 2005, a polygon $S_n\subseteqΛ_n$ was constructed, and it was conjectured that $Λ_n=S_n$; this holds for $n\le3$. We show that the conjecture fails for every $n\ge5$. The vertices of $S_n$ are eigenvalues of circulant Laplacians built from powers of the directed $n$-cycle. To first order, no perturbation of these circulants moves such an eigenvalue out of $S_n$; however, adding chords with nonconstant weights moves it along an edge of $S_n$ to first order and, with an explicit coefficient, beyond the supporting line of this edge to second order. Consequently, every edge of $S_n$ not incident to $0$ or $1$ contains interior points of $Λ_n$, except possibly, for even $n$, the two horizontal edges, whereas the four edges incident to $0$ or $1$ lie on $\partialΛ_n$. For $n=4$, whose only other edges are horizontal, the question has recently been settled, $Λ_4=S_4$, by computer-assisted proofs of D. Z. Liu and L. Marshall; Liu also proved that $Λ_n$ is not convex for $n\ge5$. We certify an explicit weighted counterexample for $n=5$, lying only $1.5\cdot10^{-3}$ outside $S_5$, and an unweighted one for $n=7$: the directed $6$-cycle with a duplicated vertex. Its eigenvalue outside $S_7$ is also an eigenvalue of the two-chord digraph that ends the above perturbation; for the analogous digraphs of order $n$, the excess is asymptotic to $\frac{π^2}{2n^4}$. We also observe that $S_n$ is a zonotope, describe $Λ_n$ in terms of eigenvectors, and prove that $S_m\subseteq S_n$ whenever $m\mid n$.

papers.title: Inter-Categorical Subobject Analysis
papers.abstract: We introduce a systematic way to use the subobject functor on any category to set up a framework for generalized topological and measure-theoretic notions and inferences. Concretely, we develop two connected calculi: 1. a fourfold calculus derived from notions of smallness and density that generalizes, among other things, topological density and measure-theoretic negligibility, 2. a twofold calculus that generalizes topological and measure-theoretic inference procedures. The resulting theory is distinguished in that it is inter-categorical in character: its definitions can be applied not just to describe smallness and density of subobjects in any category and classify morphisms by how they handle them, but also functors and natural transformations by how they transform them, somewhat like the theory of limits but with a simple and intuitive conceptual meaning that applies to each incarnation. We provide examples of these notions from many areas of mathematics and outline their unfolding throughout category theory as we add assumptions that bring them closer to classical settings, which we complete by generalizing the topological duality of open and closed subsets and outlining a possible framework for a categorical measure theory. Central to this interaction is the subobject 2-functor and the 2-category of upward-bounded preorders, so in the last part of the text we provide a study of their function. Concretely we derive representation theorems for this 2-functor and 2-category and a conjecture about how to generalize these theorems to n-categories.

papers.title: On possible Turán densities under general uniformity conditions
papers.abstract: The Turán problem asks how dense a hypergraph can be while avoiding a prescribed family of subhypergraphs. For a family $\mathcal S\subseteq2^{[r]}$, an $r$-graph is $\mathcal S$-uniformly dense in the sense of Reiher, Rödl, and Schacht if, in every large collection of ordered vertex tuples selected by joint restrictions on the positions in each $S\in\mathcal S$, at least a prescribed proportion of the tuples form edges. Ordinary and minimum $\ell$-degree Turán densities correspond to $\mathcal S=\{\{1\}\}$ and $\mathcal S=\{\{1,\ldots,\ell\}\}$, respectively, for $1\le\ell<r$. This survey collects results on possible Turán densities within this framework and gives a complete description of these values for many choices of $\mathcal S$.

papers.title: The sublevel Flood bifiltration: towards scalable 2-parameter persistent homology
papers.abstract: Multiparameter persistent homology is a rapidly developing branch of topological data analysis that improves the robustness of single-parameter persistent homology to outliers, while still capturing the metric characteristics of the data. However, a notable limitation is its lack of scalability. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach for efficiently computing 2-parameter persistent homology on large point sets. Our work extends the Flood filtration, originally developed for single-parameter persistence. Our construction, called the sublevel Flood bifiltration, offers a scalable approximation of the sublevel offset bifiltration. We show that it benefits from theoretical stability properties and describe how to compute it efficiently. We demonstrate the performance of our approach in classification tasks on low-dimensional synthetic datasets, where density awareness is critical, as well as on real-world time series datasets.

papers.title: Biran decomposition and relative symplectic cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $(M,ω)$ be a closed monotone integral symplectic manifold with monotonicity constant $τ>0$, and let $D\subset M$ be a symplectic hyperplane section of degree $0<k<τ$. By Biran's decomposition theorem, $M$ is the union of a symplectic disk bundle over $D$ and the skeleton of the complement $M\setminus D$ equipped with its Liouville structure. In this paper, we compute the relative symplectic cohomology of circle subbundles of this disk bundle over $\mathbb{Z}$ in terms of the quantum cohomology of $D$. This relative symplectic cohomology depends on the radius of the circle bundle relative to a certain critical radius. For a broad class of pairs $(M,D)$, we prove that the relative symplectic cohomology over $\mathbb{Z}$ does not vanish for supercritical radii. Therefore, circle bundles of supercritical radii are heavy subsets, which yields infinite dimensional quasi-flats in the Hamiltonian diffeomorphism group with respect to both the Hofer metric and the spectral metric over $\mathbb{Z}$. We also establish that if the degree $k$ of $D$ is greater than one, the skeleton of $M\setminus D$ is SH-full over $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$, and hence non-displaceable in $M$ by any symplectomorphism.

papers.title: Exclusion vs Noncolliding Dynamics in Markov Processes
papers.abstract: Let $(ξ_t)_{t \geq 0}$ be a continuous-time Markov process taking values in a countable state space $E$. We consider $k$ copies of $ξ$ started from distinct positions, and write $X = (X_t)_{t \geq 0}$ for the resulting process of configurations in $E^k$. We compare two forms of interaction between the particles: the first is conditioning the particles to never collide (noncolliding dynamics), and the second is simply switching off any jumps that would cause two particles to occupy the same position (exclusion dynamics). We show under mild conditions on the tail probabilities of the collision time that the dynamics are related by an explicit exponential martingale change of measure of one another. This generalises a recent result in the integrable probability literature relating TASEP on the ring to asymmetric walkers conditioned to never collide.

papers.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
papers.abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers average to a non-positive value. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

papers.title: A Formalism for Merging Power Series in Solving Multinomial Equations: Master Series and Master Numbers
papers.abstract: It is shown that all solutions of the canonical equation y^a = 1 + a*x*y^b with arbitrary complex exponents a, b (case m = 1) and of its limiting cases - the binomial root y = (1 + a*x)^(1/a) at b = 0, the exponential y = e^x at a = 0, b = 0, and the Lambert equation y = e^(x*y^b) at a = 0 - as well as the logarithms of these solutions (case m = 0), are expressed by a single power master series M(m; a; b; x) = m + x + ((m - a + 2b)/2!) x^2 + ((m - a + 3b)(m - 2a + 3b)/3!) x^3 + ... For multivalued solutions beyond the radius of convergence, a geometric criterion for selecting the conjugate series (the same master series, but with a different set of parameters M(m; a'; b'; x')) is proposed, ensuring branch continuity on the complex plane. This representation of power series in terms of master numbers not only allows one to compute coefficients in degenerate cases where the gamma-function representation loses meaning, but also provides a transparent analytical algorithm for the merge operation on master series. The method is illustrated on problems in gas dynamics and plasma physics, where it is demonstrated that physically realizable states require the application of conjugate series beyond the radius of convergence of the basic expansion.

papers.title: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses
papers.abstract: We study smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses. This widely studied framework bridges i.i.d. sampling and adversarial covariate selection through a smoothness parameter $\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}$, which bounds conditional covariate densities relative to a fixed, unknown base measure. We propose Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm that achieves sublinear regret $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\text{Pdim}(\mathcal{F}) \textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}} T})$ for function classes with bounded pseudo-dimension. The algorithm aggregates a carefully constructed family of experts using Hedge, with a prior that links regret to the number of disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function. We bound this number by exploiting covariate smoothness. This answers an open problem posed in \cite{blanchard2025agnostic} on the minimax optimal adaptive regret of the smoothed online regression problem. We establish a matching lower bound for the class of linear predictors. The main intricacy of the lower bound lies in explicitly constructing a challenging sequential covariate distribution supported on mutually orthogonal hyperplanes. This construction may be of independent technical interest. Finally, we revisit the well-specified setting and quantify the effect of response noise. For conditionally $ν^2$-subGaussian responses, we extend the existing lower bound under realizable responses by showing that the minimax expected regret is $Ω((1\vee ν)\sqrt{(\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}-1)dT})$ for a function class of VC dimension $d$. A corresponding upper bound for ERM matches this dependence on $ν$.

papers.title: Nearly optimal packings of equally sized rainbow forests
papers.abstract: For every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that whenever $m$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\varepsilon$ and $1\le k\le2m$, every simple graph with $km$ edges and at most $m$ edges of each color contains at least $(1-\varepsilon)m$ edge-disjoint forests, each with $k$ edges of distinct colors. This gives the packing conjectured by Montgomery, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov throughout this range, even when adjacent edges may have the same color. For every $k>2m$ there is a graph on $k$ vertices with $km$ edges of distinct colors and no $k$-edge forest. Applied to $K_n$, the theorem gives $(1-o(1))\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ edge-disjoint rainbow spanning trees whenever each color occurs on at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ edges.

papers.title: Product subcomplexes and intersection complexes of weakly special square complexes
papers.abstract: For compact nonpositively curved square complexes and $\mathrm{CAT}(0)$ square complexes, we define product subcomplexes as equivalence classes of local isometries from products of graphs with embedded coordinate fibers and use them to give a common definition of intersection complexes, reformulating the constructions in the author's earlier paper ``Quasi-isometry invariants of weakly special square complexes'' (Topology and its Applications 307 (2022), 107945). Within this framework, we recover the intended deck quotient description for compact two-sided weakly special square complexes and the quasi-isometry correspondence for their universal covers. Under a simplicity hypothesis on the compact complex, our intersection complex agrees with the image-defined reduced intersection complex in that paper, while finite counterexamples show why images alone do not determine the quotient in general.

papers.title: A bar operation on the double affine Hecke algebra
papers.abstract: We construct a bar-type operation for the affine Hecke algebra $\Ha$ attached to a symmetrizable Kac--Moody group. Our main tool is a geometric bimodule defined using the equivariant $K$-theory of a suitable version of the Steinberg variety for this Kac--Moody group. Using elements of this bimodule corresponding to standard and costandard Hodge $D$-modules on the Kashiwara flag variety, we define a bar operation on $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ by relating the left and right actions of $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ on this bimodule. A central issue is that the resulting formulas for the bar operation do not preserve the algebra itself and naturally produce infinite expansions. To address this, we introduce certain completions of $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$ on which the bar operation is well-defined. For this construction, we prove a number of combinatorial finiteness results for products in $\mathcal{H}_{W}^a$. In affine type, we further analyze the level-zero part of the algebra and obtain an explicit combinatorial formula for a bar operation on a suitable localization of Cherednik's double affine Hecke algebra. In this case the bar operation itself is not an involution but we also show that this bar operation becomes an involution when the lattice parameter $q$ is set to $1$.

papers.title: There Are No Nontrivial Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
papers.abstract: In his seminal work from 1973, Delsarte conjectured that the Johnson schemes admit no nontrivial perfect codes. We prove this fundamental conjecture which is central in combinatorial coding theory. Our arguments combine lower bounds on the design strength of a perfect code with divisibility conditions for the size of a metric ball. We show that the ball size divides the greatest common divisor of specified binomial coefficients. An exact formula for this gcd implies squarefreeness and localizes a unique power of each prime divisor of the ball size to a short interval. Lloyd polynomials, explicit prime estimates, and bounds for linear forms in logarithms then exclude all radii except for $1$ and $2$. Additional arithmetic arguments handle these two remaining radii.

papers.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

papers.title: A $\sqrt{2}$-Approximation to the Bilu-Linial Conjecture
papers.abstract: Bilu and Linial conjectured that if $d\ge 2$, then every $d$-regular graph $G$ has an edge signing $σ:E(G)\to\{-1,1\}$ such that its signed adjacency matrix $A_σ$ satisfies the Ramanujan bound \begin{equation*} ρ(A_σ)\le 2\sqrt{d-1} \end{equation*} and they proved that \begin{equation*} ρ(A_σ)=O\!\left(\sqrt{d\log^3 d}\right). \end{equation*} Using a method of interlacing polynomials, Marcus, Spielman, and Srivastava confirmed one side of this conjecture that there is a signing $σ$ for which \[ λ_{\max}(A_σ)\le 2\sqrt{d-1}. \] By constructing an auxiliary bipartite graph from a balanced orientation of $G$ and applying a bipartite signing argument, we prove that every finite simple graph $G$ of maximum degree $d\ge 3$ admits an edge signing $σ$ such that \[ ρ(A_σ) \le 4\sqrt{\left\lceil \frac d2\right\rceil-1} \le 2\sqrt{2(d-1)}. \] This gives a new proof of Ravichandran and Srivastava's bound $2\sqrt{2(d-1)}$.

papers.title: Generic vanishing subschemes of codimension three
papers.abstract: We classify geometrically nondegenerate GV subschemes of codimension three in indecomposable principally polarized complex abelian varieties of dimension $g\ge6$. Every such subscheme is a translate of $\pm W_{g-3}(C)$ in the Jacobian of a smooth curve $C$. We also compute the cohomology of all twists of $I_X\otimes L$ by topologically trivial line bundles, and characterize the hyperelliptic case by a jump of $h^1$.

papers.title: Pauli Supported Invariants for Periodic Graphs-Derived Hamiltonians
papers.abstract: We introduce a graph invariant obtained from Pauli decompositions of Hamiltonians derived from local graph neighborhoods. Given a rooted h-hop neighborhood, we construct a local adjacency operator, embed it into a common Hilbert space dimension, and define its Pauli-support set as the collection of Pauli strings appearing with nonzero coefficients. For periodic graphs, we prove invariance under lattice-compatible graph equivalence and establish converse results under root-separation hypothesis. The framework naturally extends to Lie closures, commutants, and Cartan-type structures generated by the associated Pauli supports. We further discuss extensions to aperiodic graphs with finite local complexity and make connections to cut-and-project models of quasicrystals and notably, Penrose tilings. From a quantum information perspective, the resulting invariants provide a operator-theoretic description of graph-based Hamiltonians and offer a new mechanism for comparing graph-based quantum systems through Pauli-support data.

papers.title: Total Generalized Variation for Inverse Problems Involving Piecewise Linear Finite Elements
papers.abstract: Higher-order regularization has shown improved results over first-order methods such as total variation. Piecewise linear discretizations are required in applications such as electrocardiographic imaging, where the forward operator is only defined for weakly differentiable functions. In this paper, convergence of a piecewise linear finite element discretization is shown for the non-symmetric second-order total generalized variation functional in a denoising setting. Both the function and the auxiliary variable are discretized with piecewise linear finite elements. Additionally, this convergence result is extended to a spatiotemporal setting after the spatiotemporal function space is comprehensively introduced. In both cases, discrete minimizers converge to the continuous minimizer with rate $h^{1/4}$ in the mesh size $h$, matching the best known rate for finite element discretizations of total variation in the same general setting. Numerical experiments on regular and unstructured meshes are consistent with the theoretical convergence rates and indicate faster convergence in practice, with observed rates of $h^{1/2}$ in the spatial and $h$ in the spatiotemporal setting relative to a high-resolution reference solution. For image denoising and inpainting on a standard benchmark dataset, reconstruction quality is comparable to related piecewise constant and piecewise linear methods, while using half the degrees of freedom of the piecewise constant discretization. The spatiotemporal case is discussed using the example of the inverse problem in electrocardiographic imaging. On three synthetic two-dimensional test cases, the proposed functional outperforms Tikhonov and spatiotemporal total variation regularization, reducing the relative error by 12.5 to 43.1% over first-order Tikhonov regularization.

papers.title: On the variation of slopes over moduli stacks of Galois representations
papers.abstract: In studying slopes of p-adic eigenforms, focusing on eigenforms with a fixed residual Galois representation is a standard approach. In this paper, we go further and explicitly study how slopes vary as the residual representations vary over a characteristic p space that is closely related to Emerton and Gee's moduli stack of Galois representations. This space, which was introduced in work of Dotto, Emerton, and Gee, is simply a chain of projective lines. We prove that as we move in one direction along this chain the slopes of eigenforms satisfy a snaking property: the n-th slope increases (resp. decreases) for n odd (resp. n even). Our method of proof involves first showing that another sequence of slopes, called the k-derivative slopes, follows its own snaking pattern over the moduli. This is quite interesting in its own right, as these slopes are closely related to slopes of L-invariants attached to eigenforms of level exactly divisible by p. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture, recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao, is "stable under direct sums". We determine how p-adic slopes of modular forms vary as their associated Galois representations modulo p vary over moduli of Galois representations. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao is "stable under direct sums".

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent
papers.abstract: Gradient descent (GD) is one of the most fundamental algorithms in optimization. Yet even for smooth convex objectives, the optimal rate among predetermined nonnegative stepsize schedules has remained unresolved. Altschuler and Parrilo [Mathematical Programming, 2025] showed that their recursive silver stepsize schedule achieves an $O(n^{-p_{\mathrm{sil}}})$ rate, where $p_{\mathrm{sil}}=\log_2(1+\sqrt2)\approx1.2716$, improving upon the classical $O(n^{-1})$ rate of constant-step GD. Although the optimality of $p_{\mathrm{sil}}$ has been well supported by numerical evidence for small $n$, a matching lower bound has remained missing. In this paper, we prove an $Ω(n^{-p_{\mathrm{sil}}-o(1)})$ lower bound for GD, showing that $p_{\mathrm{sil}}$ is the optimal convergence exponent. Additionally, we prove an anytime lower bound that matches the exponent $2p_{\mathrm{sil}}/(1+p_{\mathrm{sil}})\approx1.1195$ of the known upper bound [Zhang, Lee, Du, and Chen, COLT 2025]. Building on the approaches of [Ma and Chen, 2026; Jung, Cho, and Yun, 2026], we select specific iterations as checkpoints at which the GD trajectory explores a new coordinate, and we couple these coordinates using a chain of local functions. Our main technical contribution is a local hard function that bends the GD trajectory between successive checkpoints, resulting in a sharpened lower bound. For each prescribed stepsize schedule, we maximize this bound over admissible checkpoint sets. A recursive analysis of this maximum then yields a lower bound matching the silver exponent for every such schedule.

papers.title: Todd's relation conjecture and binary relations for multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: We prove Todd's relation conjecture: all $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values are generated from the fundamental binary relation by the operators $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}\circ \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$; moreover they are also generated by $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}\circ\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$. The $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$-part of this conjecture has been proved by Chang, Chen and Mishiba. We prove the whole conjecture for Carlitz multiple polylogarithm values, which implies the $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$-part for multiple zeta values. We also determine all fixed relations and binary relations. Let $\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by binary relations of weight $w$, and let $\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by fixed relations. We derive generating functions $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^{q+1}(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}$ and $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^q(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}.$ Our results are based on the recent work of Im-Kim-Ngo Dac on the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values, and a system of transfer theorems between multiple zeta values and multiple polylogarithm values.

papers.title: Bounded Ratios of Lorentzian Polynomials I: The Ternary Theory and Optimal Bounding Constants
papers.abstract: We study bounded coefficient ratios and their optimal bounding constants for ternary Lorentzian polynomials. For every degree $d\geq2$ and every fixed ternary $M$-convex support, we prove that bounded ratios are generated by those of quadratic derivatives. We express the optimal bounding constants through a variational formula. For full support, we determine all linear relations among the logarithms of triangular ratios in every degree. For ternary cubics, we compute sharp constants for products of any two distinct triangular ratios. Finally, we compare the bounds for Lorentzian polynomials with those for volume polynomials and rank-three matroid basis counts.

papers.title: Fast Gauss Sums via Flash Attention
papers.abstract: Gauss kernel sums are the computational core of maximum mean discrepancies (MMDs), kernel gradient flows, Stein variational gradient descent (SVGD), and many other kernel methods. At the same time, softmax attention has received an extraordinary amount of hardware-aware code engineering, culminating in FLASH attention. We show that Gauss kernel sums with arbitrary, signed weights can be evaluated via FLASH attention: two small input augmentations turn the normalized softmax reduction into the unnormalized Gauss sum, without writing a single line of custom GPU code. For feature dimension $D>8$ in fp16, this approach beats compiled PyTorch code in speed and memory, and PyKeOps kernels in speed and accuracy at comparable or lower memory. Its memory scaling remains linear.

papers.title: The Order of the Non-universal Tree of a Hilbert Space with Respect to the Haar Basis
papers.abstract: In his 1994 doctoral thesis, Bossard introduced the notion of the non-universal tree $T_{NU}(X)$ associated with each separable Banach space $X$ which does not contain an isomorphic copy of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Together with the order operation defined on well-founded trees, we obtain a method of classifying the complexity of separable Banach spaces by the degree of isomorphism of finite-dimensional subspaces of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Despite further refinement of this concept in later years, we are unaware of any specific instances of direct exhibitions of the order of the non-universal tree for a concrete space and basis. We show that if $H$ is any separable Hilbert space, then $o(T_{NU}(H)) = ω + 1$ when taken with respect to the Haar basis for $C(2^\mathbb{N})$, demonstrating that the class of Hilbert spaces is the least complex class with respect to this measurement when considering this basis.

papers.title: Fredholm and Sturm--Liouville Type Characterizations of the Limit Measure for the Kac Killing Penalization for Lévy Processes
papers.abstract: We study Kac killing penalization for one-dimensional recurrent Lévy processes with respect to a finite positive compactly supported measure. We first establish the penalization limit along an independent exponential clock and characterize the function governing the limiting law in terms of the renormalized zero resolvent. We show that this function is uniquely determined by a Fredholm integral equation together with a natural normalization condition. Our main result identifies an equivalent distributional characterization: the limiting function is the unique solution, subject to a prescribed growth condition at infinity, of a Sturm--Liouville-type equation involving the infinitesimal generator of the Lévy process and the penalizing measure. The key ingredient is the identity that the renormalized zero resolvent is a fundamental solution of the Lévy generator. When the process has a finite second moment, we give an equivalent increment condition at infinity. These results extend the classical Brownian Sturm--Liouville characterization and, in particular, provide its nonlocal analogue for recurrent stable processes. Finally, we identify the limiting process as a Doob h-transform of the associated Feynman--Kac subprocess and obtain a path decomposition.

papers.title: Complemented Copies of $c_{0}$ in Positive Tensor Products of Banach Lattices
papers.abstract: A result of Cembranos states that a non-trivial injective tensor product of a $C$-space contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$, and in particular fails the Grothendieck property. We establish a positive analogue of the Cembranos theorem for tensor products of Banach lattices. If $E$ and $F$ are infinite dimensional Banach lattices, one of which contains a copy of $c_{0}$, then the Wittstock tensor product $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$. If $F$ is in addition reflexive, then $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ fails the positive Grothendieck property.

papers.title: Fröberg's Conjecture for Products of Linear Forms: Split Powers and Inherited Syzygies
papers.abstract: Fröberg's conjecture predicts the Hilbert series of a polynomial ring modulo general forms. We study explicit products of linear forms over fields of characteristic zero. In four variables, six $d$th powers fail to attain the predicted series for $d\ge4$. We fix seven rational directions, take five $d$th powers, and split the sixth generator between the two remaining directions with exponents $\lceil d/2\rceil$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$. The quotient has the predicted series for $1\le d\le30$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $d$, its Hilbert function agrees with the prediction in every degree $q\le(11/5-\varepsilon)d$ or $q\ge(73/32+\varepsilon)d$. In contrast, for $d\ge4$ the predicted series cannot occur if each of the six forms has a linear factor of multiplicity at least $(15d+91)/16$. In three variables, relations among five powers $L_i^e$ give relations among the products $L_i^eM_i$. For five general pairs of linear forms and $e\ge36$, these relations and the pure-power Hilbert function give a lower bound whose error is at most $55$ in every degree and is zero through degree $\lfloor(7e+5)/4\rfloor-2$. The maximum excess over the comparison proposed by Shapiro is $(10/3)e+O(\sqrt e)$.

papers.title: Randomized Block Davidson Eigensolvers for Plane-Wave Density-Functional Theory
papers.abstract: Iterative diagonalization is the dominant cost of plane-wave density-functional theory (DFT), with search-space orthogonalization scaling particularly quickly with problem size and the number of target states. We present a randomized block Davidson-type eigensolver that replaces Euclidean orthogonalization with randomized Gram-Schmidt in a sketched inner product, requiring only a single pass over the basis while keeping its conditioning bounded independently of the input vectors. This modification changes only the Rayleigh-Ritz step, which becomes a definite generalized Hermitian eigenproblem. Ritz extraction remains exact, preserving true Ritz pairs and the interlacing property that makes each band energy an upper bound on the true one. The method is implemented in mixed precision for CPUs and GPUs from a single Julia code, interfaces matrix-free with DFTK, and is released in the open-source RandESC library. On sparse test problems with a fixed number of eigenpairs, the sketched solver overtakes its deterministic counterpart beyond matrix dimensions of about $2\times 10^4$ and is $25\%$ faster at $5\times 10^5$. In full self-consistent field DFT calculations, the benefits of sketching depend on the application case. With standard pseudopotentials and plane-wave cutoffs, efficiency gains are limited. As the number of requested states grows with system size, orthogonalization savings are offset by the generalized eigenproblem. However, some highly accurate pseudopotentals require larger cutoffs, and in this regime, the randomized solver is measurably better by $6\%$ overall. Its relative efficiency also improves as simulated systems get larger.

papers.title: On the Maximum Number of Vertices that Belong to Every Metric Basis
papers.abstract: Resolving sets of graphs have been widely studied since their introduction in the 1970's by Slater and, independently, by Harary and Melter. The minimum cardinality of a resolving set of a graph $G$ is called the metric dimension of $G$ and is denoted by $\dim(G)$. In this paper, we concentrate on the existence of vertices in a graph $G$ that belong to all metric bases of $G$, i.e. resolving sets of cardinality $\dim(G)$. Such vertices are called basis forced vertices, and we denote the number of them by $\mathrm{bf}(G)$. We show that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/3(n-\dim(G)-1)$ for any connected nontrivial graph $G$ of order $n$. In addition, we show that this bound can be attained. Furthermore, it also implies that $\mathrm{bf}(G)\le 2/5(n-1)$ holds for any nontrivial connected graph $G$. This result answers a question posed by Bagheri \emph{et al.} in 2016. Moreover, we provide a complete realization of the parameters $n$, $\dim(G)$ and $\mathrm{bf}(G) \ge 1$ within the previous bounds. We consider some extremal cases related to basis forced vertices in a graph, in particular, we give a full characterization of the graphs with $\mathrm{bf}(G) = 2$ and $\dim(G) = n-4$.

papers.title: Weighted bond posets and a new chromatic symmetric function
papers.abstract: The classical bond lattice of a graph was used in a formula of Whitney to compute the chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we use weighted versions of the bond lattice, to introduce and study a new polynomial and a new symmetric function invariant of a graph. Examples of the new polynomial invariant include the classical Narayana polynomials (for the path graph), the tree-Eulerian polynomials (for the complete graph), and the binomial-Eulerian polynomials (for the star graph). These examples suggest an interesting connection to $h$-polynomials of general graph-associahedra. We prove that for any chordal graph, our polynomial graph invariant is $γ$-positive. Multiweighted bond posets yield a symmetric function graph invariant that is an analog of the chromatic polynomial. The highest degree homogeneous component of this symmetric function is of particular interest. The parking function symmetric function introduced by Haiman arises as an example, as do symmetric functions studied by the first author in connection with multibracketed Lie algebras and with colored exterior algebras. The $γ$-positivity result mentioned above is a specialization of an $e$-positivity result for the highest degree homogeneous component, which we prove for any chordal graph using the theory of lexicographic shellability. We conjecture that this symmetric function is Schur-log-concave, which specializes to Huh's log-concavity theorem for the chromatic polynomial.

papers.title: A Game-Theoretic Characterization of Feedback Capability for Fully Coupled Vector-Valued Nonparametric Systems
papers.abstract: We study feedback stabilization for the discrete-time system $x_{t+1}=f(x_t)+u_t+w_{t+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with unknown $f$ and arbitrary bounded disturbances. For scalar plants, the sharp feedback capability threshold under generalized Lipschitz uncertainty is $\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$. We treat fully coupled vector-valued systems, where scalar order and interval recursion are unavailable and coupling precludes a coordinatewise reduction. We introduce a response-history escape game whose adversarial objective requires a finite envelope and an unbounded state radius. Borel determinacy, invariance under a change of finite initial history, and slope monotonicity define a game value $Γ_d$. One causal feedback law stabilizes every plant in the uncertainty class against every bounded disturbance sequence whenever $L<Γ_d$. At every $L\geΓ_d$, each causal feedback law and each initial state admit a globally $Γ_d$-Lipschitz plant whose state norms tend to infinity with zero disturbances. Thus stabilization is possible exactly below the critical value. We also prove $Γ_d=1+(\log d)/(2d)+O((\log\log d)/d)$, with explicit coefficients in bounds on both sides of the remainder. Explicit finite-dimensional bounds give $Γ_d>1$ in every dimension and $Γ_2\ge 7/5$. A nearest-neighbor law achieves the planar guarantee. The values are nonincreasing in dimension, and comparison with the scalar theory yields $Γ_1=\frac{3}{2}+\sqrt{2}$.

papers.title: A congruence obstruction to Roman's bound for Zarankiewicz numbers
papers.abstract: Let z(m,n;s,t) be the largest number of ones in an m x n zero-one matrix with no s x t all-ones submatrix. Roman's 1975 inequality gives a general upper bound for s >= 3, with improvements known in special parameter ranges. We show it is not attained on much of the range just below the design threshold T = (t-1)C(m,s)/(s+1). For n = T-c with 1 <= c <= sT/(s+2), Roman's bound equals the counting bound. Viewing columns as sets of row indices (points), attainment forces all but at most one column to have cardinality s+1 or s+2. These two sizes contribute multiples of d = gcd(s,C(s+1,2)) to the coverage count at each point. At each point, the unused coverage is congruent to mu modulo d, with a correction for the possible exceptional column. With r = c mod s and sigma(r) a slack depending only on s, the bound drops by at least one whenever 1 <= sigma(r) < d and m*mu != s*sigma(r), or mu != 0 and m*mu > s*sigma(r). The first needs s odd and is confined to one residue class; the second covers the whole interval when mu != 0 and m is sufficiently large. For s = 4, t = 2, m = 28 all 2730 values of n are covered. For odd s, when c = (s+1)/2 and an s-(m,s+1,t-1) design exists we obtain the exact value z = (s+1)(T-c). We also locate the obstruction relative to linear programming: the refined program of Davies, Gill and Horsley (2026) still attains the Roman vertex on an explicit family of such parameters.

papers.title: Real morsifications via the trace map
papers.abstract: We prove that every reduced real plane curve singularity admits a real morsification. This settles a question of A'Campo and Gusein-Zade, later stated as conjectures by Leviant--Shustin and by Fomin--Pylyavskyy--Shustin--Thurston. In particular we overcome the main obstruction that remained posed by conjugate pairs of nonreal branches. Our new main ingredient is a construction that produces the divide from a nodal smoothing of two normalization disks. This is what we call the trace map. For real branches, it recovers Gusein-Zade's construction using Chebyshev polynomials. For pairs of complex conjugate branches with distinct tangents, the construction gives an explicit formula for the divide in terms of the Puiseux data. The general method consists in a delicate combination of the trace map with A'Campo's translations and contractions to produce divides and real morsifications for all reduced real plane curve singularities.

papers.title: Classification of some $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank 6
papers.abstract: A fusion category $\mathcal{C}$ is said to be $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic if the group $G(\mathcal{C})$ of invertible objects is isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, and the remaining simple objects form an orbit under the action of $G(\mathcal{C})$. In this paper, we give a partial classification of spherical $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-quadratic fusion categories of rank six. More precisely, we show that its Grothendieck ring $\mathcal{K}_0(\mathcal{C})$ must be one of nine fusion rings if the fusion rule multiplicities are less than $20$, and the categorifications of five of them are previously known. We prove that one of the last four fusion rings can be realized as de-equivariantization of a near-group fusion category of type $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}+8$.

papers.title: At least seven modes in a heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture
papers.abstract: A Gaussian mixture density can have more modes than components. It has been conjectured that the maximum number of modes of a $d$-variate $k$-component Gaussian mixture density is $\binom{d+k-1}{d}$, which equals six for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. We construct an explicit family of equally weighted heteroscedastic three-component bivariate Gaussian mixture densities with at least seven distinct nondegenerate modes, showing that this conjectured upper bound fails for $(d,k)=(2,3)$. To the best of our knowledge, this provides the first counterexample to the conjecture across all pairs $(d,k)$.

papers.title: Fundamental group schemes of globally F-regular varieties
papers.abstract: Let X be a globally F-regular projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. We show that the Nori fundamental group scheme of its regular locus is finite and linearly reductive. Finiteness is the counterpart of theorems of Xu and Braun on the fundamental group of the smooth locus of a complex log Fano variety. The key input is that if a cover of a splinter is a torsor in codimension one and induces an isomorphism on global functions, then its structure group is linearly reductive. We then show that towers of such covers stabilize, both over globally $F$-regular varieties and, in mixed characteristic, over the globally $+$-regular schemes considered by Cai-Lee-Ma-Schwede-Tucker.

papers.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
papers.abstract: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.

papers.title: Positive definite matrices and involutions: the manners of their infinite cousins
papers.abstract: Matrices and involutions in/on the algebras $B(\mathbb{R})$ and $B(\mathbb{C})$ of real (resp., complex) row- and column-finite $ω\timesω$ matrices are studied. It is proved that any positive definite $\mathbb{R}$-algebra involution on $B(\mathbb{R})$ (resp., any positive definite conjugate-linear involution on $B(\mathbb{C})$) is given by conjugating the transpose involution (resp., the conjugate-transpose involution) with a positive definite matrix from the algebra in question. All positive definite matrices in these algebras have Cholesky factorizations within the algebra. Examples are constructed to show that such positive definite matrices need not have any eigenvalues for their canonical action on column-finite column vectors, and they need not have any square roots in $B(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: A New Look at the Classical Estimation Problem
papers.abstract: Bahadur's \emph{Lectures on the Theory of Estimation} develop the classical theory of point estimation inside the geometry of Hilbert space, and they record with unusual honesty where the theory strains: the locally best unbiased estimate depends on the parameter, a two-point parameter space yields an estimate Bahadur calls absurd, the odds in binomial sampling have no unbiased estimate, and the virtues of maximum likelihood remain heuristics. We present a subset of the lectures in Bahadur's notation and, at each strain, make one small modification: for each sample point, an estimate $τ$ becomes a function on the parameter space rather than a point in it. The result is the continuum of null hypotheses that Fisher, in 1955, identified with the theory of estimation; we call this \emph{generalized estimation}, and $τ$ a generalized estimator. Bahadur's own definition of an estimate, square-integrable at every distribution in the family, already supplies the domain. The payoffs are tracked lecture by lecture: estimators that exist at boundary samples where point estimates do not; an elementary lemma showing that no pointwise criterion admits a uniformly optimal estimator, which explains why admissibility, minimaxity, Bayes averaging and unbiasedness arose; assessment by information, $Λ(τ)$, with the score attaining the Fisher information bound uniformly by a three-line argument; Cramér--Rao attainment and sufficiency recovered as equality cases of that bound; and the maximum likelihood heuristics converted into exact statements about the score. Nothing classical is overturned; the classical apparatus is explained by Fisher's characterization of estimation as a continuum of significance tests.

papers.title: A major origin of quantumness
papers.abstract: A system property is considered to be elementary, when any further refined specification is impossible. Any two elementary properties of a classical system mutually exclude each other. However, this does not hold anymore for a quantum system, where mutual exclusivity becomes a special relation. This orthogonality relation becomes our first axiom. It is sufficient to define states in an abstract setting and we then introduce two simple, but far-reaching further basic axioms for the states, which mimic the quantum mechanical correspondence between the pure states and the rank-one projections. All examples that we can identify origin from operator algebras or certain Jordan algebras and require the Gleason theorem. The identification of further cases is an unresolved challenge. If some exist, they might result in promising new mathematical models for an extended quantum theory. The non-existence would mean that our extremely basic postulates bring us unexpectedly close to common quantum theory. In any case, the distinction between inequality and mutual exclusivity of elementary system properties appears to be a major origin of quantumness. Our basic approach does not encompass the non-atomic von Neumann algebras of type II and III, which play a crucial role in quantum field theory, and we present a modification of the axioms to include them.

papers.title: Continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation on the integers and the real numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, the continuous solutions of the complex Kac--Bernstein functional equation \[ f_1 ( u + v ) f_2 ( u - v ) f_1 ( u' + v' ) f_2 ( u' - v' ) = f_1 ( u + v' ) f_2 ( u - v' ) f_1 ( u' + v ) f_2 ( u' - v ) \] are classified for $ \mathbb{ Z } $ and $ \mathbb{ R } $. By using this classification for $ \mathbb{ Z } $, we consider a generalization of the Kac--Bernstein theorem on the one-dimensional torus $ \mathbb{ T } $ by Baryshnikov--Eisenberg--Stadje from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures. Similarly, the original Kac--Bernstein theorem on $ \mathbb{ R } $ is generalized from probability Borel measures to complex Borel measures.

papers.title: Regularity and Decay for Navier-Slip Fluid-Structure Interaction in Exterior Domains
papers.abstract: We study the linearized motion of a spherical rigid body immersed in an incompressible viscous fluid occupying the whole space, under Navier slip boundary conditions with friction. While semigroup regularity and decay estimates are well understood for the no-slip case, such results have been limited to bounded domains in the slip setting. By exploiting the geometric regularity of the sphere, we establish strong $L^q$-regularity, bounded analyticity, and sharp $ L^q-L^r$ estimates for the corresponding fluid-structure operator. These results would provide a foundation for constructing strong $W^{2,1}_q$ solutions and Kato-type solutions to the corresponding nonlinear system.

papers.title: Non-orbit 3-representation-finite symmetric algebras
papers.abstract: We construct two $3$-representation-finite symmetric algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero that are not orbit algebras of repetitive categories. This answers a question of Darpö and Iyama in the negative.

papers.title: Matroid Contention Resolution with Concentration
papers.abstract: Contention resolution schemes (CRS) are widely used for rounding fractional solutions subject to combinatorial constraints. Their guarantees are typically in expectation. Such guarantees alone do not ensure that covering constraints hold, limiting the applicability to problems with covering requirements. We prove lower-tail concentration bounds for the random-order CRS of Adamczyk and Włodarczyk (AW) under the intersection of $k$ matroid constraints.
