In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing. For infinitesimally rigid sections we compute the GV contributions, recovering the $E_8$ theta product over a $(-1)$-curve. We formulate the corresponding conjecture for families of sections.

papers.title: Schatten and weak Schatten classes of composition operator differences on Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We investigate Schatten and weak Schatten class membership of differences of composition operators on the standard weighted Bergman spaces over the unit disk. We prove that the known sufficient condition for Schatten p-class membership is also necessary for 0<p<2, thereby completing the characterization for all p>0. We also characterize when differences of composition operators belong to weak Schatten classes for every p>0. Both results are expressed in terms of local-mass conditions involving the pseudohyperbolic distance between the inducing maps, and yield two-sided (quasi-)norm estimates.

papers.title: Fibrations and nilpotent collapsing structure
papers.abstract: We construct fiber bundles, singular fibrations, and nilpotent collapsing structures for Riemannian manifolds with lower Ricci curvature bounds under additional geometric assumptions. For every $n$ and $D>0$, there exists $ε(n,D)>0$ such that a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold $M$ satisfying \[ \operatorname{diam}(M)\le D,\qquad \operatorname{sec}_M\ge-1,\qquad \operatorname{Ric}_M\ge-ε(n,D) \] admits a finite cover of degree at most $C(n)$ that is a smooth fiber bundle over a nilmanifold. The fibers have finite fundamental group, and the base dimension equals the Hirsch rank of $π_1(M)$. If $π_1(M)$ is torsion-free, then $M$ itself fibers smoothly over an infranilmanifold with simply connected fibers. We next consider a Gromov--Hausdorff convergent sequence $M_i\to X$ of closed Riemannian $n$-manifolds with uniformly bounded diameter, $\operatorname{Ric}_{M_i}\ge -(n-1)$, and the $(ρ,δ)$ local rewinding Reifenberg condition, where $ρ>0$ is fixed and $δ$ is sufficiently small. For all sufficiently large $i$, we construct singular fibrations $\bar{F}_i:M_i\to X$ that are $ε_i$-Gromov--Hausdorff approximations, with $ε_i\to0$, and whose fibers are homeomorphic to infranilmanifolds. Under the same local hypotheses, complete, possibly noncompact manifolds admit nilpotent collapsing structures on their $ε(n,ρ)$-collapsed regions.

papers.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
papers.abstract: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem. Our theorem also applies more generally to higher order stability, Frobenius weights, and braided vector spaces. As a special case of our theorem, we can deduce stability lines depending only on when $H_0(\mathrm{Hur}^c_n,\mathbb{Q})$ stabilizes, which are sharp in some cases. We apply this to two families of Hurwitz spaces to obtain bounds on the secondary term for (1) the number of $S_d$-degree $d$ function fields with squarefree discriminant, and (2) Cohen-Lenstra moments.

papers.title: Preserving Ramsey ultrafilters with tree forcings
papers.abstract: We define a wide class of tree forcings that we call $\textit{normed-tree forcings}$ and prove that they can preserve Ramsey ultrafilters. These include $\textit{fat-tree forcings}$ as particular cases. As an application, we prove the consistency with $\mathsf{ZFC}$ of $\mathfrak{d}=\mathfrak{u}=\aleph_1 < \mathsf{minLc}=\mathfrak{c}=\aleph_2$, where $\mathfrak{d}$ denotes the dominating number, $\mathfrak{u}$ the ultrafilter number, and $\mathsf{minLc}$ the minimum localization cardinal. This solves some open questions about pairs of classical cardinal characteristics, such as the consistency of both $\mathfrak{e}_{\mathsf{ubd}}$ and its dual strictly larger than $\mathfrak{u}$.

papers.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
papers.abstract: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$. It controls, in a range of degrees, the restriction of natural transformations $\mathrm{id}\to F$ to the orthogonal complement of the collection, and it is computed from the collection by a finite complex. For collections of line bundles on surfaces whose Hom divisors have nonnegative canonical degree, the tensor product with a skyscraper sheaf has height exactly two, and the projections of skyscraper sheaves form a two-dimensional family of point-like objects in the orthogonal complement. We apply these tools to Orlov's rationality conjecture. A smooth projective complex surface is rational if its derived category has a full exceptional collection in which all members except possibly one are line bundles, or one that consists of at most three completely orthogonal blocks of arbitrary objects; we also obtain rationality in several cases with four blocks or with a hereditary component. If $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of the form $(M_i\boxtimes\mathcal O(a_i))$, then the $M_i$ with relative degrees of a fixed parity form a full exceptional collection on $S$; consequently $S$ is rational whenever $S\times\mathbb P^1$ has a full exceptional collection of line bundles. Finally, we show that the general case of the conjecture for surfaces is equivalent to the surjectivity and injectivity of two maps in Hochschild cohomology.

papers.title: Degree-three Euclidean spanning trees within a factor of 1.514 of the minimum
papers.abstract: For every finite point set $X$ in a Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, we prove that there is a spanning tree of maximum degree three and total length at most $(757/500)\MST(X)=1.514\MST(X)$, where $\MST(X)$ denotes the unrestricted minimum spanning-tree length. More strongly, for any root and any finite list of other points, there is a Hamiltonian path starting at the root whose length is at most $1.514$ times the sum of the root-to-point distances. The proof follows the rooted-path and variable-block framework used in earlier work, and applies Young's weighted-distance inequality to explicit rational mixtures of paths. Eight ordered radius regions cover the normalized domain. Their local estimates require only 29 vertex comparisons, all certified by rational arithmetic. The cover uses the three thresholds $1/4$, $3/8$, and $1/2$; its largest block has nine vertices. We give complete proofs of the normalization transfer, the global induction, and the terminal cases with zero or one actual tail point. We also give a fixed-dimensional cross-polytope lower bound, present Zbarsky's orthogonal simplex-cluster construction in explicit coordinates, and compare their finite-dimension bounds. The base cases complete the upper-bound argument before the lower-bound constructions are presented.

papers.title: Optimal Production Scheduling for Multi-Product Mineral Manufacturing
papers.abstract: Short-term scheduling in multi-product mineral manufacturing requires coordinating material movement and production across interconnected processing stages while addressing confirmed customer orders and longer-term production requirements. This work develops a generalized network-based, lexicographic multi-objective optimization (MOO) scheduling framework for these systems. The formulation represents the progression of material from raw-material supply through production and inventory to customer fulfillment. A sequential objective hierarchy first prioritizes fulfillment of confirmed customer orders and then progressively directs feasible production capacity toward cumulative targets supplied by the facility's demand-planning process. This approach ensures that the performance achieved for each higher-priority objective is preserved before subsequent targets are considered. Selected product-line activation decisions are represented using generalized disjunctive programming (GDP). An industrial mineral-manufacturing case study demonstrates the proposed framework's ability to generate feasible shift-level schedules and preserve the intended operational priorities with practical computational performance.

papers.title: 2-Walk-regular graphs with $k_2$ at most twice the valency
papers.abstract: In this paper, we characterize $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and $k_2\leq 2k$, generalizing a result of Koolen and Park, and classify the distance-regular graphs satisfying these conditions. We also classify $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and at most $4k+4$ vertices.

papers.title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
papers.abstract: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $π$. We show that $π^2 = p\,α_*$ for a unique automorphism $α$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius. For $p \ge 7$ this gives the list of Frobenius types of the Weierstrass points: eight types, each with its Weil polynomial, a congruence condition on $p$, and its number 15, 3, 3, 7, 1, 1, 3 or 1 of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational $(2,2)$-kernels; when all Weierstrass points are rational, the 2-Tate pairing on $J[2]$ is determined by $p \bmod 8$. We then prove closed formulas, in terms of class numbers of imaginary quadratic orders and of $ζ_{\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt p)}(-1)$, for the mass of the curves of each type and for the mass of the rational kernels whose quotient is a product of elliptic curves. For $π^2 = \pm p$ the total masses are due to Ibukiyama and to Xue and Yu; our proofs use the 2-adic Tate modules, the symmetry of the Richelot correspondence and Eichler's mass formula, and, for the other curves, modules over orders of a quartic CM field. The kernels are counted through gluings of supersingular elliptic curves. As a consequence, the proportion of rational kernels with decomposed quotient is of order $p^{-1/2}(1+L(1,χ))$, where $χ$ is the quadratic character of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-p})$. All formulas agree with an exact enumeration for the 37 primes $7 \le p \le 173$. Finally we describe the graph of $\mathbb{F}_p$-rational Richelot isogenies, which is far from connected in the range computed, and discuss what these results say about its use in isogeny-based cryptography.

papers.title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
papers.abstract: To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected. As an application, we prove that among one-ended right-angled Coxeter groups, splitting over a subgroup of an unbounded product subgroup is a quasi-isometry invariant. We also establish several features shared by maximized hyperbolic spaces and curve graphs, including the existence of dead ends and visibility of boundaries. Moreover, when the boundary is nonempty, it is non-compact if and only if the defining graph contains an induced 4-cycle.

papers.title: Extremal Projectors and the Virasoro Algebra
papers.abstract: Extremal projectors are universal operators projecting onto the highest weight space in a representation. Their existence and uniqueness (as formal series) are known for a broad range of Lie superalgebras and quantum groups. We consider a class of Lie superalgebras that contains reductive finite-dimensional Lie algebras as well as the Virasoro algebra. We prove the existence and uniqueness of an extremal projector for this class. The existence proof is given in terms of a recursive algorithm which can be used to compute the coefficients. To illustrate the method, we compute the terms for the Virasoro extremal projector up to order 6. Furthermore, we formulate a conjecture for the denominators of the truncated extremal projector of the Virasoro algebra. We provide symbolic computational evidence up to order 6 and prove a weaker version of the conjecture.

papers.title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle.

papers.title: Geography of Klein bottle Luttinger surgery
papers.abstract: We propose and study a modification of Auroux's uniqueness question on Luttinger surgery by replacing Lagrangian tori with Klein bottles. In Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, we introduce two simple graphs whose connected components give bounds and, in several cases, exact counts of Klein bottle Luttinger equivalence classes. In Kodaira dimension zero, we provide examples of numerical invariants supporting infinitely many equivalence classes and prove a homological non-triviality theorem for Lagrangian Klein bottles in all symplectic Calabi--Yau surfaces with positive Euler characteristic. In positive Kodaira dimensions, we construct examples in which Klein bottle Luttinger surgery changes the symplectic Kodaira dimension.

papers.title: The Kazdan-Warner equation on a finite graph with a Neumann boundary condition
papers.abstract: We study the Kazdan-Warner equation $Δu = c - h \mathrm{e}^u$ on a finite connected domain $Ω$ of a locally finite graph, with Neumann boundary data $\partial u / \partialν= g$. We reduce the boundary condition to homogeneous form and use variational methods and upper and lower solutions to study solvability. Let $c_g \mathrel{:=} |Ω|^{-1}\int_{\partialΩ} g\, \mathrm{d}μ$, and let $ψ$ solve $Δψ= c_g$ with boundary data $\partialψ/ \partialν= g$ and zero mean on $Ω$. When $c = c_g$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ changes sign and $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. When $c > c_g$, a solution exists if and only if $h$ is positive somewhere in $Ω$. When $c < c_g$, solvability requires $\int_Ωh \mathrm{e}^ψ\, \mathrm{d}μ< 0$. Under this condition there is a threshold $-\infty \le c_-(h) < c_g$ such that a solution exists for $c_-(h) < c < c_g$ and no solution exists for $c < c_-(h)$. If $h \le 0$ and $h \not\equiv 0$, a solution exists for every $c < c_g$.

papers.title: A Free Lunch: Gradient Averaging Achieves Optimal Statistical Efficiency in Newton Sketch
papers.abstract: We study statistical inference for online sketched Newton methods, in which each Newton system is approximately solved by an inner randomized sketching solver. Existing work reveals a computational--statistical trade-off: the sketching solver (and its accelerated variants) reduces the per-step cost of Newton methods from $O(d^3)$ to $O(d^2)$, but the randomness introduced by sketching also inflates the limiting covariance of both the last and the averaged Newton iterates. In this work, we address this trade-off via gradient averaging. We show that simply replacing the stochastic gradient with a moving average at each step can mitigate, and in some cases eliminate, the trade-off in Newton sketch. Importantly, gradient averaging requires no additional oracle evaluations and leaves the contraction bound of the inner sketching solver unchanged. In particular, we prove that the last sketched Newton iterate with gradient averaging attains a limiting covariance no larger than that without gradient averaging, while the averaged iterate even attains the minimax optimal limiting covariance, matching that of the exact Newton method. To our knowledge, this is the first analysis showing that randomness introduced to improve computational efficiency need not compromise statistical efficiency as long as proper gradient estimates are used. The key analytical challenge is that gradient averaging destroys the crucial martingale difference structure underlying central limit theorem arguments. We overcome this challenge by analyzing the coupled two-timescale recursions governing the iterate and the gradient estimator. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression support our theoretical covariance comparisons.

papers.title: Circular decompositions for hyperbolic genus one knots
papers.abstract: We consider hyperbolic genus one knots having two or more non-isotopic, disjoint, genus one Seifert surfaces, with the property that the complementary regiones are handlebody pairs. We determine whether or not these knots have circular width equal to $(3)$. Moreover we give bounds on their circular widths. We also give explicit examples of such knots having three or five non-isotopic genus one Seifert surfaces and compute their circular widths. In particular this shows that many of these knots are non-almost fibered.

papers.title: Wei-Norman Factorization of Frenet-Serret equations and the Cardan Lock
papers.abstract: Frenet-Serret equations for particles moving along differentiable curves, in the case of non-constant curvature and torsion, are considered in the framework of the Wei-Norman factorization of the propagator using the Lie algebra of the rotation group. It leads to a system of coupled linear equations that are highly coupled if Euler or Cardan angles are used, but that can be uncoupled if the Cartan basis in the Lie algebra is used, resulting essentially in a Ricatti equation. However, since the rotations algebra is not a solvable algebra, the global Wei-Norman Theorem does not apply and singularities in the solutions of the system of equations appear at certain points, related to the \text{gimbal o Cardan lock}. Notwidthstanding, a detailed study of the limit at these points shows that in most of the cases the propagator is well defined and gimbal lock is avoided.

papers.title: Conditional limit theorems in dynamical systems
papers.abstract: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures. We then establish conditional exponential decay of correlations and the Strong Law of Large Numbers for both deterministic and quenched random systems. We also obtain a conditional Central Limit Theorem, Large Deviation Principle, and Berry--Esseen theorem, with additional assumptions in the quenched random case. We also derive standard (non-conditional) limit theorems on the surviving set of points that never enter the hole.

papers.title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in Čech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates. We validate our approach through experiments on synthetic datasets, and present novel examples of $K(\mathbb{Z}/2, 2)$-coordinates not addressed in prior work.

papers.title: Gumbel Fluctuations of the Maximum of the Airy$_1$ Process
papers.abstract: We establish the Gumbel limit for the maximum of the Airy$_1$ process over $[0,N]$ as $N\to\infty$, with explicit centering of order $(\log N)^{2/3}$ and scale $(\log N)^{-1/3}$. The proof starts with a two-term expansion for the tail of the maximum over a fixed interval. Its leading term determines the centering, while the second term gives the joint-exceedance asymptotic for touching intervals. We then bound joint exceedances in separated unit intervals, uniformly over gaps up to a fixed multiple of the square root of the threshold. Covariance and mixing estimates control the larger gaps and complete the blocking argument.

papers.title: Theorems of the Alternative and Nonnegativity Certificates for Systems of Jensen-type Polynomials with Universal Quantifiers
papers.abstract: We introduce Jensen-type polynomials, a class of possibly nonconvex polynomials that extends the Jensen inequality for SOS-convex polynomials while retaining natural sums of squares (SOS) certificates for nonnegativity. We show that polynomials with essentially nonpositive coefficients belong to this class and establish a composition principle that yields further examples, including componentwise univariate compositions and compositions with structured quadratic maps motivated by source-localization loss functions. We then derive theorems of the alternative that provide SOS certificates for infeasibility of systems of strict inequalities involving Jensen-type polynomials and universally quantified variables. We illustrate our results through two applications, with numerical examples. First, we show that source-localization problems admit an exact SOS reformulation under a simple dimension condition, and that an optimal solution can be recovered by solving a semidefinite program (SDP) and applying the explicit Jensen map. Second, our SOS certificates yield two {\it convergent} SDP hierarchies for semi-infinite optimization with Jensen-type polynomials, providing upper and lower bounds on the optimal value. We also establish finite-convergence and solution-extraction results, under flat truncation rank condition and the associated Jensen maps.

papers.title: Faster polynomial-space algorithms for poset problems
papers.abstract: We give a polynomial-space, deterministic, exact algorithm for counting linear extensions of partial orders over $n$ elements, with running time $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n}) \subseteq O(2.829^n)$. This improves upon the long-standing bound of $O^*(4^{n})$ attainable by standard divide and conquer (Savitch 1970, Gurevich and Shelah 1987). Our algorithm uses a similar balanced splitting approach as the classical algorithm, but applies it only to the elements outside a largest antichain. For the elements of the antichain itself we develop a formula based on inclusion-exclusion that accounts for the ways in which they can appear in a linear extension. The technique is also applicable to other problems on posets, which we illustrate by solving the well-studied jump number problem in a similar running time of $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n})$ and polynomial space. To our knowledge, these are the first polynomial-space algorithms with a running time below $4^n$ for both problems.

papers.title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
papers.abstract: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent. We also show that the equivariant central charges have no poles in the spectral parameter, compute their monodromy and their asymptotics at $z=0$, and formulate an equivariant mirror symmetry conjecture for GKM manifolds.

papers.title: Almost all vertex-transitive graphs and digraphs are Cayley
papers.abstract: We prove that almost all vertex-transitive digraphs are Cayley digraphs, and that almost all vertex-transitive graphs are Cayley graphs, as the number of vertices tends to infinity through all positive integers. The proportions of Cayley objects are at least $1-2^{-n/4+o(n)}$ for digraphs and $1-2^{-n/24+o(n)}$ for graphs. This proves the McKay--Praeger conjecture and its digraph analogue.

papers.title: Statistical robustness and time consistency in risk averse optimization
papers.abstract: The aim of this manuscript is to investigate risk measures which are not necessarily convex. We show that law invariant coherent risk measures are not robust with respect to contamination of the probability measure, in the sense that an arbitrarily small contamination can change their values by an arbitrary amount. This contrasts with the Value-at-Risk, which is robust against such contamination. In addition, we show that for a given law invariant risk measure and a given policy, one can construct, under mild conditions, conditional risk measures with respect to which this policy is time consistent, in the frameworks of both Markov Decision Processes and Stochastic Optimal Control.

papers.title: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
papers.abstract: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver. For a three-parameter rank-two extension family, we determine the splitting types and distinguish the nonzero splitting strata by the determinant of a quantum connecting map. For general non-diagonal rank-two connections, we derive noncommutative Riccati equations for invariant graph submodules and formulate the global splitting problem in terms of holomorphic projectors. We also discuss twisted positive Hochschild cocycles and formulate a variational principle and a conformal-stability conjecture. On the algebraic side, we explain why both the bare sheaf category of the quantum projective line and the Artin--Zhang category of the quantum plane inherit classical Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting. We distinguish these results from unrestricted standard-line splitting, which fails for polynomial gauges, and outline a differential quantum GAGA programme with explicit attention to regularity and equivariance.

papers.title: On Green's Conjecture for Curves on Anticanonical Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove Green's conjecture for smooth curves $C$ on rational surfaces $X$ such that $-K_X|_C$ is effective on $C$. In addition, on birationally ruled surfaces $X$ of irregularity $q \geq 1$ carrying an effective anticanonical divisor, we show that Green's conjecture holds for all smooth curves $C$ on $X$ covering the base curve with degree at least $2$, provided the latter has only finitely many gonal pencils or the gonality of $C$ is special with respect to the ruling.

papers.title: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
papers.abstract: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A. Hanlon, J. Hicks, and O. Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

papers.title: A 5/2 Guarantee for Echelon Stock (s,S) Policies in One-Warehouse Multi-Retailer Systems
papers.abstract: We study a periodic-review warehouse serving multiple heterogeneous retailers with stochastic demand and fixed costs and lead times at both echelons. We construct a deterministic echelon stock (s,S) policy whose long-run expected average cost is at most 5/2 times the optimum over all nonanticipative policies. The guarantee holds when, as in a retail chain with common service penalties, the uniform backlog penalty and heterogeneous retailer holding rates are at least the warehouse holding rate and heterogeneous retailer setup costs are at most 3/2 times the supplier's. The latter setup-cost condition extends beyond supplier setup-cost dominance: a retailer dispatch may incur a setup cost up to 50 percent higher than a supplier order's. Demand vectors are i.i.d. over periods with finite positive means, and demands of different retailers may be correlated. Each retailer selects the full cycle of its single-location plan or a shifted cycle of half its width, under an inflated setup cost, and the warehouse serves requests in arrival order, allowing partial shipments. The upper bound on the policy's cost includes each retailer's mirror cost, which prices the warehouse imbalance created by that retailer's batching. The upper and lower bounds share a pooled supplier problem and add one problem per retailer, giving a factor independent of all lead times and the number of retailers. For arbitrary nonnegative setup costs and associated retailer demands, a consolidation policy holds allocated stock until a dispatch threshold is met and gives a factor below 4.9. On 864 instances built from Walmart store sales, the simulated cost of an integer-rounded implementation of the FIFO policy averages 1.45 times the lower bound and reaches 1.75, and our analytical upper bound on its cost is below 1.94 times the lower bound; both ratios to the lower bound have nearly the same mean at every supplier lead time.

papers.title: A locking-free enriched linearized neural network for linear elasticity
papers.abstract: Volumetric locking remains a fundamental challenge for neural-network Galerkin methods in nearly incompressible elasticity. We introduce the \emph{locking-free enriched linearized neural network} (LF-ENN), to the best of our knowledge, the first neural-network Galerkin method with a rigorous locking-free guarantee. Building on the enriched Galerkin framework, the method combines neural approximation with a structure-preserving enrichment that reduces the discrete incompressibility constraint to a graph-Laplacian problem. This construction enables divergence-free corrections and error estimates uniform in the Lamé parameter $λ\in(0,\infty]$. Nitsche boundary enforcement and tailored stabilization overcome the lack of conventional finite element trace inequalities for neural trial spaces. Under suitable approximation and mesh-resolution assumptions, we establish stability and error estimates independent of network width, mesh size, and $λ$, including an $O(h^s)$ estimate for reduced-regularity solutions with $s>1/2$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions confirm locking-free behavior and demonstrate substantial gains in displacement accuracy. In particular, LF-ENN achieves approximately twelve times smaller displacement error than a higher-order locking-free enriched Galerkin method while using fewer than one-third as many unknowns. These results establish a rigorous neural Galerkin framework that combines incompressibility robustness with markedly improved approximation accuracy.

papers.title: Bourin's Crossed-Heinz Inequality in the Operator and Frobenius Norms
papers.abstract: For positive semidefinite matrices $A, B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $0 < t < 1$, we establish Bourin's crossed-Heinz inequality for every dimension $n \ge 1$ in both the operator norm and the Frobenius norm. In the operator norm, we prove the sharp inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ by normalizing $\|A + B\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ to $2$ and decomposing the normalized crossed-Heinz sum into $P_t P_{1-t} + Q$, where $P_t$, $P_{1-t}$, and $Q$ are self-adjoint contractions. In the Frobenius norm, we establish the sharp quantitative inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 + 4t(1-t)\|A - B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2$ via an exact nonnegative remainder decomposition, showing in particular that $\|A^t B^{1-t} + B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \le \|A + B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ holds with equality if and only if $A = B$.

papers.title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference II: General convex penalties
papers.abstract: For smooth penalties and group Lasso, Part I (https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02624) analyzed approximate leave-one-out (ALO) cross-validation by comparing its weights with the trace correction used in mean-field inference. For a $C^2$ penalty $R$, the matrix entering these corrections is $A=[\nabla^2R(\widehat b)+X^TDX]^{-1}$, where $\widehat b$ is the full-data estimator and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of fitted loss curvatures; for group Lasso, the penalty and loss curvatures are first restricted to the active support before taking the pseudoinverse. The obstacle to extending this argument to general convex penalties was the lack of an explicit formula for the matrix $A$ entering these corrections. For every finite-valued strongly convex penalty, we construct such a matrix from ordinary derivatives of the penalty response at the observed subgradient. Its projection--pseudoinverse formula separates the response space and penalty curvature, fixed by conditioning, from the explicit design dependence. This supplies the missing ingredient to extend the probabilistic argument of Part~I. The construction recovers the inverse Hessian for smooth penalties and the active-group inverse for group Lasso, including inactive boundary groups. In the proportional regime, for Gaussian designs with general positive-definite covariance and covariance-scaled strong convexity, we obtain unconditional bounds comparing both ALO and mean-field predictions with exact leave-one-out predictions in regression and single-index models. The expected average squared prediction error is $O(n^{-1})$, and the expected absolute criterion error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, under bounded, 1-Lipschitz loss scores and suitable test functions. The matrix and ALO weights use only observed data; the mean-field correction additionally uses the design covariance. The proofs are formalized in Lean~4.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
papers.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

papers.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathscr{E}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$ and let $μ$ be a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ whose values on $\mathscr{E}$ are finite but unbounded. Applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E)}{μ(E)}\right\}_{E\in \mathscr{E}}$ yields a finitely additive measure $\varphi_μ$, which can be viewed as a generalized normalization of $μ$ to total mass one. To obtain a nontrivial necessary condition on $μ$ for the resulting measure $\varphi_μ$ to be invariant, we establish two results of independent interest: we extend the Yosida--Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures and prove a theorem previously stated by Bingham and Ostaszewski concerning translates of sets of Haar measure zero. The first theorem yields a decomposition of $μ$ into a purely finitely additive component and two countably additive components, respectively singular and absolutely continuous with respect to Haar measure. Using the second result, we show that the invariance of $\varphi_μ$ implies that the singular component $μ_s$ is negligible relative to $μ$ and can be removed without changing $\varphi_μ$. A counterexample demonstrates that the purely finitely additive component $μ_p$ need not have these properties.

papers.title: Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincaré inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.

papers.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover for strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential decay of density gradients and second velocity derivatives are established. In contrast, if an initial vacuum occur, then it will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

papers.title: Iso-Multiplication Modules over Noncommutative Rings: Triangular Classification and Rational Rigidity
papers.abstract: A right A-module M is called iso-multiplication if for every submodule N of M there is a two-sided ideal B of A such that N ?A MB. We construct noncommutative examples of isomultiplication modules which are not multiplication modules, including triangular algebras of arbitrary dimension. We classify all iso-multiplication modules over T_2(k) without a finitegeneration assumption. For a semiprime right Goldie ring we prove that the classical localization of an iso-multiplication module is multiplicity-free. Further consequences address composition length and local rings; we distinguish these from standard Morita, Ore-localization, and chaincondition results.

papers.title: Covering hypercubic grids by polygonal trails: capacity bounds and the optimum for $P(4,3)$
papers.abstract: The classical nine-dot puzzle asks for a polygonal trail through a square grid using as few segments as possible. We study its higher-dimensional analogue on $P(n,k):=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^k$ for integers $n,k\ge2$, allowing arbitrary real vertices and unrestricted segment directions, and denote the minimum number of segments by $h(n,k)$. For $n\ge3$ and $k\ge2$, we give a geometric proof of the previously stated capacity bound: a trail of $r\ge1$ segments meets at most $1+r(n-1)$ grid points. Refinements of this bound, combined with exhaustive finite checks, establish $h(4,3)=23$ and $h(5,3)\ge32$. We also exhibit a $22$-segment trail through $63$ points of $P(4,3)$, the maximum possible, and a $23$-segment covering trail contained in $[0,4]^3$, which settles the corresponding box-constrained problem. The general capacity theorem, a large-grid lower bound refuting a previously proposed formula for $h(n,k)$, and the boxed construction are verified by the Lean 4 kernel, whereas the finite exclusions use native reflection and additionally trust the native compiler and runtime. A companion technical note provides the computational specification and reproducible proof artifacts.

papers.title: Detour different-distance sets in graphs
papers.abstract: The detour distance $D(u,v)$ between two vertices of a connected graph is the length of a longest $u,v$-path. A set $S$ of vertices is a detour different-distance set if no vertex outside $S$ has the same detour distance to two vertices of $S$. We study the lower and upper detour different-distance numbers $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)$ and $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$, the smallest and largest orders of maximal such sets; this is the detour analogue of the different-distance sets of Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder. The two notions coincide on trees, cycles, complete bipartite graphs and the Petersen graph, but differ in general: for instance, detour different-distance sets may contain triangles or induce $4$-cycles. We determine both numbers for many families, among them wheels, fans, windmills, hypercubes, helms, flowers, books, ladders, prisms, Möbius ladders, crowns, gears, Dutch windmills and complete multipartite graphs, and for joins, coronas and lexicographic products. We prove that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)$ is at most the detour diameter; that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=n-1$ if and only if $G$ is a path; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=1$ whenever two vertices are joined by Hamiltonian paths to all other vertices; that $\mathrm{dd}_D(G)=\mathrm{DD}_D(G)=2$ for Hamiltonian-laceable graphs and, more generally, for bipartite graphs in which each part contains two vertices whose detour distances to the other part are constant; and that $\mathrm{DD}_D(G)\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ for Hamiltonian graphs.

papers.title: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension. This gives explicit flow-box coordinates, closed formulas for hitting times, return times and orbit averages, and a Newton iteration that computes them with quadratic convergence; in dimension one it recovers Mukhamedov's theorem that interpolated orbits are balls. I then show that the analytic maps $g$ congruent to the identity modulo $p^c$, coefficientwise, are exactly the time-one maps of such fields, and that the field is congruent to $g - \mathrm{id}$ modulo $p^{c+1}$. So the interpolated iterates of Bell and Poonen are flows of this kind, and I obtain a quantitative minimality criterion: if the displacements $g_i(x_0) - x_0$ of $d$ such maps span $p^k\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, the group they generate acts minimally on the ball of radius $p^{-k}$ about $x_0$. Where the argument of Cantat and Jang gives an orbit closure containing some open set, this names the ball, at every level $k$ and in every dimension; for $d = 2$ and $k = 1$ it is Jang's criterion for Markoff surfaces, which I test numerically at $7830$ points. Finally, the formal logarithm of $\mathbb{G}_m$ or of an elliptic curve is the rectifying coordinate of an explicit field, so the local divisibility $v_p([t]z) = v_p(z) + v_p(t)$ for $v_p(z) \ge 1 + c$, deep in the kernel of reduction, follows from the metric identity alone.

papers.title: The chromatic-AT choosability of Pseudo-Halin graphs
papers.abstract: The \emph{Alon-Tarsi number} $AT(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits an orientation $D$ with maximum outdegree at most $k-1$ in which the number of even Eulerian subdigraphs differs from the number of odd Eulerian subdigraphs. A 2-connected planar graph $G$ with minimum degree at least 3 is called a \emph{pseudo-Halin graph} if deleting the edges on the boundary of a single face $f_0$ yields a tree. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the class of pseudo-Halin graphs in which no two interior vertices are adjacent and every interior vertex has odd degree (equivalently, graphs obtained by iterated Hajós sums of wheels with an odd number of exterior vertices). In this paper, we completely determine the chromatic number and the Alon-Tarsi number of all pseudo-Halin graphs. Specifically, by structural induction and the method of $AT$-orientations, we prove that $AT(G)=χ(G)=4$ if $G\in\mathcal{A}$, and $AT(G)=χ(G)=3$ otherwise. Consequently, every pseudo-Halin graph is chromatic-AT choosable.

papers.title: Star decomposition of complete multipartite graphs
papers.abstract: We study minimum degree-sum conditions for decompositions into stars of sizes $k$ and $k+1$, where $k\ge3$. Write $σ(G)=\min_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)+d(v))$, and let $c_k$ be the least integer threshold guaranteeing a $\{K_{1,k},K_{1,k+1}\}$-decomposition for every finite simple graph. Using Tarsi's sufficient condition, we prove that $K_n$ admits such a decomposition whenever $n\ge2k$. Together with the obstruction $K_{2k-1}$ of Zhao and Wu, this gives the optimal integer threshold $4k-3$ for complete graphs. For complete multipartite graphs, we establish the sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge9$ when $k=3$ by a finite computational verification and an extension argument. For every $k\ge3$, the complete tripartite graph $G_k=K_{k^2-k-1,k-2,1}$ satisfies $σ(G_k)=k^2-1$ and has no such decomposition. Consequently, $c_k\ge k^2$, even when the class is restricted to complete multipartite graphs. The optimal integer threshold in this class is therefore $9$ for $k=3$. Sufficiency of $σ(G)\ge k^2$ for complete multipartite graphs with $k\ge4$, and the exact values of $c_k$ for general graphs, remain open in this study.

papers.title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
papers.abstract: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

papers.title: Error accumulation in reverse diffusion with an imperfect score: beyond path-space analyses
papers.abstract: Diffusion modeling is a popular method of sampling from a complex, high-dimensional distribution $p$ using learned approximations of its (noised) score functions. Generating a single sample requires simulating the reverse diffusion process, which requires many queries to the learned scores. Thus, a priori, the learning errors can easily compound. Indeed, in existing theoretical analyses, the sampling error (as measured in total variation distance to $p$) accumulates polynomially with the horizon of the stochastic process. This is a consequence of bounding the error of the output law by the error of the law of the entire reverse diffusion path. In this paper, we demonstrate that by circumventing the "path-space" analysis, the error accumulation of the diffusion sampler can be mitigated when $p$ satisfies a Poincaré inequality. Moreover, we achieve this result as a special case of a broader framework that applies to any distribution $p$, but relaxes the error metric from total variation distance to a weaker metric capturing all sample statistics that do not "witness" the multimodality of $p$. We then zoom out from analyzing the diffusion sampler to the information-theoretic question: given a learned score with some error bound, how accurately can we identify $p$? We show that, for any given bound on the Poincaré constant of $p$, the diffusion sampler already nearly achieves optimal total variation error.

papers.title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
papers.abstract: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.

papers.title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
papers.abstract: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic. This has two major operational consequences. First, leaving the high-debris equilibrium requires a large cut in launch rates. Second, in the low-debris equilibrium, fragment counts respond with a delay as the launch rate rises past a tipping point. Removing bistability is desirable, and we show that fragment count-indexed admission control can achieve this. The least restrictive such policy lengthens the lag, whereas an exponential tilt of this policy makes the fragment count track its equilibrium with a bounded lag. Furthermore, admitting more launches can reduce the rate of completed missions, and under a unimodality condition a threshold rule on the debris fragment count maximizes this rate at equilibrium.

papers.title: Efficient Variance-Aware Reinforcement Learning in Time-Inhomogeneous Linear MDPs
papers.abstract: We study variance-dependent reinforcement learning in episodic time-inhomogeneous linear Markov decision processes (MDPs) with feature dimension $d$, horizon $H$, and $K$ episodes. While recent works have established variance-dependent regret with $\tilde{O}(1)$ deterministic-regime overhead for linear mixture MDPs (Zhao et al., 2023) and worst-case nearly minimax optimal regret $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{H^3 K} + d^7 H^8)$ for linear MDPs (He et al., 2023),, existing variance-aware analyses for linear MDPs (Li and Sun, 2023; Huang et al., 2023) rely on a coarse concentration step whose resulting regret guarantees retain a polynomial $\tilde{O}(K^{1/4})$ additive term even in deterministic environments. We propose VA-LSVI-UCB++, a computationally efficient algorithm that achieves the variance-dependent regret bound $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{H\min\{\mathrm{Var}_K^*,\mathrm{Var}_K^π\}}+d^5H^4)$, where $\mathrm{Var}_K^*$ and $\mathrm{Var}_K^π$ denote the cumulative conditional variances of the optimal value function and the played policies' value functions along the realized trajectory. Our result adapts to the minimum of the two realized trajectory variances, recovers the worst-case minimax optimal leading term $\tilde{O}(d\sqrt{H^3 K})$, and collapses to $\tilde{O}(d^5 H^4)$ in deterministic environments, free of polynomial-in-$K$ dependency. At the core of our analysis is a simultaneous three-way reference-advantage decomposition for the optimistic, pessimistic, and squared value function estimators coupled with variance self-bounding and Freedman-type value-difference arguments, which tightens the pessimistic and second-moment confidence radii by a factor of $\tilde{O}(d H)$ and removes the inverse-variance-floor blowup.

papers.title: Modeling fluid--solid interaction in three-dimensional granular systems: Two-way coupling of SPH and LS-DEM
papers.abstract: This paper presents a two-way coupled fluid--solid interaction framework for granular systems based on the level-set discrete element method (LS-DEM) and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH). The proposed method is mesh-free, fully Lagrangian, and equipped with a seamless description of arbitrary solid shapes. In particular, a level-set representation of grain geometry is used for both contact detection and fluid--solid coupling, allowing for realistic, highly irregular grains to be handled within a unified computational framework. Moreover, the method incorporates a convenient treatment of moving boundaries and admits a simple computational implementation. The capabilities of the proposed SPH--LS-DEM framework are demonstrated through several numerical benchmarks involving dam-break flow, flow through porous media, granular collapse, and cyclic loading of a saturated granular specimen. The study sets the stage for several extensions to multiphysics problems across disciplines.

papers.title: Perspectives on the hidden subgroup problem over unitriangular groups
papers.abstract: We investigate the quantum Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) over the upper unitriangular group $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$. While efficient quantum algorithms were discovered for some families of non abelian groups and nil-2 $p$-groups, no efficient algorithms are known for groups of nilpotency class higher than 2. The only techniques known for such groups scale exponentially in the size of the input. We first study the group $U_4(\mathbb{F}_p)$, the smallest upper unitriangular group exhibiting nilpotency class three. We analyze the application of the Pretty Good Measurement approach used for Heisenberg groups and show its limits. We then focus on the more general case $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$ to adapt existing techniques to this particular structure. In particular, we derive an algorithm for cyclic subgroups as a subroutine for a general algorithm, although it is not efficient in the size of the group. Our results highlight the difficulties introduced by the increasing nilpotency class and suggests some directions for an efficient quantum algorithm for the HSP over $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$.

papers.title: Spectral Pricing of Corridor Products under Layered Local Volatility
papers.abstract: We price corridor products under a $N$-layered local volatility, piecewise constant in the price and in time, with knock-out barriers. A spatial scale transformation and the GIT method reduce the killed Green's function to a symmetric tridiagonal system of fixed size $N-1$. With equal scaled layer widths the spectrum follows from one tridiagonal eigen-decomposition together with the explicit eigenfunctions that vanish at every interface. For general scaled layer widths an exact counting theorem locates every eigenvalue. Consecutive time intervals of constant volatility are connected by a matrix that re-expands the solution in the eigenbasis of the preceding interval, and the result converges exponentially in the number of retained terms in the eigenfunction expansion. Allowing the killing rate to vary between layers preserves this construction. On a single time interval, the corridor accrual distribution is then recovered by inverting the time and Fourier transforms, without introducing an additional state variable. Exact representations for Greeks and layer vegas follow by differentiation. In our benchmarks the method agrees with independent calculations near rounding error and keeps full accuracy at volatility interfaces, where the tested uniform finite-difference (FD) grids lose one order of convergence. The method computes the accrual law about sixty times faster than the tested FD scheme that includes accrued time as a second state variable.

papers.title: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
papers.abstract: The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits. In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian. The conditional measures on the fibers are either uniform on finite sets or convex combinations of at most two homogeneous measures associated with split simple subgroups of $\mathrm{PGL}_k(\mathbb{R})$ containing the principal $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$. Another objective of our work is to relate weak-$*$ limits of probability measures on $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ supported on the projective classes of lattices orthogonal to integer vectors with limiting distributions of the corresponding normalized Frobenius numbers. This correspondence gives limit laws for vectors sampled from certain proper subvarieties, extending J. Marklof's work on sampling from full-dimensional domains. Specifically, together with our results for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ orbits in $X_{n-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, this correspondence gives limit laws for primitive integer vectors sampled from $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbits. Using an earlier result of the first author and Shapira, we obtain analogous laws for integer vectors sampled on level sets of certain quadratic forms, as the level tends to infinity.

papers.title: Spectral Stability and Convergence of the Unnormalized Graph Laplacian on Noisy Point Clouds
papers.abstract: The first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the unnormalized graph Laplacian of clean samples from a manifold, suitably scaled, approximate those of a weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator. However, the samples are usually observed with noise and therefore need not lie on the manifold. We build the clean and noisy graph Laplacians, with bandwidth $\varepsilon$, on the clean samples and on the noisy observations, where the noise is arbitrary but bounded by $δ$. We show that, with high probability, the first eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the noisy graph Laplacian are close to those of the clean one: the eigenvalues within $O(δ/\varepsilon)$, and the subspaces spanned by the first eigenvectors within $O(\sqrt{δ/\varepsilon})$, whether or not the eigenvalues are simple. Consequently, if $δ$ is small enough relative to $\varepsilon$, the noisy graph Laplacian approximates the weighted Laplace-Beltrami operator at the same rate as the clean one. We also show that, for large noise, we can get the same rate as the clean graph Laplacian by first using a denoiser, and then building the graph Laplacian on the denoised observations.

papers.title: Multiple transition points for an epidemic model
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with a spatial epidemic model on the $d$-dimensional square lattice that extends the contact process in two ways by assuming that each site is occupied by a social cluster of $N$ individuals rather than a single individual, and that infected individuals can be either asymptomatic or symptomatic. Newly infected individuals begin as asymptomatic and develop the symptoms at a spontaneous mutation rate $γ$, and all infected individuals recover at rate one. The model also distinguishes between external (between adjacent clusters) and internal (within clusters) infection rates for each state. Our analysis shows that, when either asymptomatic or symptomatic individuals only spread the disease externally and at a subcritical rate, while the other class only transmits the disease internally and at a large rate, the system exhibits at least two phase transitions with respect to the mutation rate $γ$ when social clusters are large. Specifically, the epidemic dies out for extreme values but survives for intermediate values of the mutation rate.

papers.title: 3-Cube-Free Sets in Cyclic Groups
papers.abstract: A set is called $3$-cube-free if it contains no configuration of the following form: $\{x,y,z,x+y,x+z,y+z,x+y+z\}$. We study the maximum density of $3$-cube-free sets in finite cyclic groups. As observed by Meng, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_m$ has size at most $2m/3$, and this bound is sharp whenever $3\mid m$. Our main result shows that there exists an absolute constant $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every $m$ not divisible by $3$, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ has size at most $\left(2/3-\varepsilon\right)m$. Thus, in this setting, the natural $2/3$ barrier can be uniformly improved. Long and Wagner conjectured that every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_{2^n}$ has size at most $5\cdot 2^n/8$. We also establish this conjecture for 3-cube-free sets whose density in the layer of odd residues is at least $2/3$. Together with induction, this reduces the conjecture to the case where this density lies in $(5/8,2/3)$.

papers.title: Federated Differential Privacy with Batch Contamination
papers.abstract: We study mean estimation under federated differential privacy (FDP) constraints and batch contamination, considering both Gaussian and heavy-tailed distributions. In the homogeneous setting, where sample sizes and privacy budgets are constant across servers, we show that the costs of privacy and contamination disentangle. Under a bounded $v$th moment condition, with $v \in (1, \infty)$, the cost of batch contamination is of order $(\varepsilon/n)^{2-2/v}\vee \varepsilon^2/n$, where $\varepsilon$ is the contamination level and $n$ is the per-batch sample size. This reveals a phase transition at $\varepsilon\asymp n^{1-v/2}$, for $v > 2$, which is the first of its kind in the literature. We develop a two-stage procedure that achieves the minimax rate up to poly-logarithmic factors. A key component is a private smoothed voting procedure tailored to the FDP setting that provides optimal sensitivity control. For heterogeneous batch sample sizes and privacy budgets, we introduce a batch partitioning framework that groups batches with comparable per-batch sample sizes and privacy budgets. Surprisingly, the minimax rate is determined, up to poly-logarithmic factors, by the most informative group of batches. Consequently, in some regimes, it is minimax optimal to use only an arbitrarily small proportion of the data set. Heterogeneity also introduces interactions between the costs of privacy and contamination, in contrast to their disentanglement in the homogeneous setting. For unknown contamination level, we propose an adaptive, near-minimax optimal Lepski-type extension for the heterogeneous Gaussian setting, designed specifically to prevent privacy leakage by ensuring no repeated use of data points.

papers.title: A Feasible-Domain Reduction Approach with Objective-Loss Guarantees for Multilevel Multiobjective Linear Programming
papers.abstract: In some approaches to decentralized multilevel multiobjective programming, each decision-maker selects a compromise and restricts the feasible region before passing the decision to the next level. However, these restrictions do not necessarily limit the deterioration of objective values at preceding levels. This paper studies how to choose variable bounds that keep such losses within prescribed tolerances. We establish exact conditions using linear programming duality and derive simpler bounds based on objective coefficients. We also examine the choice of restriction widths and establish guarantees for successive reductions. A two-level numerical example illustrates the results and the influence of tolerances on the final compromise.

papers.title: Bounded-Order Non-Identifiability in Latent Structure Block Models: The Fiber in Closed Form
papers.abstract: A graphon is determined by all of its homomorphism densities, but motif-based methods use finitely many. We compute exactly what that truncation costs in a natural family: latent structure block models whose positions lie on $K$ rays, equivalently degree-corrected block models of rank two. For a given radial law, the configurations that agree on every graph with fewer than $2K-1$ vertices form a one-dimensional fiber, which we give in closed form with explicit endpoints; the friendship graph $F_{K-1}$ is its unique edge-minimal separator, so no fixed motif order serves every $K$. The separating signal is suppressed by a factor of at most $m_1^{2(K-1)}$, where $m_1$ is the mean squared slope, about $10^{-4}$ at $K=4$: detecting it from motif counts would take about $10^{15}$ nodes in a single graph, at any edge density. The information is nonetheless in the graph; the fiber belongs to the statistic, not the model. Common spectral pipelines, which count no motifs, still slide along the fiber by more than a third of its length at ordinary densities, with confidence regions that almost never contain the truth, while model-based fits of the same embedding do not. We give practitioners four checks: whether a fit is at risk, what to run instead, why a confidence interval will not warn, and how wide the remaining ambiguity is.

papers.title: Quadratically Regularized Medians in Metric and Wasserstein Spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new class of robust aggregators in Wasserstein spaces. After proving that all the commonly used Wasserstein barycenters are manipulable by one single corrupted input through a novel first-order optimality condition, we generalize both to the metric setting and to fractional exponents the concept of Lipschitz resilience introduced recently by Allouah, Guerraoui, Hoang and Villemaud. We proceed to show that adding a quadratic regularization to Wasserstein medians defined either in terms of the $W_1$-metric or linearized $W_2$-metric are resilient in that sense, by leveraging fine convexity estimates along generalized geodesics and flat interpolations. We finally show that iteratively solving the latter problem amounts to performing a Majorization-Minimization approximation of $W_2$-medians.

papers.title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
papers.abstract: Geometric convolutions on Riemannian manifolds depend on the geometry of the underlying domain, making stability under metric perturbations a fundamental question in geometric deep learning. This paper studies this question for parallel transport convolution through methods from differential geometry and analysis. On a fixed compact manifold, we establish that, for a continuous input signal and a continuous reference kernel supported in a sufficiently small normal neighborhood, the convolution output depends continuously in $L^2$ on the Riemannian metric in the $C^2$-topology, under the specified localization and transport-path conventions. The analysis develops perturbation estimates for geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps, and uses these estimates to compare the transported kernels. A central difficulty is the cut locus, which obstructs uniform comparison of the transport construction over the entire manifold. We address this difficulty by combining uniform estimates away from the cut locus with integral bounds on neighborhoods of arbitrarily small volume, while also controlling the change in the Riemannian volume measure. The resulting qualitative stability theorem connects perturbation theory for Riemannian geometric constructions with the analysis of spatial convolution operators in geometric deep learning.

papers.title: The Gini Index of an Integer Composition
papers.abstract: We extend the discrete Gini statistic on integer partitions to integer compositions by rearranging the parts in decreasing order. Under the uniform distribution on the $2^{n-1}$ compositions of $n$, the resulting statistic has a rational ordinary generating function for its aggregate values, as well as a rational generating function for its second moments. More generally, the generating function of every fixed raw moment is rational, although the bivariate generating function encoding the entire distribution is not. We obtain an exact formula for the mean and prove that the variance of the unnormalized statistic is asymptotic to $10n^3/189$. The normalization used for partitions has mean tending to $2/3$, in contrast to the limit $1$ under uniform random partitions. Using the separator representation of a random composition and a renewal-reward argument, we prove a central limit theorem: its centered, normalized Gini statistic has asymptotic Gaussian fluctuations with variance constant $40/189$. We also prove that the ordinary classical Gini coefficient of the composition parts tends to $1/3$ and satisfies a central limit theorem with variance constant $20/189$.

papers.title: Binomially Weighted Partition Statistics: Generating Functions, Asymptotics, and Dominance
papers.abstract: For an integer partition $λ=(λ_1,λ_2,\ldots)$, we consider $M_m(λ)=\sum_{i\geq1}\binom{i+m}{m+1}λ_i$, where $m\geq0$. We prove conjugation and Frobenius-coordinate identities for this family and obtain its ordinary and bivariate generating functions. Differentiating the bivariate product gives exact formulas for the mean and variance under uniform sampling of partitions of $n$. For fixed $m$, we show that $\mathbb E[M_m]\simζ(m+3)(\sqrt{6n}/π)^{m+3}$ and determine an explicit positive constant multiplying $(\sqrt{6n}/π)^{2m+5}$ in the variance asymptotic. The family encompasses the row sum underlying the discrete Gini statistic and, after conjugation, a linear combination giving the Wiener index of starlike trees; the associated normalized statistics have contrasting limits under uniform random sampling. We also prove that every $M_m$ is strictly decreasing along the dominance order. Consequently its level sets are antichains, providing coefficient-based lower bounds for the width of the dominance lattice.

papers.title: Compactifying the $G_2'$-Hitchin component via almost-complex curves
papers.abstract: By studying limits of induced metrics of equivariant almost-complex curves in the pseudosphere $\mathbb{S}^{2,4}$, we compactify the $G_{2}'$-Hitchin component.

papers.title: The Double Entropy Fit Index (DEFI): An Information-Theoretic Approach to Dimensionality Reduction and Clustering
papers.abstract: We introduce the Double-Entropy Fit Index (DEFI), a regularized information-theoretic criterion for selecting among candidate graph partitions and reduced representations. DEFI couples entropy-based compression with relevance preservation and penalizes model dimensionality, cluster imbalance, and partition fragmentation. An exact Rényi-2 entropy identity shows that partitioning alters both spectral concentration and graph-volume normalization, explaining why unregularized entropy minimization can favor degenerate solutions. Across a 243-condition population-analytic factor recovery benchmark, DEFI achieved an overall exact recovery rate of 97.2\% (versus 75.0\% for EGA-TMFG, 45.8\% for TEFI on von Neumann entropy). In controlled local candidate batteries (distinguishing the true model from adjacent $K \pm 1$ and factor-split alternatives), DEFI identified the correct partition in 99.2\% of replications. Across ten clustering benchmarks, DEFI-guided Gaussian mixtures achieved a mean ARI of 0.929, exceeding HDBSCAN (0.809), Ward clustering (0.700), and conventional GMM criteria (0.501-0.580), with gains concentrating where standard criteria over-extract components.

papers.title: An explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations
papers.abstract: We develop an explicit domain-preserving projection scheme for scalar stochastic differential equations whose solutions evolve in a prescribed interval. A Lamperti-type transformation converts the original equation into one with additive noise, whose drift may be singular near finite boundaries or grow polynomially at infinity. The proposed domain-preserving projected Euler-Maruyama (DPPEM) scheme combines an explicit Euler-Maruyama step with projection onto a step-size-dependent interior interval. Under one-sided Lipschitz, boundary, and weighted growth assumptions, with projection parameters chosen according to the coefficient growth and available moment orders, we establish strong order one convergence for admissible moment orders. The analysis combines local consistency and stability estimates with moment and boundary negative moment bounds for the exact solution. Numerical moment bounds follow from the convergence estimate, while numerical negative moment bounds are obtained under additional conditions. Estimates for the inverse Lamperti map yield strong order one convergence for the original equations in the CIR, Heston 3/2, CEV, Ait-Sahalia, and bounded interest-rate models under the stated model conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the predicted convergence rates and compare computational costs with the Lamperti backward Euler-Maruyama scheme.

papers.title: Twisting and foam inequalities for the upsilon invariant
papers.abstract: We describe two families of bounds on the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó invariant $Υ_K(t)$, one controlling its behavior under inserting full twists into a knot and one controlling a limited class of foams, or singular cobordisms between knots. By constructing certain explicit foams, we show that these two formal properties of $Υ$ together exactly determine $Υ_K(t)$ for all torus knots. This generalizes previously observed behavior at $t = 0$, Livingston's slice-torus invariants, and at $t=1$, Sato's unoriented analogue. Our foam bounds on $Υ$ make significant use of Alishahi's generalization of $Υ$ to knotted graphs. Along the way we compute Alishahi's invariant for all theta-graphs lying on the Heegaard torus in $S^3$. We also relate the evaluations of $Υ$ for torus theta-graphs to a distinguished family of properly embedded 2-complexes in the 4-ball sharing many properties with Batson's surfaces.

papers.title: Protection Group of Colored Links
papers.abstract: Colored links provide a mathematical framework for studying the topological stability and classification of three-dimensional topological vortex configurations. Earlier classifications in settings of physical interest relied on system-specific invariants. Here, we introduce a universal invariant of colored links, the \textit{protection group}, interpret earlier classification results as computations of this group, and compute it in new examples.

papers.title: Periodicity of Entire Solutions of $ff''=H^2$
papers.abstract: Let $f$ denote a transcendental entire function. The so called Yang's conjecture asserts that if for some integer $k$ ($\geq1$) the product $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic, then $f$ must be also periodic. In this paper, we prove that when $k=2$ for a given periodic transcendental entire function $H$, and $f$ is an entire solution of the equation $$ff''=H^2,$$ then \(f\) must be periodic.
